﴿If there are two sisters, then for them is two-thirds of what he leaves. And if there are brothers and sisters, men and women, then the male has the equivalent of the share of two females. Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray. And Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾ (Part of verse 176 of Surat al-Nisa').

In the first verse under discussion, one of the brothers has a sixth of what is left when he stands alone; if there are others with him, they share in a third. This applies when they are maternal brothers. As for the verse in which the Truth singles out two sisters for two-thirds of the estate when there is no male agnate with them, it concerns full (ashqa') brothers or paternal brothers. Thus the Qur'an explains and clarifies with absolute precision.

What, then, does His saying "without causing harm, a commandment from Allah, and Allah is All-Knowing, Most Forbearing" mean?

He, glory be to Him, wants to establish justice, so there is no harm to anyone whatsoever in the application of the law of Allah, because harm comes only from desires that corrupt the division of Allah. There may be someone who wishes that the paternal uncle not inherit from the daughters of his full brother or paternal brother, or another who wishes that the sons of brothers, full or paternal, not enter into the inheritance of the aunt or the daughters of a full or paternal uncle. To such people of desire we say: liability follows gain (al-gharm 'ala qadr al-ghanm). By Allah, if you died and left daughters, and they had an uncle, is it not required of the uncle to raise the daughters? Why would the Truth compel the uncle to care for his brother's daughters if the brother died and left nothing? Therefore you must pay attention to the reality of the matter when the uncle's share in the inheritance comes. And we must know that before liability stands gain.

We have said that the Noble Qur'an must be taken in its entirety concerning the rulings. If in this Surat al-Nisa' the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, says in its final verse:

﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning kalala: if a man dies leaving no child and he has a sister, then for her is half of what he leaves, and he inherits from her if she has no child. But if there are two sisters, then for them is two-thirds of what he leaves. And if there are brothers and sisters, men and women, then the male has the equivalent of the share of two females. Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray. And Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾ (176, Surat al-Nisa').

What, then, is the difference between the kalala in which Allah gives the lone sister half and two sisters two-thirds, and the kalala in which Allah gives the lone one a sixth, and gives those more than one who share in the third without distinguishing the male from the female?

We must distinguish between one kalala and another kalala.

They agree that the deceased has no root and no branch. But the matter here concerns brothers.

We say: brothers have multiple sources. These sources are either brothers from the same father and mother, or paternal brothers, or maternal brothers. If there is a full brother or a paternal brother, he is of the original agnates ('asaba asilah), and these are the two meanings in verse 176 of the same surah.

Thus the verse of the sixth and third that we are discussing now concerns maternal brothers. So the kalala is either one in which the heir is only a maternal brother, or a paternal brother, or a full brother. The rulings for each therefore differ, because the position of each differs from the other. Otherwise, if an orientalist read this verse and read the other verse, both of which concern the inheritance of kalala, and wished to seek something with which to attack our religion and attack the Qur'an, he would say, God forbid: the Qur'an is contradictory. It says once that the kalala gets a sixth, once a third, once a half, once two-thirds, and once that the male has the share of two females! We respond to whoever says this: you have not noticed the actual and real intent of kalala; therefore you understand something and miss other things.

The Truth said: "after any bequest that is made or debt." We should note that in every inheritance there is this "afterness," meaning inheritance comes into effect only after the bequest that must be executed and the debt.

We should ask: which is executed first, the bequest or the debt?

The answer: without doubt it is the debt, because debt is an obligation of right upon the liability (dhimma), whereas bequest is voluntary. How, then, could the bequest, which is voluntary, be given precedence over the debt, which is obligatory upon the liability?

When He says "without causing harm," we must know well that the law of Allah will harm no one. And what is meant by this? It is meant for the testator. Sometimes the deceased dislikes some of those entitled to their share of his inheritance, so he comes to bequeath the prevention of their inheriting or the reduction of their portions, or he comes to a distant person whom he wants to give something of the inheritance, while not giving it to one of his family and relatives whom he dislikes, who are entitled to his inheritance. So he acknowledges a debt owed to that person. Even if he acknowledges a debt that consumes the entire estate, the person takes the debt, and thus the heirs are left with no inheritance.

This happens in life and we see it. Some people Allah has given daughters but has not given them a male child to be their agnate. One of them says to himself: the paternal uncles will enter, and the sons of the paternal uncles will enter into my inheritance, so he wants to distribute the estate to his daughters only, and he writes a debt upon himself to the daughters. We say to this person: do not act unjustly. You looked at the fact that these people inherit from you, but you must look at the opposite side, which is that if you die and leave your daughters nothing, and they have no agnate, who is responsible for them? It is the paternal uncles. So here liability stands against gain. And why do the daughters bring the paternal uncles before the judges to take maintenance from them in the case of the father's death without his leaving any wealth? How, then, do you withhold from your brothers what Allah has decreed for them?

And there are some people, one of whom wants that his paternal uncles or brothers not be given anything for any reason. What does he do? He sets up a bequest. Therefore Islam limited the bequest to a third, so that no harm comes to the heirs.

Some of these people have tried to claim falsely that there is a debt upon them, and that the debt consumes the estate so that the relatives take nothing.

A person in this situation must know that he stands, at every moment of life or death, before Allah, and every person is trustee over himself.

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, said:

﴿Your fathers and your sons—you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit. An obligation from Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾ (Part of verse 11, Surat al-Nisa').

The Truth calls our attention not to harm anyone by any conduct, because it is a commandment from Allah regarding everything connected to the ruling: inheritance, bequest, and payment of debt. All of that is a commandment from Allah, and the commandment is not from a creature to a creature, but from Allah; therefore it carries obligation and duty. Glory be to Him who said: ﴿He has ordained for you of religion that which He enjoined upon Noah﴾ (Part of verse 13, Surat al-Shura).

The commandment here is an obligation, and likewise the Truth says:

﴿And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right. That is what He has enjoined upon you, that you may reason.﴾ (Part of verse 151, Surat al-An'am).

Since the commandment comes from the Supreme Owner, it means that it is an obligation. And the Truth, glory be to Him, concludes the verse we are dealing with with faith-inspired reflections: "And Allah is All-Knowing, Most Forbearing." That is: beware lest you act in a way that the judiciary may approve and enforce, but which does not clear you before Allah, because it has been established upon falsehood.

An example: there is a person who dies with a debt upon him; then the debt must be settled. But if a man writes a debt upon himself that is not real, in order to deprive some of his relatives of inheritance, he must know that Allah is All-Knowing of the intentions behind actions. If you are blinded to the judgment of the earth, you will not be blinded to the judgment of heaven.

This is a matter that requires knowledge that penetrates intentions. So the matter of judiciary is a dispute between human and human, but the matter of religious obligation, and what the Truth has made obligatory, is a matter between the Lord and His servants. Therefore the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said in a noble hadith: "I am only a human being, and you bring your disputes to me. Perhaps one of you is more eloquent in his argument than another, and I judge for him according to what I hear. So whoever I give to him something of the right of a Muslim, it is only a piece of the Fire; let him take it or leave it." (1)

The Messenger teaches us that he is a human being, meaning he does not possess knowledge of the unseen or the inner workings of matters. When Muslims bring their cases to him, one of them may be more capable of eloquence and fluency of tongue and can turn falsehood into truth, while the other has little resourcefulness; the Prophet judges according to the evidence presented, but the actual state of affairs contradicts the sequence of truth. Therefore he teaches us that he is human, and that when we bring disputes to him, none of us should use fluency of tongue to take what is not his right; for even if he takes something that is not his by the ruling of the Messenger (ﷺ), let him know that he is taking a piece of the Hellfire.

So this means we must be cautious in matters, and not be blinded, nor take something by the authority of the judiciary while neglecting the matter of religion. Matters connected with religion are not permissible for the believer to touch. Beware of thinking that the ruling of any ruler makes lawful what is forbidden or forbids what is lawful. No. What is lawful is clear, and what is forbidden is clear, and the judge must rule by clear evidence. An example: suppose you borrowed a thousand pounds from someone and he took a note from you; then the borrower paid what he owed and said to the lender: "When you go home, please send me the note." Then the decree of Allah preceded, and the family of the deceased said: "The note is with us," and they went to court to take the debt. Here the judiciary rules that the debt must be paid again, but the religious ruling in this differs: the man has paid the debt, and it is absolutely not valid for the heirs to take the debt again if they know that their deceased relative obtained his debt-payment.

Therefore the Truth says to us: "And Allah is All-Knowing, Most Forbearing," so that we distinguish between religious obligation and judiciary. The Truth tells us that He is "Forbearing," so beware of being deceived into thinking that because someone did such a thing and Allah did not take vengeance on him in this world, his conduct was lawful. The non-punishment by Allah in this world does not indicate that his action was lawful; rather, it is forbearance, respite, and deferral from Allah, but there is punishment in the Hereafter.

(1) Narrated by Malik, Ahmad, al-Bukhari, Muslim and Abu Dawud, from Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her.

After the statement of these matters, the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿These are the limits of Allah, and whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great triumph.﴾ [4:13]

The rulings mentioned earlier and the matters that preceded them are all the limits (hudud) of Allah. When Allah sets limits, that is, He prevents right from being confused with right, or right from being confused with falsehood, He is the one who sets the limits, and He is the one who separated rights from rights.

When we separate rights from rights in houses and lands, we set clear boundaries, and the meaning of "hadd" (boundary) is a dividing line between two rights, so that no one takes what is not his from another. The boundaries we create ourselves, to which many people may not pay attention, are of two kinds. One kind concerns construction and is not to be exceeded in building: when someone wants to build, the first builds on land that is his right, and the walls are adjoining one another. When a farmer plants beside another farmer, each farmer plants in his own land, and between the two plots there is a boundary, and this occurs for benefit.

But let us suppose that a farmer wants to plant rice, and his neighbour will not plant rice. The land of the one who will not plant rice may receive excess water, for water suits rice but may spoil other crops. Therefore the ruling here is that the rice grower sets up a boundary called "the boundary of neighbourhood" (hadd al-jiwara) to prevent harm, and this is not a "boundary of ownership." The rice grower here reduces his cultivation by a distance of two metres and makes with them the boundary of neighbourhood, so that the water with which the rice is irrigated does not spill over into the neighbour's land. It is a boundary that prevents harm, and it differs from the boundary that prevents appropriation.

Thus, from the standpoint of a person protecting himself from causing harm to others, he must heed the clear saying: "Do not make your right reach the limit of another's boundary, but make your right in benefiting lie far from your boundary." This applies to ownership, and that is when your benefit from everything you own will harm your neighbour. Likewise Allah deals with us, and in commands He says:

﴿These are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them﴾ [2:229].

And in prohibitions He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿These are the limits of Allah, so do not approach them﴾ [2:187].

That is, when you receive a command, do not transgress that command, and this is ownership; and when you receive a prohibition, do not approach the thing forbidden. An example of this is the prohibition of wine. The Truth does not say, "Do not drink wine," but says: "Indeed, wine, gambling, stone altars and divining arrows are an abomination from the work of Satan, so avoid it." That is, do not go to the place where these things are found in the first place; be on one side, and these things on another side.

Therefore we said, in the story of Adam eating from the tree: Did the Truth say, "Do not eat from the tree," or did He say, "And do not approach this tree"? Glory be to Him, He said:

﴿And do not approach this tree﴾ [7:19].

This is a limit called "the limit of non-harm." He commanded non-approach so that a person is not afflicted with desire or the appetite to eat from the tree. Likewise the gatherings of wine, because they may entice you. In commands He, glory be to Him, says: "These are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them," and this concerns ownership.

In prohibitions He, glory be to Him, says: "These are the limits of Allah, so do not approach them." And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ says this hadith: "The lawful is clear and the unlawful is clear, and between them are doubtful matters which many people do not know. Whoever guards against doubtful matters has safeguarded his honour and his religion, and whoever falls into doubtful matters falls into the unlawful, like a shepherd who grazes around the sanctuary, about to fall into it. Indeed, every king has a sanctuary, and indeed the sanctuary of Allah on His earth is His prohibitions. Indeed, in the body there is a lump of flesh: if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt; indeed it is the heart" (1).

Therefore avoid the limits of Allah. An example is the saying of the Truth:

﴿And do not have intercourse with them while you are devoted to worship in the mosques. These are the limits of Allah, so do not approach them. Thus Allah makes His signs clear to mankind that they may be God-fearing﴾ [2:187].

The Truth commands the one secluded in the mosque that when his wife comes to discuss some matter with him, the believer must comply with Allah's command by not having intimate contact with the wife in the mosque, and he should not bring matters close to intimate contact, because that is among the limits of Allah. And He says: "These are the limits of Allah, so do not approach them."

Here, in matters of inheritance, the Truth says:

﴿These are the limits of Allah. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever; that is the great triumph﴾ (Surat an-Nisa').

After the statement of the limits, it would have sufficed for the Truth to say: "Whoever obeys Allah," but He said: "Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger," and this is to make clear that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has the right to set limits of his own regarding what is made lawful, and to set limits regarding what is made unlawful. This is a delegation from Allah to His Messenger in that he legislates; therefore do not say about everything, "I want the ruling from the Qur'an."

We see some who say: "Between us and you is the Book of Allah; whatever we find in it to be lawful, we deem lawful, and whatever we find in it to be unlawful, we deem unlawful." These did not notice that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is delegated in legislation, and he is the one who said:

﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾ [59:7].

He ﷺ is delegated by Allah, and those who call for judgement by the Qur'an alone wish to cast doubt on the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They appeal to the Book of Allah, and they forget or ignore that in the noble Book there is a delegation from Allah to His Messenger ﷺ to legislate.

They say: "Between us and you is the Book of Allah; whatever we find in it of lawful we deem lawful, and whatever we find in it of unlawful we deem unlawful." Their saying such a thing is evidence for the truthfulness of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in what he says, for if they had not said it, we would have said: O Messenger of Allah, you said: Al-Miqdam ibn Ma'di Karib narrated, he said: The Prophet ﷺ made unlawful "things on the day of Khaybar, among them the domestic donkey and other things, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: It is about to be that one of you reclines upon his couch, narrating my hadith, and he says: Between us and you is the Book of Allah; whatever we find in it of lawful we deem lawful, and whatever we find in it of unlawful we deem unlawful. And indeed what the Messenger of Allah has made unlawful is like what Allah has made unlawful" (2).

How, O my master, O Messenger of Allah, would that be, when no one has said this statement?

Therefore their foolish saying is evidence for the truthfulness of the Messenger in what he reported. The Truth subjects them so that they utter such a saying, so that we may infer from the words of the Prophet's opponents the truthfulness of the Prophet's words.

The Truth says: "Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit him to gardens." The one who obeys Allah and His Messenger in this world is the one who takes up the obligation and applies it, and the reward is entry into Paradise in the Hereafter. But is the admission to Paradise the method of the religion, or is it the reward for the religion?

It is the reward for the religion, and the subject of religion is conduct in this world. Whoever walks on the path of Allah in this world enters Paradise in the Hereafter. The Hereafter is not the subject of religion; rather, the subject of religion is this world. When you want to isolate this world from religion, we say to you: you have not made a subject for religion. Beware of saying: the subject of religion is the Hereafter, because the Hereafter is the abode of reward. And in our lives we take this example: is the examination the subject of the curricula, or do the curricula, which the student reads throughout the year, form the subject of the examination?

The curricula that the student studies are the subject of the examination. Likewise the world is the subject of religion, and the Hereafter is the reward for whoever succeeds and whoever fails in the subject; therefore beware of saying: "world and religion," for there is no separation between the world and religion, because the world is the subject of religion. The world is opposed by the Hereafter, and both belong to religion. The world is a field and the Hereafter is the harvest. By this we refute those who say that the world is separate from religion.

Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He admits him to one garden, or two gardens, or gardens. Does the particle "man" (whoever) indicate the singular? No. "Man" indicates the singular, and it indicates the dual, and it indicates the plural. For example, we say: "Whoever I met yesterday came," and we also say: "Whoever I met yesterday, the two of them came," and we say thirdly: "Whoever I met yesterday, they came..." So "man" is suitable for the singular, the dual and the plural.

The Truth here does not speak of singular or plural. As we said at the beginning of al-Fatiha:

﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ [1:5].

Although the analogy would be to say: "You alone I worship, and You alone I ask for help," the Truth, glory be to Him, said: "You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help," to clarify for us that all the believers are one unit in worship.

And there are those who say: if "man" indicates the singular, we have observed its wording; and if it indicates the dual or plural, we have observed its meaning.

To one who says that, we say: this statement is not scientifically established, because no one has said that the word "man" is for the singular. Rather it is set for the singular, the dual and the plural. So do not say: use the word "man" out of regard for the wording or out of regard for the meaning, for the word "man" is set for three meanings: the singular, the dual and the plural.

A noble brother asked me in one of the sessions: why does the Truth, glory be to Him, say in Surat ar-Rahman:

﴿And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾ [55:46].

I said to him: the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, opened Surat ar-Rahman with:

﴿The Most Merciful, taught the Qur'an, created man﴾ [55:1-3].

After that the Truth said:

﴿He created man from clay like pottery, and He created the jinn from a smokeless fire﴾ [55:14-15].

And He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿We will attend to you, O two worlds (humans and jinn)﴾ [55:31].

And the Most High said: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass; you will not pass except with authority﴾ [55:33].

So whoever fears the standing before his Lord, whether he is of the jinn or of mankind: if he is of the jinn he has a garden, and if he is of mankind he has another garden. Thus whoever fears the standing before his Lord has two gardens.

And some say: two gardens for each one of mankind and jinn, because Allah does not suffer from a shortage of places. When He willed from eternity to create creatures, He numbered them, from Adam until the Hour is established, and He treated all of them as believing and obedient, and He established for each one his place in Paradise; and He, glory be to Him, treated all of them as disobedient, and established for him a seat in the Fire. This is so that no one may understand that the matter is a shortage of places.

When the owner of the garden enters his garden, the garden of the disbeliever that was prepared for him on the supposition that he was a believer remains. Therefore the Truth says:

﴿And that is the garden which you have inherited for what you used to do﴾ [43:72].

Thus the believers inherit what had been prepared for others had they believed.

So the meanings we find are correct in every style of the Qur'an.

Here the Truth says: "He admits him to gardens beneath which rivers flow." We must understand that the river is the channel in which water flows, not the water itself. The Truth says: "gardens beneath which rivers flow." So where do the rivers flow?

Do the rivers flow beneath their crops, or beneath their buildings? We know that crops need water, and we want to keep water away from buildings, how? But nothing is impossible for Allah, because these are divine designs.

Creatures may dig a river, and afterwards we find seepage striking the buildings; but the designs of the Truth, with the ease of power, make it so that gardens have rivers of water flowing beneath them, and no seepage occurs from them, whether from beneath the buildings of the gardens or beneath their crops. And the one who turns to the method of his Lord and asks Him to pour out and inspire him, He, glory be to Him, gives and bestows. The Truth says at one time: "gardens beneath which rivers flow," and at another time He says: "gardens in which rivers flow beneath them." This is possible and that is possible.

His saying, glory be to Him, "gardens in which rivers flow beneath them" may suggest that the rivers come from another place and flow and pass beneath the gardens. No. They also flow from them, as Allah the Most High says: "gardens beneath which rivers flow," so that no one thinks there is someone who can cut off water from you from above. They are self-generated rivers. And when we read that rivers flow beneath the gardens, with what is in them and who is in them of palaces, someone may say: can I not take from these and

2 Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, from Jabir.

Then the Truth (exalted is He) presents the counterpart, saying: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits, He will admit him to a Fire, abiding therein; and for him is a humiliating punishment.﴾ [4:14]

He, glory be to Him, had said earlier: "These are the limits (*hudud*, the boundaries set by God) of Allah." The limits either specify commands alone, or specify prohibitions alone. So they encompass both: that the obedient one obeys them, or that the disobedient one disobeys them.

If you obey, then you have the reward of obedience, and you take the Gardens, the eternity, and the great triumph.

But what about the one who disobeys? For him there is the counterpart, and this is his position and his recompense: that for him is punishment.

﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits, He will admit him to a Fire, abiding therein; and for him is a humiliating punishment.﴾

Here we find "a Fire" (*naran*) in the singular, and there we find "Gardens" (*jannat*) in the plural. This is a first observation. And if we are attentive and turn toward the Book of Allah, and know that the Speaker is Allah, we find a second observation: the eternal abiding of the believers in the Gardens, whereas the disbeliever will enter the Fire. The Truth did not say "fires" (*niran*), and the Truth did not say "abiding" in the plural (*khalidin*). Why? Because the believers will be in Paradise on couches facing one another, visiting one another, and each one enjoys all the Gardens. Also, when a person has much righteous deed and his children who shared with him in faith fall short, the Truth, glory be to Him, joins his offspring to him, and he and his offspring are in bliss and Gardens as an honour to him. So the Gardens are together, and this is more conducive to intimacy.

But the situation differs for the disbeliever. Allah will not join anyone to him, and each one will take his own fire. So that they do not find companionship with one another while in the Fire, intimacy will not be extended to them either. Each one is in his own fire, exactly like solitary confinement in a cell. None of them will find companionship with another tormented one. Thus there are "Gardens," "Fire," "abiding" (*khalidin*) and "abiding" (*khalidan*), and every use of the word has a meaning. The obedient one has Gardens in which he finds companionship with his offspring and his brothers, the people of faith, and they will all abide together in the Gardens. But the disobedient one is in the Fire alone, "abiding," "and for him is a humiliating punishment."

Punishment may be painful in a single instance. An example of this is when one person hurts his enemy, and the enemy steels himself so that the one who tortures him sees no gloating from him. The poet says:

*"I display my steadfastness before the scorners,*
*and I do not waver before the vicissitudes of time."*

So he conceals the pain from his opponent. But this is in the world. In the Hereafter, however, there is a humiliation of the self. The punishment of Allah combines pain and humiliation. Beware of thinking that anyone can steel himself as humans steel themselves when punishment befalls them in this world. The punishment of the Hereafter is humiliating and abasing to the self, both at once.

Thus we find that the first stage of Surat al-Nisa' dealt with the unity of the human being as a father, and his unity as a mother, and it dealt with how Allah spread from the two of them many men and women. The surah also dealt with what occurs, by the decree of Allah, to some of His creatures: that they are left as orphans, weak. He, glory be to Him, willed the preservation of a dignified life for the human soul. Therefore He required us to do good and show affection to orphans, and He set out the manner of faithful dealing with them, and that we be guardians who uphold justice and a good, chaste intention regarding their wealth, until they reach the age of maturity and receive it.

The surah also dealt with another matter: the preservation of a dignified life for women and children within the social fabric. The Arabs used to deny women inheritance, and also deny inheritance to whoever had not thrust a spear, struck with a dagger or sword, or taken part in repelling an aggression. So Allah, glory be to Him, willed that this humiliated and oppressed group should take its right, so that both elements might live in dignity, preserve life in honour, resolve and strength. The Truth therefore legislated a specified share for women, differing from the share of men, whether small or large. After that He digressed to speak about rights in inheritance. He, glory be to Him, made clear the limits He prescribed for this matter. Whoever wishes the Gardens of Allah, let him obey Allah and His Messenger in what He has set as limits. And whoever is content to forgo these Gardens, let him disobey Allah so that he will abide in the Fire.

So human life is a gift from Allah to His servants. And from His generosity, glory be to Him, He brought into existence, before creating it, that which sustains the dignified life of this honoured human being. Thus man came to good, and good did not come to man. That is, the Truth, glory be to Him, did not create man first and then afterwards make for him the sun, the moon, the earth and the elements. No. Allah created these elements that serve man first, and prepared them to receive the new arrival, the human being whom He chose to be a vicegerent on earth. So the good on earth by which we preserve life preceded the existence of man, and this is care from the Truth, the Merciful, toward His honoured creature, who is man. And Allah made for man a means of propagation and linked it to the process of enjoyment. This means of propagation differs from the means of propagation in plants and animals, for the means of propagation in all living things serves only the preservation of the species.

He, glory be to Him and exalted, willed that enjoyment accompany the means of human propagation, because the hardships that the raising of offspring requires are many, so Allah must place in the process of reproduction a pleasure that entices man.

By this, the Truth, glory be to Him, willed to bring forth the weak in order to make from them a strong life.

The Truth also enjoins us regarding the orphan among humankind. Someone may say:

"Since the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, enjoins us so that we may raise from the orphan a strong human being, and that we do good to the orphan, why did Allah will that the orphan's father should die?" We say: The Truth set this matter so that human life should not be a *darbat lazib* (an inevitable, binding matter, an obligation) upon Allah. He creates the human being with a specified lifespan, known to Him, glory be to Him, and unknown to the human being. A human may die as a foetus, or as a child, or as a youth, or as a man, or in old age. Indeed we find in life an aged human being who is still living among us, and his great-grandson dies. Why?

Because Allah willed to conceal the matter of death from people. There is no knowledge for a human of the age he will live, nor of the time of death, nor of the place of death, so that each of us is always ready to die at any moment. And since a person lives ready to die at any moment, he must be ashamed to meet Allah in disobedience. Also, let us know that the faithful method is a method that makes the believers, all of them, like a well-compacted structure, each part strengthening the others. So when a man dies and leaves an orphaned child, and this orphan finds fathers from the believing society, then the faithful method settles in the orphan's heart as tranquillity and certainty. And among the wisdom of death is that no one should be tested regarding his father, or regarding the means that Allah grants to fathers, but rather we should all be connected to Allah.

And since the Truth, glory be to Him, has set for us the means to preserve life, and has set for us the manner of striving on the earth so that life may be preserved through movement upon it, He has also set the noble means for preserving the species, and has made the movement of the root (the parent) benefit the branch (the offspring). He did not make man alone move for his own sake, but rather He made him desire to move in life with a movement that suffices him and those he supports. And the Truth makes clear to man: your movement upon the earth will benefit your children too.

For this reason Allah, glory be to Him, placed in the soul of every father the instinct of tenderness and love. We see this instinct as one of the signs of Allah, firmly established in the souls of fathers. Therefore the father strives in life so that he and his children may benefit. And one who moves widely in life may reach a time when the return of his movement suffices him for the rest of his life, because he moved with resolve and sincerity, and Allah bestowed upon him abundant provision. And a man may strive for twenty years or more and secure for himself and for his children after him abundant wealth. And there is one who toils and labours in life and earns a livelihood that suffices him and suffices his children and grandchildren.

Thus we find that those who move do not benefit alone, only, but the society benefits too. And the lofty wisdom of Allah willed that wealth be divided by the laws of inheritance, so that wealth spreads and is distributed among the children and thus circulates in society. This is called *al-tafteet al-insiyabi* (gradual, flowing dispersal of wealth). For example, we find a man who owns a hundred *faddans* (a unit of land) and has a number of sons and daughters. After the man's death, the sons and daughters inherit his entire estate, and thus the wealth is dispersed among the children by gradual, flowing dispersal, not by the compulsory distribution that breeds rancour and enmity. The Truth wishes us to respect the movement of the one who moves, and that the return of his life's movement be his, and for those he supports. So He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿Indeed, the life of this world is but play and amusement. And if you believe and fear Allah, He will give you your rewards and will not ask you for your wealth.﴾ [47:36]

He, glory be to Him, does not say to any individual: "Give me the wealth that I gave you." And I said earlier: He, glory be to Him, makes a servant tender toward a servant, so He says:

﴿Who is it that would lend to Allah a goodly loan so He will multiply it for him and he will have a noble reward?﴾ [57:11]

Indeed Allah, glory be to Him, respects the servant's movement, and respects what the servant has possessed by his sweat. And the Truth enjoins the wealthy servant: your brother, the poor servant, is in need, so lend to Me, Allah, by giving charity (*sadaqah*) or zakat (obligatory alms) to your poor brother. He did not say to the wealthy servant: "Lend to your brother." Rather He said "lend to Me." Why? Because He, glory be to Him, is the One who summoned creation into existence, and He is the guarantor of their provision, all of them, the believer among them and the disbeliever. Therefore He guaranteed provision for all, and commanded the means to respond even to the disbeliever, because He, glory be to Him, is the One who summoned him into existence.

And He, glory be to Him, instituted this inheritance so as to bring about the gradual, flowing dispersal of ownership, so that there would not come a compulsory dispersal in which some of the children, having grown up in blessing and taken from life whatever they desired, find themselves, when that compulsory dispersal comes upon them, among the needy whom sudden events have overtaken with deprivation. They were not prepared for this sudden poverty. But when the gradual, flowing dispersal comes, each one prepares himself for what he will receive, with a contented self and according to his capacity for movement. For this reason the Truth said:

﴿Indeed, the life of this world is but play and amusement. And if you believe and fear Allah, He will give you your rewards and will not ask you for your wealth.﴾ [47:36]

He, glory be to Him, does not say: "It is I who gave you this wealth, and it is I who granted you this provision," even though He, glory be to Him, is in truth the One who owns you and provides you this wealth. But He makes clear to you your right in movement, and so He says after that:

﴿If He should ask it of you and press you, you would be stingy, and He would bring forth your rancour.﴾ [47:37]

For if He pressed you for it, you would be stingy with it, because you gained it through toil and sweat. But what is the difference between a person who did not squander upon himself, but lived moderately, and then left something for his children; and one who brought in his entire income and squandered it on what Allah has forbidden, and wasted himself on narcotics and other things? What is the difference between this one and that one?

The difference is the Truth's respect for the effect of a person's movement in life. Therefore He makes clear: "I do not ask you for your wealth, because if I asked you for your wealth you might be stingy, for your wealth is the return of your labours."

And the Truth says: "and He would bring forth your rancour." When rancour appears and emerges in society, then woe to the whole society. For this reason we find that every one of these compulsory movements gives rise to the emergence of rancour throughout society, and when rancour appears in society, everything beautiful comes to an end. Therefore the Truth established the foundations and means for preserving a dignified life.

He established foundations for the weak, by which He protects them, and likewise for the women who were deprived of inheritance before Islam. And the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, made for the inheritance of children, sons and women limits: "These are the limits of Allah," and beware of transgressing these limits, for when a person transgresses these limits, he must be among the people of the Fire, God forbid. For Allah has set those rules for preserving your life and the life of those you support.

There is another kind of preservation, which is the preservation of the species, because a human being has a limited lifespan in life and will come to an end. Therefore a person must preserve the species in others. How? We marry so that Allah may bless us with offspring, sons and grandchildren, and the links continue. And this is the preservation of the human species.

The Truth wishes this preservation of the species to be dignified. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, commands us to preserve the species by, that we

The commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 4, verse 15:

Listen to the word of God:

﴿And those of your women who commit lewdness, bring against them four witnesses from among you. And if they testify, then confine them to the houses until death takes them or God ordains for them a way.﴾ (4:15)

"Allati" (the ones who) is a relative pronoun for a group of females, and I see that this is specific to the sufficiency of a woman with a woman. What does He mean by His saying: "bring against them four witnesses"? He, glory be to Him, intends by it the protection of honour, so that no one may assail the honour of another. Rather, the truth must place for it a strong precaution, because honours will be wounded. And why "four" in testimony? Because they are two who enjoy one another, and it is required that two should testify against each one, so that they become four. And if this happens and we have seen, known and been certain, what do we do?

He, glory be to Him, said: "confine them to the houses", that is, detain them and imprison them from movement, and do not give them a means of meeting, until death takes them, "or God ordains for them a way", and God has ordained it.

To those who say that this matter concerns an act between a man and a woman, we say: the word "allati" here is a relative pronoun for a group of females. As for when it is between a male and a male, in that case the Truth says:

﴿And the two of you who commit it, harm them both. But if they repent and amend, then leave them alone. Indeed, God is ever Accepting of repentance, Merciful.﴾ (4:16)

The verse here concerns the meeting of a man with a man, and therefore the first matter concerns the woman with the woman. And why is the punishment, in the matter of a woman's meeting with a woman seeking pleasure, confinement to the houses until death takes them? Because this is an evil and a plague that must be besieged, for this evil means complete corruption, since a woman is not screened from a woman; so that a woman be imprisoned until she dies is better than that she become accustomed to lewdness. We do not know what harms will result, and science is still deficient. He who created is He who legislated that a man should meet a woman within the framework of marriage and what is required in it of dower and witnesses. And He, glory be to Him, prepared the woman for receiving and prepared the man for sending, and this is a natural matter; so when a sending enters upon a receiving that is not its own, interference occurs.

If the meeting is not in the legislated manner that the One who created us has determined, then something wrong and harmful must occur. When we connect an electrical wire with another wire of the same type, that is, negative with negative or positive with positive, fires ignite, and we say: "an electrical short circuit has occurred", meaning the electrical connection was wrong. If a wrong electrical connection in a few wires has caused what harm it has caused, is it not the case that a wrong connection in sexual relations is harmful to human beings?

I say this so that it may be recorded, because science will reveal, sooner or later, that God has a secret. When a man is joined to a woman by the method of God, "marry me..." and she says to him, "I have married you", the Truth makes the meeting natural. But if a difference occurs in sending and receiving, there will be a destructive, striking short circuit, and these are the fires in society.

I repeat this so that it may be recorded and said to future generations: those before us were guided to a breath of the breaths of God, and they did not incline to laziness, but faith guided them to be connected to God, so they perceived the breaths of God. And the Truth is the One who says:

﴿We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves, until it becomes clear to them that it is the Truth﴾ (part of 41:53).

If we have been guided to knowing that the connection of a correct wire with a correct wire gives beautiful light, but if an error occurs in the connection, a short circuit happens and fires result from it, then likewise in the human relationship, for the matter is male and female.

And the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾ (part of 51:49).

So if beautiful light results from the correct connection between positive and negative in non-human things, and fires result if the connection is wrong, what then of the human being?

On some of our journeys abroad, we asked some people:

"Why have you allowed a man several wives, and not allowed women several husbands?"

They wish to stir up the woman's resentment and anger against the religion of God, so that the naive woman, rebelling against her religion, says: "There is no justice in this religion." So I asked those who asked me: "Do you have places where sexually licentious youths rest?"

The answer was: "Yes, in some states there are such places."

I said: "What precautions have you taken for people's health?"

They said: "Periodic sudden medical examinations."

I said: "Why?"

They said: "So that we may isolate any woman who has any disease."

I said: "Does that happen with every married man and woman?"

They said: "No."

I said: "Why??" They fell silent and did not answer, so I said: "Because the reality is that a married woman with one man is a vessel for that man alone, and no disease arises from her; but disease arises when the water of many men multiplies in one place."

Thus the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, wants to preserve the species in a clean state; therefore He said: ﴿And those of your women who commit lewdness, bring against them four witnesses from among you. And if they testify, then confine them to the houses until death takes them or God ordains for them a way.﴾ (4:15)

By "your women" here is meant the Muslim women, because we do not legislate for others, since they do not believe in God. And the demand for testimony is from four Muslims, because the Muslim knows the value of honour and justice. And if they testify, then let the judgment of God take effect by confinement in the houses.

We have known this in what in the modern age is called quarantine, in which we place people with infectious disease. There is a difference between those afflicted with "an infectious disease" and those afflicted with "ruin and disgrace". If we isolate people with infectious disease, how then should we not isolate those afflicted with ruin and disgrace? Therefore the Truth says: "confine them to the houses until death takes them or God ordains for them a way", meaning that each of them remains in isolation until the Angel of Death comes to each of them. The books of legislation have related to us that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) applied the verse to fornication that occurs between a man and a woman, and not between two women.

On the authority of ʿUbada ibn al-Samit, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Take from me, take from me: the virgin with the virgin, a hundred lashes and exile for a year; and the married with the married, a hundred lashes and stoning."¹

Then legislation came afterward and clarified the matter of the prescribed punishments: that the virgin with the virgin is lashing, and the married with the married is stoning. Some people say that stoning is not mentioned in the Qur'an.

We reply: And who said that legislation came only through the Qur'an? The Qur'an came as a miracle and as a method for the foundations, and as we said before, the Truth said:

﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it﴾ (part of 59:7).

Afterward we take up the matter: when there is a binding text for a ruling, we may understand the ruling from the text or we may not; if we understand it, it has practical application in the Prophetic biography.

If the Messenger (ﷺ) had not come with the text only, but also with the practice itself, then the example is in the actual carrying out of the prescribed punishment, because the deed is stronger than the text. The text may exist without being applied for a reason such as abrogation of the ruling, for example; but the deed is application. The Messenger stoned Mâʿiz, who had confessed, and he stoned a Jewish man and a Jewish woman when they came asking to alter the ruling of stoning found in the Torah. So the deed of the Messenger is stronger than the text, especially since the Messenger is also a legislator. Someone once said: "Stoning is for the one who is married; what then do we do with a married man who has committed fornication with a virgin girl?"

The ruling here: the man is stoned and the girl is flogged; if the two are in agreement in the case, they take one ruling, and if they differ, each takes the ruling that suits him.

And when the Truth spoke of the punishment of slave women, He said:

﴿Upon them is half of the punishment for free chaste women﴾ (4:25).

From this is understood flogging only, because stoning cannot be divided into two halves. So the slave woman receives half the punishment of the free woman, for the free virgin who commits fornication is flogged a hundred lashes, and the slave woman is flogged fifty lashes.

Since the slave woman has half the punishment of the chaste woman, there is no punishment except that which can be halved, and stoning cannot be halved; the proof is definitively from the act of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who is a legislator and not one who derives rulings, and the Messenger of God stoned. And why does the slave woman receive half the punishment of the free woman? Because slave women are held in disregarded dignity, whereas free women are not. Hence Hind, the wife of Abu Sufyan, said: "Does a free woman commit fornication?" She said this while in the violence of her pre-Islamic ignorance. That is, fornication is not the characteristic of free women, whereas the slave woman's dignity is disregarded, since she is open to assault and is nobody's honour.

Therefore upon her is half the punishment of chaste women. Some have asked about the situation of a married slave woman who committed fornication, and stoning has no half.

We say: stoning removes life, so there is no halving with it; thus "half of what is upon the chaste women of the punishment", and punishment is that which causes pain. We cite in support of this a verse to show the decisive opinion that punishment is one thing and killing and taking away life is another thing; we find this verse is the word of the Truth on the tongue of Solomon, peace be upon him, when he missed the hoopoe and did not find it:

﴿I will surely punish him with a severe punishment, or I will surely slaughter him﴾ (part of 27:21).

So punishment is other than slaughter, and likewise punishment is other than stoning. As for what some who wish to create an uproar argue, that there is no stoning because the slave woman has half of what is upon chaste women and stoning admits no halving, we say to him: what you cite is false, because God distinguished between punishment and slaughter, and said on the tongue of Solomon: "I will surely punish him with a severe punishment or I will surely slaughter him." If punishment is other than taking life by slaughter, then punishment is also other than taking life by stoning. Therefore no one should attempt to escape the text and understand it other than its reality. Let us discuss the matter by reason:

When a person assaults a virgin, what is the circle of assault on honour in the case of the virgin? It is narrower than the circle of assault on the married woman, because the married woman is usually married, so the most that happens to a virgin is that the assault is on her honour and the honour of her father and brother. As for the married woman, the assault is also on the honour of her husband, and thus the circle of assault is larger; it is an assault on the honour of the father and mother. Brothers and uncles are like the virgin's, and in addition to that the husband and the successive children. If fathers and mothers are a generation that ends, the children are a generation that endures; therefore the shame endures. The enduring of shame cannot be equal to a patch that lacks this breadth; if we equate the two by flogging, this means the one who executes the ruling has not noticed the breadth of the wound to honour.

The wound to honour in a virgin is confined and may end, because it is among contemporaries such as father, mother and brothers; but what do you say, O one who executes the ruling, regarding the married woman who has children who reproduce? It is a broad patch. Would God, who is just, equate a married woman and a virgin with flogging alone? This is by no means possible.

Therefore the matter must be taken from what the Messenger of God clarified, he being the second legislator, who was distinguished not only by understanding the text, but because he has the right of legislation in what has no text! So we shall adopt what he did, for the Messenger of God indeed stoned, and it ended with this ruling becoming definitive: the married with the married is stoning, and the virgin with the virgin is flogging, and the virgin and the married each takes his ruling, and the ruling applies perfectly; thereby we guarantee the purity of preserving the species, because preserving the species is a fundamental matter in life, by preserving the life of the individual and preserving his species. The preservation of the individual's life is by maintaining him, bringing him up well and feeding him lawfully; and preserving the species is by safeguarding the purity of intermingling.

The Truth, glory be to Him, supplies His creation when they neglect the method of God, with what draws their attention to the method from those who do not believe in the method of God; He brings us the proof from the mouths of those who do not believe in the method of God, so that it becomes clear to you that the method is sound.

¹ Narrated by Muslim on the authority of ʿUbada ibn al-Samit.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 4, verse 16

I have previously explained that when a man sees a young man looking at one of his female relatives (muhārim), he is stirred, becomes agitated, and wishes to kill him. But if this young man comes by the lawful path of God, and the father of the young man says to the father of the girl: "I want to propose your daughter for my son," then the situation changes, the faces relax, and joy is celebrated.

It is the word of God that affects the chemical make-up of the soul and produces all this radiance and cheer. The announcement of such events with drums, lights and decorations is clear evidence that a need has been fulfilled and has had its effect on the human soul, the effect that God intended from connection through the clean, noble and chaste path.

Every connection outside this noble and chaste path must produce a defect in the human constitution, leading to psychological and physical epidemics that a person may not be able to repel, as is happening now.

On this basis, the word of the True One, glory be to Him, is:

This was an initial stage, until the Messenger applied the establishment of the hadd (prescribed punishment).

﴿And the two of you who commit it, harm them both. But if they repent and amend, then leave them alone. Indeed, God is ever Accepting of repentance, Merciful.﴾ (4:16)

God, the Exalted, is Tawwāb (Accepting of repentance) and Raḥīm (Merciful). We know that the form of intensity (ṣīghat al-mubālagha) regarding God does not mean that an attribute of God is sometimes weak and sometimes strong; all of God's attributes are one in absolute perfection. I said before: when I say "fulān akkāl" (so-and-so is a great eater), the meaning may differ from my saying "fulān ākil" (so-and-so eats). By this form I exaggerate in describing a person who eats a lot. Does he eat much in a single meal, or is the meal's quantity limited but this person multiplies the meals, so that instead of eating three times he eats five times? Then it is said of him "akkāl", meaning he multiplies the meals, even though each meal in itself has not increased in size.

Or he comes to a single meal and eats many times what an ordinary person eats in an ordinary meal, eating four loaves instead of one, and we say: he is "akūl" (a great eater). Thus the form of intensity in creation either arises from the strength of a single event, or arises from the repetition of a single event.

When you say "God is Tawwāb", it means that when He accepts the repentance of this one and that one and of millions upon millions of people, repentance is repeated. And if the Truth accepts repentance for major sins, is that not a great repentance? He is Tawwāb and Raḥīm because He, glory be to Him and exalted, is characterised by the greatness of wisdom and the power to create and originate. He is the One who created the human soul, then legislated laws for it, and afterwards criminalised whoever opposes these laws, and after criminalising departure from the laws, He set a penalty for the crime.

Legislation in itself cuts off excuse. Once the Truth has legislated, no one can say "I did not know", because that is the law. When He criminalises, this is a notice from Him that the human soul may weaken and bring things contrary to the method. We are not angels. Glory be to Him: when He legislates, He cuts off excuse; and when He criminalises, it is a notice that this may happen. After that He punishes. There are acts that are criminal, yet the First Legislator has not criminalised them and has not set a law for them, not out of negligence on His part, but because criminalisation comes as a branch.

God, glory be to Him, has decreed that the human soul may do such things, such as theft: He set a limit (ḥadd) for theft, and the human soul may weaken and steal, or commit adultery. Therefore the ḥadd exists. But there are things for which He brings no criminalisation or penalty, as if He, glory be to Him, wished to show us, by a hidden hint, that these are matters the intellect could not have imagined. An example is sodomy (liwāṭ). He mentioned no ḥadd for it. Why? Because sound human nature (al-fiṭra al-salīma) does not do it, as proof that sodomy exists among humans and does not exist among animals.

But the fact that the Truth does not criminalise an act does not mean it is not counted in the reckoning. No, it is counted in a stronger way, because criminalisation and penalty for criminalisation show that the act may happen. When He leaves a matter without criminalisation, this means that sound human nature should not do it, and therefore He did not set a ḥadd or criminalisation for it, and left the matter to the Messenger of God (ṣallā Allāh ʿalayhi wa-sallam), who is charged with legislation, to set a ḥadd for this matter.

So the absence of a text on a crime or a penalty for a crime does not mean that there is no reckoning for it. No. There is a reckoning, and the penalty may be more severe. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) commanded that the doer of sodomy and the one to whom it is done be thrown from the top of a mountain. Their punishment is to die by being thrown from a high mountain; so the penalty is greater than stoning. Thus we know that the absence of criminalisation and the absence of a penalty set for any matter unfitting to reason and to sound human nature is evidence that the matter is not permitted. The Truth did not leave those matters in silence; rather, it is a hidden hint that this must not happen, as proven by the fact that it does not happen among animals, which are lower than humans.

After that, the human who commits such foul ugliness may plead that it is a bestial desire. We say: would that your desire, which errs in expressing itself, were bestial, for beasts never do such an act. A female animal does not approach another, and likewise no male animal approaches another male, and when a female animal is pregnant she does not allow any male animal to approach her. So the foul ugliness of intercourse contrary to what God has legislated may be called a human desire, for beasts do not commit those deviant acts. Whoever calls desire bestial wrongs the animals. And the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, despite these sins, makes clear to us that He is the Tawwāb, the Merciful. Why?

Consider the wisdom in repentance and in its acceptance. If no sin had occurred from the person who believes, the obligation (taklīf) would lose its necessity. The meaning of taklīf is a process in which a person struggles with himself and strives to resist carrying out sins, or to compel himself to the hardship of obedience.

The person's resistance to sins, submitting to the obligation of faith, is evidence that taklīf is a true matter, called "taklīf"; otherwise God would have created us like the angels and the matter would have ended. When God legislates repentance, this shows that man is weak and may at some day weaken before some sin. This does not mean that God expels him from His servitude; rather He sets a penalty, and setting a penalty for the sinner is evidence that He, glory be to Him, has not removed from the fold of Islam or of taklīf the one who chose Islam and disobeyed. If we supposed that the Truth had not legislated repentance, then cursing would become the fate of everyone who weakens before a desire, and the sinner would become a rebel who cares not and no longer heeds taklīf, going into people's honour and committing all evils.

So when God legislated repentance, He closed to people the door of those who are lost (al-fāqidīn), who commit a sin and then persist in it. Yet when He, glory be to Him, relents toward the sinner, He shows mercy to the one who did not sin, for He is the One who said: "Indeed God is ever Accepting of repentance, Merciful." If the Truth had said only that He is Tawwāb, every one of us would sin so that the attribute would be with him and established in him inevitably. But He also said "Tawwāb Raḥīm", meaning that He shows mercy to some of His creation, so they do not commit any sin from the beginning. Mercy is that you do not fall into sin.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 4, verse 17:

Then, after that, the Truthful, Exalted One legislates repentance: ﴿Repentance with God is only for those who do evil in ignorance and then repent soon. Those are the ones to whom God turns back in forgiveness, and God is ever Knowing, Wise.﴾ [4:17]

Let us attend to the precision of the Qur'anic expression. He, glory be to Him, says: "Repentance with God is only..." Someone may say: since God has legislated repentance, I will do whatever I wish of disobedience and then repent afterwards. We say to him: you have not considered the wisdom in the concealment of the hour of death. What revealed to you that you will live until you repent? Death may seize you suddenly while you are in disobedience. You must attend to the precision of the Qur'anic text:

﴿Repentance with God is only for those who do evil in ignorance and then repent soon. Those are the ones to whom God turns back in forgiveness, and God is ever Knowing, Wise.﴾ (Surat an-Nisa').

"Doing evil in ignorance" means without keeping in mind the appropriate punishment for the sin. Had a person kept the punishment in mind, he would not have committed the disobedience. Rather, he ignores the punishment. Therefore the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said:

("The adulterer does not commit adultery while he is a believer, nor does the thief steal while he is a believer, nor does the drinker drink wine while he is a believer.")(1)

Had his faith been sound and he were fully mindful that faith obliges him not to commit adultery, and that the punishment for adultery is flogging or stoning, he would not have done that act.

God has said: "Repentance with God is only for those who do evil in ignorance and then repent soon." There are those who commit disobedience, plan for it, rejoice in it, boast of what they committed, and take pride in the time of the sin. And there are those upon whom sin befalls, and as soon as it ends they remain regretful, strike themselves, punish themselves, and ask: why did I do that?

To distinguish between the two, let me give an example. Two people each prepare to travel to Paris. One of them asks before his trip about the experience of those who have lived in the French capital, and tries to obtain the addresses of places of amusement and debauchery. As soon as he goes to Paris, he immerses himself in pleasure, and when he returns he keeps boasting of the sins he committed.

The other travelled to Paris to study, and while he was there he committed a sin under temptation and adornment. So he is a person upon whom sin befell, without planning. After the fervour of desire subsided, he drowned in regret, and after returning he concealed the time of the sin. Thus we see the difference between the one who plans the sin and the one upon whom sin befalls.

When God decreed the matter of repentance for His creatures, He showed mercy to all creatures by regulating this repentance. Otherwise the world would have drowned in endless evils, beginning from the first person who deviated once and then took deviation as his practice. What matters in the penitent is that he has done evil in ignorance and then repented soon. When the Messenger (ﷺ) defined the meaning of "soon", he said:

("Indeed God accepts the repentance of the servant as long as he has not reached the death rattle.")(2)

And the dialogue that took place between the Truth and Iblis:

﴿He said: "My Lord, because You have led me astray, I will surely make [evil] attractive to them on earth and mislead them all, except among them Your chosen servants."﴾ (Surat al-Hijr, 39-40).

Iblis said this and thought that he would destroy all of mankind and lead them into disobedience, except the servants of God whom He chose and purified for Himself. But God frustrated his expectation and legislated the acceptance of the servant's repentance as long as he has not reached the death rattle, that is, the stage when the soul leaves the body. If the servant offers repentance at the moment of the death rattle, what does society gain? Society gains nothing from such repentance, because he repented at a time when he had no further evil in him. Therefore the servant must repent before that, so that society is spared the evils of sins. Does "Repentance with God is only for those who do evil in ignorance" mean that he repents first and then God turns to him?

He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Then He turned to them so that they might repent. Indeed, God is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾ (Surat at-Tawbah, part of 9:118).

Here the scholars stood and were right to ask: does the servant repent first and then God accepts the repentance, or does God turn to the servant first and then the servant repents? The explicit wording of the verse is: "Then He turned to them so that they might repent." And we say: Does someone repent on his own initiative, or did God legislate repentance for the servants? God legislated repentance, so the servant repented, and then God accepted the repentance.

So we are faced with three matters: God legislated repentance for the servants, and no one invented his repentance and imposed it upon God; that is, no one originated repentance. Rather, He who created us all decreed that a person may be weak before some desires, so He instituted the legislation of repentance. This is what is meant by His saying "then He turned to them", that is, He legislated repentance for them, and afterwards the servant turns to God, "so that they might repent", and after that acceptance comes from God, who says:

﴿Forgiver of sin and Acceptor of repentance﴾ (Surat Ghafir, part of 40:3).

Reflect on the expression "Repentance with God is only..." and you will find it at the height of generosity. If a poor man in debt refers his creditor to a wealthy servant, the creditor rejoices, because the wealthy one will settle the debt and pay it to the creditor. How much more so with repentance, which God has referred to His own Self with all His perfection and beauty. He has made repentance incumbent upon Himself, not upon His creatures, and no one can retract it. Then He said: "then they repent soon", meaning that the servant hopes for repentance from God. And when He said: "Those are the ones to whom God turns back in forgiveness", meaning that He, glory be to Him, is the Accepter of repentance and the Forgiver of sin. And when He, glory be to Him, says: "and God is ever Knowing, Wise", we know that every legislation for anything requires broad knowledge of what can occur and arise. Those who flounder in human legislations, why do they legislate today and then revise the legislation tomorrow? Because at the time they legislated, something that could happen escaped them, and when what was not in their minds occurred, they corrected their legislation.

So disorder arises from the legislator's lack of knowledge of all the circumstances of those for whom he legislates, past, present and future. The human legislator may fail to grasp past events, because he grasps them only within his own environment or in the environment to which their news has reached. Thus he cannot grasp the past, nor the future, and likewise the present, since the present in one environment differs from the present in another. We know that the barriers of the unseen are three; that is, what makes a thing unseen to a person is three matters:

The first matter: the past time and what happened in it that contemporaries did not see and did not know. Therefore the past is withheld from humans by the veil of events that occurred in that past. This is why God, glory be to Him, draws our attention to the confirmation of His Messenger (ﷺ), saying:

﴿You were not on the western side when We decreed the command to Moses.﴾ (Surat al-Qasas, part of 28:44).

The Messenger of God was not with Moses at the moment God decreed the command to Moses, yet the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was unlettered and could not read or learn history. He also says:

﴿You were not with them when they cast their pens to see which of them would take charge of Mary, nor were you with them when they disputed.﴾ (Surat Ali 'Imran, part of 3:44).

That is, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) did not witness those times whose news came to him from God. The Messenger is unlettered by the testimony of all and did not sit with any teacher. So the one who pierced the veil of time and informed the Messenger of those events is God.

The second matter: the veil of the present, where the veil does not come from time, since time is one, but the veil comes from difference of place. I know what happens in my place, but I do not know what happens in places other than the one where I exist. The veil of the present is not limited to place alone, but extends to the human self, in that a person conceals something within himself. The Truth says:

﴿They say to themselves: "Why does God not punish us for what we say?"﴾ (Surat al-Mujadilah, part of 58:8).

Here God informs His Messenger of something present and concealed in the souls of his enemies. By God, had they not said it within themselves, they would not have believed the Messenger's report about God that came to him. God has broken through, before His Messenger, the veil of the self and the veil of place.

The third matter: the veil of the future, and the Qur'an says:

﴿The multitude will be routed and will turn their backs.﴾ (Surat al-Qamar, 54:45).

We note that the word "will be routed" contains the letter "sin" (sa), which indicates the future. This verse was revealed in Mecca at a time when the Muslims were few, oppressed, and unable to defend themselves. When 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may God be pleased with him) heard it, he was agitated and said to the Messenger of God: "What multitude is this?"

Then the multitude came at Badr and turned its back. The announcement took place in Mecca, and the events occurred after the Hijrah. The Hijrah was, in chronological order, future relative to the Muslims' presence in Mecca.

Could He have said: "The multitude will be routed and will turn their backs" unless it were actually going to happen?

Had something else happened, the believers in Him would have denied it.

The Messenger (ﷺ) said that as a proclamation from God, with certainty, and God puts it on the tongue of His Messenger as proof, which the opponent grasps, and then confirms its truth, because the One who said it is the One who creates events and knows them.

And concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, who was big, a stallion, held in awe and renown, and one of the leaders of Quraysh, the Truth says:

﴿We will brand him upon the snout.﴾ (Surat al-Qalam, 68:16).

That is, We will strike him with the sword in a blow that leaves a mark on his nose in its uppermost part. Then the Day of Badr came, and they found the blow on al-Walid's nose. God said it on the tongue of His Messenger in a past time, and the future time brought it about. When this matter occurs, those who believe in Muhammad and in the Qur'an revealed to Muhammad become certain of the Messenger's truthfulness in everything. They take the small detail and magnify it, so they believe what he tells them of the affairs of this world and the Hereafter. They say:

If the Messenger of God informs us of an unseen matter that will occur in the Hereafter, he is the truthful and trustworthy one, and they take from the actual events of this world what serves as evidence for the truth of the events of the Hereafter.

God concludes the verse: "and God is ever Knowing, Wise", that is, Knowing of the legislations, so He legislated repentance, because of His knowledge, exalted is His majesty, that if He had not legislated repentance, a person who sinned only once would have been the cause of the world's misery, for then he would be despairing of God's mercy.

So out of His mercy toward the world, God legislated repentance. And He is Wise, so beware lest it occur to you that the Truth protected only the criminal when He legislated repentance for him; He, glory be to Him, has protected others too. When we hear the tense used for the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, as in His saying "was" (kana), we should not say that by analogy with our own time or our own capacities. Rather, everything related to the Truth must be taken within the scope of "There is nothing like unto Him."

A disbeliever may say: "God's knowledge was," and try to understand it as knowledge that has occurred and cannot be repeated now. No, God's knowledge was and still is, because God does not change, and since God does not change, what is established for Him from eternity is established for Him forever. Wisdom is putting a thing in its place. Since He, glory be to Him, has decreed the placing of the thing, the thing came from knowledge, and when the thing corresponds to its place, this is absolute wisdom.

And the Truth says:

﴿Repentance with God is only for those who do evil in ignorance and then repent soon. Those are the ones to whom God turns back in forgiveness, and God is ever Knowing, Wise.﴾ (Surat an-Nisa', 4:17).

He, glory be to Him, legislated repentance so that His servants would repent, and if they repent, He accepts their repentance, and this is founded upon comprehensive knowledge and firm, precise wisdom. Look at the precision of the phrase "Repentance with God is only...". When there is a positive verb, one says "upon whom"; but when there is no positive verb, one does not say "upon whom", but uses negation. When the Truth determined repentance as incumbent upon Himself and made it binding on Himself, for those who do evil in ignorance and repent immediately, He also points out their opposite, saying: { Repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death comes to one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have repented now," nor for those who die while they are disbelievers. }

(1) Narrated by Ahmad and al-Bukhari from Abu Hurayrah. In a version from Muslim and Ahmad: "Nor does one of you embezzle while he is a believer, so beware, beware." 'Abd al-Razzaq added: "Nor does one snatch plunder while he is a believer."

(2) Narrated by Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak.

Here the Truth clarifies that the repentance of those who commit evil deeds does not exist "from nearby." They differ from those whose repentance Allah has decreed to accept: those who live with the values of the method (manhaj) present in their souls, though their souls weaken once. As for those whose repentance is not accepted, they are the people whose souls have strayed from the method in many directions. They did not commit a single "sū'" (a single lapse), but rather committed "sayyi'āt" (evil deeds). The one who committed a single lapse means that he is weak in one aspect, so he exaggerates and strives in the other aspects of obedience, where he has no weakness, in an attempt to conceal his weakness.

You see examples of this person among those who go to great lengths in establishing projects of good. These projects come from people who have been excessive toward themselves in one area where they could not control themselves, so they turn to many areas of good, and they increase in doing good, hoping that Allah will erase the evil deeds they left and gave up.

From this we know that no one can outwit Allah. The one who has taken his comfort in one area, Allah makes clear to him: "I will come to exhaust you from other directions, for the benefit of My method." Allah sets upon him illusion, and he imagines what the evil deed will do to him, so he rushes to doing good. It is as if the Truth says to the evildoer: "You have enjoyed one area, and My method and My religion have benefited greatly from you. You build mosques and schools and give charity to the poor, all of this because you have one evil deed."

Therefore, no one can plot against Allah. The Qur'an described the person with an evil deed by describing this slip with the word "sū'," but it described the one who has strayed far and deep from the method of Allah as doing "sayyi'āt," so he is not the owner of a single point of weakness; rather he commits multiple evil deeds, persists in misguidance, and the matter does not stop there. He postpones repentance until the moment the term is reached. Indeed, they may not even attribute the good that comes from them to religion, as the atheists (mulhida) do, or the ignorant who do not know that every good is commanded by religion.

An example of this is the doctrine of "Freemasonry." It is said that this doctrine was devised by the Jews. What appears in the conduct of Freemasons is that they gather to do some good from which society benefits, while what is hidden of the actions of the leading members of Freemasonry is that they serve the aims of Zionism.
