1 Narrated by al-Bukhari, Ahmad, al-Nasa'i and al-Tirmidhi.
2 Narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah.

The Truth, glory be to Him, created the universe and in it are kinds (ajnas), and each kind includes two species (anwa') or types, and under each type are individuals. When you see a kind divided into two types, know that the two share the requirement of the kind and then differ in the requirement of the type. If they were one thing, they would not have been divided into two types. The same holds for individuals. When we look at inanimate matter (al-jamad), we find that it is a general kind, yet it is divided into different elements, and each element has a different function. For example, if we want to erect a building, that building requires sand, requires cement, requires bricks, and requires iron. The whole kind of inanimate matter shares in building construction, but cement has a function, gypsum (al-jibs) has a function, sand has a function, and al-marw, which is pebbles (al-zilt), has a function. So you do not take the function of one thing for another. Likewise, humanity is divided into two types: maleness, embodied in men, and femaleness, embodied in women. Between them is a shared measure that unites them as one kind, and then between them there is difference according to the difference of their types. If you wanted to put one type in place of the other, you could not.

Therefore, it is absurd that God should create two types from one kind, and then you come and say that this type must be like that type. We also know this about time. Time is the container of events, meaning every event must have a time, but every time has an event that suits it. Time, which is the day, is the container of the event within its time, and the night is also a container of the event within its time. But the event of the night is tranquility and rest, and the event of the day is movement and activity. If you were to reverse this, putting this in place of that, you would be overturning things and combining opposites.

We have made clear that God draws our attention to something on which we disagree by means of something on which we agree. So He makes clear to you: return what you disagree on to what is agreed upon. Concerning time, no one disagrees that you make the night a dwelling, a garment, rest and calm, and the day for movement, and all people do this. The Truth, glory be to Him, makes clear: just as He made time a container for movement, yet the movement of this differs from the movement of that. Does that mean that night and day are opposites, or contraries, or complementary?

They are complementary, because the rest of the night was only made so that the movement of the day would be sound. You sleep and rest in order to resume a new activity. So the night is what helps the day in its task. If a person were to wake up at night and then come to morning, he would not be able to do anything. So what aided the movement of the day? It is the stillness of the night. The Truth, glory be to Him, shows that this is a matter agreed upon among all people, religious and non-religious. So if you disagree that maleness and femaleness must be identical in work, movement and type, we say to you: No. This is an agreed matter in the case of time, so take what you have agreed upon as evidence for the soundness of what you disagree about. For this reason God set forth the example, saying: ﴿By the night when it covers﴾ (Surah al-Layl).

When the night covers, stillness comes. Then the Truth said:

﴿By the day when it displays itself﴾ (Surah al-Layl).

When the sun rises, movement stirs. Then He brought the matter of difference, and after it He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿And by Him who created the male and the female, indeed your efforts are diverse﴾ (Surah al-Layl).

That is, each kind has a function.

Thus we know that the human being is divided into two types: maleness and femaleness, and in both there is shared work and a shared characteristic. Each of them is a human being who has human dignity and has freedom of belief. There is no man who compels a woman into a belief. We gave the example of the wife of Noah, the wife of Lot, and the wife of Pharaoh.

So the shared measure is freedom of belief, and no type has authority over another. Likewise, there is freedom of rational thought in matters of importance. We have also known how Umm Salama, may Allah be pleased with her, advised the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during the Battle of Hudaybiyya with an opinion that saved the Muslims from a dreadful division before the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). We have known the story of Bilqis, the queen of Sheba, who was able to conclude a matter that the men had abandoned. So it is possible for a woman to have reason and for a woman to have thought, and even before Islam there were women who had originality of opinion and wisdom in counsel in their own sphere.

For example, history tells us that the king of Kinda heard of the beauty of a woman called Umm Iyas, daughter of Awf ibn Mihl al-Shaybani, and he wished to marry her. He summoned a woman from Kinda called Isam, who had good manners, eloquence, intelligence and a fluent tongue, and said to her: Go until you know for me the situation of the daughter of Awf. That is, he sent her as a matchmaker. When she went to the mother of Umm Iyas, whose name was Umama bint al-Harith, and informed her of what she had come for, the mother sent for the daughter from her tent and said to her: This is your aunt who has come to look into some of your affairs, so do not conceal from her anything she wishes to see of your face and character, and answer her questions about what she asks you. When Isam was alone with the girl, she did what her mother had instructed. She uncovered for the matchmaker Isam all that she wanted of her beauties. Then the matchmaker spoke her famous words: "Abandoning deception is when the veil is removed," and this saying became a proverb, meaning that when the veil is removed a person sees the reality. Isam returned to the king, and he asked her: What is behind you, O Isam? He was asking: What news have you brought from Umm Iyas? She said: I have churned the butter from the buttermilk. Al-makhd is shaking the milk in the waterskin to separate the butter from the milk, and this means that her journey had produced a result.

He said to her: Tell me.

She said: I will tell you truly and honestly. She described her from her hair to her feet, a description that enticed the king. He sent to her father, proposed, and she was brought to him in marriage.

On the night of the wedding, we see the wise mother advising her daughter in her field of work, in the field of her motherhood, in the field of her femininity. The mother said to her daughter: "O my daughter, if advice were to be left for the sake of good manners, it would be left for you, meaning that as a mother she trusts her daughter's good manners and does not need advice in this matter. But it is an aid to the heedless and a reminder to the intelligent. Tomorrow you will go to a house you have not known and a companion you have not become accustomed to. So be to him a servant and he will be to you a slave. Remember from me ten characteristics that will be a treasure for you."

Look at the characteristics that a woman draws from the field of her mission. The mother's words continue: "As for the first and second: keep company with him with listening and obedience, and contentment with what is sufficient. As for the third and fourth: take care of what his eye sees and what his nose smells, so that his eye never falls upon anything ugly from you, and he never smells from you anything but the finest fragrance. As for the fifth and sixth: be attentive to the time of his meal and calm at the time of his sleep, for disturbing sleep brings anger, and the heat of hunger inflames. As for the seventh and eighth: manage his wealth and be considerate toward his household and his dependants. As for the ninth and tenth: do not divulge his secret and do not disobey his command, for if you reveal his secret you will not be safe from his treachery, and if you disobey his command you will provoke his anger. And beware after that of rejoicing when he is in sorrow, and of sorrow when he is joyful."

So Umm Iyas took these pieces of advice to her husband, and she bore him sons and daughters, and she was happy with him and he was happy with her.

That is advice from a mother that shows the utmost reason, but in what? In the field of her mission. So God gives a woman and grants her the ability to reason, and she has a field, and this reason usually comes only in her field. Because the field of the man has a movement that requires firmness and severity, while the movement of the woman requires tenderness and compassion. Proverbs in our daily lives confirm this. When the man enters his house and wants to sleep, his small child may come crying and screaming, and the father flares up at his wife, curses the child and curses his mother, and may say words like: "Stifle his breath, for I want to rest." The mother takes her child, goes and pats his shoulder and quiets him, and the child responds to her. This is the mission of the mother. Therefore we find that severe historical events bring the man forward in his place and the woman in her place.

For example: our master Ibrahim, peace be upon him, settled Hajar and her son Isma'il in a valley without vegetation. She said to him: Will you leave us in a place where there is not even water? Is this a place you have chosen by your own opinion, or did God make you descend here? He said to her: God has caused me to descend in this place. She said to him: Go as you wish, for He will not waste us. This is the mission of the woman. Hajar, with a child, in a place lacking the first requirement of life, which is water. Look at her tenderness and compassion, what did she do? She ran between al-Safa and al-Marwa; she climbed the mountain until her strength was exhausted.

Whoever goes to Hajj or Umrah and experiences these seven rounds knows the utmost that a woman can endure for the sake of her son, because this is a situation of tenderness and compassion. Her son wanted to drink. It was as if God said to her: You have striven, but I will provide for you from where you do not expect. You ran between al-Safa and al-Marwa, and the water sprang up beneath your son's feet. So she was truthful in her words: "He will not waste us." Had her striving produced the water, we would all have thought that striving is what brings water. But strive and do not put your trust in the striving; rather trust in the Supreme Provider. This is a clear matter in our mother Hajar.

When the test of sacrifice came, Hajar disappeared from the stage, and the role of our master Ibrahim came with his firmness, resolve and prophethood. He saw in a dream that he was sacrificing his son. Where was his mother in this? She had disappeared from the stage, because this situation does not accord with her feelings and compassion. So each of them has a mission, and success is in proportion to this mission. For this reason the Truth says: ﴿And do not wish for that by which God has made some of you exceed others﴾. So whenever you see one kind taking something and another kind taking something else, beware of letting your mind be occupied and wishing, saying: "I want this." Rather, ask God from His bounty, because the words "and do not wish" are a prohibition against wishing for what God has favoured some over others. For this reason He says: ﴿And ask God from His bounty﴾. And as long as you ask God for His bounty, there is hope here that He will give you.

Some may see a problem here and ask: How does He forbid us from wishing for what God has favoured some of us over others, saying ﴿And do not wish for that by which God has made some of you exceed others﴾, when God's favour by its nature makes some of us exceed others, as evidenced by His saying ﴿and raised some of you above others in degrees﴾? Moreover, I hope to ask God so that He may give me, since He, glory be to Him, only commanded us to ask so that He might give us.

We say: No. Wishing (tamanni) is ordinarily to seek something impossible or something not customary, whereas asking and supplication are about reaching for something you can obtain. So make this clear: do not go into the realm of wishing. For this reason they gave the example of wishing with the verse of the poet:

"Would that youth might return one day,
so I could tell it what old age has done."

The poet wished that youth would return one day. Is this possible? It is not possible. Or someone may say: Would that the stars came close to me so I could string them together. Can that happen? No. But this saying shows that the thing is beloved, even if it is not customary, or it is impossible. So asking must be within the bounds of what is possible for you. The Truth makes clear: do not look enviously at what God has favoured some of you over others. And since God has favoured some over others, a person should ask, not in the realm of what God has given someone else and seek it for himself and take it from another, but in the realm of being successful in displaying what God has favoured you with. For this reason we find that the Truth, in the verses on favouring, says:

﴿And God has favoured some of you over others in provision﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 71).

And what is provision? Is it only money? No. Provision is everything from which one benefits. So forbearance is provision, knowledge is provision, courage is provision; all of this is provision. And His saying, the Truth: ﴿that by which God has favoured some of you over others﴾ makes us ask: Who is the one favoured and who is the one favoured over? Because He said "some of you," and He did not explain it to us. So some are favoured and some are favoured over.

Another question: which "some" is favoured and which "some" is favoured over? Every person is superior in something and inferior to others in some

Then the Truth (exalted is He) says:

﴿And to every one We have appointed heirs of what the parents and the close relatives leave, and those with whom your oaths have bound you—give them their share. Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, Witness.﴾ [4:33]

Whenever you see the word "لكل" (likul, "to every") with tanwin, know that there is an implied noun, and its original form is "لكل إنسان" (likulli insan, "to every person"). The noun was omitted and the tanwin came in its place, like His saying:

﴿Then why, when it [the soul] reaches the throat, and you at that time are looking on—﴾ [56:83–84]

Here the tanwin is in "حينئذ" (hina'idhin, "at that time"), meaning "when the soul reaches the throat." So "حين بلغت الروح الحلقوم" was omitted and the tanwin in "حينئذ" was substituted for it. Thus the tanwin came in place of the omitted word.

As for the Truth's saying ﴿ولكل جعلنا موالي﴾ (wa-likullin ja'alna mawali), "الموالي" (al-mawali) is the plural of "مولى" (mawla, here meaning heir or kinsman by alliance). Before the verses of inheritance were revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) established brotherhood ( mu'akhah) between the Emigrants and the Helpers, and they used to inherit from one another through this brotherhood. There was also a thing called "مولى المناصرة" (mawla al-munasara, the ally in support), which is that two men would bind themselves to each other, and each would say to the other: "I am your brother and you are my brother; my war is your war, my peace is your peace, my blood is your blood; you inherit from me and I inherit from you; you pay blood-money (ta'qil) on my behalf and I pay on yours. That is, if you commit an offence, I will pay for it on your behalf, and if I commit an offence, you will pay for it on my behalf." This is brotherhood.

These had a share in the estate of the deceased. So the Truth explains: to every person, men and women, We have appointed heirs of what the parents and the close relatives leave—that is, they have a share of it. And the allies of support also have some of the inheritance likewise. So beware lest you come and say: "No, no, you must give them their share, which was stipulated for them," namely one-sixth.

But was that ruling retained? No. It was abrogated, and Allah revealed His saying:

﴿And blood relatives are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾ [8:75]

Since Allah has said ﴿And to every one We have appointed heirs of what the parents and the close relatives leave﴾, the meaning is: and to every person among the heirs is a portion of what the parents and the close relatives leave. So beware of saying: "They have gone, so we will not give them anything." No—those with whom they were in agreement and bound their oaths to it, give them their share, in confirmation of the Truth's saying ﴿give them their share. Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, Witness﴾. So Allah is Witness over this, and Witness over whether you carry it out or do not carry it out.

Afterwards he came to speak on a matter connected with the words of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others﴾. He said:

﴿Men are in charge of women﴾. The first thing we turn our attention to is that some of them did not explain the verse except with regard to a husband and his wife, although the verse speaks of men in general and women in general. The verse is not restricted to a husband and wife: the father is in charge (qawwam) of his daughters, and the brother of his sisters. Let us first understand "men are in charge" and what it means, and consider whether this gives women superiority and standing or whether it gives them burden. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, asks us to respect a cosmic matter. He is the Creator who perfected everything He created, and He clarified the matter of faith: "Men are in charge of women." Whoever opposes it must show, if there is anything that leads to opposition. As for the woman who is afraid of this verse, we find that if she were not blessed with a male child she would be angry. If we ask her, "Why, then?", she says, "I want a son to protect us." How can you oppose this matter?

Let us understand what "qawwam" means. Qawwam is one who exceeds in standing (al-qiyam). The Truth here used the standing that involves exertion, and when you say, "So-and-so stands over the people," meaning he never rests. So why do you take "qawwamun 'ala al-nisa'" to mean suffocation? Why do you not take it to mean striving for their interests? The man is charged with the task of standing over women, that is, to carry out what sets the matter right. We find that the Truth used the word "men" in its generality, and the word "women" in its generality, and one thing He spoke of afterwards in His words: ﴿by what Allah has given preference to some of them over others﴾. So where is the preference found?

The aspect of preference is that the man has the toil, the striving across the earth, and the seeking of livelihood, so that he may provide women with a decent way of life when he takes care of her. In the story of Adam, peace be upon him, there is an example for us, when the Truth, glorified is He, warned Adam and his wife about Satan, Iblis, who was commanded to prostrate with the angels to Adam and refused. Thereby we knew Iblis's prior enmity toward Adam and its reason:

﴿He said, "Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?"﴾ (part of verse 61, Surah al-Isra’).

And the Truth made clear to Adam: when you descend to the earth, remember this enmity, and know that he will not leave you, and will continue to lead you astray and tempt you, because he does not want to be disobedient alone, but wants to gather others from the kind he refused to prostrate to their father Adam. He wants to lead them astray, just as he tried to lead Adam astray:

﴿Indeed, this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so let him not remove you both from the Garden﴾ (part of verse 117, Surah Ta-Ha).

Did the Truth then say: "So you both will be miserable," or "So you [sing.] will be miserable"? He, glorified is He, said:

﴿So you [sing.] will be miserable﴾ (part of verse 117, Surah Ta-Ha).

So when misery and struggle came to the earth, the woman was screened, and the address was to the man. This shows that qawwamah requires toil, effort, and striving, and this task falls to the man.

We note that when mentioning preference He said: ﴿Men are in charge of women by what Allah has given preference to some of them over others﴾. He said "some of them" because when He preferred the man, since he is qawwam, He also preferred the woman for another thing, which is that she is the dwelling (sakan) where the man rests, and she performs her task.

Then comes the justification of qawwamah: ﴿and by what they spend from their wealth﴾. Wealth comes as a result of movement and as a result of toil. The one who toils, we say to him: you are a qawwam. So the woman should rejoice in that, because He, glorified is He, gave hardship and toil to the kind qualified for it. But her task, though it is a great task, suits the quality required of her first: tenderness, compassion, kindness and gentleness. Such qualities were not given to the man, because earning does not require these matters; rather it requires strength, resolve and firmness. So God's words "qawwamun" mean that they exceed in standing over the affairs of women.

It clarifies for women: do not think only that this is a story of husband and wife. Consider that standing applies to the affairs of daughters, sisters and mothers. It is not correct to take "qawwam" to mean domination, because the task of standing was given to the man with hardship, and it is a difficult task for him to exceed in standing over the affairs of those whose matters are entrusted to him.

﴿and by what they spend from their wealth﴾. If marriage is a pleasure for the female and the male, and both enjoy it and both desire offspring, then since the enjoyment is shared and the seeking of offspring is also shared, the obligations that follow from that do not fall on each of them equally, but fall on the man alone: dowry and maintenance, even if the woman is wealthy; the Sharia does not require her to lend to her husband.

So the qawwamah of men came to women as a relief and removed hardships from them. Why then should the woman grieve over it? "Men are in charge of women," that is, they stand in a continuous standing, because one is not called qawwam merely for being a standing person; the one standing performs a task once, but "qawwam" means one who is continuously in charge.

﴿Men are in charge of women by what Allah has given preference to some of them over others and by what they spend from their wealth﴾. Since we toil and exert ourselves for women, there must be a task for women that corresponds to that, which is that she be a dwelling for him, and this too contains preference.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, has set forth at the beginning of the verse a ruling that must be adhered to, because it is the ruling of the Creator who perfected everything He created. He clarified the matter of faith: "Men are in charge of women." Then He brought the justifications, saying: ﴿by what Allah has given preference to some of them over others and by what they spend from their wealth﴾. The Truth continues: ﴿So righteous women are devoutly obedient, guarding in secret what Allah has guarded﴾. The righteous woman is the woman who has remained upright on the path that her Creator set for her in her kind. As long as she is righteous, she is devoutly obedient (qanitah), and qunut is constancy in obedience to Allah. From it comes the qunut of Fajr, which we recite, and we supplicate and stand longer in the prayer in which there is qunut.

The devoutly obedient woman is humbly submissive to Allah. So when she is submissive to Allah, she adheres to the path and command of Allah in what He has ruled, that men are in charge of women. ﴿So righteous women are devoutly obedient, guarding in secret what Allah has guarded﴾. "Guarding in secret" indicates the preservation of chastity. The woman, when the guardian who protects her and her honour is absent from her, such as the father for the daughter, the son for the mother, the husband for the wife, every woman is under the guardianship of someone, and she must guard his absence. For this reason, when the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, defined the righteous woman, he said in a hadith about the world:

"The world is entirely a provision, and the best provision of the world is a righteous woman" (1).

The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, set down a standard for the righteous woman in which he said:

(The best of women is she who pleases you when you look at her, obeys you when you command her, and does not oppose you in herself or in her wealth in what you dislike) (2).

And what does a man need more than that? The words "she pleases you when you look at her" — beware of directing this only toward beauty, the beauty of form. No: when you see her, gather all the qualities of goodness in her, and do not take one quality and leave another, because the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, warned us against taking one quality in a woman and leaving another; rather we must take her in the totality of her qualities. He said:

"A woman is married for four things: for her wealth, for her lineage, for her beauty, and for her religion. So win the one with religion; may your hands be rubbed with dust" (3).

What is required is that you do not look at one angle of beauty, but look at all angles. If you look at the angle that occupies people, the angle of beauty, you will find it the least of the angles regarding the making of a woman, because the lifespan of this matter is the "honeymoon," as they say, and then it ends, and afterwards the other qualities appear. If you enter upon a single criterion, that she be beautiful, you are deceiving yourself and thinking you want her to be a lady of the salon! We say to you: this quality's span of time is brief, but what remains for you is that she be trustworthy, sincere, and a good manager. For this reason, failure arises in the household from men entering marriage on one standard only, the standard of physical beauty, and this single standard has a short life; after a while it goes and its intensity cools. Then the man's eyes awaken to look at other aspects of beauty and find none, and failure occurs. Therefore one must take all the angles together. Beware of taking one angle; the best of angles is that she has religion. Likewise, the standard for a woman's acceptance of a husband: the best of angles is that he has religion. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: (If one comes to you whose character and religion you approve, then marry him; if you do not, there will be temptation on earth and widespread corruption) (4).

When a man consulted the master al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, he said: marry her to one who has religion; if he loves her and honours her, and if he dislikes her, he will not wrong her.

So religion guides us: one must look at the matter that will have a long life in an extended lifetime. Then, if she wants to be successful, she must see the framework of her kind and excel in it. If she has time, she may widen the circle of her task within her home. If she has children, she should learn sewing and make and sew her clothes and her children's clothes, thus saving money; or learn embroidery so as not to pay a wage; or learn nursing so that if her child falls ill she can nurse and care for him; she should learn so that she can dispense with a private tutor who takes money from the household income. If she still has time, let her learn plumbing to save the cost of a plumber if a water tap breaks, or learn electrical repair to fix a light switch. A woman can do any work while sitting in her home and provide income to meet the needs she cannot do herself. A woman is among "those who guard the unseen," not by improvisation of her own or by choice, but by the method that God has set for guarding the unseen...

What is the method God has set for guarding the unseen? She guards her honour and her husband's wealth in his absence, so she looks at the openings through which temptation comes and refrains from them. She does not go out into the streets except for a pressing need or necessity, so that she does not see anyone who tempts her or whom she tempts, because these are the preliminaries of guarding, and she does not go into the crush of life. After that we say to her: "Guard the unseen." Rather, she must consider what God has made clear in that. If you are compelled to go out, then lower your gaze. For this reason He, glorified is He, said:

﴿And tell the believing women to lower their gaze and guard their private parts and not reveal their adornment except what appears of it﴾ (part of verse 31, Surah al-Nur).

If a woman does not lower her gaze, an emotional turning arises, because every feeling in a person has three stages: the stage of perception, the stage of finding it within oneself, and the stage of inclination, that is, turning the matter into behaviour. We always give the example of the rose. As you walk, you see a rose in a garden; the mere seeing of it is perception. If the rose pleases you, you fall in love with it and like it, this is called wijdan (emotional experience). If you move to pick it, this is the act of inclination (nuz'uwi). So how many stages? Three stages:

Perception, then emotional experience, then inclination.

And when does the Sharia intervene? The Sharia always intervenes at the stage of inclination. It says to you: you looked at the rose and we did not object to that; you loved it and it pleased you, and we did not say anything to you. But when you came to extend your hand to take it, we said to you: no, the rose is not yours.

So you are free to perceive, and free to find it within yourself; but when you move to take it, we say to you: no, it is not yours. And even if it pleases you, grow a rose for yourself in the house, or ask its owner, for example.

So legislation intervenes in the area of inclination, except in the matter of women, where legislation intervenes from the very beginning of perception, because the One who created us knew that if we perceive beauty, we look at it, and feelings and desires will be generated toward what we see and crave. When perception and desire occur, they cannot be separated from inclination, because you, as a man, are composed chemically such that if you perceive beauty and then feel emotion and desire, desire is not calmed except by inclination. So the Sharia makes clear to you: I have shown you mercy from the very beginning, and I intervened from the start of the matter. Everything I intervene in at the stage of inclination, except women, for whom...

2. Narrated by Ahmad, al-Nasa'i and al-Hakim.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 4, verse 35:

And His saying: ﴿And if you fear a breach between the two⦆ means that the breach has not yet occurred; rather, you fear that a breach may occur. And what is "shiqaq" (breach, discord)? Its root is from "shaqq" (splitting), and "shaqq" means to separate one thing from another. "Shaqqtu al-lawh" means I separated its two halves from each other. So the phrase "shiqaq baynahuma" (a breach between them) indicates that the two have joined through marriage and have become one thing. Whatever separates two such parties is a "shiqaq." For through marriage and intimate companionship, the man has joined with his wife. This is what God said: ﴿And how can you take it back when you have gone in unto each other and they have taken from you a solemn covenant?⦆ (Qur'an 4:21).

This meaning is confirmed in another verse:

﴿They are a garment for you, and you are a garment for them⦆ (Qur'an 2:187).

This means that the woman is enveloped by the man and the man is enveloped by her. The man covers her and she covers him. When the matter goes beyond the two of them, the Truth says: ﴿And if you fear a breach between the two⦆. Who are those who fear? Is it the guardian of the affair (walī al-amr), or the close relatives of her guardians and of her affairs? That is, the people for whom this matter is of concern.

﴿And if you fear a breach between the two, then send an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family⦆. They are the environment and the family sphere. So we should not leave matters until the breach occurs. Islam and the Qur'an alert us that everyone in the family's circle must be alert to the psychological conditions that confront this family, whether he is a father, a brother, or a relative. He must be attentive to the family's circumstances and not leave matters until a breach occurs, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿And if you fear a breach between the two⦆. So the breach has not occurred, and the matter must not be left until a breach occurs. ﴿And if you fear a breach between the two, then send⦆. This statement is also addressed to the general guardian (walī al-amr), if his eyes are alert to the fact that he oversees the relations of all households. But this is not feasible in light of the responsibilities of the guardian in the modern age. Therefore, the one who will be able to implement this command must be the prominent members of the family on both sides, and everyone who has standing in the family should observe the family's trajectory, and say: "We see such and such."

We take an arbiter from here and an arbiter from there, and we examine the matter that will lead to a storm before the storm occurs. The interest has moved from the spouses to one of the husband's relatives and one of the wife's relatives. These two have no apparent dispute with their evidence, the problem has not yet crystallized, and neither of them has a prior judgment in mind. It is possible that there are things between the spouses, but the arbiter from the husband's side and the arbiter from the wife's side have nothing in their minds, and since the two are entrusted with the task of judging, they must agree on what happens, such that if the two see that it cannot be set right except by divorce, they rule for divorce. People may understand that the arbiters are people who reconcile the spouses, and if the ruling does not please them, the spouses remain in discord. No. We choose an arbiter from here and an arbiter from there.

What the two arbiters say must be implemented, for this matter has been restricted to the two arbiters, so He said: ﴿If they both desire reconciliation, God will bring about harmony between them⦆. It is as if the fundamental task is reconciliation, and the two arbiters must enter with the intention of reconciliation. If God does not bring harmony between them, then it is as though the two arbiters entered with the intention of not reconciling.

Each arbiter must fear for himself and strive to be sincere in the pursuit of reconciliation, because if he is not sincere, the matter will turn into a disgrace for him. He who created everyone, the husband, the wife, the arbiter from the husband's family and the arbiter from the wife's family, said: ﴿If they both desire reconciliation, God will bring about harmony between them⦆. So let the two proceed under this matter and persist sincerely in bringing them together, because when God states a cosmic principle, each one governs himself and his movement within the scope of this principle. When God states a general principle, He is the All-Knowing, the All-Aware. An example of this is His saying:

﴿And indeed, Our soldiers will be the victorious⦆ (Qur'an 37:173).

He, glory be to Him, said that, so let every soldier be keen to be a soldier of God, because if he is defeated we will say to him: "You were not a soldier of God," and he will fear this. So the placing of the cosmic principle within a doctrinal framework is so that a person mobilizes all his capacities toward succeeding in the task. When God says: ﴿If they both desire reconciliation, God will bring about harmony between them⦆, beware of being deceived by the resolution of the two arbiters or by the intelligence of the two arbiters, for these are means. We always emphasize: beware of being deceived by means, because everything comes from the highest Causer. Note the precision of the wise statement: ﴿God will bring about harmony between them⦆. He, glory be to Him, did not say: "If they both desire reconciliation, they will bring about harmony between them." Rather, He reserved for Himself the grace of bringing harmony between the spouses.

And He concludes the verse: ﴿Indeed, God is ever Knowing and Acquainted⦆, that is, with the conditions of the husband, the conditions of the wife, the conditions of the arbiter from his family, and the conditions of the arbiter from her family, for they are encompassed by His knowledge. Each one must be keen about his conduct, because he is accountable for every movement that surrounds this matter; our Lord is All-Knowing and All-Aware.

What is the difference between "ʿalīm" (All-Knowing) and "khabīr" (All-Aware)? Knowledge may be acquired from the knowledge of others, but expertise (khibra) belongs to one's own self.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 4, verse 36:

After the Almighty had spoken of the rulings previously mentioned concerning marriage and the prohibited (muharramat), and we took from their counterpart the permitted (muhallalat), and He spoke of one who is unable to afford [marriage] (ṭawl), and He spoke of wealth, warning us not to consume it falsely (bil-batil), and He spoke of the condition between man and woman, then after that the Truth drew our attention, directed us and alerted us to the highest methodology, which is His saying, glorified is He:

﴿Worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and be good to parents, and to relatives, orphans, the needy, the neighbor who is near of kin, the neighbor who is a stranger, the companion by your side, the wayfarer, and those whom your right hands possess. Indeed, Allah does not love one who is self-deluded and boastful.﴾ [36]

When the Truth says: ﴿Worship Allah and associate nothing with Him﴾, it means: beware of entering into any of these matters in disobedience to Allah in His methodology. Worship ('ibadah) is the obedience of the worshipper to the one worshipped. So do not take it to mean only the acts of worship we perform, such as: prayer (salah), fasting (sawm), zakat, and Hajj, because these are the pillars of Islam (arkan al-Islam). Since these are the pillars and foundations upon which Islam is built, then Islam does not consist only of the pillars; rather, the pillars are the foundations upon which Islam is built, and the foundations upon which a house is built are not the whole house. Therefore, Islam is a multi-faceted structure. As for those who try to take from the classificatory term, or the technical term in the sciences, and say: "Worship consists of prayer and what relates to it, zakat, fasting, and Hajj, because they are called in books of jurisprudence 'ibadat ('acts of worship')" — we have said that this is the technical name, but every command from Allah is worship.

For this reason, some people say: "We worship Allah and do not work." We say to them: worship is the obedience of the worshipper to the command of the one worshipped, and do not understand the expression as meaning only the rites (sha'a'ir). The rites are a declaration of the continuous allegiance to Allah, and they give a charge to face the events of life. But the rites alone are not all of worship; transactions (mu'amalat) are worship, and the true concept of worship is that it includes the cultivation of the earth ('imarat al-ard). The Almighty said:

﴿O you who have believed, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Jumu'ah, then proceed to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trade.﴾ (Surah al-Jumu'ah, 62:9)

It is as if He removed them from trade to prayer, and He did not remove them from emptiness, but removed them from the movement of trade. He mentioned "trade" because it is the activity whose profit comes directly; for when you plant a crop you wait a period that may be long or short for the fruits to come out, but the fruit of trade comes directly: you sell and take the profit immediately. And trade, as we know, organizes all the movements of life, because the meaning of trade is that it is an intermediary between producer and consumer. When you sell a commodity, this commodity came from a producer, and the producer seeks an intermediary to sell it to a consumer, and this consumer you find is also a producer, and the producer you find is also a consumer. Production and consumption are an exchange, and the movement of all life is in selling and buying, and as long as there is selling there is buying. This is a continuation of the movement of life. The seller always loves to sell, but the buyer may not love to buy, because the buyer will pay money and the seller will gain money. So Allah makes clear: leave this transaction whose profit comes directly, and answer the call to the Friday prayer. But what after the prayer? The Truth says:

﴿And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek of the bounty of Allah, and remember Allah often that you may succeed.﴾ (Surah al-Jumu'ah, 62:10)

So this is also a command. If we obey the first command, ﴿then proceed to the remembrance of Allah﴾, then the command in ﴿disperse within the land﴾ likewise requires obedience. Thus all of this is worship, and the whole movement of life becomes worship: if it is prayer, it is worship, and fasting is worship, and beyond that... does prayer not need the sustenance of life? You must have the necessities of life in order to pray. And what are the necessities of your life? They are food, drink, shelter, and clothing, and that without which an obligation cannot be fulfilled is itself obligatory. Thus the totality of the movement of life is a chain of worship. For this reason the Almighty says:

﴿Worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. He produced you from the earth and made you inhabitants therein.﴾ (Surah Hud, 11:61)

So every work that leads to the cultivation of the universe and the drawing out of the secrets of Allah in existence is considered worship to Allah, because you bring forth from the treasures of Allah that He deposited in the earth what draws people's attention to the cosmic truth that faith came with.

Beware of thinking that worship is only the classificatory worship in jurisprudence, the "section of 'ibadat" and the "section of mu'amalat." No, all of it is worship, but other life activities do not show worship directly, because you work for your benefit, whereas in prayer you take from your time; so we called it "true worship." The other operations are done by one who does not believe in a god as well; he too goes out into life, plants, and manufactures.

Why were they called "'ibadat"? Because the like of them does not come from one who is not religious. The other works, such as the cultivation of the universe and worldly benefit, are done by one who is not religious, but every command of Allah that we obey is named worship. This is the concept of worship that must be confirmed for us: that we purify the work by the minds that Allah created for us, with the energies created for us, in the created matter, which is the earth and its elements, so that we may elevate existence to a level that makes us happy and pleases Allah.

﴿Worship Allah and associate nothing with Him.﴾ After all that was said previously, our Lord drew our attention to a matter we must always observe in all our conduct: that we comply with the command of Allah in His methodology, and not associate anything with Him, because shirk harms the human's position in existence. If you are in a work, beware of placing the means (asbab) before your mind in front of the Highest Causer (al-Musabbib). Rather, intend the face of Allah in every work.

The Truth gives the example of the monotheist's ease and the polytheist's hardship, saying:

﴿Allah presents an example: a man in whom are partners disputing with each other and a man belonging entirely to one man. Are they equal in comparison? Praise be to Allah! But most of them do not know.﴾ (Surah al-Zumar, 39:29)

This is a slave owned by a group, and the group is divided and quarrelsome, and he does not know how to reconcile the commands of each of them, which conflict; if he pleases this one, he angers that one. So he is a slave whose energy is scattered, whose effort is divided, and whose attention is split. But the slave belonging to one master receives no command except from one master and no prohibition except from that same master. The Truth lays out the matter for His servants in the form of a question, and He is the All-Knowing of everything, so that the believer shares with Him in the answer; when the Truth says, "Are they equal?", here the human presents it to his intellect and wants to answer. What does he say? He will answer by the nature of innate disposition and the nature of the logic of Truth, saying: "No, my Lord, they are not equal."

So you, O believing servant, have said it yourself, and Allah did not impose it upon you. The Almighty has put it to you as a question from Him, so that your answer will be one for which you will find no other answer. If you are thus, O believing servant, and have found ease in existence and your energy is devoted to one command and one prohibition, then you become a master in the universe, and you will not find in the universe anyone who takes your servitude from you to the Creator. That is our ease in carrying out the saying of Allah: ﴿Worship Allah and associate nothing with Him,﴾ because associating partners with Allah, God forbid, burdens its bearer. Would that the polytheists, when they associate, took the help of Allah and did not take the help of the partners! But Allah abandons the polytheist servant, for He, glorified is He, says:

("I am the most independent of partners from partnership. Whoever does a deed in which he associates another with Me, I abandon him and his partner.")(1)

So the Truth abandons the polytheist servant. Would that the polytheist servant took his share from Allah as a partner... but rather the share of Allah is removed from him, because Allah is too self-sufficient to have anyone else as a partner with Him. Thus the polytheist is left without a stock of faith, and lives in toil and fatigue. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, follows His worship with kindness to parents, so His saying, majestic is His majesty, comes: ﴿and to parents, kindness﴾. The two parents are the father and the mother, because they are the direct cause of your existence, O believer. And since your worship of Allah is a branch of your existence, then your being created from a father and a mother as two causes should draw your attention to the first cause; that draws your attention to the One who originated the chain up to the first human, Adam, peace be upon him.

﴿And to parents, kindness.﴾ Look at the station that Allah gave to the parents, the father and the mother. The address is to you, O Muslim, to worship Allah, and the obligation is upon you as a branch of existence; because the address is to one who is accountable (mukallaf), and obligation is a branch of existence, and the two parents are the direct cause of your existence. If you ascend the cause, the parents—from where did they come? From parents, and so on until you reach Allah. So the matter ends with the One; because obligation goes from the obligating to the obligated, a branch of existence. Existence has an apparent cause, which are "the two parents," and when you trace the chain it leads to Allah; He, glorified is He, commanded: worship Me and associate nothing with Me. Then: ﴿kindness to parents.﴾ The word "kindness" (ihsan) indicates exaggeration in excess giving, which we call the station of ihsan.

﴿And to parents, kindness.﴾ When the Almighty, glorified and exalted is He, joined the parents with His worship, because He is one God and we do not associate anything with Him, He did not deny or address their faith or disbelief; because there is another verse in which He says:

﴿And if they strive with you to associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them, but accompany them in this world with appropriate kindness.﴾ (Surah Luqman, 31:15)

True, do not obey them, but respect them, because they are the direct cause of existence, even if this cause opposes the One who created and originated it, who is Allah, majestic is His power. "And accompany them in this world with appropriate kindness": kindness (ma'ruf) is done by a person toward one he loves and toward one he does not love. Beware that your heart be attached to them if they are polytheists, but accompany them in this world with kindness. For this reason He said: "and accompany them in this world," meaning, look after their interest in worldly affairs with kindness from you. Kindness is what you do toward one you love and toward one you do not love. The Truth says: "and to parents, kindness," and He repeats it in multiple verses. It was mentioned earlier in Surah al-Baqarah when He said to us:

﴿And [recall] when We took the covenant from the Children of Israel: Worship none but Allah, and to parents, kindness.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 2:83)

After that comes this verse we are discussing: ﴿Worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and to parents, kindness.﴾

After that comes also His saying, glorified is He:

﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited you: that you not associate anything with Him, and to parents, kindness.﴾ (Surah al-An'am, 6:151)

And after that the Almighty, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents. His mother carried him with hardship and bore him with hardship, and his gestation and weaning are thirty months.﴾ (Surah al-Ahqaf, 46:15)

It also comes in Surah al-'Ankabut, where He says:

﴿And We have enjoined upon man goodness toward his parents.﴾ (Surah al-'Ankabut, 29:8)

But if they strive with you to associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. If the parents are polytheists, we must still be kind to them in custom (ma'ruf), and kindness, as we have explained, is for one you love and one you do not love; but what is forbidden is inner affection (widdah qalbiyyah). For this reason He said: ﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger.﴾ (Surah al-Mujadilah, 58:22)

There is no contradiction, or even apparent contradiction, between the verse we are discussing and the verse of Surah al-Mujadilah. There are verses in which the Truth spoke and joined His worship with kindness to parents, and there are two verses in which the command concerning parents comes independently.

That is in His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents.﴾ (Surah al-Ahqaf, 46:15)

And in His saying, glorified is He:

﴿And We have enjoined upon man goodness toward his parents.﴾ (Surah al-'Ankabut, 29:8)

In it there is "ihsan," and in it there is "husn." "Ihsan" is that you do beyond what Allah has obligated upon you, sensing that He sees you. If you do not see Him, then He sees you. And "ihsan" comes from "ahsana," meaning that He approved the obligation and added to what He obligated. When a person exceeds what

1 Narrated by Muslim and Ibn Majah from Abu Hurairah.

And he spoke about giving, generosity, magnanimity, liberality and the open hand. Then He, glory be to Him, brought the discussion of the opposite, which is:

﴿Those who are niggardly and enjoin niggardliness upon people, and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty. And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.﴾

And what is the meaning of bukhl (niggardliness)? It is the hardship of giving. When a person cuts off a need from his own special wealth to give it to another, he finds that a hardship and does not willingly engage in it. But the generous man has an open hand and magnanimity; he finds rest in doing good. Thus, bukhl means the hardship of giving. Niggardliness may exceed its limit and go beyond the bounds by a person's stinginess with something whose giving does not harm him and whose withholding does not benefit him, because he does not want to give at all. This niggardliness and miserliness exist in the soul of the miser, for first he has been niggardly toward himself. So if he has been niggardly toward himself, would you expect him to be generous toward people?

The poet depicts a miser named "Isa" and wishes to censure him, because he is extremely stingy. He shows the image of niggardliness as being not only toward people but toward himself as well, in what its giving does not harm and its withholding does not benefit him. And since he is stingy with himself, his stinginess toward others will be expected:

Isa is stingy with himself,
and he is neither lasting nor eternal.
So if he could, for the sake of his stinginess,
breathe through a single nostril...

He is so stingy that he thinks, if he could breathe through one nostril, he would do so, so as not to breathe through both nostrils.

Another poet also gives an image showing how the miser prevents himself from magnanimity and humanity, saying:

O son of my uncle Muhammad, if your house,
with a needle, the courtyard of the home would be too narrow for it,
and Yusuf came to you asking to borrow a needle
to sew the torn shirt, you would not do it.

The poet depicts that if Prophet Yusuf came to this miser and said to him, "Give me a needle so that I may sew the torn shirt which Zulaykha tore," and this miser has a house whose courtyard is filled with needles, he would still be stingy and refuse.

So the miser is one who is constricted in giving, to the point that he is constricted even about giving something whose giving does no harm and whose withholding does not benefit him. And the Truth says concerning the misers:

﴿And let not those who are niggardly with what Allah has given them of His bounty think that it is good for them. Rather, it is bad for them. They will be encircled by that about which they were niggardly on the Day of Resurrection. And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ (Surah Al 'Imran).

So the Truth makes for the miser, of what he withheld, a collar around his neck. Had the miser given a little, the collar would have been light around his neck on the Day of Resurrection. But the miser, whenever he restrains himself from giving, the collar grows heavier.

The Truth also said concerning those who hoard gold and silver:

﴿And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah — give them tidings of a painful punishment. On the Day it is heated in the fire of Hell and their foreheads, their sides and their backs are branded with it: "This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard."﴾ (part of verse 34 and verse 35, Surah At-Tawbah).

If their hoarding is of large amounts, then what is heated of it in the Fire will be much, and they will be branded with it. So a person must lighten for himself the branding. Those who are niggardly are not content with this moral baseness within their souls, but love that it should spread to others, as if they have fallen in love with niggardliness. It pains them to see a generous person; the miser says to you, "Do not spend," because he is pained when he sees a generous person, and he wants all people to be misers, so that no one may be better than him.

He knows that generosity is better, as evidenced by his wanting all people to be misers. Niggardliness is withholding what you have been given from one who has not been given it. Is niggardliness only in wealth? No, rather it occurs in every endowment you have been given which is lacking in others and which they need; if you withhold it, you are within niggardliness. Whoever is niggardly with his power to aid the one who lacks power, and whoever is niggardly with his knowledge toward one who does not know, this is niggardliness; and whoever is niggardly even with forbearance toward the foolish, this is also niggardliness. If you have a capacity for forbearance, then give it out. So niggardliness means: you withhold something God has given you from one who needs it. A teacher, for example, who has ten students learning a craft and tries to conceal the secrets of the craft from them, he has been niggardly.

﴿Those who are niggardly and enjoin niggardliness upon people﴾. The verse's meaning is broad enough to encompass every matter, material or moral. We also take it in its elevated meanings. The People of the Book used to know his description, peace and blessings be upon him, and they knew him as they know their own sons. When he came to them confirming what was with them, they disbelieved in his message, peace and blessings be upon him, and concealed their knowledge of him from the people, and concealed their knowledge of what he brought of knowledge, though he was the truthful and the one confirmed. This is niggardliness at its height, and after that they continued to enjoin niggardliness upon people.

You know that the Ansar had the Ansari magnanimity, and when the Emigrants came to them, they shared their wealth with them. Even the blessing which Allah planted in the heart of the believer as jealousy over it, lest anyone attain it even if he dislikes it, namely the blessing of women: for a man, even if he dislikes his wife, he is jealous that anyone should take her. Yet the Ansar shared their wives. How many a man was married to more than one, divorced a wife in order to marry her to an emigrant. The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, elevates the magnanimity of the Ansar to the point that the Ansari would come to the emigrant and say to him: "Look at one of my wives or one of my wives, and choose what pleases you, and I will divorce her and you may marry her."

What lofty magnanimity is this? If you are a person of blessing and you are a believer, you love to extend the effect of your blessing to others; if you have a luxurious car, you may love to give it in charity, but a woman, no. Yet this magnanimity came from the Ansar, and they said: "These are emigrants who have left their families." This was a spiritual elevation in the very selves of the Ansar.

The Emigrants came to them, and among them were young men overflowing with vigor, and Quraysh had prevented their families from them, so they had no wives. The Ansari would say: "Why should I not divorce one of my wives, so that my brother the emigrant may marry her to relieve his desires? And at the least of what it involves, I would prevent his gaze from turning to what is forbidden." But the Jews, the polytheists and the hypocrites would say to them: "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah." The Noble Qur'an speaks of this situation:

﴿They are the ones who say, "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse." And to Allah belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not understand.﴾ (Surah Al-Munafiqun).

They misjudged those who believed in the Messenger of Allah, and thought that if they did not spend on them, they would turn away from their faith. They forgot that the believing Emigrants had left their wealth and left their lands. Whoever leaves his wealth for emigration in the way of Allah, would he disbelieve on account of finding nothing? No; for he has left everything in the way of Allah. Here is Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr, the pampered one among Quraysh, whose mother lavished blessings upon him, the owner of perfumes; then he went to Madinah and wore a sheepskin, and the Prophet (ﷺ) looked at him and said to his companions: "Look at how faith has transformed your companion." When the hypocrites, like 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy, say to the Ansar: "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse," they think the believers could sell their faith for a morsel of bread, as if they had forgotten that the one who sells his faith for a morsel is one who carries a false principle; but whoever embraces and believes in a true principle finds its sweetness in the soul, and his reward is stored with his Lord. He does not turn away from it. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said:

(I came to the mosque, and Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr came upon us in a patched cloak of his, a sheepskin patched with fur; he had been the most pampered youth in Makkah and the most luxurious. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw him, he recalled the luxury he had been in and saw his present state, and his eyes filled with tears for him. Then he said: "Are you today better, or when one of you is brought a bowl of bread and meat in the morning?" We said: "We are then better; we are relieved of burdens and free for worship." He said: "Rather, you today are better than you were then.")¹

We say: You must remember well that among the sweetness of certainty and the sweetness of faith is that the believer sacrifices everything for the sake of the elevation of faith. But the people of false principles admit no one else into them except on payment in advance; that is, they buy them. So if you see a principle that buys human beings, know that it is a false principle. Had it been a true principle, a person would pay for entry into it his precious wealth, and even sacrifice his own soul in its way.

Among the wonders of the principles of Islam is that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took the pledge for himself at the Pledge of 'Aqabah, the Ansar said to him: "If we are faithful to this, what will be ours?" As if they were saying: "You took your share; what is ours?"

Look at the loftiness of faith and the certainty of the Chosen One that faith itself is the reward. Did he promise them that they would possess the earth? Did he promise them that these oppressed ones would be the ones to be established in it? No; rather he said to them: "For you is Paradise." Had he said to them, "For you is the rulership of this world," there would have been room for objection; it is true that the world submitted and humbled itself to them, but some of them died before the world drew near to them and was subdued, so where is the truth of the prophecy?

Thus he spoke to them of the certain thing, the thing in which the believer finds himself the moment he dies. He said: "For you is Paradise." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, with a band of his companions around him: "Come, pledge allegiance to me that you will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit fornication, nor kill your children, nor bring a slander which you invent between your hands and feet, nor disobey me in what is right. Whoever of you fulfills it, his reward is with Allah; and whoever commits any of that and is punished for it in this world, it is an expiation for him; and whoever commits any of that and Allah conceals it, his matter is with Allah: if He wills, He punishes him, and if He wills, He pardons him."²

He did not deceive them that they would be men of authority, nor did he say to them, "You will sit on the carpets and the world will be subservient to you"; rather he said to them at the beginning of the pledge: "For you is Paradise." So beware lest any of you covet anything except Paradise. For this reason the Ansar are beloved to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When the Battle of Hunayn came and the Emigrants were given some of the spoils while the Ansar received none, the Ansar found something in their souls. The Messenger of Allah addressed them with a faith-inspiring appeal and said:

"Are you not pleased, O assembly of the Ansar, that people should go away with sheep and camels while you return with the Messenger of Allah to your dwellings? By Him in whose hand is Muhammad's soul, were it not for the Emigration, I would have been a man of the Ansar. If people took one valley and the Ansar took another valley, I would take the valley of the Ansar. O Allah, have mercy on the Ansar, and the sons of the Ansar, and the sons of the sons of the Ansar."³

Then the people wept until they wet their beards, and they said: "We are pleased with the Messenger of Allah as our portion and our share."

What spiritual loftiness is this! But the hypocrites said to the Ansar: "Do not spend your wealth on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse."

But the believers did not disperse. They had left comfort and wealth in Makkah and came to emigrate; they did not come to take a presumed, limited, meager luxury, and what was promised them of certain, vast, lasting bliss sufficed them. They knew by faith that worldly luxury either escapes you by death or escapes you by change of fortune; but the bliss of the Hereafter has no limit at which it ends, and it neither escapes you nor do you escape it.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾. When you see something concealing something, you must understand from it that this concealing means preventing something that by its nature wants to come out. As they say: "Conceal blood, for if you do not conceal it, it will find a path." As if wealth or knowledge wants to come out to people, but its possessors conceal it. The natural disposition of every provision, whether material or immaterial, is that it seeks a path, because everything is created to serve man. When a person comes and bars something of what is created to serve man and holds it back, he thereby prevents the concealed thing from its mission; for everything is created to serve the children of Adam. So when you hinder it from this service, the thing grieves; and let your imagination extend to the point that inanimate things also grieve.

﴿So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them﴾ (part of verse 29, Surah Ad-Dukhan).

So the heaven and the earth have a weeping, and it is not the weeping of tears, but rather...

¹ Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the Book of the Description of the Day of Resurrection, chapter on the condition of Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr after Islam; also recorded by al-Hakim, and mentioned by Ibn Sa'd in his Tabaqat and by Ibn al-Athir in Usd al-Ghabah.
² Narrated by al-Bukhari.

Therefore He, glory be to Him, makes clear: the miser will not only suffer punishment, but will suffer a humiliating punishment. Then the Truth, glory be to Him, presents the opposite, namely those other than the miser, and says:

﴿And those who spend their wealth to be seen by people, and do not believe in Allah or the Last Day. And whoever has Satan as a companion, then evil is he as a companion.﴾ [4:38]

This noble verse speaks of the one who spends, but the purpose is unclear to him. His purpose is weak, because he spends to be seen by people; he intends by his spending to show off before people. For this reason, those who know the grace of Allah say: "Choose the one who values your gift." When you give something to a person, he values that thing according to his means and abilities, whether with a word of praise, for example, or otherwise. But how does Allah, glory be to Him, value a gift given for His sake? The price must necessarily be great.

So the wise person looks to whom he will give the blessing. We have an example in our master 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, when the merchants learned that a caravan of goods was coming to him. All the merchants came to buy the goods from him in order to sell them and profit, and he said to them: "I have been offered more than your price." In the end he said to them: "I have sold it to Allah." Thus our master 'Uthman traded with Allah, and He raised the price of his merchandise. As for the one who gives to be seen by people, we say to him: you are a loser, because you did not value your blessing; rather you cast it away at a worthless price. What will people do for you? They may envy you for your blessing and wish to take it from you, so why do you show off to them? This, then, is a failed and losing transaction. For this reason the Truth said:

﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their wealth in exchange for that they will have Paradise.﴾ (Qur'an 9:111)

Since He, glory be to Him, is the One who buys, the price must be great, because He gives a bliss in which there is no loss: in Paradise a blessing does not escape a believer, nor does he escape it. The one who shows off to people is a loser and does not know the principles of trade, because he has not tasted trade with Allah. For this reason, in another verse, his deed is likened to:

﴿Like the example of a smooth rock with dust on it; a heavy rain strikes it and leaves it bare.﴾ (Qur'an 2:264)

"Safwan" is the smooth stone (marw), its plural being marw, and they are white, shining stones. The marw is smooth and not rough, but it has some crevices into which dust can enter; and because the marw is very smooth, even a little water, even a drizzle, washes away the dust. The one who spends his wealth to be seen by people is one for whom the matter of faith has become clear, but faith has not yet taken root in his heart. If you knew that you wanted to sell a commodity and there was a merchant offering a higher price for it, why would you give it to the one with the lower price? If you do so, you have lost and suffered loss. So the Truth makes it clear to you: as long as you want to be seen by people, you do not have faith in the One who buys at the highest price, and so you are a failed merchant in the world of economics. For this reason we have said: let everyone, when he gives, beware of pride in giving. Giving is received by Allah with a good reward, but he must not give with noise and publicity that exposes his giving. For this reason the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said among the seven whom Allah will shade in His shade on the day when there is no shade but His:

("A man who gave charity and concealed it, until his left hand does not know what his right hand spends.")

When the righteous servant gives, he knows that his hand is the upper hand, and the upper hand is better than the lower hand. So let him conceal the lowliness of the hands of the needy from people and not make it visible.

But Allah, the Exalted, does not want to restrict the scope of giving, so He says:

﴿If you disclose your charities, they are good; but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you, and He will remove from you some of your misdeeds. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ (Qur'an 2:271)

So disclosing charity is not prohibited if the one who does it intends to be an example. The main thing is that showing off be removed from the heart at the moment of giving charity. The Truth makes clear: beware lest you spend while there is showing off in you. As for one who pays zakat while there is showing off in his heart, Allah does not deprive the needy of the gift of a giver, because He, glory be to Him, affirms: "Take from him," though he is the loser, because he will not receive reward, but the community benefits.

Indeed, those who spend their wealth to be seen by people are among those who "do not believe in Allah," because He, glory be to Him, is the Giver, and He loves that a Muslim place his giving into His hand. ﴿And do not believe in Allah or the Last Day.﴾ If they believed in the Last Day, they would see the enduring reward. So if you love your blessing, take the blessing and try to make it fruitful, i.e., abundant in fruit. The one who has not given charity from his wealth and has not spent it, even on himself, has finished the matter of his wealth, and his wealth has reached its limit with him at this point; but the one who spends it in the way of Allah will find it in the Hereafter, and so he will have prolonged the life of his wealth.

The miser is the enemy of his wealth, because he has not been able to make it fruitful. For this reason the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, says in the noble hadith:

("When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah, the Exalted, will descend to His servants to judge between them, and every nation will be kneeling. The first to be called will be a man who memorized the Qur'an, a man who was killed in the way of Allah, and a man of abundant wealth. Allah will say to the reciter: Did I not teach you what I sent down to My Messenger? He will say: Yes, my Lord. He will say: Then what did you do with what you were taught? He will say: I used to stand with it in the hours of the night and the hours of the day. Allah will say to him: You lie, and the angels will say: You lie. Allah will say to him: Rather, you wanted it to be said: So-and-so is a reciter, and it has been said. And the owner of wealth will be brought...")

But did religion tell you: do not do it? No; do it, so that people benefit in spite of you.

When the miser's wealth increases, he has deprived himself of this wealth; then a son of his comes wanting to enjoy the wealth. For this reason it is said in the countryside: "The hoarder's wealth goes to the pleasure-seeker." No one is able to deceive his Creator, ever! So He, glory be to Him, makes clear: "I have given you a blessing that You have not given to anyone, but I will facilitate the path for one who obeys Me. Beware of thinking that you have deceived Me when you were stingy; your stinginess falls upon you. So you have restricted your provision by stinginess; if you had spent, Allah would have given you much good: ﴿And whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it.﴾ But you left it to your heirs, and they will take it so that their provision becomes abundant. Also, when you withhold wealth from others, you have made the way easy for one who spends."

How? Suppose a person is generous, and his generosity does not let him hide from the beggar, and people hope in him. Then his income does not suffice for his obligations; if he has "two plowlands," he sells one plowland to rejoice in giving to the needy, and when he sells the plowland, someone who hoards will buy it, so the hoarder has made the way easy for the generous one. Beware of thinking that you can deceive the One who created you, created the universe, and gave you this blessing. This is like the one who commits a sin and whom Allah honors with repentance and return to Him. We say to him: beware of believing that you have ever stolen a desire from Allah. You have stolen a desire that will eventually inflame you and make you do good deeds like it twenty times over, because He, glory be to Him, has said: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds.﴾ (Qur'an 11:114)

So you will not deceive your Creator, for He will place it behind you, and you will do much good. Likewise, to the miser we say: you will facilitate the way for a generous, lavish giver. The Truth, glory be to Him, at the end of the verse explained the cause that led to this. The causes are many, but they are gathered in the word "Satan." Everyone who prevents you from the path of guidance is a satan, beginning with the desires of your soul and the heedlessness of your mind from the method. Behind all these matters there is a satan whispering to you, and we call all of these "satan," because Satan is the one who distances you from the method. There are satans among the jinn and satans among mankind. The soul, when it leads a person not to adhere to the method, because adherence to the method will make him miss an opportunity for a desire, is a satan. The soul that sees immediate desire and loses a limitless deferred desire is a satan. So Satan is the one who made them stingy and commanded people to be stingy. When Satan is a companion of a person, it means he is attached to him, and "qarin" (companion) is one who is bound to someone.

The word "qarn" is also applied to a period of time of one hundred years, because it binds generations to one another. Satan is a qarin, that is, one who clings to his companion and is attached to him, so the Truth says: ﴿And whoever has Satan as a companion, then evil is he as a companion,﴾ that is, wretched is this companion, because he is the companion who neither benefits me nor turns me away from a harmful course.

For this reason people may love one another in this world because they gather in disobedience. But in the Hereafter, what do they do? The Truth says:

﴿Close friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous.﴾ (Qur'an 43:67)

Because the righteous help one another in obedience; one of them says to his companion: you used to help me in obedience, you used to guide me and remind me if I was heedless, so love between them increases. But a person curses the one who misled him, and the first we curse on the Day of Resurrection is Satan; likewise Satan is the first to disown us. So when the dispute comes, you find Satan saying to those he misled and led astray:

﴿And I had no authority over you except that I invited you and you responded to me.﴾ (Qur'an 14:22)

Authority (sultan) is the high power that compels those beneath it. A person's body and structure are compelled by the authority of material force, and he is subdued in his beliefs by evidence and argument. Compulsion over matter controls the form, but it does not control the heart; you may be weak before a strong person, yet you hold a whip for him and say: "Prostrate to me," and he prostrates and submits. In that way you have subdued the form, but you have not subdued the heart. This is material authority which subdues the form. But if a person comes to you with proofs and convinces you, this is the subjugation of persuasion, and the power to subdue minds by persuasion is also a kind of authority.

So authority comes from two directions: an authority that subdues the form, and an authority that subdues the understanding of the heart. The authority of the form makes you submit against your will; the authority of argument and proof makes you act with your own consent. Satan says to those who followed him: O you who made me a companion to you, do not part from me; you are fools. I have no authority over you, and I did not have such power that I could compel you to commit sins, nor did I have a proof or argument to persuade you to commit sins; but you were heedless. I only pointed to you, and I do not possess power to subdue your matter, nor a proof to dominate your minds:

﴿And I had no authority over you except that I invited you and you responded to me; so do not blame me, but blame yourselves.﴾ (Qur'an 14:22)

So the blame is upon you yourselves; for this reason the Truth says:

﴿I cannot help you, nor can you help me.﴾ (Qur'an 14:22)

What does "bi-musrikhikum" mean? It is the cry of one in a crisis he cannot bear, whose means have been exhausted; then he seeks help from another and cries out to others, calling on them to rescue and aid him. The one who responds to him and comes to save him is said to have "removed his cry," so "asrakhahu" means he hastened and answered his cry. Satan says: if you seek my help, I will not help you, and you will not help me; each of us has learned his responsibility and capacity. As for man, the Truth says:

﴿And We have fastened every person's bird of fortune to his neck.﴾ (Qur'an 17:13)
