So whoever takes Satan as a companion, "then evil is he as a companion." The word "sa'a" (evil) is like the word "bi'sa" (wretched); both are used to blame and condemn a thing, that is, wretched is it that Satan should be a companion to you, because Satan took upon himself a covenant before Allah that he would not mislead those who obey Him, and would mislead all others among mankind.

When you reflect on the verse, you find that the Truth says: ﴿And those who spend their wealth to be seen by people, and do not believe in Allah or the Last Day, and whoever has Satan as a companion, then evil is he as a companion.﴾

So the verse addresses a kind of spending whose reward Allah nullifies. The spending of the one who shows off extends its benefit to others, but the one who shows off does not benefit from it; rather, it has only diminished his wealth and has not borne fruit with his Lord.

The Truth draws our attention to the fact that all of this is due to the obstacles to faith, which requires of a person that he be alive in every movement...

The Most High says next:

﴿And what would be upon them if they believed in God and the Last Day and spent from what God has provided them? And God is ever Knowing of them.﴾ (39)

His saying, glory be to Him, "And what would be upon them" — what harm, burden or injury would befall them from faith and from spending in the way of God? He, glory be to Him, is not asking them about what would afflict them from that; rather, He, majestic is His state, is censuring them, rebuking them, describing them, and branding them with ignorance and heedlessness regarding what would benefit them.

Consider the student who plays around and so fails: you say to him, "And what would be upon you if you had studied?!" That is, what harm would come to you from this? So this means that such a phrase is only said to a person who has the capacity to perform the act, and such a student is able to study. But we do not say to a person who has a trait with no choice in it, such as shortness of stature for example, "What would be upon you if you were tall?!" This is a statement that neither benefits nor is correct.

So "what would be upon you" is said only to one who has the voluntary capacity to be that way; as for one who has no capacity not to be that way, it is not said to him. We say this because the sect of the Jabriyya said: whoever disbelieves cannot believe, so the disbeliever remains a disbeliever. But they did not pay attention to our Lord's saying: ﴿And what would be upon them if they believed in God and the Last Day﴾. The meaning of this statement is that the door is open. Otherwise, if they were bound to disbelief, our Lord would not have said: ﴿And what would be upon them﴾. This verse does not only refute the doctrine of the Jabriyya; it demolishes the entire doctrine of the Jabriyya. Man is not compelled to an act and the matter is ended, as they say: "like a feather in the wind." As the poet said:

*He cast him into the sea, bound, and said to him:*
*"Beware, beware of getting wet with the water!"*

We say to them: you have attributed injustice to God, God forbid, for God, glory be to Him and exalted, did not ask man to believe in Him unless He had placed in him a voluntary power by which he chooses between alternatives. You did not perceive the reality of the writing of everything from eternity, so you took from it that which people must necessarily carry out, and you did not notice that there is a difference between something being written so that it is compelled, and something being written because He knows it.

He, glory be to Him, wrote—why? Because He knew from eternity that His servant would choose this and choose that. Thus the writing is not for compulsion but on account of prior knowledge. Knowledge is an attribute of disclosure, not an attribute of influence.

To clarify this, we say: attributes are of two kinds: an attribute that discloses things as they are, regardless of whether it compels or does not compel; and power, which is an attribute of bringing into being, not an attribute of disclosure. An example of this is the dean of a college who comes and says to a professor of some subject: "A prize has come to me for the outstanding student in such-and-such subject, so make an examination for the students so that we may give this prize to whoever deserves it." The professor of the subject says: "There is no need for an examination, for I know them and I know their positions in earnestness, their positions in diligence, and their positions in understanding of knowledge; so-and-so is the first, give him the prize." The dean is not convinced, so he himself sets an examination or brings other professors to set the examination apart from this professor. Afterward, the student whom the professor had already identified wins first place.

Now, when the student answered the questions that had been set for him, was there someone forcing the student who won first place to write the scientific material that earned him the prize? No. Then why did the professor say that about him? Because he knew who among them had the capacity of knowledge. The professor judged first because he knew.

And to God belongs the highest likeness, before and after: the Most High gave people choice among alternatives, but He made clear: "I know that My servant will choose this and that." So this is prior knowledge, not compulsion by power. Power has influence, while knowledge has no influence and no compulsion. And God's saying here: ﴿And what would be upon them if they believed in God﴾ — His saying ﴿And what would be upon them﴾ means: what harm would befall them. The word "upon them" always reveals to a person what is incumbent on him; therefore it does not say "for them" but says: what harm would have befallen them had they believed in God. For this reason the Truth says: ﴿those who think that they will meet their Lord﴾ (Qur'an 2:46).

He did not say, glory be to Him, "those who are certain." Rather, mere supposition of meeting God led them to do righteous deeds, so what of when the servant is certain? The one who is certain performs righteous deeds all the more. For this reason this matter cleared al-Ma'arri of what they accused him of, namely that he denied resurrection. It is true that at the beginning of his life he said:

*The days have shattered us until we are*
*like glass, but no recasting is returned to us.*

They said: his saying "no recasting is returned to us" means that he denies the Truth's power to resurrect us a second time. Yet it may be interpreted otherwise: that no recasting returns to us in this life, and we do not see that whoever dies returns a second time. We also say: he said this at the beginning of his life. But at the end he said:

*The astrologer and the physician both claim*
*that bodies are not gathered. I say to you both:*
*If your saying is true, I am not a loser;*
*but if my saying is true, the loss is upon you both.*

He asks the physician and the astrologer to cease corrupting minds with doubt. Suppose he believed there is no resurrection, and another believed there is resurrection. We say to him: either resurrection comes, and then it proves false the one who said there is no resurrection; or resurrection does not come, and then what harm did the one who believed in resurrection suffer? And if resurrection comes, who has lost? Whoever denied it will lose. So the one who denies resurrection gains nothing, while the one who says there is a resurrection does not lose, and so on.

As for the Truth's saying "And what would be upon them": it is a question about what harm would befall them "if they believed in God and the Last Day and spent from what God has provided them." Whoever gives charity and places it into God's hand, God invests it on behalf of the giver; but when someone does that to be seen by people, it yields returns with those who do not give, and thus they have lost their wealth and lost the multiplication of their wealth in God's hand through reward in the Hereafter. ﴿And what would be upon them if they believed in God and the Last Day and spent from what God has provided them, and God is ever Knowing of them.﴾ God's knowledge is pervasive, and He, glory be to Him, knows hidden things; He, glory be to Him, encompasses all things in knowledge. Therefore the Truth says next: ﴿Indeed, God does not wrong [even] an atom's weight; and if it is a good deed He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.﴾ (40)

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 4, verse 40:

﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong (anyone) by an atom's weight. And if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.﴾

Injustice (zulm): its root meaning is the desire to benefit from another's effort. When you wrong someone, you are taking his right, and his right is what he obtained through his effort and sweat, while you take it without effort or sweat. It follows from this that the wrongdoer is usually strong. But what about the one who wrongs a person for the benefit of another person? He himself did not benefit from his wrongdoing, but someone else did. This is worse than the first. On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Hasten to good deeds before trials come like pieces of the dark night. A man will be a believer in the morning and a disbeliever in the evening, or a believer in the evening and a disbeliever in the morning, selling his religion for a worldly commodity."

This is because he wronged a person for the benefit of another servant, while he himself took nothing for himself.

So injustice is either benefiting from the fruit of another's effort without toil yourself, or benefiting another person through someone else's effort. As for Allah, glory be to Him, if we consider Him as the Strong, the Possessor of strength, and (far be it from Allah to wrong) if He wanted to wrong, what would His wronging look like? Injustice is proportionate to the strength of the wrongdoer. So when the strong wrongs, his wrong is unbearable. Then why would He wrong? What would He want to take, when He is the Giver? He, glory be to Him, is self-sufficient, and He will not take from this to give to that. All of them are equal in relation to Him, because He, glory be to Him, has taken neither a consort nor a son. All are equal, so why would He wrong?

For Allah, injustice is rationally and logically impossible. It is not possible for Allah to waste the reward of a good deed or to multiply an evil deed. This does not occur, and Allah is the Giver of all blessings to all people. Since He is the One who gave all blessings, He, glory be to Him, does not benefit from the effects of His creation. The Real, glory be to Him and exalted, negates injustice from Himself in His saying: ﴿And your Lord is never unjust to the servants﴾ (part of verse 46, surah Fussilat).

The word "ظلام" (zallam, "very unjust") is like our saying: so-and-so is "akkal" (a great eater) and so-and-so is "nawwam" (a great sleeper). It differs from our saying "so-and-so is sleeping," meaning he slept once. But "nawwam" means he persistently sleeps a lot. That is, he either exaggerates the action, or he repeats the action. Exaggeration, as we know, comes once because the action is single but intense, and once because the action is ordinary but repeated. This is exaggeration. So His saying, glory be to Him and exalted, ﴿And your Lord is not a great wronger﴾ negates exaggeration, and this does not require negating other than exaggeration. We say: if Allah were to wrong, His wrong would be proportionate to His power, and so it would be great and abundant. And if He were a wrongdoer, His wrong would encompass and reach all creation, and so it would likewise be great and abundant. But Allah, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong (anyone) by an atom's weight.﴾ He, glory be to Him, counts an evil deed as one evil deed, but as for a good deed, He multiplies it. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong (anyone) by an atom's weight.﴾ "Mithqal" (weight): it means heaviness and weight, and heaviness is the magnitude of the earth's gravitational pull on an object. When the weight of an object is small and you drop it from above, it falls slowly, but a heavy object, when you drop it from above, falls quickly, because its gravitational force is stronger. When a person looks at the word "mithqal" and expresses it as weight, the standard of the balance here is "the atom" (dharrah). What is the "dharrah"?

The scholars said about it: it is the head of a small ant that is barely visible to the naked eye, or the ant itself. This is one saying. Or the dharrah, as Ibn Abbas said when asked about it: he took some earth from the ground and blew on it. When he blew, the dust scattered in the air. He told them: each one of these is called a "dharrah," and it is what we call "haba'" (floating dust). Now we are in one place and we see nothing in the air, but look at a beam of light, through any hole through which sunlight enters. At the moment you see a hole through which sunlight enters, you see much dust floating. The important point is that you only see it moving in a ray of sunlight. It was present and we inhale it, so what made me not see it? Because it is so small and fine that it exceeds the capacity of the eye to see it. So the dharrah is one particle of this dust, and its name is "haba'," and the singular of haba' is dharrah.

The Real, glory be to Him and exalted, clarifies for us that everything is measured down to its smallest degree of weight, which is the dharrah, which is the haba'. We do not see it except in confined light, because in strong light we do not see those particles. Rather, we see them only in a light that has one source and penetrates. Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, does not wrong (anyone) by an atom's weight. This is only an illustration, because the dharrah can be enlarged, and what can be enlarged can be reduced. The Real said this when human beings did not have the instrument by which the dharrah could be split. Then it happened that man was able to do so. After the First World War, Germany produced cylinders for splitting the atom, or "the indivisible part," as philosophers in ancient times described it. The meaning of "indivisible" is that nothing smaller than it can exist. They did not consider that anything that has matter, if it accepts enlargement, also accepts reduction. The important point is that the instrument that perceives smallness should be available to man.

An example of this is when artificial satellites were launched and took a picture of New York City from the air. The picture came out small of New York City. Afterwards they enlarged the picture, and they brought out the numbers of the cars that were moving. How did this happen? The small picture contained more precise details that the naked eye cannot see, and when it is enlarged everything becomes clear, even car numbers, which had been invisible. If you were in New York at this hour, would you appear in it? You cannot appear. Why? Because your image has been reduced to such a degree that you cannot be seen at this size, and so on. When light is confined, the beam of light that enters a place has the power to reveal the particle of dust that you were not seeing.

So a light created by Allah is one in which the dharrah appeared. Could an atom on earth be hidden from the light of the Creator? It cannot be hidden from Him, glory be to Him, because the light that He created revealed the dharrah and the dust that was present and that we do not see. An atom on earth will not be hidden from the Light of Lights.

Thus we know that the matter, with respect to Allah, is a definite process. When they invented the cylinder for splitting the atom, it was like sugarcane juice. We know that a stalk of sugarcane is placed between two iron columns. Each column is called a "cylinder." When they bring the two cylinders close together and pass the sugarcane stalk between them, the distance between them must be narrow, so that when the stalk passes through it is squeezed. Thus, the narrower the gap between the two cylinders, the greater the squeezing. As long as the two cylinders move, each one over the other, there is a very tiny space here. The German scientists tried to narrow the two cylinders to a degree that would split the atom for us, and they succeeded, and there appeared something smaller than the atom.

The superficial people who lie in wait for Islam and the Book of Allah, looking for a way to find an opening in it, said: Allah said ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾. They took it to mean that it is the smallest thing, and it became clear that there is something smaller than an atom's weight, because the atom was split. We said to them: you took one verse and forgot verses. The Qur'an came as a miracle to address diverse societies from the time of the Messenger of Allah until the Hour comes. So there must be in it what satisfies minds from the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until the Hour comes. If the giving of the Qur'an had been poured out once in the age of the message, the subsequent centuries would have come with no giving from the Qur'an. So our Lord willed that the Qur'an be the miracle and the method containing the rulings and universal principles, and these are matters understandable for the age of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until the Hour comes. But there are still cosmic facts and laws of the Real in existence that have not yet appeared, and He, glory be to Him, gives each age according to the extent of its understanding.

When we learn the secrets of a cosmic matter, no ruling is added to us. When we learn a matter, for example the matter of the atom and its splitting, and there are indications of it in the noble Qur'an, that does not add any ruling to us. Rather, the rulings remain as they are. The rulings are clear in every way, because whoever does them is rewarded, and whoever does not do them is punished. The people over whom the Hour will come are like the people who lived in the time of the Prophet, peace be upon him. Therefore the rulings must be one. As for the fact that the Qur'an is a book of rulings, this is a matter clear beyond any addition. The contemporary of the Messenger of Allah did not understand a ruling and then a person in our time comes to understand a different ruling. Rather, all rulings are equal.

The Qur'an as a miracle is also a miracle for everyone. There must be a miracle for every generation and for every age. The inimitability (i'jaz) comes through the cosmic signs, which if we did not know them, nothing would happen with respect to the rulings. For example: if we did not know that the earth rotates, would our benefit from the earth decrease? No. We benefit from the earth whether we know it is round or not. But the Real, glory be to Him and exalted, addresses minds with what they can bear. When minds advance, become enlightened, and are illuminated by their scientific ambitions regarding the universe, then the Qur'an, if it does not support them, does not oppose them.

When they split the atom, the skeptics said: our Lord strikes the atom as an example of the smallest thing: ﴿And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾. But there is something smaller than the atom. We answer them: you looked at one verse and forgot verses. As we said, you did not notice that those who split the atom into electrons, ions, positive and negative charges, then tried to split what had been split. The verse we are discussing now: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong (anyone) by an atom's weight﴾ satisfied the minds that know this original atom, which is one thing. And why do we not hear the saying of Allah: ﴿And you are not engaged in any matter, nor recite from it any part of the Qur'an, nor do you do any deed, but We are witness over you when you are involved in it. And not absent from your Lord is any [part] of an atom's weight within the earth or within the heaven or anything smaller than that or greater, but it is in a clear register.﴾ (surah Yunus, 61)

So there is an atom, and there is something smaller than the atom. You did not take into account that "smaller" here is a comparative form, and there is no "smallest" unless there is a "small." So there is an atom, and there is something small compared to the atom, and there is something smaller than the small. Thus there are three stages. If they split the atom, we have in the Qur'an a basis that speaks of smallness. If they split what was split, we have in the Qur'an something smaller, because every smallest must be preceded by a small. And if you split what was split, we still have in the Qur'an a basis that precedes your minds in innovation. If you say splitting is permissible, and if you say assembling is permissible, that is because it is smaller and larger, splitting or assembling. What is reasonable is that you say: the smallest and the small are not absent, and the atom is likewise not absent. How then is the greater expressed as not absent, when it is apparent and clear?

We say to you: the speaker is our Lord. A thing is not perceived either because it is subtle, extremely fine, so that sight does not reach it and it is not seen. Also, it is not perceived because it is great in a magnitude greater than sight can encompass. When you see a large mountain at a distance of two or three kilometers, you do not perceive it, because it is greater than your sight's radiation can encompass. But the matter with respect to Allah is different. There is no tiny thing that He does not see, and no great thing that He does not see. So it must be ﴿nor anything smaller than that or greater.﴾ In another verse He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿He knows what enters into the earth and what emerges from it and what descends from the heaven and what ascends therein. And He is the Merciful, the Forgiving.﴾ (surah Saba, 2)

Observe the precision of the Real in responding to the denial of the Hour, which is a cosmic matter that applies to all ages. He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And those who disbelieve say: "The Hour will not come to us." Say: "Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you. [He is] the Knower of the unseen; not absent from Him is an atom's weight within the heavens or within the earth, nor anything smaller than that or greater, but it is in a clear register."﴾ (surah Saba, 3)

It would have been enough for Him to say: the Hour is coming. But He clarified: know that the Hour is coming, and everything you have done is recorded. Why do they say: the Hour will not come? This is a kind of self-deception, because they did not...

[Footnote 1: Narrated by Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and Ahmad.]

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 4, verse 41:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and bring you as a witness against these people?﴾

Whenever you hear the word "how" (kayf), know that there is something astonishing. For example, you say: "You insulted the sultan, so how did they confront you, and you found him in front of you—what did you do?" Confronting the sultan itself was a matter beyond imagination. Thus, whatever is being marvelled at is introduced with "how." An example of this is His saying, the Truth:

﴿How do you disbelieve in God?﴾ (part of verse 28, surah al-Baqarah).

This means an expression of wonder at a calamity and disaster, which is disbelief in God. So tell us: how did this come about? It is an astonishing matter. And we say: how will the condition of these disbelievers be, how will the condition of these disobedient ones be, on the final Day of Gathering? ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness﴾. The "witness" (shahid) is one who testifies to establish a truth. We know that the Truth informed us: ﴿And there was no nation but that a warner had passed among them﴾ (part of verse 24, surah Fatir).

This warner is a witness over that nation that he conveyed the method (al-manhaj) to them, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is a witness over his community that he conveyed. So His saying: ﴿and bring you as a witness against these people﴾—who are they? Let us look at His saying: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness﴾, and he is their messenger who conveyed the method of God. And how will the situation be when he comes and says: "I conveyed to them the matter, and they have no excuse, for I informed them of it." "And bring you," O Muhammad (ﷺ), "as a witness against these people." So is the meaning of "these people" the witnesses who are the messengers, or against these deniers of you? And will you also be a witness against these people just as you are a witness over your community? Either of the two meanings is valid. Why?

Because God brought His book, the miracle, and in it is what establishes that the messengers conveyed to their nations. So when the Messenger recorded in his book, the miracle and the method-book, that the messengers had conveyed to their nations, he will also testify: "They conveyed to you, by the evidence that our Lord told me in the book of the miracle and in the method." Our Messenger will be a witness against these deniers to whom he was sent, who are the nation of the call. So this meaning is apt, and likewise the other meaning is apt. There is no correct meaning that contradicts another correct meaning in the Book of God, and this is the greatness of the Qur'an. The greatness of the Qur'an lies in its giving many radiances, like the facet of a diamond: the diamond is precious and valuable because it is hard and is used for cutting, and every atom in it has a radiance, whereas other minerals have a single radiance; but every atom of diamond has a radiance. That is why they say it shines and glitters: all its particles give off radiance.

The Almighty, glorified and exalted, makes clear that the condition of these people will be dreadful when the Day of Gathering comes, the Day of Resurrection. And they say: "We have conveyed to you." Or the Almighty has presented this matter concerning the messengers and their nations, and concerning our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and his community, or concerning all nations. We too will be witnesses:

﴿That you may be witnesses over mankind, and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ (part of verse 143, surah al-Baqarah).

This is a distinction for the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), because the community of Muhammad is the only community to which God granted security to carry the method until the Hour is established. No prophets will come after the Messenger of Allah. So He says: ﴿That you may be witnesses over mankind, and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾. Thus, by the explicit text of this verse, we have taken up the continuation of the message.

On the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

{Recite the Qur'an to me." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I recite to you when it was revealed to you?" He said: "Yes, I love to hear it from others." So I recited the surah of al-Nisa' until I came to this verse: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and bring you as a witness against these people?﴾ He said: "That is enough," and behold, his eyes were shedding tears.} (1)

If the witness wept from the weight of the verse, how will the condition of the one witnessed against be? The witness who will testify wept at the verse. Yes, because you know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had his heart filled with mercy for his community. That is why we said: the Messenger of Allah's eagerness for his community led his Lord to offer him the charge of his community, after the Almighty knew the extent of his care (ﷺ) for this community:

﴿Perhaps you will kill yourself with grief that they do not become believers﴾ (surah al-Shu'ara', 3).

The affair of his community (ﷺ) worried him greatly, even though the Truth had made clear to him: "Upon you is only the conveying, and it is not upon you to guide them in fact," and he (ﷺ) knew this. Rather, his eagerness and mercy for his community made him love that they should believe. He (ﷺ) feared for his community a situation in which he would testify against them among those who will testify against them on the Day of Gathering. When the Almighty saw that His Messenger was preoccupied with the matter of his community, He said to him: "If you wish, I will place the matter of your community in your hands."

Observe the Muhammadan greatness, the understanding of God, and the perceptiveness: he said to Him: "No, my Lord. You are more merciful to them than I am." It is as if he (ﷺ) were saying to the Creator: "Shall the matter of them be transferred into my hand, when I am their brother? You are their Lord and my Lord. Could I be more merciful to them than You?" It might have been expected that the Messenger would say: "Yes, give me the charge of my community." But he (ﷺ) said: "O Lord, You are more merciful to them than I am." So how did the Lord respond to him? He, glorified be He, said: "I will not disgrace you concerning them, ever." And He, glorified be He, knows the mercy of the master of mankind (ﷺ) toward his community.

On the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As (may Allah be pleased with them both), that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited the saying of God, mighty and majestic, about Abraham: ﴿My Lord, they have indeed led many people astray. So whoever follows me is of me...﴾, and the saying of Jesus (peace be upon him): ﴿If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾. Then he raised his hands and said: {O Allah, my community, my community," and he wept. Allah, mighty and majestic, said: "O Gabriel, go to Muhammad—and your Lord knows best—and ask him what makes him weep." So Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him and asked him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed him of what he had said, and he knows best. Then God said: "O Gabriel, go to Muhammad and say: Indeed We will please you concerning your community and will not grieve you."} (2)

"So how will it be when We bring": that is, how will the condition of these disobedient deniers be... "when We bring from every nation a witness," who has discharged and conveyed from God His purpose for His creation? "And bring you as a witness against these people"?

(1) Narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim and Ahmad.
(2) Narrated by Muslim.

On surah 4, verse 42, from the commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66):

﴿On that Day, those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were levelled over them, and they will not conceal from Allah any statement.﴾

When you see "yawma'idhin" ("on that day") and notice that it carries tanwin (nunation), know that it is a substitute (ʿiwad) for something omitted, and the omitted matter here is more than one sentence. The meaning becomes: "On the day when We bring forth from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness over these people." And on this day, ﴿those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger﴾, because they will be confronted with a reality they used to deny. They did not believe that the account was serious; they used to think that the Messenger's words were mere speech that would come to an end. So when the Day of Resurrection surprises them, what will their position be?

﴿Those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were levelled over them.﴾ And what is the meaning of "tusawwa bihim al-ard" ("the earth levelled over them")? It is like when you say, "I will level the earth with so-and-so," meaning you will trample him so thoroughly that he is brought down to the level of the ground.

﴿And they will not conceal from Allah any statement.﴾ How, then, can they not conceal any statement from Allah, when He says in another verse:

﴿He will say, "Remain in it in humiliation, and do not speak to Me."﴾ (Surah al-Mu'minun, 23:108)

The Truth (al-Haqq) says this about them because the matter has stages. Sometimes they speak and lie; they lie when they say:

﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.﴾ (6:23, part of the verse)

And they will say of the idols they worshipped:

﴿We worship them only that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position.﴾ (39:3, part of the verse)

So His words, ﴿and they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾, are evidence that speech comes forth involuntarily, and its speaker cannot keep it hidden. Concealment (al-katm) means that you obstruct something which, by its nature, comes out of something else, so you hide it. In the Hereafter, none of them can conceal a statement, because the power of speech will no longer lie only in the organ of speech, as was the case in this world alone. Rather, they will find themselves having presented confessions of their sins, with their tongues and with their limbs, for speech is not only by the tongue. The tongue will testify, the skins will testify, the two hands will testify, indeed all the limbs will testify.

So the matter is not under anyone's control. Why? Because there is what we call "the authority of capability" (wilayat al-iqtidar), meaning that there is one who is capable and there is that over which he has capability. To bring the image closer: when a battalion of the army has a commander over it, and then the battalion undertakes a mission, the general rule in such a mission is that this commander is given the authority of command, and the soldiers must obey him and not disobey military orders. If this commander issues an order that causes a battle to fail, and the soldiers go to the higher commander above him, whom they call the officer superior to the junior officer, then the soldiers have a different account with him. They can say: "It was he who told us, and we carried out his orders."

I say this to bring the meaning closer at the moment of standing before the Truth, glorified and exalted is He. When Allah, glorified is He, created man, He created his limbs responsive to his will, and his will shaped according to his choice. The will of the obedient is to obey a command and avoid a prohibition; the will of the disobedient is the opposite: he does not obey the command nor avoid what is forbidden. One man wanted to drink wine, so his foot walked, his tongue spoke to the man who would hand him the cup, his hand reached out and took the cup, and he drank. And the limbs, when they go in the Hereafter to the One who arranged this affair, will say to Him: "O Lord, he used me for such and such." Why? Because the capability of the will had been withheld:

﴿To whom belongs the dominion this Day? To Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ (40:16, part of the verse)

Neither I nor anyone else will have a will in the Hereafter. Since I have no will, the hand speaks and confesses: "He used me for such and such, and I was, O Lord, subjugated to the capability of his will that You gave him. As soon as he wills, I carry it out. When he wanted me to strike someone, I did not refuse." The tongue confesses to his cursing so-and-so, or his praising another. So all of this is the authority of capability of the will over the capabilities of the limbs. But if you go back to the One who granted capability to the will, you will find that no one has a will of his own. It is as if the limbs, when they do what is not willed by Allah, because they are subject to the one who wills while he is not obedient, become unwilling; therefore they carry out the commands of their owner while unwilling. When his will is loosened and they find the opportunity, they say what happened:

﴿And they will say to their skins, "Why did you testify against us?" They will say, "Allah has made us speak, who made everything speak."﴾ (41:21, part of the verse)

﴿On that Day, those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were levelled over them,﴾ because the disbeliever will say:

﴿"Would that I were dust!"﴾ (78:40, part of the verse)

**Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 4, verse 43:**

﴿O you who believe, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying, nor in a state of janabah (ritual impurity after sexual intercourse), except while passing through, until you have washed. And if you are ill, or on a journey, or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself (al-ghaʾit), or you have touched women, and you find no water, then take clean earth (saʿidan tayyiban) and wipe your faces and hands with it. Indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving.﴾

Here the Truth moves us from commands, from acts of worship and from not associating anything with Allah, and from the warning against spending to be seen by people, and from the fact that He, glory be to Him, does not wrong anyone, and that we will all be gathered before Him on a day when there is no shade but His shade. After that, He wanted to connect us to Himself through the act of worship that makes you declare your loyalty to Allah every day, five times. Glory be to Him, He shows you that you should turn to Him with the totality of your mind, thought and spirit, so that nothing of you is absent.

He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾. Why did He not say: "Do not pray while you are intoxicated"? That is, do not draw near to prayer, do not stand up for it, and avoid it. This contains an indication of abandoning intoxicants. So what is the meaning of "do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated"? The meaning is that they did not approach prayer when they drank wine, so the prohibition of intoxicants had not yet come through legislation. This matter passed through stages, because when religion came to confront a nation that was in a gap between messengers (fatrah min al-rusul), meaning its connection with the messengers had grown distant, it came to matters of belief and spoke about them with a decisive, final word with no gradualism in it. The belief in one God and the non-association of partners with Allah are matters with no stages and no leniency in them. But matters that relate to habit (ilf al-ʿadah) came with commands in stages. So we do not force or compel habit away from what it is accustomed to, but rather we try to proceed gradually in matters subject to habit, as long as there is something that leads to habituation.

Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, out of His mercy toward those for whom He legislates, made stages in matters of habit and routine. So this is one of the stages: ﴿do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾. And prayer (al-salah) is: the known sayings and actions, beginning with takbir and ending with taslim, with their specific conditions. This is prayer in the Islamic technical sense, although prayer in the general linguistic meaning is simply supplication (mutlaq al-duʿa').

"Sukara" is the plural of "sakran", who is one who has drunk what covers his intellect. The root of the matter comes from al-sakr, which is what is used to block a river. When water flows, they place a dam, and this dam stops the flow of the water. Likewise, wine, at the moment one drinks it, stops the flow of thought and intellect. From this meaning, "do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated" implies that prayer takes you five times a day to meet Allah, and intoxication (sakr) and its after-effect (khumar), which is the trace of the intoxicant that remains in the soul, would prevent you from approaching prayer in the close intervals during the day. Thus He made them break their habit with periods that lengthen the distance from intoxication. And since they had become accustomed to abandoning it throughout the day until the night prayer (ʿisha'), one of them would pray ʿisha' then drink and sleep. So he had remained the whole day without drinking. This is one of the stages, and Allah, the Exalted, established in this matter stages that the human soul can accept.

When He first came to speak about wine, He said:

﴿And of the fruits of the date palms and grapes, you take from them intoxicant and good provision﴾ (part of verse 67, surah al-Nahl).

It is noted here that "intoxicant" (sakar) is placed before "good provision" (rizq hasan), so there is in it intoxicant and there is in it provision. It is as if, when they were eating grapes or dates, this was provision, and Allah described the provision as good. But they also used to take grapes and make wine from them, so our Lord placed "intoxicant" first, because they do that with it, but He did not describe it as good. Rather He said: "you take from it intoxicant", while the word "provision" was described as good.

By Allah, when we hear "intoxicant and good provision", do we not understand that being intoxicant means it is not good, since the opposite of good is bad? It is as if He said: "And of the fruits of the date palms and grapes you take from them intoxicant, that is, a bad drink, and good provision." And because of your concern with intoxicant, He placed it first. After that, what happened? When the Truth, glory be to Him, wants to bring a ruling, its preface is like advice (nasihah). Advice is not a legal ruling, and advice is that it is made clear to you while you choose. The Truth says:

﴿They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: In them is great sin and benefits for people, but their sin is greater than their benefit﴾ (part of verse 219, surah al-Baqarah).

He, glory be to Him, only explained the matter, and you are free to choose. So He said: ﴿Say: In them is great sin and benefits for people﴾, but the sin is greater than the benefit. Did He tell us what to do? No, because He wants to make the intellects comfortable so that they weigh the ruling from themselves, and so that a person reaches the ruling by himself. So He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿and their sin is greater than their benefit﴾. Since the sin is greater than the benefit, what are the criteria for alternatives? The criteria for alternatives appear when you compare two alternatives, then you know the lesser of the two evils and the greater of the two goods.

So when the Truth says: ﴿In them is great sin and benefits for people, and their sin is greater than their benefit﴾, this is advice, and since it is advice, the good is for a person to follow it and to entrust Allah with his advice. But there is no ruling here, so there remained people who drank and people who did not drink. Then an incident occurred in which a man came to pray and recited surah al-Kafirun, and because his intellect was blocked, he said: "Say: O disbelievers, I worship what you worship" (qul ya ayyuha al-kafirun aʿbud ma taʿbudun). The matter reached its peak, and here the ruling came: we do not interfere with you whether you are intoxicated or not, but your intoxication must not lead you to disbelieve in prayer. So ﴿do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾. This is a prohibition, a command and an obligation.

﴿Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾. Since we do not approach prayer while we are intoxicated, we will take a period in which we abstain, so there is an habituation to abandoning it. After that, there occurred the story in which they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to give a ruling on the matter of wine. They said to the Prophet: "Make clear to us a complete explanation regarding wine," so the Truth revealed His saying:

﴿Indeed, intoxicants, gambling, idols and divining arrows are an abomination from the work of Satan, so avoid it﴾ (part of verse 90, surah al-Ma'idah).

So His saying: ﴿O you who believe, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾ is one of the stages of gentleness in the prohibition of wine. He prohibited it for a time, and this time is the time in which a person meets his Lord. It is as if He is saying: "Do it far from prayer, but when you come to Me, you must come with the totality of your thought and the totality of your intellect." ﴿Until you know what you are saying﴾. So this gives us a ruling: that one who is intoxicated does not know what he is saying. This is one point. And since he does not know what he is saying, if it is in ordinary matters, let him say what he says. But in worship and in the Qur'an, it is not proper that he reaches this level. When you reach this level, our Lord intervenes and says: ﴿Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying﴾.

Then He brought another ruling: ﴿nor in a state of janabah except while passing through, until you have washed﴾. And what janabah is, is well known: it is the effect resulting from the meeting of a man and a woman. It is said that it is the pleasure in which thought is absent from its Creator, and this is a pleasure they call "the coupling of pleasures" (jimaʿ al-ladhdhat), because it works in the body with that particular tremor that takes the essences of the body. For this reason it was said: "It is the light of your eyes and the marrow of your shin, so increase it or reduce it." That is, I give you this capacity, and you are free. We wash to restore vitality to the human soul, and no one has any business with these matters as long as they are carried out in the light of the Sharia of Allah. Our concern in this is to obey the command of our Lord and to wash from janabah, whether we understand the wisdom behind it or do not understand it.

﴿Nor in a state of janabah except while passing through﴾. If the intended meaning is prayer, then ﴿do not approach prayer﴾ due to intoxication or janabah, and He did not say "do not pray". The place of prayer is the mosque, so His saying ﴿do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying, nor in a state of janabah﴾ means: do not approach prayer. And approaching (al-qurb) is liable to mean going to the mosque. It is as if He is saying: do not go, unless the mosque is the only path to water.

﴿And if you are ill, or on a journey﴾, that is, if you have an excuse that prevents you from water. ﴿Or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself (al-ghaʾit)﴾. Al-ghaʾit is low, slightly descending ground, and they used to relieve their needs there. It became a term for relieving oneself. Each of us refers to it with many expressions. One says: "I want to go to the place of water," and another asks: "Where is the restroom (dawrat al-miyah)?" In this there is gentleness in speaking about an act that the soul finds repulsive. For this reason, in common expressions we say: "I am going to do what people do," meaning I am not unusual in relieving my needs, since everyone does this.

So our Lord, the Exalted, says: ﴿Or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself, or you have touched women, and you find no water, then take clean earth﴾. And from the mercy of Allah toward the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ), and from the kindness of the Truth toward it, is that the legislation came so that a person would be inclined toward it, because it is legislation. So do not say to me, for example: "I perform wudu' so that I clean myself." Rather we say to you: Do you perform wudu' to clean yourself, and when you lack water, you come with dust to put on your face? So do not say to me "cleanliness" or such things. It is the permission to perform prayer with what Allah has prescribed. He said to me: "Perform wudu', and if you do not find water, then perform tayammum." Does He transfer me from water that cleans to wiping my palms with dust and then touching my face with them? Yes, because the matter is a command from Allah, whether you understood its reason or did not. For this reason the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

(I have been given five things that were not given to any prophet before me: I was helped with terror over a distance of one month's journey; the earth was made for me a place of prayer and a means of purification, so whichever man of my nation the time of prayer reaches, let him pray; spoils of war were made lawful for me, which were not lawful for anyone before me; I was given intercession; and every prophet was sent to his own people specifically, while I was sent to all of humanity.)(1)

﴿Then take clean earth﴾, that is, that you be certain that it has no impurity on it. ﴿Then wipe your faces and hands with it﴾. The matter includes "janabah" and includes such and such... and "tayammum". So His saying ﴿wipe your faces and hands﴾ does not mean that tayammum is merely a substitute and replacement for wudu'. In wudu' I rinse my mouth, I rinse my nose, I wash my face, I wash my hands, and I wipe my head and ears, for example, while I am speaking about the pillars and the sunnah. In this verse, the Truth clarifies that since the matter is with clean earth and dust, that is valid whether it is for minor ritual impurity (al-hadath al-asghar) or for janabah. So it is enough for you to wipe the face and hands.

﴿Wipe your faces and hands﴾. Some of them asked: Is it one strike in which we touch the earth, or two strikes? We say: He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿wipe your faces and hands﴾. Some scholars said: one strike, and some said: two strikes, and all of them are facilitation. This lightening is appropriate to the word "pardoning" (ʿafw), so the Truth says: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving﴾. But what happened here that mentions forgiveness? Because He forgave us and covered over for us the hardship of the necessity to search for water, and He made it easy and granted us the concession of tayammum.

(1) Narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim and al-Nasa'i, from Jabir.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 4, verse 44:

﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book? They buy error and wish that you would go astray from the way.﴾

When the Truth, glory be to Him, wishes to affirm a matter of the cosmos in order to pave the way for a matter of the beliefs that guard the order of the cosmos, He addresses His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saying: "Have you not seen" (alam tara). Seeing (ru'ya) is an act of the eye, and the act of the eye is connected with the disclosure of events to which the eye is exposed, and the seen object carries its evidence with it. The heard object's evidence is derived from the truthfulness of its speaker, and the truthfulness of its speaker is a matter of suspicion: is he lying or telling the truth? As for the seen, its evidence is with it. That is why they said: "There is no 'where' with the eye" (laysa ma' al-ayn ayn), meaning that when you have seen a thing, do not ask "where is it?" And "hearsay is not like eyewitnessing" (al-khabar laysa kal-ayan): the report you hear is not like direct observation. Thus direct observation carries its proof with it, and one does not say, "Prove that so-and-so is wearing a white robe, while you can see him."

So when the Truth wishes to affirm a matter, He says: "Have you seen" (ara'yta). Therefore, if you relate to a person the deviation of another person, he may believe you or not believe you; but if he sees the person gambling or drinking wine, and you then say to the one you previously told: "Have you seen the one I told you about?", the seeing is the proof. When the Truth, glory be to Him, addresses His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with "Have you seen", we look at the matter: if it was witnessed by the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was seeing it, then "have you seen" is in its literal sense, as He says to him:

﴿Have you seen the one who forbids (9) a servant when he prays (10)?﴾ (Surah al-Alaq).

He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had seen it, so is "have you seen" in its literal sense or not? And why does He come with the interrogative particle of "have you seen", even though he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had seen one who forbids a person from prayer? And why did He not say: "You have seen the one who forbids a servant when he prays"? No; because the Truth wishes to affirm the report in stages. Sometimes the report is news heard by the ear, sometimes it is a sight seen by the eye, and sometimes He does not say to him, "You have seen," but questions him with "have you seen," so that He awaits his answer. Thus the answer comes from the addressee himself and not from the speaker, and this is the most emphatic kind of clarification and the most emphatic form of verification. So when the Truth, glory be to Him, addresses him with "have you seen", we say: was that a scene witnessed by the Messenger of Allah, who saw it, so that the seeing is in its literal sense? But if the matter was not contemporary with the Messenger of Allah, and then Allah addresses His Messenger, saying:

﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant (1)?﴾ (Surah al-Fil).

We know that the companions of the elephant were in the year of his birth, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, so when He addresses His Messenger the scene was not before him, and "have you not seen" here means "did you not know." Why did He deviate here from "did you know" to His saying "have you not seen"? Because when the Truth, glory be to Him, addresses His Messenger with a matter from Himself, He makes clear to him: if I inform you of something, know that I am more truthful than your eye. When He, glory be to Him, says "have you not seen," this means that you have knowledge from the Truth, glory be to Him, and the report of the Truth is not like the report of creatures, because the report of creatures admits of truth and falsehood, but the report of the Truth means only truth. So the sight of your eye may betray you, because you may be heedless and not see the whole reality, but when the Truth, glory be to Him, informs you, He will inform you of every aspect of the reality. Thus the report of the Truth is more reliable and more emphatic than the sight of the eye. And when He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Have you seen the one who forbids (9) a servant when he prays (10)?﴾ (Surah al-Alaq), this one represented the first; and when He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant (1)?﴾ (Surah al-Fil),

it is as if you see them now; "have you not seen" means as if the scene were before you.

So the means of affirming things are: a report from a created being, which admits of truth and admits of falsehood — this is one; a seeing by a created being, which admits that it has absorbed all of what is seen or has encompassed only part of it — and a report from a Creator who encompasses everything, so the report of the Creator must be the most reliable of reports in their confirmation.

﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book?﴾ This verse came while Jews were contemporary with the Messenger of Allah. He actually saw that they had been given a portion of the Book, because they were People of the Book; yet they buy error and do not speak the truth, so this is a matter of direct observation for the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. And when He sent Muhammad, He made him the seal of the prophets and closed with him the caravan of prophethood, and this means that prophethood had a caravan. In every age a prophet came in proportion to the expansion of life, to the degree of the encounters of beings in life, and to the degree of the diseases and afflictions that appeared in society. But Allah knew from eternity that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would come in a period whose message and method would organize and encompass all the matters of time until the Hour is established. It is a time in which Allah knows that the differences of transport will end and the differences of barriers will end, so that news breaks out in the farthest east and highest point, and you hear it in the farthest west and highest point; news in the west you hear in the east. A disease appears once in America, and a day or two later it appears in any country.

So distances have ended, and transport has made the world like a single piece. In the ancient society, because of the difficulty of communication, diseases were isolated regionally, and each disease in one community might not reach another community; these people had a disease that did not reach the other community. Therefore the Truth used to send a messenger to each community to treat its diseases. But when the world has been joined in this joining, there must be one messenger who gathers all people together, because the matters of diseases will be one. We now see every day wonders: whenever an incident happens there, we find it here.

So the message must be unified. And when the message is unified, no messenger comes afterward to correct it; the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came as the seal. Therefore Allah took the covenant from every messenger to give glad tidings to his people that a seal messenger would come, so that among the people of every religion there would be a reassurance, so that when a messenger comes they recognize the news of his arrival and say: "Our messengers have already told us." That is why the Truth said:

﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: "Whatever I have given you of Book and wisdom, then there will come to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him."﴾ (part of verse 81, Surah Al 'Imran).

Then He said:

﴿He said: "Do you affirm and accept My burden on that condition?" They said: "We affirm." He said: "Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses."﴾ (part of verse 81, Surah Al 'Imran).

So the Messenger of Allah is witnessed by all the messengers; therefore he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, affirmed the religions of all the messengers, and his religion came with the religions of all the messengers, because they are with him on his method with which he was sent. Those who are joined to belief in heaven through the earlier messengers, if the report of the message of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, reaches them, their fanaticism for their religion may make them turn away from it. So the Truth gave them the leaven of faith and made clear to them: a seal messenger will come, so O all peoples, be alert: when the seal messenger comes, you must believe in him. And they had in their books the indications and the announcements. So Allah gave them a portion of the Book. And look at the precision of the Qur'anic expression: "Have you not seen" O Muhammad "those who were given a portion of the Book" — this statement came carrying for them their excuse if they missed something of the Book, because He will say in another verse:

﴿And they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of﴾ (part of verse 13, Surah al-Ma'idah).

And since they forgot, they are excused; but those among them who have sufficient knowledge, "those who were given a portion of the Book," were supposed to have their ears attentive to the voice of the caller to the final truth, and this was known to them before; therefore our Lord says to us: ﴿And they used to seek victory over those who disbelieved﴾ (part of verse 89, Surah al-Baqarah).

They used to say to the idolaters of the Arabs: "We are awaiting the seal prophet whom Allah will send, so that we will precede you in believing in him; and if we precede you in believing in him while you remain in your disbelief, we will kill you with him as the people of 'Ad and Iram were killed." So they were holding fast to belief in heaven. Tell me: if they said this, and they are known to be People of the Book, why did they disbelieve in the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace? The disbelievers of Quraysh did not say, "We are People of the Book"; rather they were in a period between messengers. So it was supposed that when the messenger came, the People of the Book would race to believe in him, because it had previously been announced to them that they would warn the Arabs of him. Allah gave them an elevated station, but out of their baseness they did not benefit from it; so the Truth says:

﴿And those who disbelieve say: "You are not a messenger." Say: "Allah suffices as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book."﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 43).

He made you witnesses to the truth of the call: He is a witness and you are witnesses. This is a great station, but they did not pay attention to that station and boarded the sinking ship of obstinacy: ﴿So when there came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it﴾ (part of verse 89, Surah al-Baqarah).

But we must be alert to the fact that when the Truth, glory be to Him, sends a doctrinal matter into the cosmos and an opponent opposes it, thinking he harms Allah, we say to him: No. You do that out of desire in your soul. But the Truth will make it a means of support for the seal religion, and you will be a dupe in this position. So beware lest you think you are able to confiscate the intentions of Allah, when you have denied Muhammad and our Lord has made you say this word to the polytheists of Quraysh. Look at what this word will do. And so you may know, by your denial, what you have offered to faith: you thought you had clashed with faith. No. You strengthened and supported faith, but through deception! And upon you is a burden.

When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came and announced his call from his Lord, the pagan Arab idolaters said: "This prophet is the one the Jews threatened us with; come, let us race to believe in him before they race us."

So did they serve faith or not? They served faith. So let no sinner think he can extinguish the light of Allah, for Allah perfects His light even if the disbelievers hate it. An example of this is when our Lord changed the qibla, making clear: O Muhammad, I know that you are eager and longing to face the Ka'bah, and I had first directed you toward Bayt al-Maqdis for a purpose. But I will direct you to the Ka'bah, and you must note that when I direct you to the Ka'bah, the foolish ones, "that is the Jews," will say:

﴿What turned them from their qibla which they used to face?﴾ (part of verse 142, Surah al-Baqarah).

They ask: what made them leave the qibla they used to face? If the qibla of Abraham was the Ka'bah, why did he not face it from the beginning? They will say this. And a Qur'an was revealed with it, recited and recorded. And from their deception at the moment the qibla changed, they said that statement too, and did not notice that the Truth had said beforehand:

﴿The foolish among the people will say: "What has turned them from their qibla?"﴾ (part of verse 142, Surah al-Baqarah).

So despite their intelligence, they said this statement, which shows that disbelief is dark and the disbeliever is in darkness, not knowing how to support himself. And Allah made disbelief a means to faith. Had they truly been intelligent and possessed insight, then as soon as the Qur'an said: ﴿The foolish among the people will say: "What has turned them from their qibla which they used to face?"﴾, they would have gathered some of them and said: "The Qur'an says that we will say such and such; come, let us not say it, so that the Qur'an will not be truthful." But they were unable to do that. So the disbeliever is a dupe. They think that by their disbelief they will obliterate faith in God. No; because Allah has made disbelief a means to faith, and the noble hadith says:

("Indeed Allah supports this religion through the corrupt man.")(1)

So the Truth, glory be to Him, makes clear: these were given a portion of the Book, and it was supposed that those given a portion of the Book would be the first to believe. But they did not believe; this is the first rank. And would that they had confined their evil to this, so the matter would stop there and remain hanging on them. But they buy error, not only in their own souls, but they want to lead others astray too, and this is the second stage. For there is one who goes astray in himself, and he is free; but that he should try to lead others astray—

1 Narrated by al-Bukhari.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 4, verse 45:

﴿وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِأَعْدَائِكُمْ ۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِاللَّهِ وَلِيًّا ۖ وَكَفَىٰ بِاللَّهِ نَصِيرًا﴾ [٤:٤٥]

It may be that you have knowledge of your enemies, so it is said: "You know your enemies." But Allah knows the enemies all together, because you may have an enmity between yourself and your own self, or an enmity from your wife, or an enmity from your children, or all of these enmities or some of them. These people, in outward appearance, a human being cannot fully discern their enmity, but Allah knows them and what they conceal. Therefore He says: ﴿And Allah is most knowing of your enemies.﴾

He brought this after His saying: ﴿And they wish that you would go astray from the way﴾, meaning: lest we say, "These are People of the Book," or "They are Muslims like us," and so on. Since Allah is the most knowing of the enemies, He will not deceive us nor cheat us, so we must pay attention to what the Truth says, that they are our enemies. Then He says: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as a Protector (wali)﴾. When He says this, the statement means that you do not want any other protector after that, as people say: "So-and-so has sufficed me" (kafani fulan); that is, you may need this and that, then you say: "But I have known so-and-so, and he has sufficed me from all that, meaning he does not make me need anyone other than him, because I find with him the sufficiency that suffices me in every movement of my life."

﴿And sufficient is Allah as a Protector.﴾ Yes, He is sufficient as a Protector, because other human beings only possess the causes (asbab), while Allah, glorified and exalted, is the One who created the causes, so He possesses what is above the causes. For this reason He reassures us, saying: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out. And will provide for him from where he does not expect﴾ (Surat at-Talaq).

The "wali" (protector) is always the one who is directly close to you, that is, one who is near you. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as a Helper (nasir)﴾. So there is a close one, and there is also a helper. There may be someone close to you who does not help you, but Allah is the Protector (wali) and the Helper (nasir). So since the matter is one of battle: ﴿And Allah is most knowing of your enemies, and sufficient is Allah as a Protector, and sufficient is Allah as a Helper﴾, the Truth was alerting us: beware that you say we seek support from anyone. Do what is within your capacity to do, then leave what is beyond your capacity to Allah. For this reason, the Truth, glorified and exalted, made clear to us: beware that you take your enemies as protectors, and beware that you say: "What shall we do, and we are weak, and we want to be under the protection of someone? And what shall we do about our enemies?" Do not say that, for Allah has informed us: "I will help you with terror, by casting fear into the hearts of your enemies, so that they will be routed without cause while they have strength and dominance. If you have no weapons, I will help you with terror." Since He will help us with terror, this is sufficient; for at the moment He helps me with terror, my enemy will leave his weapon and I will take it. For this reason He said: "Do what is within your capacity," and He did not say: "Prepare against your adversaries what will achieve victory for you," for He, glorified be He, is able to help us with terror:

﴿We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, because they associated with Allah that for which He had not sent down any authority﴾ (part of verse 3:151).

And since He has cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, all their means become for the believers, and the matter is concluded.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 4, verse 46:

The Truth (al-Haqq) spoke in Surat al-Nisa' about the first creation and made clear: "I created you from a single soul, which is Adam, and then I created from it its spouse, and then I spread from the two of them many men and women." The wide dispersal of men and women is so that the caliphate (khilafah) of mankind may endure. But how does this come about? He, glory be to Him, made clear: "I want a strong society, and beware lest the orphan be lost among you." And then, since I want this caliphate to continue, let the orphans take their share. He, glory be to Him, spoke of the inheritance, then spoke of the foolish who are not trusted with their own property, and after that spoke of the manner of marriage.

So this whole process is to build for us a complete system of life, because the caliphate on earth requires the continuation of this caliphate through procreation, and procreation does not achieve its purpose unless it is procreation of the strong; the procreation of the weak is of no benefit. If there is an orphan among you, you must look after him; if there is a foolish person among you who cannot manage his property, then you manage his property for him. Strive to leave the movement of your life to the people who will come after you, until your souls are strong enough to move. He, glory be to Him, made clear the method of inheritance, and commanded that you marry, but marriage has its conditions, which He has made clear. Then He gave us the general method: ﴿And worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and be good to parents﴾, and He explained all these rulings.

After that, what is the wisdom in His, glory be to Him, returning us a second time to the Jews? The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, completes the rulings. Delivering rulings is one thing, and bringing the soul to conform to God's will in the rulings is another. So He makes clear to us that there are people who will know the ruling but cannot bring themselves to abide by it, and they know it just as you do; they have only bought misguidance. So this is an explanation for us; it is a tangible reality, and He does not come to us with informative or prescriptive speech only, as you might say: "It happens or it does not happen." Rather He brings us events from the reality of the universe, and warns us: beware lest you be like them. So He said: ﴿Among those who are Jews are those who distort words from their places﴾. Tahrif (distortion) is that you use a word that bears two meanings, a good meaning and a bad meaning, but you intend from it the bad. Like one who says: "As-sam 'alaykum wal-'iyadhu billah" (may death be upon you, and God forbid), which on its surface seems to say "as-salamu 'alaykum" (peace be upon you), but he says "as-sam", meaning "death". So the word has within it what gives the appearance of good, but the enemy bends it toward evil.

Like this is what they said to the Prophet: "Ra'ina" (qala ra'ina), which comes from ri'ayah (attention, consideration), but they were taking it from ra'una (foolishness). So the command comes: leave the word that bears two meanings, and cut off the road to the word that admits two directions, because the speaker may intend by it good and may intend by it evil. So the meaning of distorting speech is that the speech admits of this and admits of that. The example of this: a man went to a tailor to have a qaba' (a garment worn over clothes and fastened with a belt; perhaps what is called a caftan) sewn for him, and the tailor was "karim al-'ayn", that is, he had one eye. The man was not pleased with the sewing of the qaba', so he said: "By God, since I will be disgraced before people by this garment that he sewed for me, I must say a poem about it that will expose him among people." So he said:

"Amr sewed me a qaba', would that his two eyes were equal."

So his saying "would that his two eyes were equal" reveals what? Does he, then, wish that his sick eye were like the healthy one? Or does he wish that the healthy eye were like the sick one? So the speech admits of good and of evil. Similarly they have related to us that one of the governors asked the preacher to revile Sayyiduna 'Ali, may God honour his face and his household, and to curse them from the pulpit.

The preacher said: "Excuse me."

The governor said: "No, I bind you by oath to do it."

The preacher said to him: "If you bind me by oath to do it, I will ascend the pulpit and say: 'So-and-so ordered me to revile 'Ali,' then say after me: 'May God curse him.'"

He said to him: "Say nothing." The governor had understood the preacher's intent and his ability to use speech with two meanings.

And the Truth says: ﴿Among those who are Jews are those who distort words from their places﴾. I want you to pay attention to the fact that the Qur'anic style, in some places, uses the same words but shifts from one expression to another, so it appears to superficial observers that the matter is repetition, but it is not so. For example, He says once: ﴿They buy error in exchange for guidance﴾, and once He does not mention guidance as the price of error, saying: ﴿They buy error﴾, and they did not notice that the guidance of the innate nature (fitrah) is obliterated in them here. Another example is the saying of the Truth:

﴿They distort words from after their places﴾ (Qur'an 5:41).

And in the verse we are presently reflecting upon, He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿They distort words from their places﴾. So the matter has a root among them: the speech sent down from God was first placed in its true position, then they removed it, changed it, and put in its place other speech, like their distortion of stoning by putting the prescribed punishment in its place.

As for His saying ﴿from after its places﴾, it indicates that they lifted the sacred speech from its rightful place and placed it in a place of falsehood, through interpretation and distortion according to their whims, as their desires required. It is as though it had places, and it was worthy of them. When they distorted it, they left it like the estranged stranger with no place of its own. So at one time they replace God's speech with speech of their own, and at another they distort God's speech by interpreting it according to their whims.

﴿And they say: "We hear and we disobey."﴾ They say an audible statement, "We hear," and then they say within themselves, "We disobey." So their saying "We hear and we disobey" has in their intention "we disobey," so their saying "we hear" means only hearing with the ear. As for "we disobey," it means disobedience to the obligation; they said aloud "we hear" and said "we disobey" secretly, or they said "we hear" while concealing disobedience. ﴿And "Hear, without being made to hear"﴾: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the one who makes you hear, as proven by your saying "we hear." So what do you intend by your saying "hear"? Do you ask that he listen to you because he says speech that does not please you and you will reply to him? Or do you wish to use a word that admits other meanings, and turn it into unbefitting meanings, like your saying "without being made to hear," meaning what would not please you, or "without being made to hear," meaning "may you not hear"? For they wish him, God forbid, deafness. It may also be abuse from the expression "asma'a fulan fulanan," when one reviles and insults another. So the speech admits of multiple readings.

﴿And "Hear, without being made to hear," and "Ra'ina," twisting their tongues﴾. They did not say "ra'ina" from ri'ayah (care) but from ru'unah (foolishness). So He said: No. Leave this word, for they would take from it a word by which they intend to harm the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And "layy" is the twisting of a thing; and twisting is turning the two strands of a rope you are twisting away from straightness, and this twisting gives it strength. And they perform these operations, why? Because they understand that these give them strength.

﴿Twisting their tongues and slandering the religion﴾. Since they twist speech away from straightness, they intend evil, because the religion came as straightness. So whenever someone twists it, what does he want? ... He wants "slander against the religion." "And if only they had said: We hear," and instead of concealing disobedience they say: ﴿And we obey, and hear, and look at us﴾ instead of "ra'ina," and "unzurna" (look at us) admits no bad meaning.

So the meaning of this is that God, glory be to Him and exalted, wishes to inform the beloved ones of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that his opponents bring words that admit of disparaging the Messenger of God; therefore He makes clear: beware of saying the words they say, for they intend in them the aspect of evil, and you must keep far from words that can turn into evil. So if they had said "we hear and we obey, and hear, and look at us," it would have been better for them and more upright. But when you hear the word "but" (lakin), know that the matter came contrary to what the Legislator intends, because He says: ﴿But if they had said﴾, yet they did not say, so the matter came contrary to the Legislator's intent.

﴿But Allah cursed them for their disbelief﴾. "Curse" (la'n) is expulsion and removal. Does God then wrong them in cursing and expelling them? No. He cursed them only because of their disbelief. So let no one say: why did God curse and expel them, and what was their sin? We say: No. He, glory be to Him, cursed them because of their disbelief; so what came first was their disbelief, and the curse and expulsion came as a consequence of disbelief.

﴿But Allah cursed them for their disbelief, so they do not believe except a few.﴾ When you hear a negation of an act, "they do not believe," followed by an exception with "except," it affirms part of the act. You say, for example: "He does not eat except a little": the phrase "does not eat" negates eating, and "except a little" affirms some eating. So He, glory be to Him, says: "so they do not believe except a few." Belief is an act that requires an agent of the act, who is the one who believes. So I have an act and the doer of the act. When you hear an exception, you say: this exception is suitable to apply to the act, and suitable to apply to the doer of the act. The phrase "so they do not believe except a few" means: they do not believe except with a little belief, because they believe a little in prayer and in not working on Saturday, while the rest of the requirements of belief are not in their minds and they do not fulfil them. Or, "they do not believe except a few" may mean that some of them are the ones who believe, and this is correct when we say it, because some of them did in fact believe; and we also find that they believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part, so their belief is in the act itself.

And there were some of them who, after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, and the Qur'an was recited, and they saw his form and found him exactly as described among them, so they believed. But did all the Jews believe, or did a few of them believe? A few of them believed, such as 'Abdullah ibn Salam and Ka'b al-Ahbar. As for 'Abdullah ibn Suriya, Ka'b ibn Asad, Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, and others among the Jews, they did not believe.
