So if you mean that some, "a few of them," are the ones who believed, this is true; and it is also valid that the disbelievers among them believed in part of the Book and disbelieved in part. In this there is an expression from the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, which we call "preservation of possibility" (siyanat al-ihtimal), because when the Qur'an descends with such a statement, it is possible, and this is what happened, that there were people among the Jews thinking of declaring belief in the Messenger of God. If He had said "so they do not believe" only, it would have been difficult for them to declare belief; but when He says "except a few," whoever has an idea of belief knows that the One who gives this report is aware of the secrets of souls, and by possibility He preserved the declaration of belief by this small group.

1 The qaba': a garment worn over clothes and fastened with a belt; perhaps what is called a caftan.

We know that all the legislation that came down from heaven contains no contradiction, because the Legislator is one. No one will legislate a law today and then have another messenger come with a different new law. The fundamental principles of all the religions brought by the line of messengers are one. They differ only in some rulings required by the circumstances of different eras. Within a single legislation, rulings develop, especially those related to customs. Allah, glorified and exalted, is Merciful to His servants, and He would not come to a matter in which people have become accustomed to a custom, which has taken hold of them and begun to lead them to keep doing it, and then come to end it with a single word. The decisive word has come only concerning belief ('aqidah). But for matters that require habituation, the Truth (al-Haqq) is gentle in bringing them out smoothly, meaning that He makes them into stages so that a gap of transition does not arise.

We can liken the gap of transition to this: there is a person who smokes cigarettes, whose rate of smoking reaches a hundred cigarettes a day. If we say to him, "Make it fifty," then thirty, and so on, we have thereby distributed his habit over some time. Instead of the interval between one cigarette and the next being ten minutes or half an hour, we make it an hour, and so we have broken part of the habituation. Likewise, the social matters that arise from the monotony of habit are handled in stages.

Indeed, the Truth, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿O People of the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you.﴾ The Truth makes clear: We have not brought a new thing, but all of it is from what you already have. Someone may say: since it is from what they have, what is the purpose of it? We say: because there is something new in the judicial matters of the age that did not exist among them, and what has been added is the treatment of those new judicial matters. But the root of faith is present in the Qur'an, the inimitable miracle that descends from heaven: in the miracle, in monotheism, and in the matters of belief. None of these contains any disagreement.

﴿O you who were given the Scripture, believe﴾. The phrase "who were given the Scripture" is a binding of proof upon them, and it means: we are not speaking to you with words you do not know. For it says "confirming what is with you," meaning that they know well what they have. So it was incumbent upon them to compare and weigh what new thing had come to them through the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) against what they had. If they find it confirming what they have, then the matter is settled.

Then consider the threat: ﴿before We efface faces and turn them back upon their backs, or curse them as We cursed the people of the Sabbath; and the command of Allah is ever accomplished.﴾ He, glorified, calls out to them: hasten, just as we might say, "Save yourself and believe!" And the Truth says: ﴿before We efface faces and turn them back upon their backs.﴾ Tams (effacement) is erasure. The thing that is effaced is what has been wiped out after having been a distinct thing. The word "wujuh" (faces) occurs in the Qur'an with several meanings. It is used once for the body, meaning that which faces, the "face," as in His saying: ﴿On the day when some faces will turn white﴾ (Qur'an 3:106).

And we use the word once for intention, aim and direction, as the Exalted said: ﴿Yes, whoever submits his face to Allah﴾ (Qur'an 2:112).

"Aslama wajhahu" (submitted his face) means his aim, his direction and his intention.

So sometimes "face" is used for the face by which one faces, and sometimes it is used for intention. What is the connection between aim, intention and face? Because when a person intends something, he turns toward it with his face and sets out for it. So "face" is applied to the organ "face," and it is also applied to aim and intention. Since it is used in two senses, it is applied to the face known among us, and it is applied to the intention and direction that turns us, and both usages are valid.

His saying "We efface faces" is because He, glorified, has made clear: We have honored you and made for you marks that distinguish you in their form: eyebrows, two eyes, a fine nose, and a mouth, such that if you wanted to create this form you would not be able to. And He, glorified, announces: I am able to efface these faces that distinguish you, so that I turn them back upon their backs, and the face becomes like the nape, and becomes like a piece of flesh. This is if by His saying "faces" we mean the face that is in the body.

And if by "face" we mean "intention," we say: those who buy error, and those who want you to go astray from the way, and those who distort words from their places, and those who say "Ra'ina," and those who say "Isma' ghayra musma'" (Qur'an 4:46). Do they not have a direction? What is their direction in this situation, and what is their aim?

Their aim is to turn themselves away and to turn people away from following Muhammad. So it is as if He says to them: hasten and believe before We efface and erase your aim, so that it does not reach its goal, which is turning you away from faith in the Messenger of Allah. Save yourselves before that happens, lest We curse you and drive you away from Our mercy. For this reason we find that our master 'Abdullah ibn Salam, when he heard the verse, went to the Messenger of Allah with his hand upon his face and said: "By Allah, before I embraced Islam I feared that my face would be effaced."

This is evidence that he believed that the one who said these words was able to save. And in the time of our master 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, we find Ka'b al-Ahbar going to him. The verse had not reached him, but when it reached him, he went to our master 'Umar with his hand upon his face, fearing that his face would be effaced before he declared his Islam. That is evidence of his certainty that the one who said these words was able to carry them out.

Someone may say: but among them were people who did not believe, and this effacement did not happen to them. We say: did He say, "We will efface only faces"? No, He also said: ﴿or curse them as We cursed the people of the Sabbath.﴾ It is enough that there were people who believed that effacement might come, and they were from the notables of the People of the Book and from their rabbis (ahbar, scholars). Those of them who believed in the Messenger of Allah were aware of the scheming of the Jews. Our master 'Abdullah ibn Salam, before he embraced Islam, said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "I love to embrace Islam, but I fear that if I embrace it the Jews will say evil about me. So before I embrace Islam, ask them about me." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked the rabbis of the Jews: "What do you say about 'Abdullah ibn Salam?" They said: "Our master, the son of our master, our scholar and our rabbi," and they praised him. When Ibn Salam heard this from them, he said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." They said: "He is the son of such-and-such, and the son of such-and-such," and they reviled him. Ibn Salam said: "O Messenger of Allah, did I not tell you that they are a people of slander (bahtun)?"[1]

It is narrated that when 'Abdullah ibn Salam heard of the arrival of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he came to him and looked at his noble face, and knew that it was not the face of a liar. He considered him and was certain that he was the awaited prophet. He said to him: "I will ask you about three things that none knows but a prophet: What is the first of the portents of the Hour? What is the first food the people of Paradise will eat? And does the child resemble its father or its mother?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "As for the first portent of the Hour, it is a fire that will gather them from the east to the west. As for the first food of the people of Paradise, it is the extra piece of the liver of the fish. As for the child, if the man's water precedes, the child resembles him, and if the woman's water precedes, the child resembles her." He said: "I bear witness that you are truly the Messenger of Allah." Then he stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the Jews are a people of slander. If they learn of my Islam before you ask them about me, they will slander me before you." So the Jews came, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to them: "What kind of man is 'Abdullah among you?" They said: "The best of us, the son of the best of us, our master, the son of our master, our most knowledgeable and the son of our most knowledgeable." He said: "What do you think if 'Abdullah embraces Islam?" They said: "May Allah protect him from that." Then 'Abdullah came out to them and said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." They said: "He is the worst of us and the son of the worst of us," and they belittled him. He said: "This is what I was afraid of, O Messenger of Allah." Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I did not hear the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say to anyone walking on the earth that he is among the people of Paradise, except for 'Abdullah ibn Salam." And concerning him was revealed: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if it is from Allah and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to its like?﴾ (Qur'an 46:10).[2]

﴿And before We efface faces and turn them back upon their backs.﴾ If we take the effacement of the face literally, that is the matter 'Abdullah ibn Salam and Ka'b al-Ahbar feared: one went to the Messenger of Allah and the other went to 'Umar, and each of them was holding his face out of fear that it would be effaced. So His saying "We efface faces," that is, We make them like the "nape," a mere piece of flesh without distinction, or We prevent them from reaching their aim, that is, We do not enable them to reach what they wish of turning people away from faith in the Messenger of Allah. ﴿Before We efface faces and turn them back upon their backs, or curse them﴾, or drive them away from Our mercy and from the arena of faith. Then the Truth says:

﴿Allah has sealed their hearts﴾ (Qur'an 2:7).

Since they have disbelieved, we say to each of them: did you not want to disbelieve? Allah will increase the seal upon your heart, and We will also help you in this story. He, exalted, said:

﴿In their hearts is a disease, so Allah increased them in disease﴾ (Qur'an 2:10).

So if you want this, We will give you what is in your soul: ﴿then We turn them back upon their backs, or curse them as We cursed the people of the Sabbath.﴾ He, glorified, addresses the Jews, who know the story of the Sabbath and know that it was an event that occurred, and Allah drove them away, destroyed them, cursed them, and prepared for them a mighty punishment. So He does not bring a threat without a basis. No, this threat is preceded by a basis. You, O assembly of Jews, believe in it, remember it, and it has a history among you: ﴿as We cursed the people of the Sabbath.﴾ The story of the people of the Sabbath is well known, though it will come in another surah. "Sabt" (Sabbath) means rest and tranquility, and from it comes "sabat," meaning sleep. So "sabata, yasbutu" means he became still, settled and rested.

﴿Or curse them as We cursed the people of the Sabbath.﴾ Concerning cursing (la'n), they said it means expulsion and humiliation, and they said its meaning is destruction. Those who try to cast doubt on the meanings of the verses of the Qur'an say: you do not stop at one meaning of the word; either it means this, or it means that. We say to them: you do not have a mastery of the language, and even if you learn the language, your learning of it is learning a craft, not learning a faculty (malakah). Learning a craft gives you the rule, but it does not give you the ability to place a word in its true meaning or to clarify what is meant by it. And if the meaning of cursing is expulsion, then you must understand that expulsion requires one who expels, and requires one who is expelled, and requires that from which one is expelled.

And who is it that expels?

And who is it that expels?

And from what is one expelled?

When you take the meaning in this way, you find no difficulty in the meanings of expulsion being many. Suppose you are sitting to eat and your dog, which you value for guarding, comes to circle around your table. What do you do with it? You drive it away from the table; that is expulsion. Or suppose your son, for instance, has done something while you have guests, and you want to remove him from the gathering and say to him: "Go to your mother." That is expulsion.

If the son's offense is great and you have authority, you may expel him from the house so that he does not sit in it, and this is expulsion. If the son's offense is unbearable, you expel him from the village, and this is expulsion. So if a person has committed a great sin and you are a person of far-reaching power, you expel him from life entirely, and you have then removed him from all of life. So all of these are expulsion. If we mean disgrace and humiliation, cursing applies; if we mean destruction, many of them were destroyed in battles, and they suffered disgrace and humiliation, because we took their women and daughters captive, subdued them, destroyed them, and drove them out of their homes to the land of Syria and to Adhri'at, and Allah destroyed them by death. So all the meanings of expulsion apply. The verse touches all that happened to them, but it differs according to the one who expels, the one who is expelled, and that from which he is expelled.

And when the Truth says: ﴿as We cursed the people of the Sabbath﴾, this indicates that cursing has different forms. I will take from them the cursing of the people of the Sabbath. The Sabbath is one day of the week, a unit of time within the week. And we notice that the other seven days of the week contain indications of number: Sunday (al-Ahad) means one, Monday (al-Ithnayn) means two, and so on with Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, so there are five days with their numbers...

[1] Narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim and al-Nasa'i.
[2] "Qalu bahata fulanun fulanan" means he slandered him with falsehood and fabricated lies against him. The active participle is bahit, and the plural is bahit, like rasul and rusul.
Narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim and al-Nasa'i.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 4, verse 48:

After this, the Truth, glory be to Him, moves on to a fundamental doctrinal matter concerning the relationship of man with the Truth, glory be to Him, and exalted is He. He says:

﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with; but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates with Allah has certainly committed a great sin.﴾ (4:48)

This is among the most hopeful verses in the Book of Allah. Therefore, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: "What are the requirements of faith?" – that is, what is it that grants us faith? – he (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says, 'There is no god but Allah,' enters Paradise."

And on the authority of ʿUthmān (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever dies knowing that there is no god but Allah enters Paradise." (1)

We say that whoever associates others with Allah commits the greatest doctrinal treachery (khiyanah ʿuzma, "high treason"). We have taken this term from man-made laws, although man-made laws do not aim to affirm religious matters; yet their heedlessness makes us pick up from them that they also affirm religious matters. Suppose a group carried out a movement, and then one of them exploited the movement for a private benefit, and another exploited the movement so that it would be for him and not for the other, that is, to overturn him. The first, who stands upon the system, calls it high treason; as for one who does not resist with the aim of deposing the ruler but wrongs people, the ruler may punish him for what he did, but not for high treason. Thus in human law too there is high treason, and there is a deviation which does not touch sovereignty; but any movement that touches sovereignty involves the severing of necks, and every other matter is dealt with by a degree of punishment proportionate to its sin.

So the Truth, glory be to Him, makes clear: the root of the matter of faith is that Allah, glory be to Him, wants you to acknowledge that He is the One God who has no partner. When you acknowledge that He is the One God who has no partner, you enter the fortress of security. Therefore the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) says in the noble hadith: (I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah; no servant meets Allah with these two, without doubting them, except that he enters Paradise.) (2)

When Abū Dharr spoke with the Prophet in a dialogue about this verse, he said to him: "No servant says, 'There is no god but Allah,' and then dies upon that, except that he enters Paradise." I said: "Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals?" He said: "Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals." I said: "Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals?" He said: "Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals" (three times). Then he said in the fourth: "In spite of the nose of Abū Dharr!" (3)

Abū Dharr was zealous for the limits of Allah. Did the Messenger's saying, "In spite of the nose of Abū Dharr," grieve Abū Dharr? No, it did not grieve him. That is why, whenever he related it and said it, "Whoever says there is no god but Allah enters Paradise, even if it is in spite of the nose of Abū Dharr," he was joyful. Why? Because it opened the door of the mercy of the Truth. For if this were not so, what would be the difference between one who believes it and says it and one who does not say it? There must be a distinction for it. Every crime that exists in Islam, which the Truth, glory be to Him, has forbidden, means that it may occur. For example... the Blessed and Exalted One says:

﴿And the thief, male or female, cut off their hands﴾ (5:38)

This means that it is permissible for a believer to steal, and likewise he may commit adultery in some moment of heedlessness. And among the foundations of seeking forgiveness comes clear explanation: from one prayer to the next prayer is an expiation for what is between them; Friday to Friday is an expiation; Hajj is an expiation; fasting is an expiation.

On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The five prayers and from Friday to Friday are expiation for what is between them, so long as major sins are not committed." (4)

That is, our Lord has placed many gates to forgiveness and mercy, and He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with﴾. This matter is not for His benefit but for your benefit, so that the gods of men do not multiply among men, and a person is not exhausted and wretched from submitting to everyone who is powerful over him. Allah has relieved you of this and made clear to you: No, submit to One alone, and that suffices you from all submission to others; work for one face, and that suffices you from all faces. In that is rest for the believer.

Faith, then, teaches us dignity and honor. Instead of bowing to every creature, prostrate to the One who created the whole universe with the attributes of His power and perfection. No attribute has come into being for Him that was not there before. Have you added an attribute to Him? No. He created you with attributes of perfection, and with attributes of perfection He has been the Sustainer over you. You have added nothing to Him. So when you bear witness that there is no god but Allah, what is its benefit to Allah? Its benefit goes only to the servant.

That is why we have said: the Truth, glory be to Him, wants His servants to gather once every week. For you may pray obligatory prayer after obligatory prayer in your factory or your farm or any place, but on Friday you must gather with others. Why? Because it is possible that you humble yourself to Allah between you and Him, submitting, prostrating and weeping between you and Allah, but He wants this to be displayed before people, so that you see everyone who has lordship and rank prostrating and humbling himself with you before Allah. At the Hajj too, you see everyone who has rank and leadership performing the rites like you, so you say to yourself, or say to him: "We are equal in servitude; no one is elevated above another, and no one abases himself before another, but we are all servants of Allah and submit to Him alone."

So the matter is for the benefit of the servant. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with﴾, because if He forgave association, partners would multiply on earth, and when partners multiply on earth, each one would have a god, and once each one has a god, the matter is corrupted. But submission to one God, whose commands we all obey, honors us all. There is no lordship for anyone, and no servitude of anyone to anyone else. So His saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with﴾ is for our benefit.

Ibn Jurayj narrated from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Waḥshī, the slayer of our master Ḥamzah at the Battle of Uḥud, came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Muḥammad, I have come to you seeking protection; grant me protection until I hear the speech of Allah." The Messenger of Allah said: "I had wished to see you under other than protection; but since you have come to me seeking protection, you are under my protection until you hear the speech of Allah." He said: "Indeed I associated others with Allah, I killed the soul which Allah has forbidden, and I committed adultery. Will Allah accept my repentance?" The Messenger of Allah remained silent until there was revealed:

﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit adultery—and whoever does that will meet a penalty; the punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein humiliated. Except one who repents and believes and does righteous work; for those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (25:68–70).

He recited it to him, and he said: "I see a condition; perhaps I will not do righteous work. I am under your protection until I hear the speech of Allah." Then there was revealed:

﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with; but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates with Allah has certainly committed a great sin﴾ (4:48).

He was summoned and it was recited to him. He said: "Perhaps I am among those whom He does not will. I am under your protection until I hear the speech of Allah." Then there was revealed:

﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful"﴾ (39:53).

He said: "Yes. Now I see no condition," and he embraced Islam.

So the whole matter is a gentleness from the Creator toward His creation, and regarding acts of heedlessness as incidental occurrences upon mankind. And since the Truth legislates legislation, it is permissible that it occurs. But if a sin occurs from someone and then he seeks forgiveness for it, beware of bringing up his past conduct with him again and reminding him of it. Suppose someone bore false witness, suppose someone committed a sin, then sought forgiveness from Allah for it and repented. Beware of saying to him, "O false witness!" For he has sought forgiveness from the One who owns forgiveness, so do not make him a sinner in your eyes, for the matter has ended with the One who owns it.

Why? So that people are not humiliated for a sin committed. Rather, the opposite: those who have committed sins and transgressed against themselves are, in the eyes of some people, lowly and despised. That is why we say: whenever one of them is stung by repentance and regrets what he did, a good deed is recorded for him. Despite having tasted sin, he nonetheless repented of it, and this is the reason Allah replaces their evil deeds with good deeds. When we know that our Lord replaces their evil deeds with good, it is not for us to despise those who have transgressed against themselves. Rather, we should rejoice that they have repented, and not give their slip and sin a retroactive effect.

﴿And whoever associates with Allah has certainly committed a great sin﴾. "Iftirāʾ" (fabrication, slander) is deliberate lying. For there is one who tells you a matter according to his belief, and this matter is false; he says to you: "So-and-so visited so-and-so yesterday." He said that according to his belief, that they told him, or he saw a trace of the visit, although such a visit did not happen; so it is merely a lie. As for association (shirk), it is the deliberate lying against Allah, and this is described as ﴿has certainly committed a great sin﴾, because it contradicts the innate unity of the fitrah (natural disposition). As if the innate unity of the fitrah says: Do not say except what you know indeed and are certain of; rather, you must not deliberately oppose your fitrah and make a partner for Allah.

When the Truth, glory be to Him, says: "There is no god but Allah, alone, with no partner," either this word is true, and the matter ends there; or it is not true, and Allah forbid, meaning there is someone else with Him. This other has heard that there is someone who says: "There is no god but I." Did he remain silent or did he not hear? If he did not hear, then he is a heedless god; and if he heard, why did he not oppose and say: "No, there is no god but I," and bring a miracle greater than the other's miracle? Nothing of that happened. So this one does not suffice and that one does not suffice. Thus "There is no god but Allah," when Allah utters it and the Messenger of Allah brings it, and Allah says: "I am alone in the universe, with no partner to Me," and no one disputes Him in that, the matter is true for Allah by self-evidence, without any argument.

﴿And whoever associates with Allah has certainly committed a great sin﴾. Fabrication occurs in deed and in speech, and it also occurs in belief. "A great sin" means that there is a sin that is not great. "The great sin" is that which violates one doctrinal matter that encompasses all existence: that there is no god but Allah.

Then the Exalted Lord says, turning back to these Jews:

﴿Have you not seen those who claim purity for themselves? Rather, Allah purifies whom He wills, and they will not be wronged the slightest bit (fatil).﴾ [4:49]

It has already been noted, when we pointed to the Almighty's words "Have you not seen" (alam tara), that if the scene the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is addressed about was visible before him, then the seeing is literal. If it was not visible before him, and the Almighty intended to inform him of it while it was not contemporary with his seeing, then "Have you not seen" means "Have you not known." Knowledge regarding the report of Allah must be more truthful than what the eye sees, because the eye may deceive and the sight may mislead. ﴿Have you not seen those who claim purity for themselves?⟩ "Tazkiyah" (purification, self-praise) is, first, cleansing from defects, which means removing deficiency, and after that, affirming additional perfections in which there is growth. The self-purification by which they claimed purity was that they said:

﴿We are the sons of Allah and His beloved.﴾ [5:18]

The response to them on this matter came in the Almighty's words:

﴿Say: Why then does He punish you for your sins? Rather, you are human beings from among those He created.﴾ [5:18]

That is: if you are His beloved and His sons, why does He punish you? Then this claim is false. Moreover, what benefit is there in your saying it to us? Can we own anything for you? If you lie about it to Him who owns everything for you, which is Allah the Exalted, then what about us and you? The purification they practiced was that they praised themselves falsely, declared themselves free of faults, and claimed to be the sons of Allah, while they were not His sons and not His beloved. They also said:

﴿None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians.﴾ [2:111]

That too is a false claim. Here we ask: if a person purifies himself rightly, is that purification accepted? We say: we must ask what is intended by it. If what is intended is boasting, it is false. But self-purification is obligatory in a matter that necessitates it. Example: when a group boards a boat, and the captain, or the one rowing or holding the sail, is of average ability, and then a storm arises that the average-ability man cannot handle, then a person who understands steering boats during storms comes forward and tells the average man: step away from the helm, for I have more understanding, competence and ability than you in this matter, and he pushes him aside and takes the helm in his place. This is self-purification, and it is required, because the time is not a time for experiment; and he purifies himself rightly. So there is a difference between purification by falsehood and purification by truth.

We know the story of our master Joseph, and we know the story of the king's dream, in which he saw seven fat cows eaten by seven lean ones! And the opposite was expected. Look at the insight: the years of drought will consume the years of plenty. But who notices the symbols of a dream? Interpreting dreams is not a science; it is a gift from Allah that He grants to people and makes them experts in decoding the code of dreams. The evidence is that the king related this dream to the people, and they said to him: "Confused dreams" (adghath ahlam). "Adghath" is the plural of "dghth," which is mixed and tangled grass, but they were fair, and said:

﴿We are not knowers of the interpretation of dreams.﴾ [12:44]

They were fair in what they said, because the one who tells you "I do not know" has given a fatwa. As long as he says "I do not know," he will compel you to ask someone else; but if he gives you any answer, you will be satisfied with it and become entangled. So whoever says "I do not know" has answered. When they said "confused dreams," they evaded and took precaution for themselves, and said: ﴿We are not knowers of the interpretation of dreams.⟩ The Almighty had prepared the ground for Joseph while he was in prison, when the two young men entered upon him:

﴿Two young men entered the prison with him. One of them said: I see myself pressing wine. The other said: I see myself carrying bread on my head, of which birds eat. Tell us its interpretation.﴾ [12:36]

What made the two young men know that this imprisoned Joseph knew the interpretation of dreams? They said, explaining the reason:

﴿We see you as one of the good-doers.﴾ [12:36]

That means they witnessed his bearing and conduct, and knew he was a peaceable man. When a matter that concerned their own persons troubled them and pressed upon them, they said: there is no better person than this man to ask. I have said and I still repeat: values are values, the truthful is respected even by the liar, and the one who does not drink wine is respected by the drinker. This is proven by the fact that when a matter troubled them, they said: ﴿We see you as one of the good-doers.⟩

Does anyone judge another to be good unless he has a standard by which he knows goodness and distinguishes it from evil? When they said that to our master Joseph, he could have answered them with the interpretation of their dreams, but this was not his mission. Instead, he considered: why not take advantage of their need for him in a matter concerning their own persons, and then reach his own aim from them before they reach their aim from him? He was a prophet from a lineage of prophets, so he made clear to them: "And what have you seen of my goodness? I have many things":

﴿He said: No food will come to you as your provision except that I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you.﴾ [12:37]

So he purified himself. But look at why he purified himself: he wanted to take them by the hand to his Lord, as is shown by his saying:

﴿That is of what my Lord has taught me.﴾ [12:37]

So self-purification is required here, and he attributed it to Allah, and declared that this is not a privilege for himself alone, but that every one of Allah's creatures can be like him:

﴿Indeed, I have abandoned the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah.﴾ [12:37]

Then he said:

﴿And I follow the religion of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.﴾ [12:38]

So you too can be like me if you follow this path. Then he said to them:

﴿Are scattered lords better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer?﴾ [12:39]

That is: which is better, one God or many gods? You, companions of many gods, came to the companion of the one God, though plurality apparently gives strength; yet this plurality gave you weakness, because you, companions of many gods, came to the companion of the one God:

(Are scattered lords better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer.) [12:39]

So he purified himself before them in order to bring them to the side of the One who is purified, the Almighty and Exalted. Then when the king learned of it, he said: "Bring him to me, I will take him for myself," and he would be close to me. Afterward came the years of drought which he had first foretold in interpreting the dream, and he advised them to store from the years of plenty for the years of drought. The experiment was the report of things that would happen; when they came to pass, he knew the matter was not experiment but something precise. So he said to the king:

﴿Set me over the treasuries of the land.﴾ [12:55]

Thus he purified himself and gave his justification:

﴿Indeed, I am a guardian, knowing.﴾ [12:55]

Because this matter requires preservation and knowledge; it is not subject to trial, where one tries and fails, and another tries and fails. No, it requires preservation and knowledge. An example of this too: when the Prophet ﷺ was dividing the spoils, the hypocrites said to him, "Be just, O Muhammad!" He said to them: "By Allah, I am trustworthy in heaven and trustworthy on earth." So he purified himself. When, then, is self-purification required? First: that it be in truth, and that it have a purpose in the eyes of the one who knows the purification, and to whom you give the purification and praise you for what is in you and what you deserve; then this is correct purification. Therefore the Almighty says:

﴿So do not claim purity for yourselves; He knows best who is pious.﴾ [53:32]

Because you purify yourself before the One who will give the reward, and He knows. So it is foolish for a person to purify himself in situations that do not call for purification; rather, purification should be for the benefit of the Muslims, not for his own particular benefit. And the Almighty says:

﴿Have you not seen those who claim purity for themselves? Rather, Allah purifies whom He wills, and they will not be wronged the slightest bit.﴾ [4:49]

Nothing is hidden from the Exalted Lord. It may be that one feigns and affects himself before you for a period of time, but there are things you do not perceive; yet when our Lord purifies, His purification is with knowledge and experience. Nevertheless, "those who claim purity for themselves" — is their good deeds erased? No. Although they claimed purity for themselves, the Almighty will not simply take them and waste their good deeds; rather, "they will not be wronged the slightest bit," and this is absolute justice.

We know that the Qur'an was revealed in Arabic language to an Arab prophet, and those who first received it were Arabs. We know that most of its allusions were in harmony with the environment, and among them was the "palm" (nakhl), the preferred tree, because it is a tree whose leaves never fall, and everything in it is beneficial; there is nothing in the palm tree without benefit.

From Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed among the trees there is a tree whose leaf does not fall, and it is like the Muslim. Tell me what it is."

People thought of the trees of the desert, and it occurred to me that it is the palm tree. Abdullah said: "I felt shy." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell us." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "It is the palm tree." Abdullah said: "I related to my father what had occurred to me, and he said: 'That you had said it would be dearer to me than that I possess such-and-such.'" (1)

The palm has many benefits; everything we take from it finds a use, even the fiber around its base, from which we take the palm branches and make brooms, fiber, baskets (maqatif) and chairs. When the Almighty seeks an example for an abstract matter, He brings it from something perceptible in the Arab environment.

"And they will not be wronged the slightest bit." "Fatil" comes from "fatla," and its meaning is a thing between the fingers: when you rub your fingers, however clean they are, some dirt comes out like a "fatlah" (twist of dirt). Or "fatil" is the thread in the split of the date-stone and the date pit. The Almighty has mentioned three things related to the pit in the Qur'an: "fatil" here, and He mentioned "naqir," which is the small notch on the back of the pit, derived from "minqar" (beak), as if it were carved; and He mentioned "qitmir," which is the membrane wrapping the pit, like the inner shell of an egg, a soft skin. So in the date pit there are three things Allah has used: the fatil, the naqir and the qitmir.

The Almighty says:

﴿And they will not be given the slightest speck (naqir).﴾ [4:53]

So the Almighty took three things from the pit, and gives us examples from the perceptible things before us, which the Arab sees at every moment before him. The Almighty also takes examples from the sky, bringing us the example of the "crescent moon," saying of it when it is small:

﴿Like the old withered palm stalk (al-urjun al-qadim).﴾ [36:39]

The cluster of dates has stalks (shamarikh), and there is a hand that holds the stalks; this is called "urjun." When the urjun is new it is straight, but as it ages it bends and curves. So He brought them an image from the crescent in the sky and gave them an example of it on earth: "like the old urjun." The Arabs have taken many examples, but there are matters which may not be noticed, such as the Arab's saying:

"The light of the moon, which I was watching, faded, like a paring cut from a fingernail."

When you trim your nails, you find them curved. But not everyone notices this matter; he brought something clear and said "like the old urjun." So when the Almighty gives an example of an abstract matter, He comes from the perceptible matter before you to bring the meaning near to you. When you eat a date you do not pay attention to the fibre, which shows it is something trivial; so are the naqir and qitmir. Thus our Lord took examples from the pit and examples from the palm to bring the meanings close to us. "And they will not be wronged the slightest bit."

1: Narrated by al-Bukhari.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 4, verse 50:

﴿See how they invent lies against Allah. And that is sufficient as a manifest sin.﴾

And the words of the Truth, "See" (انظر), are a command to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and every address to the Messenger of Allah is an address to his ummah. We have already known that "al-iftira'" (fabrication, افتراء) is deliberate lying. {They invent lies against Allah} in their saying when they wanted to purify themselves:

﴿We are the children of Allah and His beloved ones.﴾ (Part of verse 18, Surat al-Ma'ida)

And their saying:

﴿And they say: None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians.﴾ (Part of verse 111, Surat al-Baqara)

{"See how they invent lies against Allah, and that is sufficient as a manifest sin"}. Why? Because if you lie against someone like yourself, who may believe you, that is understandable. But if you lie against God, this is outrageous audacity; therefore the Truth said: {And that is sufficient as a manifest sin.}

So lying in general is a sin, and "manifest lying" is lying against Allah. The important point is that it has not benefited you.

Then the Truth says, after that:

﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book? They believe in jibt and taghut, and they say to those who disbelieve: "These are better guided in the way than those who believe."﴾ [4:51]

His saying ﴿were given a portion of the Book﴾ means they have a connection and relationship with heaven, with the messengers, and with the books sent down from heaven upon the messengers, which carry the methods of God. Had they been people without such a share, their words would have been reasonable, since the links to heaven would have been cut off from them. Rather, these people have a portion of the Book, and the foremost purpose of the heavenly books is to bind the created being to the Creator. Binding the created being to the Creator is the training of the created being's capacities and their development, because God's means in the universe may become difficult for you, and your hand may become empty of them. So if you have no God to turn to when the means fail, you collapse, and perhaps you end your life by suicide. But the believer in God, when His means are withheld from him, says: "The means do not concern me, for I have the One who causes the means."

Thus faith in God gives you strength. Faith in God makes the believers stand on firm ground: however your means become scarce and run out, remember the Causer. When you remember the Causer, you find the horizons of your life wide. Those who commit suicide do so only because the means have closed in on them, and they know there is no escape from torment. But the believer says: "O Lord." And merely saying "O Lord" is a statement that comforts him even before it is answered, because he has turned to the Causer of causes when the means became scarce for him.

When he turns to the Causer of causes at the withholding of means, he receives the strength of faith from where he does not reckon. The moment you say "O Lord," you find yourself at rest, because you have connected your whole being to the Creator. Your being includes parts that are subdued to you and parts that are not subdued to you. And the being itself will come in the Hereafter and bear witness against the human.

The feet, the skins, and other limbs will bear witness, because in this world they were subdued to my will. I say to my hand: "Do such-and-such"; to my foot: "Strive for such-and-such"; to my tongue: "Revile so-and-so." God subjected the limbs and commanded them: "O limbs, you are subject to the will of your master in this world." But on the Day of Resurrection, will I have any will over my limbs? No, my limbs will rebel against me:

﴿They will say to their skins: "Why did you testify against us?" They will say: "God, who made everything speak, has made us speak."﴾ [41:21]

The limbs will say to us: "You used us in the world and compelled us to do things we hated, so let us today bear witness," and they will reveal their secrets, because the dominion today belongs to the One, the Subduer:

﴿"To whom belongs the dominion today?" "To God, the One, the Subduer."﴾ [40:16]

The domination of man has ended, and no one other than God has will over the limbs.

So the portion of the Book is the first thing that binds the created being to the Creator. When the created being is bound to the Creator, his means grow strong, he receives events with steadfastness, and the relief of our Lord comes to him. When we read the Qur'an, we must attend to its doctrinal scenes. We know, for example, that when our master Moses wanted to take the Children of Israel out from Pharaoh and lead them away, and before he reached the sea, the people of Pharaoh caught up with them with their armies. The people of Pharaoh were behind them and the sea in front of them, and the people of Moses said, out of faith in means:

﴿"Indeed, we are overtaken."﴾ [26:61]

By God, does anyone deny this statement? No. But what did Moses, peace be upon him, say? He did not say what his people said; rather, he looked to the Highest Causer and said with full confidence:

﴿"No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me."﴾ [26:62]

And is his statement refuted? No, it is not refuted, because he did not say "No" relying on his means. It was not within the scope of his means to escape from such a situation; rather, he said: ﴿Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾. This is the fruit of faith. When he said ﴿Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾, what did God say to him?

He said to him: ﴿Strike the sea with your staff﴾ [26:63].

He did not say to him: "Attack them and overcome them." No. Rather, He said: ﴿Strike the sea with your staff﴾, in order to give the thing and its opposite, and so that you know that the wills of the Truth, glorified and exalted, give the thing and its opposite, and no human can do the like. So when He said to him, "Strike the sea with your staff," Moses struck the sea with the staff, and Moses knew the law of water: it is flowing and fluid. But behold, the miracle is realized:

﴿So every divided part became like a great mountain﴾ [26:63].

The "ṭawd" is the mountain, and the mountain has firmness, while water has softness. How did softness pass into firmness? The function of water is to seep through; that is, it is impossible for a low area to exist with water above it, rather it must penetrate it. When Moses obeyed God's command, he wanted to reassure himself with human means, so he wanted to strike the sea so that the sea would return as it was, lest the people of Pharaoh come after him. So our Lord said to him:

﴿And leave the sea in its calm state﴾ [44:24].

That is: leave it as it is, in its standing, still state, because I want what they see of the dryness of the sea to tempt them so they descend. Then I will return the water to its seepage and close it over them, and I will have saved and destroyed with one thing.

The Truth says: ﴿Those who were given a portion of the Book believe in jibt and taghut﴾. And how is that?

After the Battle of Uhud, Huyayy ibn Akhtab, Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, Ibn Abi al-Huqayq, and Abu Rafi' came. These are the champions of the Jews. They also took seventy Jews with them and descended upon the people of Mecca, and they broke the covenant that was between them and the Messenger of God. After that, Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, their leader, came down to Abu Sufyan and said to him: "We want to pledge together that we will stand against Muhammad." Abu Sufyan said: "You are a possessor of a Book, you have the Torah, you have faith in heaven, you have a messenger, and we do not have this. Muhammad says he is a possessor of a Book and a messenger, so there is a connection between you and heaven. What assures us that you are in agreement with him against us in this affair? We do not trust your deceit, and we will not believe your words unless you come to our gods and perform the rites of worship before them and prostrate to them."

"Jibt and taghut" are two idols of Quraysh. The Jews, the people of the Torah who have a portion of the Book, went to them and submitted to them. Or "jibt" is everyone who calls to other than God, whether he is a devil, a soothsayer, or a magician; if this is "jibt." "Taghut" is from "taghā," and it is an intensive form, not "tāghin," but "ṭāghūt," which is the one who, whenever you obey him in wrongdoing, rises to more wrongdoing. Whether jibt and taghut are two idols or two gods among the gods they follow, the point is that the Jewish delegation submitted to them and prostrated, so that Quraysh would believe in the Jews' enmity to our master, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

After that, Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf asked Abu Sufyan: "What did Muhammad do with you?" He said: "He abandoned the religion of his fathers, cut off his kin, left them and fled to Medina, while we are otherwise. We give drink to the pilgrims, we feed the guest, we free the captive prisoner, we keep the ties of kinship, and we maintain the House and circumambulate it." Abu Sufyan magnified the deeds of Quraysh! So those who were given the Book, out of their enmity to Muhammad, said to Abu Sufyan and his people: "You are better guided in the way than Muhammad!"

Our Lord clarifies: O Muhammad, look at their marvels. They were given a portion of the Book, yet their enmity toward you, and their standing against your religion and against the light you brought, made them forget their portion of the Book and believe in jibt and taghut. These are the very people who used to say to the Arabs in the past: "A prophet will come from among you, we will follow him and kill you with him, as the 'Ad and Iram were killed." But here they are, going and believing in the taghut and the jibt. So is there any part of religion with such people?

The Truth, glorified be He, wants to reassure His Messenger that these people have cut themselves off from the support of heaven. If conflict or disagreement arises between you and them, know that God has abandoned them, because they left the portion of the Book that they were given. Beware that it should occur to you that these are people of a Book.

The Truth reassures His Messenger that He, glorified be He, has abandoned them, and that God is your helper, O Muhammad. Do not let it deceive you that they are possessors of wealth, or possessors of knowledge, or possessors of riches, for all of this is passing away, because their share from heaven has been cut off; and because polytheism has seized them, taken possession of them, and gathered them to itself, and they have made enmity toward you and alliance with the disbelievers their choice, those who used to seek victory over them through your mission and your messengership, as a price for abandoning faith.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 4, verse 52:

His saying "ʾUlāʾika" is a demonstrative noun composed of "ʾUlāʾ," which is for the plural, and of the "kaf," which is for addressing the Messenger of Allah. We, the Muslims, are included within his address (ﷺ). "ʾUlāʾika" refers to those who were given a portion of the Book, who believe in jibt (idols or sorcery) and ṭāghūt (false objects of worship), and who say to those who disbelieve: "These are better guided in the way than those who believe" (4:51). Or "ʾUlāʾika" refers to both the Jews and the polytheists together, and let us take it as a demonstrative pointing to all of them, in His the Exalted's saying: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed﴾. And "al-laʿn" (cursing) is either "al-ṭard" (expulsion), or "al-khizy" (disgrace), or "al-ihlāk" (destruction).

And how does Allah bring disgrace upon the disbelievers? Because you find the Islamic expansion increasing every day while their land diminishes: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts?﴾ (part of a verse of Surat al-Ra'd).

﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed.﴾ So then the one who expels is Allah. When the expeller is equal to the one expelled, he may find someone to help him; but if the expeller is Allah, there is no helper for the one expelled. "And whoever Allah curses," that is, whoever our Lord expels, "you will not find for him a helper"; because once the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, has expelled him, He instills in the hearts of all people that they should abandon him for whatever reason, so no one supports him. ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, and whoever Allah curses, you will not find for him any helper.﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 4, verse 53:

What is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Or do they have a share in the kingdom? Then they would not give the people even a speck (naqir)﴾?

He, glory be to Him, describes them with extreme stinginess and intense miserliness. That is, in reality they do not possess the kingdom of this world, nor do they possess the kingdom of God. The sovereignty belongs to Him alone, majestic is His station: He gives it to whomever He wills and strips it from whomever He wills. But if they were given the kingdom of this world and the kingdom of God, they would be stingy and would hold back what is in their hands. As He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿Say: If you possessed the treasuries of the mercy of my Lord, you would surely withhold them for fear of spending; and man has ever been tight-fisted.﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 100)

That is, you fear spending, lest the wealth in your possession diminish. So if you were to take hold of the treasuries of our Lord, you would say: "If we took from them and gave to the people, they would be depleted!" The gist of the expression is that all these people, whether the disbelievers of Quraysh or the leaders of the Jews, were preserving their status and their wealth. For the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, came to level people out. So who grieves? Those who held leadership grieve, because they do not want heads to be made equal. Would that they, when they took up leadership, had made it a good for the people, but they did not. Had they possessed the kingdom and the wealth, they would not have given the people a speck; for a human being by nature does not relinquish his arrogance, because this arrogance gives him authority, and as long as arrogance has given him authority, he does not heed the reality of faith. Indeed, the best of good is that good endures. It is not enough that you be in good and in power; rather, guarantee that it endures. This endurance you will not obtain within the lifespan of this world, whose duration is brief and whose life within it is not guaranteed. Therefore, the lasting good is there in the Hereafter:

﴿Neither cut off nor forbidden.﴾ (Surah al-Waqi'ah, 33)

So if you are eager for this standing and wish to have this kingdom, standing and greatness, do you give people any of this good of yours, so that there would be an excuse for your greed for wealth, namely that people benefit from you?

Why, then, do you want our Lord to perpetuate this for you while you are at the peak of stinginess and miserliness? It is impossible for Him to perpetuate it for you.

For this reason, the Truth, exalted is He, says in Surah al-Fajr, clarifying this process:

﴿As for man, when his Lord tests him and honours him and blesses him, he says: My Lord has honoured me. But when He tests him and restricts his provision, he says: My Lord has humiliated me.﴾ (Surah al-Fajr, 15-16)

So whoever has a blessing says: "My Lord has honoured me," and whoever has no blessing says: "My Lord has humiliated me." Then the Truth, in response to the two claims, says: ﴿No!﴾

Since He, glory be to Him, responds to the two claims with "No!", this means that both parties are lying. You are lying, O you who said: the blessing you have received is evidence of honour; and you are also a liar, O you who said: lack of wealth is evidence of humiliation. Neither the giving of wealth is evidence of honour, nor the withholding of wealth is evidence of humiliation. It is a claim that is true in one respect and fundamentally mistaken. The Truth stated the grounds for this:

﴿Rather, you do not honour the orphan.﴾ (Surah al-Fajr, 17)

That is, you have wealth but you do not honour the orphan. Therefore this wealth is a proof against you; it is not an honour for you, but will punish you with it. He adds:

﴿And you do not urge one another to feed the poor.﴾ (Surah al-Fajr, 18)

So how can wealth be an honour when it will bring you a calamity? Its absence is better. Wealth that exists with a person who does not uphold the rights of the weak in it is a burden and an evil, for the Truth says:

﴿They will be encircled with what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ (part of verse 180, Surah Al 'Imran)

So if you are very stingy, you will be encircled with a more severe collar. That is why, when the collar tightens upon him, he says: "Would that I had lightened this collar!" The Truth, in the verse we are reflecting upon, questions why they align with the camp of polytheism, abandon the share they were given of the Book, and go to say to those who disbelieve: "You are better guided than Muhammad as to the way," although they know, by virtue of the share of the Book they possess, that Muhammad is upon the truth?

They were preserving their leadership, and the camp of polytheism preserves its leadership. We know that the Jews in Medina were men of wealth, living on usury, owners of fortresses, owners of farms, and owners of knowledge. Thus they had taken every element of leadership. When the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, came, all these matters were shaken from beneath their feet, and they grieved. Likewise the disbelievers of Quraysh: they held leadership over the whole of the Arabian Peninsula, so no one from any tribe in the Peninsula could dare attack a Quraysh caravan, for the tribes feared confronting them. In the season of the pilgrimage, all the tribes would come under the protection of Quraysh. The awe they commanded came to them from the Sacred House, which God preserved and guarded, and He repelled whoever intended it harm, turned back his scheme, and utterly destroyed him. As the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, said:

﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant? Did He not make their plot go astray? And He sent against them birds in flocks, striking them with stones of baked clay, and made them like eaten stalks.﴾ (Surah al-Fil, 1-5)

The reason for this process comes in the following surah, His saying, glory be to Him:

﴿For the security of Quraysh, their security in the caravans of winter and summer.﴾ (Surah Quraysh, 1-2)

Had He, glory be to Him, not made this House for His worship, leadership would have ended and their leadership would have ended with it, so they would not be able to go on the winter journey nor the summer journey. For this reason He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿So let them worship the Lord of this House.﴾ (Surah Quraysh, 3)

Glory be to Him who gave them leadership and honour, who:

﴿fed them against hunger and secured them against fear.﴾ (Surah Quraysh, 4)

He brought them the fruits of all things, and secured them against fear when their caravans travelled to the north and to the south.

﴿Or do they have a share in the kingdom?﴾ If they had such a share, then they would not give the people even a speck, that is, they would not give them even a trivial thing.

Then the Truth says, after that:

﴿Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty? We had already given the family of Abraham the Scripture and wisdom, and We gave them a great kingdom.﴾ (4:54)

The envy here is directed at the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), because our Lord has chosen him and selected him for the message. For this reason some of them said:

﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man from one of the two cities?﴾ (43:31)

So the Qur'an is acceptable in their view. What grieves them, however, is that it was revealed to Muhammad. This is from their foolishness, and it is like the foolishness of those who said:

﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky.﴾ (8:32)

They wished for death and killing by stones falling from the sky, and they did not wish to follow the truth. This is the height of foolishness, which shows that their partisanship is a mad fanaticism. For this reason the Truth says:

﴿Is it they who would apportion the mercy of your Lord? We have apportioned among them their livelihood.﴾ (43:32)

He, glory be to Him, affirms to us that He singles out for His mercy whom He wills. So why envy? They envy the people, that Muhammad (ﷺ) came to them. Had they received what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought with fair and equitable eyes, seeking justice, they would have found that everything he brought is beautiful speech: whoever follows it, his life is adorned by it. It was required of those to whom Allah had given a share of knowledge of the Scripture that they announce the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), as what was revealed to them in their Book called them to do, and that they be the first to affirm him. But they did not do so; rather they denied and turned away from his path, and they preferred the disbelieving idolaters over him. They said that they were better guided than Muhammad as to the way.

The Truth, glorified and exalted, is living; He bestows special favours upon some of His creatures, and He loves that these special favours extend to Allah's creation. For we know that in every creature of Allah there is a special endowment of talents; so when a bestower bestows his talent upon creation, the rest of creation bestows their talents upon him. Thus, when everyone gives, he has taken the talents of all.

These are a people to whom Allah gave a share, yet they were stingy and withheld, not only with regard to a matter concerning themselves, but with regard to the matter that connects them to God: that they are people of a Book, who know from God His method and know from God the order of the procession of His messengers. The Truth, glorified be He, wants to say to them: You were given a share of the Book and did not fulfil its right; and also, were you to possess the kingdom, you would not fulfil its right, and you would not give anyone even a naqir, which is the speck on the back of a date-stone. For this reason He said:

﴿Or do they have a share in the kingdom? If so, they would not give the people even a speck.﴾ (4:53)

Thus they give neither in matters of meaning and values, nor in material things. If they have been stingy with what they have of values, they are more worthy to be stingy with what they have of material goods, and so they have become a people with no good in them at all.

Then the Truth makes clear: if these people were given a share of the Book, which identifies for them the marks of the coming final Messenger, what prevented them from believing in him first and supporting him? There is no doubt it is envy, even though he (ﷺ) came confirming what they had. Undoubtedly they envied the Messenger (ﷺ), and envy arises only from a rancorous heart, a heart rebellious against God's apportioning among His creatures. For envy, as they have said, is wishing for the removal of another's blessing, and its counterpart is "ghibta" (wishing for the like of what another has): you wish for what the other has, while he remains in God's blessing; but you want its like. If you want its like from God, you must be pleased for him. And the Truth says:

﴿What you have will run out, but what Allah has is everlasting.﴾ (16:96)

Therefore people ought to be, in Allah's giving, neither envious nor rancorous. But some people may envy others who receive gifts from the rich, out of desire that it be for them alone. For if you have a sum of money and some people in need come to you and you give them some of it, others who desire your bounty and hope for your goodness may say: you will decrease what you have by as much as you give these; for what you have is limited. But here the giving is from One whose store never runs out; so He gives you and gives others, and nothing of what He has is diminished.

Therefore ghibta is self-evident to the believer, because he knows that God's giving one person does not prevent Him from giving another; and if He, glory be to Him, granted every single person his request, that would diminish what He has no more than a needle diminishes when dipped into the sea. This is as in the sacred hadith: "O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were to stand in one open plain and ask Me, and I gave each person his request, that would not diminish what I have except as a needle diminishes when put into the sea."(1)

﴿Or do they envy the people for what He has given them﴾: envy, as we have known, is wishing for the removal of another's blessing. This wish means that you dislike that another should have a blessing, and you do not dislike another having a blessing only if you are rebelling against the One who gives blessings.

The first error the envier falls into is rejecting God's decree in His creation; and the second thing that befalls him is that, before the envied one is harmed, his own heart burns with rancour. For this reason they said: envy is a sin or crime whose punishment precedes it, for every crime's punishment is delayed after it except envy: before the envier commits envy, punishment reaches him, because rancour burns his heart. And perhaps someone will say: what is the fault of the envied one? We say: God has placed in some of His creatures an affliction that afflicts people, and envy afflicts them in their blessings and in their well-being. And what is the fault of the one killed when the killer aims his pistol to kill him with it? This is like that. The pistol is one of God's blessings in a person's hand, to protect himself with, and he has no right to use it for falsehood.

Suppose that God, glory be to Him, created in man something that hates the blessing another has. Why does not the person, when he encounters a blessing in another, remember to join it with his saying: ﴿What Allah wills; there is no power except through Allah﴾? For if you join every blessing that others have with "What Allah wills, there is no power except with Allah," you would drive the poison of your rancour from your heart. For you remember that a person has not given himself any blessing; rather our Lord gave it to him, and He, glory be to Him, is capable of every giving. It is possible that a person may be envied; but the one who finds envy in himself and wants to extinguish it must return everything to God, and since he has returned everything to God, he has set up a safeguard for himself against being an envier, and a safeguard for the blessing in another's hand against being envied. The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, explains this to us in His saying, glory be to Him:

﴿And from the evil of an envier when he envies﴾ (113:5)

So it is possible that one of us may have his heart filled with rancour over a blessing, and afterwards envy arises from it; and each of us must prevent himself from letting the current of rancour enter his heart, for the current of rancour causes a chemical change in the constitution of a person, and this chemical change is what causes the person fatigue. And what do we know but that this chemical tension from the blessing in another's possession creates reactions in a person's self and substance, and from these reactions emanates a radiation that goes to the envied one and kills him? For the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, says:

﴿And from the evil of an envier when he envies﴾ (113:5)

When you seek refuge in God from the evil of the envier, it may not be that it never touches you; it may touch you. But your seeking refuge from his evil means that if it touches you, you must say "Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un" (﴿Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return﴾) and know that this is good for you. If it strikes you in a blessing, know that this affliction contains good; so if the envier harms you in some of Allah's blessings upon you, the evil is that you are deprived of the reward for it! The afflicted one is the one deprived of reward. So when a misfortune comes to anyone and he says: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return... O Allah, You are my Lord, and You do not wish for me anything but good, for I am Your creature and You have wrought upon me nothing but good... but I may not be able to understand that good."

When a Muslim does this, Allah, glory be to Him, later makes clear to him that it was good for him. If it befalls him in his child and he says: who knows, perhaps my child whom God caused to die would have tempted me into disbelief or into stealing for him and taking bribes on his account? But God took him from me and withheld that evil from me; or that blessing might have made me arrogant, might have made me tyrannize people, might have made me transgress against creation, so our Lord says to me: be ill a little and be calm. Thus we see that the afflicted must expect good, must say "Inna lillahi," and must say: surely some good will come to me from this trial. And someone may say: we say

﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak, from the evil of what He created, and from the evil of darkness when it settles, and from the evil of the blowers in knots, and from the evil of an envier when he envies﴾ (113:1–5)

We recite and repeat this surah, and God has not protected us from the evil of enviers, and envious people envy us too!

We say to him: you have not understood the meaning of His saying: ﴿from the evil of an envier when he envies﴾. You understand it on the basis that his envy will never touch you. No, his envy may touch you, but you must know the measure of God in that touching and say: O Lord, You have made it befall me for a good that You have for me. If you do this, you have been spared the evil.

We live in a world in which we see that as the world advances in knowledge, our Lord shows us signs in His creation and in the secrets of existence that bring many meanings close to us. Those who now manufacture weapons of destruction and annihilation: the more the weapon becomes subtle, fine and imperceptible to the eye, the more violent it is, and it differs from the weapons of ancient times, when a person would throw a stone at another, then another would throw a pistol. Then it came within a state's power to make an atomic bomb of which each part is no more than the size of a nail-head, yet it kills. So the more weapons of destruction become subtle, the more intense they become. We now see all weapons work by radiation, and radiation is not a body, and the action of radiation is penetrating, yet it has no body; as the doctors say: we perform the operation without shedding blood, by means of rays, such as laser beams. So the finer the weapon, the more violent and deadly it is.

Here is an example that clarifies this. Suppose you wanted to build yourself a palace in an open wilderness, and a friend passed by and said: why did you not put iron on the windows of the first floor? You say: why? He says: here there are beasts of prey and wolves. So you put iron to keep out the wolves. Another passes your palace and says: the gaps in the iron are wide, and here there are many snakes, so you narrow the iron. A third says: there are mosquitoes here that sting and carry germs. So you put wire mesh over the windows.

Thus the more subtle the enemy, the more violent it is, and so it needs greater precaution. We know that the germ which cannot be seen comes and destroys people; the affliction that strikes people, the more subtle it is, that is, the finer and smaller it becomes, the more violent it grows. If it were large, a person could push it back little by little; but when it reaches a degree of fineness and smallness, a person cannot repel it. The most deadly germs are those that become so fine that doctors say of some diseases: we do not know a virus for them; meaning this disease-causing virus has become so minute that it exceeds the standards of microscopes.

So what prevents us from accepting that a spark of germ-like emanation may come out of the chemistry of the envier, the rancorous person whom the blessing in another's hand distresses, and that this spark, like a laser beam, goes toward a thing and destroys it? What is the barrier to this? We are already doing this, directing rays at anything, and rays are among the most deadly weapons of our time. Why should we not believe that the chemistry of the envier, when agitated, produces a radiation that goes to the envied one and destroys him? It is like any blessing our Lord bestows on you, which you then use for harm. An example is the man who has some wealth yet boils with rancour against his opponents and buys a pistol or a rifle to kill them; he takes the blessing and makes it a means of revenge, and this comes from the agitation of the inner instinct that governs human emotions.

So these people, when the Messenger of God came confirming what they had, what prevented them from believing him? There is no doubt they envied him for receiving this blessing, and they regarded the blessing of prophethood as a distinction for the messengers. Was that correct?

(1) Related by Muslim in the chapter on the prohibition of injustice, and related by Ahmad.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 4, verse 55:

Allah's saying, ﴿So among them is one who believed in it﴾. The intended meaning is belief in what came in the methodology (manhaj) of Ibrahim and the messengers who came after him, to whom Allah gave prophethood and kingship. Or, "among them" means among the People of the Book whom we are speaking about: whoever believed in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and Kaʿb al-Ahbar, for example. And "among them is one who turned away from it" means that among them are those who disbelieved in the methodology of Allah. Therefore, He, glorified is He, says after it: ﴿And Hell is sufficient as a blazing fire﴾. It is as though the result of turning away from the methodology is that nothing comes after it except the punishment of Hell, so that they burn in its fire, and it is kindled over them as a recompense for what they did.

After Allah, exalted is He, explained the procession of the messengers, which He sent in succession throughout His creation, He came to remind people of the methodology. The methodology is the original foundation of the mission of Adam and his offspring, because He, glorified and exalted is He, has said: ﴿Then when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer﴾ (part of verse 123, Surah Taha).

Adam transmitted to his descendants his knowledge of the movement of life, of the truth, and of the methodology. However, Allah has decreed heedlessness toward His methodology in His creatures, for these methodologies always come against the desires of the foolish, hasty self. But if you look at the reality of the divine methodology, you will find that it gives the self its desires, but elevated ones. An example of this is when He says: ﴿And they prefer others over themselves, even though they themselves are in need﴾ (part of verse 9, Surah al-Hashr).

Each person has things and needs them, but he finds his believing brother needs them more than he does, so he prefers him over himself. Does he prefer him over himself? No. Rather, he gives this little thing of the perishable world so that he may take in exchange what is lasting. So he takes the desire of his self but in an elevated form of desire. And to the one to whom we said: lower your gaze from what is forbidden of others' women. Outwardly, this matter means that we are withholding you from a desire you crave, but at the moment we withhold you from a desire you crave in the forbidden, perishable form, we want to fulfill for you a desire in the lawful, everlasting form. So which of them is more in love with beauty? The one who gazes intently at a beautiful woman as she walks, or the one who lowers his eyes from her? The one more in love with beauty is the one who lowered his gaze.

Indeed, religion has come only against the foolish self that wants the immediate matter even if it is trivial. It clarifies to him: be for the deferred and with it, because it remains, so it does not leave you and you do not leave it. As for any desire you take in this world, either you leave it or it leaves you; but in the Hereafter, you do not leave it and it does not leave you.

The righteous and scrupulous have known how to benefit, but the others are the foolish who did not benefit. So Allah, exalted is He, makes clear to us that regret will belong to the one who eased his self with a hasty desire and was then followed by the lasting, deferred punishment. This is the true loss. The world is the abode of changes: there comes to a person in it what pains him and what pleases him, and there is never any permanent state in it, because it is the world of changes. And as long as it is the world of changes, everything in it is subject to change. Since everything in it is changing, then the one who is in blessing may be struck by some harm, the one who is strong may be struck by some weakness, and the one who is weak may later receive strength. Otherwise, if the weak remained weak and the strong remained strong, the world would not be a world of changes.

For this reason they say: beware of wanting from Allah that His blessing be completed upon you entirely, for if the blessing were completed for you entirely while you are in the abode of changes, then expect death. The completion of blessing is like climbing to the highest point of a mountain while you are in the abode of changes: will you remain on the summit? No, you must descend. So beware of rejoicing when the matter reaches its peak, for Allah, exalted is He, makes clear: you must take this world as a passage. What tires people is that they do not set the distant goal; rather, they set near goals.

Among the foolishness of some people is that one of them grieves over the separation from a beloved or relative. Take it by logic: what is our common goal? It is death, and our return to our Creator. And when we return to our Creator, should we grieve? No, we should rejoice, because in this world we are with the means (asbab), but once we move to the Hereafter we will be with the Causer (musabbib). In this world you are with the blessing, and afterward you will be with the Bestower. So what saddens you in this? What saddens you is when you are with the blessing and do not attend to the Bestower; but if you are with the blessing and attend to the Bestower, you would rejoice that you are going to the Bestower.

And if the matter is that we reach the true Bestower and be in His care, then why grieve? And it is foolish that some people do not treat Allah, exalted is He, as they treat themselves.
