His saying: ﴿And if they, when they had wronged themselves, had come to you﴾: the matter is that they refrained from coming to you, O Messenger of God. So the first rank is that they return from what they did, and after that they ask forgiveness of God, because the sin, with respect to not coming to the Messenger, before it attaches to the Messenger, attaches to the One who sent the Messenger. For this reason they say: insulting the Messenger is insulting the One who sent him. It is true that not going to the Messenger is a matter relating to the Messenger, but if you ascend it you find it related to the One who sent the Messenger, which is God, because the Messenger brought nothing of his own. And after the Messenger's heart is content, he asks God's forgiveness for them. So, first: they come; second: they ask God's forgiveness; third: the Messenger asks forgiveness for them.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿They would have found God Accepting of repentance, Merciful﴾. So finding God Accepting of repentance, Merciful is conditional upon their returning to the Messenger instead of turning away from him, and then their asking God's forgiveness; because God did not send any messenger except to be obeyed by His permission. So when you disagree with him, do not say: "I disagreed with the Messenger." No. If you disagree with him, you have disagreed with the One who sent him, and you must ask God's forgiveness.

If you ask God's forgiveness without pleasing the Messenger, God will not accept that from you. No one can ever set right what is between himself and God except through Muhammad, peace be upon him.

When they do that, by coming to the Messenger, asking God's forgiveness and the Messenger asking forgiveness for them, they will find God Accepting of repentance, Merciful. The word "tawwab" (Accepting of repentance) is an intensive form of repentance, indicating that their sin is great.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, created His creatures and knows that passing whims come into their thoughts and souls, and that their desires may awaken at times and turn into some sins. Because He is a merciful Lord, He has shown us what erases all this heedlessness. When the servant commits a sin, will his Merciful Lord leave him just like that to the sin? No. He, glorified is He, has prescribed for him a return to Him, because God loves that His servant should turn back and return to Him, even if he was heedless through his disobedience.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, teaches us how to remove from ourselves the traces of sins. He said: ﴿And if they, when they had wronged themselves, had come to you﴾. So the remedy for this is that they come to you, because they were heedless that you speak and convey from the Truth in legislation and judgment. After coming, they ask God's forgiveness, and the Messenger asks forgiveness for them, supporting their asking forgiveness of God; then (they will find) God Accepting of repentance, Merciful.

1) Narrated by Muslim.

Therefore, one must receive faith by fully turning to everything that the Messenger of Allah brought. When the hypocrites judged by other than him, despite their declaration of Islam, the ruling was that they had gone out of the circle of faith, and the believers must take warning from this.

We notice in the words of the Truth, ﴿Fa-la wa-rabbika﴾, the presence of a negating "la," and that He, glorified be He, swore an oath saying: ﴿Then no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in what they dispute among themselves﴾. We know that the hypocrites went and judged other than the Messenger of Allah, although they testify that he is the Messenger of Allah. How can they testify that he is the Messenger of Allah and then judge by other than him, not being content with his decision? This is a matter on which the Truth passes judgment, saying: No. This can never be. So the negating "la" has come here to negate their faith and their testimony that he is the Messenger of Allah, because they judged by other than him. Once it is established that they testified that he is the Messenger of Allah and then went to another to decide between them, if this occurs, our judgment in the matter is: they will never have the honour of testifying that he is the Messenger of Allah.

Then the Truth swore, saying: ﴿But by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in what they dispute among themselves﴾. We, the creation, swear only by Allah, but He, glorified be He, may swear by whatever He wills, over whomever He wills. He swears by the mountain material: ﴿By the Mount [al-Tur]﴾ (Surah al-Tur).

He swears by the scatterers: ﴿By the scatterers, scattering﴾ (Surah al-Dhariyat).

The scatterers (al-Dhariyat) are the winds. He swears by plants: ﴿By the fig and the olive﴾ (Surah al-Tin).

He swears by the angels: ﴿By those who line up in rows﴾ (Surah al-Saffat).

But if you look at mankind, you will not find that He swore by any of the lord of this universe, who is man, except the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and He swore by his life, saying: ﴿By your life, they were wandering blindly in their intoxication﴾ (Surah al-Hijr).

"La'amruka" means: by your life, O Muhammad, they are in their intoxication wandering blindly, that is, they are in their error and misguidance, bewildered, not guided to the truth. Then Allah swore by Himself, saying: ﴿So by the Lord of the heaven and the earth, indeed it is the truth﴾ (part of verse 23, Surah al-Dhariyat).

When He says: ﴿By the Lord of the heaven and the earth﴾, He must bring His lordship to a great creation that we see, and therefore He said: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾ (part of verse 57, Surah Ghafir).

That is, if you, O human, reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth, you will find it greater than the creation of mankind.

In the verse on which our reflections are focused, Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in what they dispute among themselves﴾, and this is an honouring of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and evidence that Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, has a lofty station. Beware lest you think that when He said: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾, Muhammad had entered among mankind. He, glorified be He, makes clear: No, I will swear by him just as I swore by the heaven and the earth: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them﴾. And why does He swear by the Lord of the heaven and the earth? Because the Lord possesses tremendous, immense power: He creates, nurtures, cares for, and disciplines.

The creation of the heavens and the earth is sufficient with creation, the law of the universe, and subjugation. But when He creates Muhammad, He does not desire mere creation and bringing into existence, but desires a upbringing in which the ascents of prophethood are complete, so He says to him: By your Lord who created you, who fashioned you, who nurtured you, who qualified you to be the best of Allah's creation, to be the seal of the messengers, and to be the mercy of Allah to the worlds. He swears by all of this, saying: ﴿Then no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in what they dispute among themselves﴾. How far is it that He, glorified be He, places in us this awe by swearing by the Lord of the Messenger of Allah; do we say: we do not make Muhammad and his method the judge in our lives? So His saying: ﴿Then no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in what they dispute among themselves﴾, and the judging, all of whose root words are like "al-hukm" (judgment), "al-tahkim" (arbitration), "al-hikmah" (wisdom), and "al-tahakkum" (domination), all of these derive from "al-hikmah," which is the iron bit placed in the horse's mouth by which its rider prevents it from bolting and controls it right and left. Likewise, "al-hikmah" (wisdom) restrains each person from straying into taking the right of another. Thus arbitration, judgment, and wisdom all suggest placing a thing in its correct position.

The word "shajara" is derived from the root (sh-j-r), and when you see it, understand that it derives from the tree you know. There are plants that do not cling to one another, and there are plants that, as they grow, cling to one another and intertwine, as we see, for example, a tree intertwined with another, its branches interlaced so that the observer cannot say: this is a leaf of this tree or a leaf of that tree. And when they bear fruit, and they are of one kind, you cannot say: this fruit is from this tree, nor that fruit from that tree; that is, the matter has become mixed.

"Wa-shajara baynahum" means that a dispute and confusion arose over a matter. You go to separate this tree from that, and this fruit from that fruit. When you see trees of one kind that have intermingled and become mixed, it does not concern you, if you are the picker of the fruit, whether this fruit you have plucked is from here or from there; you take the fruit wherever you find it, and it does not matter to you whether it is from this or from that. And if you sit in the shade under a tree, it does not matter to you to know whether this shade came from the leaves of this tree or of that tree. This is the benefit of mixing what is equal. But if you want a leaf of a particular tree, you select it, because I want it for a specific purpose.

All creatures are equal, so if they were mixed, the matter should have been shared among them; but the nature of the soul is avarice, so they quarrelled. Therefore the wise judge says to the disputing parties: Do you want me to judge between you with justice, or with what is better than justice? They are alarmed and say: Is there anything better than justice? He says: Yes, it is grace (al-fadl). So long as the matter is a single brotherhood, and the good for you is like the good for me, there is no dispute; but when quarrelling occurs, separation becomes necessary.

And who separates? It is our master, the Messenger of Allah, by the ruling of the Truth's saying: ﴿Then no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in what they dispute among themselves﴾. Faith is not a saying that is merely uttered, but a saying that has a function. When you say: "There is no god but Allah" and bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, this saying must have a function: that the movement of your life is governed by the light of this saying. There is no worshipped one but Allah, no commander but Allah, no benefiter but Allah, no harmer but Allah, and no legislator but Allah. It is not merely a word you say, after which the matter ends; then when a matter comes to you that requires its application, you flee from it. ﴿Then no, by your Lord, they do not believe﴾ in the method of Islam ﴿until they make you judge﴾. This is the application: ﴿in what they dispute among themselves﴾. It is not valid that they make you judge in appearance only; rather they must make you judge willingly in the arbitration, ﴿then they find in themselves no discomfort﴾, that is, no constriction, ﴿concerning what you have decided﴾. So when the Messenger of Allah judges, do not be remiss in accepting his judgment, and do not feel constricted by it, ﴿and submit in full submission﴾, that is, they yield with complete surrender.

Therefore faith is not embodied in a saying that is uttered, but in putting that saying into operation: that you turn to it in the practical movements of life. ﴿Then no, by your Lord, they do not believe﴾ until faith is translated into a real matter, for which the Truth has chosen the most severe moments of discomfort in the human soul, which is the moment of contention that generates obstinacy and deviation from the truth. ﴿Then no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in what they dispute among themselves, then they find in themselves no discomfort﴾, because one may find discomfort and yet not speak.

And look at the three: the first: ﴿And if, when they wronged themselves, they had come to you﴾; this is one. ﴿And asked Allah's forgiveness﴾; this is the second. ﴿And the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them﴾; this is the third. These are the erasers of sins. And what brings you into the enclosure of faith is also three: ﴿Then no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in what they dispute among themselves﴾; this is the first. ﴿Then they find in themselves no discomfort concerning what you have decided﴾; this is the second. And ﴿submit in full submission﴾; this is the third. So the two matters concerning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ are: entry into the enclosure of faith, and exit from the shackle of sin.

Here is a pause, and I do not exaggerate if I say that it has occupied me for more than ten years: this pause concerns Allah's saying: ﴿And if, when they wronged themselves, they had come to you and asked Allah's forgiveness, and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance, Merciful﴾. That, O Lord, is the purification of those who lived in the time of Your Messenger ﷺ. But what of those who did not live in his time? Where is the purifier that corresponds to this for one who did not live in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ? The Messenger came to all people, so how is there a purifier for the people who lived in the time of the Messenger of Allah, while those who came after the Messenger of Allah are deprived of this purification?

This is a matter that remained in my mind, and I found no answer to it. However, I said: it has been established for me, and for some of the scholars, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, reassuring the believers in every age:

(My life is good for you: you speak and you are spoken to. And when I die, my death will be good for you: your deeds will be presented to me; if I see good, I praise Allah, and if I see evil, I seek forgiveness for you.)(1)

Look at the reassurance in his saying ﷺ: (Your deeds are presented to me; if I see good, I praise Allah, and if I see other than that, I seek forgiveness for you.)(2)

So the Messenger's seeking forgiveness for us exists. Therefore what remains is only that we seek Allah's forgiveness, and what remains is only "they come to you," that is, they come to your Sunnah and to what you left of it. He ﷺ is the one who said:

(I have left among you two things; you will never go astray after them: the Book of Allah and my Sunnah, and they will not separate until they come to me at the Pool.)(3)

Just as the living used to come to him, so we come to his judgment, his Sunnah, and his legislation, and he seeks forgiveness for us all. So this matter is concluded, and what remains is that we seek Allah's forgiveness, saying: We seek forgiveness from Allah the Great, there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting, and we repent to Him. We do this, God willing.

As for His saying, glorified and exalted be He: ﴿Then they find in themselves no discomfort concerning what you have decided, and submit in full submission﴾, that is, they find no discomfort when they submit to any obligatory ruling or judicial ruling. The obligatory ruling we know in: do and do not do. As for the judicial ruling, it is when two people dispute over something, and this requires that we accept the ruling in the dispute if it has been issued by the Messenger of Allah or by his method. Therefore we must submit in full submission in both: in the obligatory ruling, and in the judicial ruling.

1 Narrated by Ibn Sa'd from Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah as a mursal report, and al-Suyuti graded it as hasan.
2 Narrated by Ibn Sa'd.
3 Narrated by al-Hakim from Abu Hurayrah.

Here, the Truth equates the command to kill oneself with the command to leave one's homes. Killing is the forcible departure of the soul from the body by a compelling force other than natural death, and expulsion from one's homes is forced removal by a compelling force from the land in which a person lives. Thus the act of killing is paired with the act of expulsion from homes. At the moment a person is killed, he suffers, and at the moment he is driven from his homeland, he suffers. Both are grievous to a human being. The Truth brings these two rulings, which had already been applied to the people of Moses (peace be upon him), when He says: ﴿And when Moses said to his people, "O my people, indeed you have wronged yourselves by your taking of the calf, so repent to your Creator and kill yourselves"﴾ (part of verse 54, Surat al-Baqarah).

It is said that when the people of Moses heard this ruling, seventy thousand of them killed themselves. We also know that the people of Moses were expelled from their homes and went wandering in the desert (al-tih). The Exalted says: ﴿He said, "It is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander in the land"﴾ (part of verse 26, Surat al-Ma'idah).

That is, they would not enter it and would not possess it. The Truth here makes clear that Islam did not bring anything like what the earlier laws brought, in which repentance required the killing of oneself. Those laws held that the self incites its owner to oppose the method, so it must be destroyed. It is by God's kindness that He, glory be to Him, did not impose such a ruling upon us. For this reason, our master ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud, our master ʿAmmar ibn Yasir, and Thabit ibn Qays all said: "By God, if we had been commanded to this, we would have done it." Our master ʿUmar said: "By God, if we had been commanded to this, we would have done it, and praise be to God who did not do that to us." So this is kindness. It shows them: had We decreed upon them that they kill themselves or leave their homes as happened to the people of Moses, what would they have done? But our Lord answered their supplication: ﴿Our Lord, do not impose upon us a burden like that which You imposed on those before us. Our Lord, do not burden us with what we have no ability to bear﴾ (part of verse 286, Surat al-Baqarah).

The Truth has answered them. But what would have happened to you had that been decreed for you? The reason for this account is that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had a cousin on his father's aunt's side named al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwam, who is one of the Ten promised Paradise, and there was another named Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah. They were both in Medina. Whoever visits the illuminated city of Medina finds there an area called al-Harrah, whose ground is of black stones as if burnt, and in it are some hawa'it (walls), that is, orchards, because they call an orchard a ḥā'iṭ (wall). They feared the violence of floods, so they built a wall around the cultivated land to ward off the force of the flood and to define its boundaries. Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah had farmland lower than the land of al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwam. The flood came first to al-Zubayr's land and then descended to Hatib's land. We know that rain falls scattered in one place and then the water gathers in a small channel which they call a shirāj (watercourse), and from it they irrigate their orchards.

When the flood came and they wanted to irrigate their orchards, a dispute arose between al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwam and Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah. Al-Zubayr's land was higher than Hatib's, and Hatib wanted the water to pass to his land first and then al-Zubayr would irrigate his land afterward. When they brought their dispute to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), he ruled in favour of al-Zubayr, for the right was with him. The Messenger would not twist the truth merely out of kinship. Some people judge unjustly so that they become known among people for justice. Someone's son may dispute with another, and the right is with the son, yet the judge rules against his son so people will not say, "He favoured his son!" This is not justice. Justice is that you rule by the truth and then ask your son to give up his right, so that his giving becomes a favour to another. Courage is to rule by the truth, and there is a stronger courage, which is to rule by the truth even if it is against yourself, because the truth is dearer than yourself.

The text of this incident, as cited by the Imam al-Bukhari in his Sahih with its chain, says: "Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Shuʿayb informed us, from al-Zuhri who said: ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that al-Zubayr used to relate that he disputed with a man of the Ansar who had witnessed Badr, before the Messenger of God (ﷺ), concerning a watercourse from al-Harrah which both of them used for irrigation. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to al-Zubayr: 'Irrigate, O Zubayr, then send the water to your neighbour.' The Ansari became angry and said: 'O Messenger of God, is it because he is your cousin?' The face of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) changed colour. Then he said: 'Irrigate, then hold back until the water reaches the walls.' Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) gave al-Zubayr his full right at that time. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had previously offered al-Zubayr an opinion containing ease for him and for the Ansari. When the Ansari angered the Messenger of God (ﷺ), he gave al-Zubayr his full right in the clear ruling." ʿUrwah said: "al-Zubayr said: 'By God, I do not think this verse was revealed except concerning that: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves﴾'" (1).

When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) ruled for al-Zubayr that he should irrigate his crop and then release the water to his neighbour, this did not please Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah, who said: "Because he is your cousin!" The Arab speaks a word and leaves it to the listener's perception to deduce the rest, as if he meant: "You judged in his favour because he is your cousin." He twisted his cheeks. The face of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) changed for a moment, for he knew that the son of Abi Balta'ah had not appreciated the justice and judgement of the Truth. Many people who were looking for faults in Islam said: "He first ruled that al-Zubayr should irrigate, then release the water to Hatib." When Hatib became angry, the Messenger said to al-Zubayr: "Irrigate, O Zubayr, take your full right, take from the water what suffices you, then send it to your neighbour." They said: "Why did he first rule that he should irrigate and then send the water to his neighbour, and then correct the judgement?" People did not understand that al-Zubayr's land was higher while Hatib's land was lower. If you look at any valley, you find greenery and fertility at the bottom of the valley and not on the slope, because water, even if it comes from high land, will descend to low land, and if you irrigate the low land first and give it to him, nothing reaches the high land.

So the first ruling was based on ease and a favour from al-Zubayr, and the second ruling came based on justice. The Messenger, by the second ruling, namely that al-Zubayr take his full right and take from the water what suffices him, was as if saying: "We will now deal justly with you after having been accommodating to you." Then the Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves; then they find within themselves no discomfort from what you have decided and submit completely﴾.

If this is the case, what would happen if We dealt with them as the Messenger did, as with the earlier nations, when they were commanded to kill themselves or leave their homes? This ruling was carried out only by a small number of them, who were firm in faith. Thus we know that the Truth did not leave the community without obedient, committed people who perform God's command as it should be performed.

﴿And if they had done what they were instructed﴾. Even if we suppose that God had said: "Kill yourselves, or leave your homes," and then they did it, they would have found in that good beyond what was in their minds. For people must reflect and ask themselves: what is the goal of the believer when he believes in a God? And what is the goal of this faith?

You, in your worldly life, live with the causes God created for you, and when you move to God, you live with the Causer. So what would sadden you when He tells you: "Kill yourself"? He tells you: "Kill yourself," for you are moving to the Causer and will live without toil.

Indeed, the command from God is an elevation of the human being. In our worldly life we find someone who rings a bell and food comes to him, rings a bell and tea comes to him, rings a bell and sweets come to him. But the world cannot ascend to a state where, whenever a thing crosses a person's mind, it appears before him, so that he does not ring a bell nor exert himself. Would we, having made the believer live among causes, then want to move him to live with the Causer? Would this sadden him? No, because they will find something better.

If you compare the matter, you will find that the life of this world, in relation to you, is uncertain and limited, and your bliss is in proportion to your means. But when you move to meet God, you are not limited, neither by your lifespan nor by your means, but you live for a time that has no bounds, and you enjoy in it according to the vastness of God's grace.

﴿And if they had done what they were instructed, it would have been better for them and more firmly affirming﴾. This good is more firmly affirming for others, because those who see them carrying out God's command will be convinced that they are going to something better than what they have. Thus it strengthens those who come after them. Or the meaning is: if they had done what they were commanded, namely following the Messenger of God (ﷺ), obeying him, and submitting to what he sees and rules, for he does not speak from desire, that would have been better for them in their worldly life and their Hereafter, and stronger and more firmly establishing faith in their hearts, and further from doubt about it.

(1) Narrated by al-Bukhari in the chapter on reconciliation (al-Sulh), and Muslim in the chapter on virtues (al-Fada'il), and al-Tirmidhi in the chapter on judgements (al-Ahkam), al-Nasa'i in the chapter on judges (al-Qudat), and Ibn Majah in the introduction (al-Muqaddimah).

Then, if they did what they were admonished to do, [it would be better for them and firmer in establishing them], "and We would have given them from Us a great reward." And when you hear "from Us" (min ladunna), know that it is not a matter of the creation's own doing or action, but of the Creator's bounty. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, sends us His method through the messengers, but He makes clear that some people He has granted compassion and given knowledge from His presence (min ladunhu ʿilman). He says: ﴿So they found a servant of Our servants, whom We had given mercy from Us and taught him knowledge from Us﴾ (Surat al-Kahf) [18:65].

That is, the knowledge that God gave to that servant was not taught to Moses, and God's giving of knowledge is subject to His will. We already know that good deeds and works have a system: whoever does a good deed receives a corresponding number of good deeds. But there are deeds whose rewards are without reckoning, and the Truth rewards them by His own bounty. Let me give an example, and to God belongs the highest comparison. We find this represented in many of our own dealings. You say to your son, for instance: "My son, how much is your wage from me for this work?" He says: "One hundred pounds." You say to him: "This hundred is your wage, and on top of it fifty from me myself." What does this "from me myself" mean? It means that this amount has no connection to the wage of the work.

﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves"﴾. We have already known that there is a difference between killing (qatl) and dying (mawt). It is true that both involve the removal of life, but death is the removal of life without breaking the structure of the body, whereas killing is the removal of life by breaking the structure, such as when a person smashes another person's head, or fires a bullet that stops his heart. This is a demolition of the structure, and the soul does not dwell except in a structure that has specific characteristics. The soul did not depart first; rather, the structure was destroyed first, so it is no longer fit to be a dwelling for the soul. The well-known example is the electric lamp: if you throw a small stone at it, it breaks and the light goes out, even though the electricity still exists, but it gives no light except in a vessel with particular specifications. When those specifications are gone, the light goes. You then bring a new lamp with the proper specifications, and you find the light has come.

Likewise, the soul dwells only in a body with particular specifications. If you strike these specifications, whose master is the brain, with a harsh blow, you have broken the structure, and in this case the soul leaves the body because it is no longer fit for it. But death comes without breaking the structure. The confirmation of this is the saying of the Truth, glorified and exalted:

﴿Muhammad is but a messenger; [messengers have passed away before him]. So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?﴾ (Surat Al ʿImran, part of 3:144).

That is, there are two matters: there is death and there is killing. Death is the removal of life, and killing is also the removal of life, but killing is the removal of life after the breaking of the structure in which the soul dwells. It differs from death, because death is the soul's departure without killing. That is why they say: "He died a natural death (mata ḥatfa anfihi)," meaning he died on his bed and nothing happened to him.

As for the one who is killed in the cause of God, our Lord says concerning him: ﴿And do not think of those who have been killed in the way of God as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾ (Surat Al ʿImran) [3:169].

So if one who fights in the way of God has complied with God's command, he will find greater bounty. How then will the reward be for one who kills himself in compliance with his Lord's command? The testing of the self is by the self, not by the enemy. And what is the distinction of our master Ibrahim? Did the Truth say to him, "I shall cause your son to die"? Or did He tell him that someone else would kill your son? No, He said to him: "Slaughter him yourself." This is the elevation of self-sacrifice, and then the Truth ransomed Isma'il, peace be upon him, with a great ram. So when a command comes that a person kill himself, there must be a higher rank. ﴿And if they had done what they were admonished to do, it would have been better for them and firmer in establishing them, and We would have given them from Us a great reward﴾.

We are faced with two matters: either they are killed, or they leave their homes. So His saying ﴿and We would have guided them to a straight path﴾ is addressed to whom? To the one who was killed or to the one who left? It is addressed to the one who left his home, because he is still alive.

نص مكرر لاشتراكه مع الآية ٦٧: ﴿فهم إذا فعلوا ما يوعظون به﴾، ﴿وإذا لأتيناهم من لدنا أجرا عظيما﴾. وساعة تسمع ﴿من لدنا﴾ اعرف أنها ليست من شأن ولا فعل الخلق، بل من تفضل الخالق. فالحق سبحانه وتعالى يرسل لنا منهجه بوساطة الرسل، لكنه يوضح أن بعضا من الناس منحهم عطفا وأعطاهم من لدنه علما، فهو القائل: ﴿فوجدا عبدا من عبادنا آتيناه رحمة من عندنا وعلمناه من لدنا علما ٦٥﴾ (سورة الكهف).

أي أن العلم الذي أعطاه الله لذلك العبد لم يعلمه موسى، وعطاء الله للعلم خاضع لمشيئته. ونعرف من قبل أن الحسنات والأعمال لها نظام، فمن يعمل خيرا يأخذ مقابله كذا حسنة، ولكن هناك أعمال حسناتها من غير حساب، ويجازي عليها الحق بفضله هو. وأضرب هذا المثل ولله المثل الأعلى: نحن نجد ذلك متمثلا لنا في كثير من تصرفاتنا، تقول لابنك مثلا: يا بني كم أجرك عندي من هذا العمل؟ فيقول لك: مائة جنيه. فتقول له: هذه مائة هي أجرك، وفوقها خمسون من عندي أنا. ماذا تعني "من عندي أنا" هذه؟ إنها تعني أنه مبلغ ليس له دخل بأجر العمل.

﴿ولو أنا كتبنا عليهم أن اقتلوا أنفسكم﴾. لقد عرفنا من قبل أن هناك فرقا بين القتل والموت. صحيح أن كليهما فيه إذهاب للحياة، لكن الموت إذهاب للحياة بدون نقض البنية للجسم، ولكن القتل إذهاب للحياة بنقض البنية، كأن يكسر إنسان رأس إنسان آخر، أو يطلق رصاصة توقف قلبه، وهذا هدم للبنية. والروح لا تحل إلا في بنية لها مواصفات، والروح لم تذهب أولا، بل أن البنية هدمت أولا، فلم تعد صالحة لسكنى الروح. والمثل المعروف هو مصباح الكهرباء: إنك إن رميت عليه حجرا صغيرا ينكسر وينطفئ النور، برغم أن الكهرباء موجودة، لكنها لا تعطي نورا إلا في وعاء له مواصفات خاصة، فإذا ذهبت هذه المواصفات الخاصة يذهب النور، فتأتي بمصباح جديد له المواصفات الخاصة الصالحة فتجد النور قد جاء.

وكذلك الروح لا تسكن إلا في جسم له مواصفات خاصة، فإن جئت لهذه المواصفات الخاصة وسيدها المخ، وضربته ضربة قاسية، فقد نقضت البنية، وفي هذه الحالة تغادر الروح الجسد لأنه غير صالح لها. لكن الموت يأتي من غير نقض للبنية، ومصداق ذلك قول الحق سبحانه وتعالى: ﴿وما محمد إلا رسول قد خلت من قبله الرسل أفإين مات أو قتل انقلبتم على أعقابكم﴾ (من الآية ١٤٤ سورة آل عمران).

أي أن هناك أمرين: هناك موت، وهناك قتل. فالموت هو سلب الحياة، والقتل هو سلب الحياة، ولكن القتل سلب الحياة بعد نقض البنية التي تسكن فيها الروح، ويختلف عن الموت لأن الموت هو خروج الروح دون قتل، ولذلك يقولون: "مات حتف أنفه" (أي مات على فراشه، والمعنى أنه مات بغير سبب ظاهر من عنف)، أي مات على فراشه ولم يحدث له أي شيء.

والذي يقتل في الشهادة يقول فيه ربنا: ﴿ولا تحسبن الذين قتلوا في سبيل الله أمواتا بل أحياء عند ربهم يرزقون ١٦٩﴾ (سورة آل عمران).

فإذا كان من يقاتل في سبيل الله قد امتثل لأمر الله فسوف يجد فضلا أكثر، فكيف يكون جزاء من يقتل نفسه امتثالا لأمر ربه؟ إن امتحان النفس يكون بالنفس، وليس امتحان النفس بالعدو. وما الميزة في سيدنا إبراهيم (عليه السلام)؟ هل قال له الحق: أنا سأميت ولدك؟ أقال له إن واحدا آخر سيقتل ابنك؟ لا، بل قال له: اذبحه أنت. وهذه هي ارتقاء قتل النفس، فيفدي الحق إسماعيل (عليه السلام) بكبش عظيم. إذن فإذا جاء الأمر بأن يقتل الإنسان نفسه فلابد أن هناك مرتبة أعلى. ﴿ولو أنهم فعلوا ما يوعظون به لكان خيرا لهم وأشد تثبيتا، وإذا لآتيناهم من لدنا أجرا عظيما﴾.

ونحن أمام أمرين: إما أن يقتلوا، وإما أن يخرجوا من ديارهم، فقوله: ﴿ولهديناهم صراطا مستقيما﴾ لمن؟ للذي قتل أم لمن خرج؟ هو قول لمن أخرج من دياره لأنه ما زال على قيد الحياة.

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 4, verse 69:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor of the prophets, the steadfast lovers of truth (al-siddiqin), the martyrs, and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.﴾

The verb here is "yuti'" (obeys), and the one obeyed is: Allah and the Messenger. That is, this matter is the legislation of Allah together with the application of His Messenger, i.e., by the Book and the Sunnah. Whenever you find the Messenger conjoined to al-Haqq without repetition of the verb, know that the matter is one: that is, there is not a separate command for each of them; rather it is a single command, a statement from Allah and an application by the Messenger, because he is the exemplar and the model. Therefore the Truth says of a single verb: ﴿And they disbelieved after their Islam, and they planned that which they did not attain, and they did not resent except that Allah and His Messenger enriched them from His bounty. So if they repent, it will be better for them﴾ (Qur'an 9:74).

Allah enriched them with a wealth suited to Him, and the Messenger enriched them with a wealth suited to him, so the verb here is one. The enrichment here is from Allah and His Messenger, because the Messenger does not act except by the leave of his Lord and in compliance with His command, so the matter is one.

There is an issue addressed in the Book which may preoccupy many of the people who lived in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). His gathering (ﷺ) would not turn away anyone who came; one would come and sit where the gathering ended. Whoever wished to be with the Prophet constantly continued sitting, and whoever wished to see him from time to time would come whenever he wished. Thawban, the freed slave of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), loved the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intensely and had little patience being apart from him. One day he came to him, his face changed, his body wasted and emaciated, and sorrow was evident on his face. The Prophet asked him, saying: "What is wrong with you, Thawban?" He said: "By Allah, I have no illness or ailment, but I love you and long for you. I know that in this world I see you whenever I wish, but in the Hereafter you will go to 'Illiyyun with the prophets, and if I enter Paradise I will be in a dwelling below your dwelling, and if I do not enter, that is the time when I will never see you."

The text of the hadith as narrated by Ibn Jarir with his chain from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "A man from the Ansar came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was grieving. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: 'O so-and-so, why do I see you grieving?' He said: 'O Prophet of Allah, a thing I was pondering.' He said: 'What is it?' He said: 'We come to you in the morning and in the evening, we look at your face and sit with you, but tomorrow you will be raised with the prophets and we will not reach you.' The Prophet (ﷺ) did not answer him anything, and then Jibril came to him with this verse: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor of the prophets﴾. So the Prophet (ﷺ) sent for him and gave him good news.(1)"

How can such a thought come to mind? He is a person preoccupied with his love for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he reflects: will this blessing endure for him? He contemplates Paradise and its dwellings, and how the station of the Messenger will rise above all dwellings. Thawban wants to be reassured that the blessing of seeing the Prophet (ﷺ) will not end or be taken from him. He sees him in this world, but what happens in the Hereafter: either he enters Paradise or does not enter it; if he does not enter Paradise he will never see him, and if he enters Paradise, the Prophet will be in a high rank and station. So what does he do?

Look at how love for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is: Allah, glory be to Him, is gentle with such a lover whose mind is occupied with a matter that may not occur to many people. So the Truth, glory be to Him, says, reassuring these people: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those are﴾, that is, those who obey Allah and the Messenger, ﴿with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor of the prophets, the steadfast lovers of truth, the martyrs, and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.﴾ The matter came specifically regarding Thawban, after alerting minds to an issue that may preoccupy the hearts of those who love the Messenger of Allah. You are with whom you love, but the matter is not limited to Thawban. Thawban's words were a cause of opening and reassurance for all the siddiqin, the martyrs, and the righteous. These are categories that encompass all believers. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq was called "siddiq" why? Because he was the one who most fully affirmed everything that our master the Messenger of Allah said, and this statement was not subjected to debate or questioning, whether it benefits or not. When they said to our master Abu Bakr: "Your companion claims that he went to Bayt al-Maqdis and returned in one night, while we travel to it on the backs of camels for months," what did Abu Bakr say? He said: "If he said that, then he has spoken the truth."

He gave no reason for his affirmation except "if he said that," and this is the true siddiq. Whenever Muhammad said something, Abu Bakr affirmed it. And Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, did not wait until the Qur'an was revealed confirming the Messenger (ﷺ); rather, as soon as the Prophet (ﷺ) said, "I am a Messenger," Abu Bakr said, "Yes." Thus he is a siddiq.

There were preparations for people who embraced Islam earlier, because their proofs of faith preceded the Prophet's mission. They tested the Prophet (ﷺ) and knew him, so when he spoke of the message, they affirmed him immediately, because previous experiences and premises indicated that he was a Messenger. An example of this is our mistress Khadijah, may Allah be pleased with her: what did she say when the Prophet said to her that it comes to him in such and such a way and he feared it might be a jinn's possession or madness afflicting him?

Khadijah said: "No, by Allah, Allah will never disgrace you; indeed you join the ties of kinship, bear the burdens of the weak, earn for the destitute, host the guest, and assist in the calamities of truth."(2) This was the first juristic deduction (istinbat fiqhi) in Islam.

This is the meaning of ﴿with the prophets and the siddiqin﴾. And ﴿the martyrs﴾ are those who were killed in the way of Allah. But the believer, when he fights in the way of Allah, should not say: "I want to die a martyr," throwing himself into destruction. Beware of understanding it that way. You are defending a message, and you must fight your enemy without enabling him to kill you, because enabling him to kill you deprives the Muslims of a fighter. Just as the martyrs have virtue, those who remain without martyrdom also have virtue. Islam wants proofs of the truthfulness that its call is true, and only the martyrs establish this.

But can we all become martyrs? And who will carry the method of Allah to the rest? So we need those who remain and those who go to war; this one has a task and that one has a task. For this reason there is "taqiyya," which is that one shows aversion to Islam and allies with the disbelievers outwardly while his heart is at peace with enmity toward them, awaiting the removal of the obstacle, in order to preserve his life so that he may defend and strive in the way of Allah. Its cause is that Islam wants those who affirm the sincerity of certainty that when a person is killed in the way of Allah he goes to a better life and a better living; the martyr confirms this. Therefore, when the agony of death comes to them, Allah, glory be to Him, shows them what they are about to face, so they utter words that are heard by those who have not yet approached martyrdom. Some say: "Blow, O breeze of Paradise," and say a word that shows they are looking at Paradise, so that those behind them can hear.

The word "shuhada'" (martyrs) is either the plural of "shahid," which is the one killed in the way of Allah, or the plural of "shahid" meaning witness, so the shuhada' are those who bear witness before Allah that they have conveyed to those after them, just as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) bore witness that he had conveyed to them.

All the meanings revolve around the meaning of bearing witness to something one speaks of. Thereby we know that we need both: those who are killed in the way of Allah, and those who remain without being killed in the way of Allah; because the first confirms the sincerity of certainty in what the martyr arrives at, and the second gives us the continuation of conveying the call, for he is also a witness: ﴿that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ (Qur'an 2:143).

And ﴿the righteous (al-salihin)﴾: the salih is the one qualified to bear the mission of faith-based vicegerency on earth. Everything that yields benefit leaves it in its state; and if one wishes to increase the beneficial, let him raise the benefit from it. For example: water descends from the sky, then becomes streams, flows in valleys, and the earth absorbs it so that it emerges as springs. When one sees a spring of water, he leaves it and does not fill it in, and thus he has left the righteous in its righteousness. And another raises the benefit from that blessing and builds around it in order to preserve it. Thus this one has reformed by increasing its righteousness.

And there is a third who says: instead of people coming from their places with their animals to fetch water in waterskins or on the heads of carriers, why not use human intellect to advance service to people, so that water reaches people in their places? Here he builds high cisterns and connects them with pipes and tubes to everyone who wants water, so that he opens the tap and finds what he wants. Whoever does this eases matters for people, and so he is a reformer, having come to the righteous in himself and increased its righteousness.

The Truth concludes the verse with: ﴿And excellent are those as companions.﴾ And ﴿those﴾ means the prophets, the siddiqin, the martyrs, and the righteous, and there is no better companionship than this. The rafiq (companion) is the one who accompanies you always, at home and on journeys. For this reason they say: "Take the companion before the road," for you may encounter hardships and obstacles on the road, because you have departed from the routine of your habits, so take the companion before the road. We know that in matters of meaning, all are derived from sensory things, and in the human hand there is the "mirfaq" (elbow). The Truth says:

﴿So wash your faces and your hands to the elbows﴾ (Qur'an 5:6).

When a person is exhausted and his head is tired, he leans on his elbow to rest; and when he wants to sleep and finds no pillow, he also leans on his elbow. Thus the whole root derives from rifq (gentleness): "rafiq" is derived from rifq, and "mirafiq" is derived from rifq because it is gentle to the body and relieves it. In every house there are "marafiq" (utilities), which are the place for preparing food and likewise the toilet; in the countryside the marafiq increase so that there is a place to shelter the animals that serve the farmer; and the homes of the poor may be a single room containing a place for sleeping and a place for eating, and the poor man may tie his donkey in a corner of the room. But when one is well-off, he equips his house with complete marafiq: that is, the house has a separate kitchen, a place for relieving oneself, a separate stable for livestock, and likewise a separate storeroom. All of these are called "marafiq" because they relieve all people.

Thus His saying ﴿And excellent are those as companions﴾ is derived from rifq, which is: bringing ease, companionship, and comfort; and this person who obeyed Allah and His Messenger will be in the company of the prophets, the siddiqin, the martyrs, and the righteous.

Someone may say: how can all of these be together in one rank, despite the difference in their deeds in this world? Did not Allah say:

﴿And that man will have only what he strove for﴾ (Qur'an 53:39).

We say: since the believer obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger, is that not part of his striving? This obedience and love for Allah and His Messenger are part of the servant's striving; therefore there is no contradiction between the two verses, because a person's work is his striving, and it becomes his right to be in the company of the prophets, the siddiqin, the martyrs, and the righteous. The companionship may be an honor for all of them, so that they may enjoy the company; and this matter will explain to us His saying:

﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts﴾ (Qur'an 7:43).

When one sees that another's rank in the Hereafter is higher than his own, beware of thinking that he will say: "My rank is higher than this one's"; for since he left the causes in this world and lived with the Causer of causes, out of his love for Allah he loves everyone who heard the words of our Lord in this world, and says to every lover of Allah: "You deserve your rank," and rejoices for the one whose rank is higher than his.

Let me give this example, and to Allah belongs the highest example: suppose there is a class with many students, some of whom want only to pass, and some love knowledge for its own sake. When the lovers of knowledge find a brilliant student, do they hate him or love him? They love him, ask him, rejoice in him, and say: "This is first among us," because he does not love himself but loves others. Likewise the believer who has a rank in Paradise and sees another in a higher rank: beware of saying that his soul is stirred by jealousy—no. Because out of his love for his Lord and his esteem for Him, he loves whoever was obedient to Allah and rejoices for him, like the student who attains a high mark

Notes:
1. Narrated by Ibn Jarir.
2. Narrated by al-Bukhari.

The bounty of God draws its basis from man's striving. His saying, ﴿And that man will have nothing except what he strove for﴾, defined the right that is yours and that the justice of the *taklif* (religious obligation) requires. But our Lord did not say that this reward is due to you from God as a matter of right and justice. It comes from His bounty, and God's bounty is the reason for the believer's joy. However much you do in fulfilling your obligation, you will never perform it as it should be performed in relation to God. So God made it clear to us: Take note. I have imposed obligations on you, and you may act and strive, but do not rejoice in the good deeds this action will accumulate. Your joy will instead be in what your Lord gives you of His bounty. He, glorified is He, said:

﴿Say: "In the bounty of God and in His mercy, so let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate."﴾ (Surat Yunus)

This bounty of God also answers those who ask: How can a man such as Thawban, or someone other than Thawban, be in Paradise with the Prophets, the truthful ones (*siddiqun*), and the righteous? We say: Had his rank not been lower, there would be no bounty in it. He attains this bounty because his obedience to God and His Messenger was above every other obedience. As for his love for God and for the Messenger, this is from his striving and his action, through God's grant of success to him, for my success is only through God. The bounty is the reason for the believer's joy: ﴿That is the bounty from God, and sufficient is God as Knower.﴾ We are content, we rejoice, and we are satisfied with the knowledge of God, because He, glorified is He, bases His rulings on comprehensive and all-encompassing knowledge, and He knows the sincerity of the heart's love, the sincerity of affection, and the sincerity of the believer's esteem for one who surpasses him in rank.

Now that the Truth has made us secure in our believing homeland, and our Islamic community is bound together by the principles He mentioned, which are: that we render trusts to their owners. When we render trusts, we will not need to go to litigation. If some of us neglect and fail to render a trust, and a dispute arises, then judgment will come with justice. After that, we refer all our affairs to God and to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and we do not refer them to the *tawaghit* (false powers). Bring me one believing community that renders trusts and does not feel reassured.

We have learned that a trust is a right belonging to another person that you hold in your charge and must render. Everything other than you is "other," and you are "other" in relation to everything else. So all of it becomes a matter of good that is open to all people. When negligence occurs, justice comes. Justice requires a judge, and when we come to judge, we refer to God and the Messenger. Beware of referring to the *taghut* in the past. Even now, there are people like Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf. Rather, there are many *tawaghit*.

When you see a defect in the Islamic world, know that there is a defect in applying the Islamic *taklif*. How can our affairs be set right while we are far from the method of Islam's complete obligations? Had affairs been set right, that would be testimony that this method is unnecessary. But when something happens, this is evidence of the truthfulness of the *taklif*.

After He reassured us about our final destiny with the Prophets, the truthful ones, and the martyrs, God, glorified is He, made clear: Notice that every message of good that descends from heaven to earth came only to fight corruption and to eliminate corruption that has spread over the earth. This is because the human soul either has a restraint from within itself, such that it may intend a sin once, then rebuke itself and return to the method, and its immunity is intrinsic. Or the immunity is not intrinsic in the soul but intrinsic in the environment. For example, we find a person who cannot control himself, but he finds another who says to him: "This is shameful." This means the environment still contains good. The earlier nations had lost immunity and became of one form and one course, which is what the Truth depicts in His saying: ﴿They did not forbid one another from wrongdoing that they committed.﴾ (Surat al-Ma'idah, verse 79)

Thus the immunity of the self has become corrupt, and there is no immunity in the society, so heaven intervenes. But the Truth favored the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) and distinguished it over other nations, because its immunity is always in the persons of its individuals. If it is not in the individuals, then it is in the collective. The believing society cannot be devoid of an individual who says: "No." Therefore no Messenger will come after the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Had a catastrophe been going to occur that would corrupt society with no one in it saying "No," then a Messenger would necessarily have come. But Muhammad was the Seal of the Prophets, because God, glorified and exalted is He, favored the community of Muhammad by making its restraint always either from its own self, such that each individual checks himself and his soul is self-reproaching (*lawwamah*), or an immunity in the society, where each one counsels and each one is counseled. Read the saying of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He:

﴿By time! Indeed, mankind is in loss, except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience.﴾ (Surat al-'Asr)

"They advised each other" — why? Because the human soul is changeable. My soul may be stirred to depart from the method once, and another person forbids me, and I return it to him and guide him and direct him to the straight path. Another person errs, and I tell him and forbid him. So His saying "*wa tawasaw*" (and they advised each other) means: let each one of you be both an advisor and one advised. We all look at one another and observe one another; whoever is weak in something finds someone to set him straight. So it is not impossible that in the Muhammadan community there will be one who advises to good and is also advised to good, and in the single soul there may be one who advises in one situation and is advised in another situation, so that he does not refuse if another advises him, because he was advising yesterday. As they said: "May God have mercy on a man who points out my faults to me."

Now that the Truth has completed the building of the believing environment through the message of Muhammad (ﷺ), and you have become the last of the nations, He, glorified is He, reassures us that evil will not overwhelm us, and a believing immunity will remain among us, even if one people does not adhere, another people will adhere. If a human being does not adhere in all his conduct, he will adhere in some and leave others. Had heaven not intervened with a straight method, the world would become exhausted. And how would the world become exhausted? The world becomes exhausted when the methods of the Truth, which has made us vicegerents on earth, are disabled. Then the manifestations of tyranny and force dominate the manifestations of weakness, and each person's desire rules him.

In our contemporary world, we see that even among nations that do not believe in a religion, their peoples are not left to the desires of individuals. Rather, they organize life through legislation that may burden them. Nations that are not religious have set up for themselves a system that restrains the desire of the self. We say to them: You have acted according to the measure of your thinking, and according to the measure of your knowledge of human traits, and according to your knowledge of temperaments, and you have erred in this, because you legislate for something you did not create with something you did not make.

The root of legislation (*taqnin*) is that you legislate for something you made. As we have said, the one who writes the maintenance program for any machine is the one who made the machine. Would the maker of the television leave the butcher to write the maintenance program for the television? No. The one who made the television is the one who writes its maintenance law. How much more so the One who created us? He is the one who writes the law of my maintenance: "Do" and "Do not." You humans control things according to the desires of some people and say: "Do this and do not do that." On what basis did you know the evils of transgressions? Did you create the soul and know its faculties? No. This is shown by the fact that you amend your laws, and amendment occurs, as we have said, because the legislator discovers an error and corrects it, and the human legislator errs because he legislates for what he did not make. So if we do not want error to appear, let us leave legislation to the One who made, and He is God.

The commentary of al-Sha'rawi on surah 4, verse 71 (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66):

Human history confirms that corruption spreads when the method of heaven is disabled. Heaven intervenes with a message, and every message that came had opponents, namely those who profit from evil. These will not leave God's method to prevail, lest it strip them of this domination, control, oppression, tyranny and profit from evil; rather, they wage war against the messages of heaven. The Truth draws our attention to the fact that the people of evil, those who have slipped loose from the methods of heaven, and the irreligious will cause you hardship. So after you have settled yourselves in faith, be alert to your adversaries and your enemies for the sake of God. The Truth, glorified and exalted, has said regarding this matter:

﴿O you who believe, take your precautions, then go forth in groups or go forth all together﴾ [4:71].

No one says to you "take your caution" (khudh hidhrak) except when there is an enemy lying in wait for you. The phrase "khudh hidhrak" is evidence that this caution is like a weapon, just as they say: "take your rifle, take your sword, take your staff." It is as if this is an instrument you prepare to confront your opponents and guard against their schemes, and you do not wait until the schemes are upon you; rather, you must prepare yourself beforehand against the possibility of some negligence on your part. This is the meaning of taking caution (akhdh al-hadhar), and for this reason the Truth says:

﴿And prepare against them whatever you can of strength and of horses stationed at the frontier, to terrify thereby the enemy of God and your enemy﴾ (8:60).

This means: beware of waiting until they translate their hostility toward you into aggression, for they will hasten upon you and you will have no time to confront them. You believers must take caution because you have enemies, and these enemies are those who do not want the method of heaven to prevail on earth. When the method of heaven prevails on earth, people's desires will have no opportunity to manipulate the destinies of people. And those who profit from their control and their desires over people will find no opportunity for dominion.

﴿Then go forth in groups or go forth all together﴾: that is, let the going forth from you be in proportion to the caution you have. "Thubat" is the plural of "thubah," which means a group, i.e., go forth in companies after companies; and "jamee'an" means go forth all of you to confront the enemy. Accordingly, we must be on the level of the evil that threatens us. If a platoon or a company attacks us, we act as the Messenger of God (ﷺ) acted; he would send a company in proportion to the matter that threatened us, and if the matter was greater than that and required general mobilization, then we go forth all together. And note that the Truth addresses the believers, knowing that they have other inclinations that may arise in their souls even though they are believers. The soul may falter when confronting reality despite the presence of faith.

For this reason the Truth, glorified and exalted, said in Surat al-Baqarah:

﴿Have you not considered the chiefs of the Children of Israel after Moses, when they said to a prophet of theirs: "Send us a king that we may fight in the way of God"?﴾ (2:246).

It was they who were asking for fighting, and since they were the ones who asked for fighting, they should have rejoiced when the command from God to fight came to them; but God knows His servants better, so He said to them:

﴿Would you perhaps, if fighting is prescribed for you, not fight?﴾ (2:246).

The Truth clarified to them: think carefully that you asked for fighting, and beware of not fighting when We prescribe this fighting for you, for I did not impose it initially, but you were the ones who asked. And since the matter was still theoretical, they said, questioning:

﴿And what is with us that we should not fight in the way of God, when we have been driven out of our homes and our children?﴾ (2:246).

They marveled and disapproved of not fighting in the way of God, especially since they possessed the reason that requires fighting, namely being expelled from their homes and leaving their children. But what happened when the Truth prescribed fighting for them? :

﴿Then they turned away, except for a few of them. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾ (2:246).

The majority fled from fighting, and only a faithful few remained. The preludes to these fleeing from fighting were their saying, in response to their prophet when he informed them that God had sent Talut (Saul) as king to them, they said:

﴿How will he have kingship over us while we are more entitled to kingship than he, and he has not been given an abundance of wealth?﴾ (2:247).

That was the first wavering in receiving the ruling. The Truth then clarified to them the secret in choosing Talut: he is strong, and war requires strength; and he is knowledgeable, and war requires careful planning. So He, glorified be He, said:

﴿Indeed, God has chosen him over you and has increased him broadly in knowledge and stature﴾ (2:247).

When they came to fight, God wanted to test them to distinguish the strong from the weak, so Talut said to them:

﴿Indeed, God is going to test you with a river. So whoever drinks from it is not of me, and whoever does not taste it is indeed of me, except one who takes with his hand a handful." But they drank from it, except for a few of them. And when he had crossed it, he and those who believed with him, they said: "We have no power today against Goliath and his soldiers."﴾ (2:249).

The testing here was to know who among them could control himself, and to test the endurance of each fighting man; so drinking from that river was not permitted except a single handful. They drank from the river except a few of them; thus God wanted to purify them with a new purification. When they saw Goliath's army they said:

﴿We have no power today against Goliath and his soldiers﴾ (2:249).

And what was the necessity for all these purifications? God wanted that the defense of His method be borne only by those who are truly believers, and they are the ones who said:

﴿How many a small company has overcome a large company by permission of God﴾ (2:249).

And His saying:

﴿So they defeated them by permission of God﴾ (2:251).

Why did our Lord give us this image of purifications? So that we understand that the human soul, when confronted with a ruling theoretically, has a position; when confronted with it as application, it has a position, even if only in words; and when confronted with it in actuality, it has a position. In any case, a few of the few were those whom God helped. Thus He, glorified be He, wants to instill in our souls that it is He who defeats and He who overcomes, in confirmation of His saying, the Truth:

﴿Fight them; God will punish them by your hands﴾ (9:14).

Accordingly, the Almighty Lord clarifies for us: "I told you, 'Go forth in groups or go forth all together'" — and know that the human soul is the very same human soul, and it will be shaken when it confronts the command to be applied. For this reason He says here, in His words, the Truth:

﴿And among you is one who will surely lag behind. So if a misfortune strikes you, he says, "Allah has certainly blessed me, for I was not present among them as a witness."﴾

So when we call one of you to war, he may lag behind and falter, just as He says in another verse: ﴿What is [the matter] with you that when you are told, "Go forth in the way of Allah," you adhere heavily to the earth?﴾ (part of verse 38, Surat al-Tawbah).

And ﴿ithaqaltum﴾ (you adhere heavily) means that there is someone who grows heavy, that is, who lets himself sink down to the earth by his own choice. We must distinguish between one who is brought down by the pull of gravity alone and one who assists gravity in bringing him down. So the meaning of " athaqala" is that he slowed down and inclined, and this is evidence that he wants to shirk the duty. These people did not merely delay; rather, they swore oaths to that effect. Among them were those who discouraged and slowed others from the raid, such as the hypocrite ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy.

﴿And among you is one who will surely lag behind﴾ — so understand this and take this safeguard against whoever obstructs the advance of the method before the battle even begins, so that when the battle occurs we will have known our strength and prepared ourselves on the basis of fierce fighters, not on the basis of those who delay and drag their feet. For there is one who rejoices at remaining alive when he sees the defeat of the Muslims or the killing of some of them, because he was not with them. So the Truth makes such people manifest and says: ﴿So if a misfortune strikes you, he says, "Allah has certainly blessed me, for I was not present among them as a witness."﴾ He has held back and remained behind, and when misfortune comes upon them, whether killing or defeat, he says to himself: "Praise be to Allah that I was not with them."

So his sluggishness, his staying behind, and his delay from jihad were deliberate and determined within himself. This is the height of boastfulness: he opposes our Lord, and yet despite that he says, "Allah has blessed me." He is like the one who steals and says, "Allah has covered for him." This is the speech of one who has not understood the faithful method. So he says: ﴿"Allah has certainly blessed me, for I was not present among them as a witness."﴾ He was not with them and was not a martyr, and yet he regards this as a blessing. For this reason some of the knowers said: whoever says this has entered into shirk, for in his view misfortune is either killing or defeat. Then what will be the stance of the one who shirks, adheres heavily, and delays when there is booty or victory? The Truth says: ﴿And if a bounty from Allah comes to you, he will surely say, as if there had been no affection between you and him, "Oh, I wish I had been with them, so I would have achieved a great success." 73﴾

Therefore, the reason behind his saying, "Would that I had been with them," is not a retraction of what he had held in his heart at first. Rather, it is regret that he missed the spoils of war. The Almighty, glory to Him, introduces here a parenthetical clause within the verse that gives us a snapshot of faith, saying:

﴿And if a bounty from Allah should reach you, he would surely say, as if there had never been any affection between you and him, "Oh, I wish I had been with them, then I would have achieved a great success."﴾

The parenthetical clause is His saying: "as if there had never been any affection between you and him." Faith-based affection has no price with Him. Had he possessed even the slightest measure of it, he would not have said at the outset, "Allah has blessed me, for I was not present with them as a witness," and he would have been among the fighting Muslims. But he desires only victory and spoils, and he keeps away from the Muslims when defeat befalls them or some of them are martyred.

Thus the Truth reveals to us the stance of those who hold back, and makes clear: beware that you be affected by these people when they cause others to lose heart, or when they urge you to flee in a body. Know that among you are those who discourage, those who lag behind, and those who are sluggish, who care only to take a share of the spoils. For this reason they praise Allah that you were defeated and they were not with you, and they love the spoils and wish for them if you triumph while they were not with you. Beware that you be affected by this, since you have been given this immunity so that you are not taken by surprise by their stance toward you and so that you may be aware of them. Immunities are nothing but the training of the body, if it is a physical immunity, or training in meanings, if some misfortune occurs and you already have an idea of it, so that you build your reaction on that basis.

When an illness attacks us, we take the very microbe of the disease in a dormant form and administer it to the patient. Through this, the body perceives and feels that it has immunity. Then, when the microbe attacks the body in an active form, the body's resistive forces engage with it and encircle it. It is as though giving immunizing injections is a training and stimulation of the body's resistive forces, which God has deposited in your blood so that they may perform their task. Likewise, in matters of meaning, the Truth makes clear to you: there will be among you those who do such-and-such, so that you prepare yourselves to receive these things in advance and are not taken by surprise by them, for if you are taken by surprise, you may collapse. So beware that you be affected by this.

Then Allah says:

﴿So let those fight in the cause of Allah who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter. And whoever fights in the cause of Allah and is killed or triumphs, We will bestow upon him a great reward.﴾ (4:74)

The root *sh-r-y* (شرى) and the root *ishtara* (اشترى) both denote exchange and mutual giving, as in *muqayada* (barter, the direct exchange of goods). You say: "I bought (ishtaraytu) this garment for a dirham," meaning you took the garment and gave the dirham. *Sharā* can also mean "to sell," as in Allah's words:

﴿And they sold him for a paltry price, a few counted dirhams, and they were of those who were indifferent to him.﴾ (12:20)

The company that found Prophet Yusuf (peace be upon him) in the well were "of those who were indifferent to him." Afterward they sold him for a paltry price. So *sharā* is one of the verbs that can mean both selling and buying, because the seller and the buyer are equal in the transaction in terms of value. In earlier times people relied on barter for goods. There was no circulating currency. One person would give some grain and take some dates, another would trade dates for grain. What turned the matter into a form of buying and selling was the existence of goods that were sold for money.

What is the difference between goods and money? Goods are direct sustenance (rizq mubāshir), and money is indirect sustenance (rizq ghayr mubāshir).

For example, you eat a loaf of bread that costs five piasters. But if you own a mountain of gold and you need a loaf and cannot find one, will the mountain of gold benefit you? No. So the loaf is direct sustenance, because you will eat it, whereas gold is indirect sustenance, because with it you buy what benefits you. With this we can define the matter: the goods from which you benefit directly are direct sustenance, and we pay their price with what we do not benefit from directly. Allah, glorified and exalted, wishes to conclude with the believer a transaction involving selling and buying. You know that the seller gives goods and takes a price, and the buyer gives a price and takes goods. And Allah says here:

﴿So let those fight in the cause of Allah who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter.﴾ (part of 4:74)

So the believer here gives up this world in order to take the Hereafter, which is represented by Paradise, the reward, and the station of the martyrs. For this reason Allah says in another verse:

﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for that they will have Paradise.﴾ (part of 9:111)

And after it He said:

﴿So rejoice in the exchange you have made.﴾ (part of 9:111)

That is the transaction which Allah concludes with the believers. He, glorified be He, wishes to give us what enables us to recognize profitable transactions. Each of us in his life loves to conclude a profitable deal, by giving something and taking something greater than it. For this reason He says in another verse:

﴿They hope for a commerce that will never perish.﴾ (part of 35:29)

Here too it is commerce (tijāra). When you want to conclude a deal, you must compare the thing you give with the thing you take, and then distinguish between them. What must be sacrificed for the sake of the other?

Allah has described life as "the world" (al-dunyā), and there is no description lower than this. Let me clarify the matter: you will give the world and take the Hereafter. If what you take is greater than what you give, then the transaction is profitable. The world, however long it lasts, comes to an end. Do not ask "how old is the world?", because it does not concern you whether the age of the world is a thousand centuries. Rather, the age of the world for each individual is the measure of his life in it. Otherwise, if it lasts for others, what benefit is it to me?

So the value of the world is the measure of your lifespan in it, and the measure of your lifespan in it is limited. Although average lifespans have risen in the twentieth century, some say that the average lifespan in America is seventy or sixty-five years, yet that does not prevent death from taking a child, a youth, a man, or an old man.

The age of the world for every human being is the measure of his life in it. So do not compare it with its existence among others, but compare it with its existence in relation to you. Suppose it is certain but limited to seventy years, for example. You will find that your enjoyment during it, however great and grand it becomes, is limited.

Each of us keeps being raised until he reaches maturity (ḥulm). When he reaches maturity and has a personal life of his own, that is, his will is no longer dependent on his father or mother, whereas in childhood all his reliance was on his family. His father brings him clothing and he wears it, brings him food and he eats it, directs him and he turns. But when he has a personal identity of his own, he says to his father: "I don't like this color! I don't like this food! I will not go to this faculty!" A person does not have an independent self unless he reaches a stage of life in which he can beget someone like himself. When he becomes like that, we say to him: "This is maturity," and it is this that gives you personal value.

If you plant a melon seedling, you tend it with water, pruning and fertilizer while it is still small, and you look after it so that it does not come out deformed, until it ripens. At the time it ripens, the main concern has moved from the seedling to the fruit, the melon, so it is said that it has acquired a self of its own. For if you cut it open to eat it, you find that the pulp (lubb) has ripened, and if you plant its seeds, another seedling comes from them.

But if you pick the fruit before ripening, you may find the pulp white and not yet ripe, and those seeds are not fit, because they will not come up and bear fruit like it. If the pulp is half white and half black, it has not fully ripened. But if you find its pulp brown and dark, it is fit for planting and for fruiting, and you find the sweetness in step with the ripeness of the seed. If fruits ripened before seeds, people would hasten to eat the fruit before the seeds were nurtured and ripened, and the species would be cut off. For this reason our Lord did not make the sweetness of the fruit come until the seeds had ripened. So it is with the human being. Allah says:

﴿And when the children among you reach puberty, let them ask permission just as those before them asked permission.﴾ (part of 24:59)

When a person is a child, we leave him to play and frolic in the house and to see this and that. But when he is able to beget someone like himself and his manhood is complete, he must ask permission. When a person is in this condition, he acquires a personal identity. Let us suppose that he will live a number of years, around fifty-five years, after he has acquired a personal identity and is able to beget. He will spend his adolescence in learning until he becomes fit to earn, live, and enjoy. Then let us ask: how many years will he enjoy? We will find it to be a small number of years.

So life is limited, and enjoyment in it is according to one's capacities. He may live in a flat of two rooms or in a flat of three rooms, or in a small private house, or even in a palace. He may ride a car or walk on his feet. In short, it is according to his means. But in the Hereafter the situation is entirely different. He will surrender himself to a life whose duration is unlimited. If you compare the limited with the unlimited, you will find the victory belongs to the Hereafter, because it is certain, and its bliss is according to the vastness of Allah's bounty and power. So it is better for us to sell the world and take the Hereafter, and this will be the profitable transaction that never perishes.

And why does Allah bring the servant into this process of sale? Because Allah, glorified and exalted, before offering you the transaction so that you enter into the sale which exhausts you, whether you are killed or kill in the cause of Allah, must clarify to you the means by which you attain success in the Hereafter. You will not obtain this success by words alone. Rather, look at the program for which you will fight: it is the establishment of a society in which every person discharges the trust (amāna) that is his. No one will object to this except those who want to take the sweat of people and build their bodies from their toil and exhaustion. Bring a society that does not believe in Allah, and say: "O people, we want each one of you to discharge the trust he holds. We want to rule with justice." Then the people of that society will rejoice.

So in order to protect society, we must discharge trusts and establish justice. Before that, He commanded us to worship one God so that we would not be scattered. Then He enjoined us to honour parents and near relatives, or orphans and the needy.

Tell me, by Allah: if this were not a religion from heaven, but legislation from the people of the earth, would there be anything more just than this?

Such a program, which guarantees the security of all, deserves that a person defend its application. Before the fighting was imposed on us, He, glorified be He, made clear: this is the society for which you will fight. Know that when you go out to fight, the most that can happen is that you will be killed, and so you will take the transaction of the Hereafter, and the distance to your goal will be shortened, because everything is measured by the time of its goal.
