If you are killed, the period to reach the goal is shortened, and you arrive at Paradise. Foolishness is what afflicts people when a dear one or a beloved dies, so they drown in grief. We say to them: "Are we not all proceeding towards this goal? Why then drown in grief?"

Allah, glorified and exalted, rewards whoever is killed in the cause of Allah with a life in the unseen world, and in it there is also sustenance. Some people think that if they open the grave of a martyr they will find him alive and provided for. We say to them: Allah did not say that the martyrs are alive in your sight, but alive in His sight, in the unseen world. Allah requires of the one who has been convinced of Islam that he spread it, that Muslims treat one another justly so that their affairs are set right, and that they confront the people of evil who know only the outward aspect of life.

The heavens did not command fighting before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger, before Muhammad (ﷺ), used to convey his message to his people. If they believed, it was good, and if they did not believe, heaven would intervene with punishment: a violent wind, a quake, a cry, the earth swallowing them, drowning. So the messenger before Muhammad (ﷺ) would convey, and heaven would punish whoever did not believe. Fighting only occurred when they themselves proposed it, as with the Children of Israel. Allah says:

﴿Have you not considered the eminent men of the Children of Israel after Moses, when they said to a prophet of theirs: "Appoint for us a king, that we may fight in the cause of Allah."﴾ (part of 2:246)

It was they who proposed it. But the fighting that establishes the principle and spreads the program, to raise the word of Allah and to establish the security-bearing caliphate of faith upon the earth, was not legislated except through the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Allah did not entrust one creation with another except the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ), for He made it trustworthy. You are trusted to take over from heaven the discipline of the one who opposes, and thereby you have attained the high level in the program and the high level in the message. Allah honoured His Prophet, saying:

﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them.﴾ (part of 8:33)

So fighting came, and the Muslims fought, while they were weak in the face of corrupt societies that were strong. The poet says:

"The strong one remains upon error,
and a flock of the weak follows along."

If this fighting had not been brought by a religion, would not the nations that have no religion take it up to set their affairs right? They fight. So why should it be permissible for them to fight in order to establish their principles, but when a religion comes to legislate fighting, they say: "No. This is a religion of the sword"?

We say to them: By Allah, then why do peoples fight one another? You find peoples fighting, and you find one injustice fighting another injustice. When justice appears to dislodge an injustice, do we stand in its way? No. And this is so that we may know that the matter is one of a message from heaven, not the tyranny of individuals who gathered or plotted a coup by which they would dominate the people.

Islam came, and those who believed in it were the weak who could not fight. They had no power to protect even themselves. This is so that we know that when the truth comes, it usually does not come from strength, but comes from a weak person who has suffered greatly in order to establish faith. Islam was proclaimed and called to by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Makkah, but it did not triumph as a religion there, and it did not shine forth except from Madinah. Makkah was the city of Muhammad (ﷺ), and there was his tribe, Quraysh, who had grown accustomed to lordship over the whole Arabian Peninsula, and no one could approach it with aggression. No power could stop its caravans trading to the south or to the north.

Any tribe feared to confront them on the road, because the tribes would come to Quraysh at the season of Hajj, and every tribe feared the vengeance of Quraysh, so

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 4, verse 75:

The verse begins with an expression of wonder. After clarifying the reward for fighting in the way of Allah, it was necessary that this fighting be consistent with human nature (fitrah). In our ordinary speech we say: "What is the matter with you that you do not do such-and-such?" As if we were asking about the reason for abstaining from an act that nature and reason both call for. If a person does not do it, not doing it becomes strange and wondrous. So fighting in the way of Allah, after Allah has made clear that it yields magnificent results, whoever does not do it becomes an object of wonder. For this reason the Truth says: ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight in the way of Allah﴾, that is, to raise high the word of Allah. Sometimes fighting comes about when the believing person stands beside the oppressed one who has been harmed because of his religion. This too is for raising high the word of Allah.

He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight in the way of Allah and of the oppressed men [and women and children]﴾. That is, fighting takes place in the way of Allah and for the deliverance of the oppressed, and in this there is a stirring of human resolve, so that the fighter stands up to lift punishment from the oppressed. Indeed, we fight even out of humanity, for the sake of the oppressed people, to rescue them from torment; for as long as they remain steadfast in faith under this torment, that is evidence of the strength of their faith, and they are more deserving that we defend them and rescue them from torment.

He, glory be to Him, gives us this in the form of an expression of wonder: ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight in the way of Allah and of the oppressed men [and women and children]﴾. It is as if the logic of reason, emotion and religion all dictate that we fight; so if we do not fight, this is a matter requiring investigation.

When our Lord presents such a matter, He presents it on the basis that all people are equal in seeing it as something that causes wonder, just as His saying, the Truth: ﴿How do you disbelieve in Allah﴾ (Qur'an 2:28).

That is: how do you disbelieve in our Lord, O disbelievers? This is a strange matter that does not enter the mind; so let them tell us then: how do they disbelieve in our Lord?

﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight in the way of Allah and of the oppressed men﴾. The word ﴿and of the oppressed﴾ is followed by ﴿men﴾, and it is supposed that a man has strength; this draws our attention to the circumstance that made the man oppressed, and whoever comes after him is weaker still. ﴿Of the oppressed men, women and children, who say: Our Lord, bring us out of this town whose people are wrongdoers, and appoint for us from Yourself a protector, and appoint for us from Yourself a helper﴾. The persecution of the disbelievers toward them reached the point that they supplicated Allah to bring them out of this town whose people are wrongdoers, and the town is "Makkah".

The story of these people tells of some of the believers who were in Makkah and had no tribal support that would enable them to emigrate after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had emigrated. They were prevented from emigrating, and they remained upon their religion, so they became oppressed: men, women and children. The persecution that befell them was fierce persecution that showed no mercy even to children. So the Truth says to the believers: ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight in the way of Allah and of the oppressed men, women and children?﴾

And when these were oppressed, what did they say? They said: ﴿Our Lord, bring us out of this town whose people are wrongdoers, and appoint for us from Yourself a protector﴾. The wording of the supplication indicates that they would not be brought out, but rather that there would remain among them people who trusted in themselves that the protector of their affairs from among the Muslims would come to them; it is as if it conveyed to us that there would be a conquest of Makkah. And so it was.

Allah appointed for them from Himself the best of protectors and the best of helpers, who is Muhammad (ﷺ); so he took charge of them in the best manner of taking charge and gave them the mightiest victory.

Among this group of the oppressed were "Salamah ibn Hisham," who was unable to emigrate, "al-Walid ibn al-Walid," "Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah," and "Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl ibn 'Amr." Our master Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "I and my mother were among these oppressed women and children, and they would constrain us so that we could not go out. Such people were owed support." Therefore Allah inclines the hearts of their believing brothers toward them and stirs up zeal in them so that they fight in their cause; for the oppression of the disbelievers toward them is fierce, not distinguishing between men, women and children in the punishment.

﴿Those who say: Our Lord, bring us out of this town whose people are wrongdoers, and appoint for us from Yourself a protector, and appoint for us from Yourself a helper﴾. And the Messenger of Allah and the Muslims became their helpers.

And then the Truth (Allah) says: ﴿Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the cause of the Taghut (everything worshipped besides Allah, or the transgressor). So fight the allies of Satan. Indeed, the plot of Satan is ever weak.﴾

We have known that the taghut is one who exceeds the limit and is extreme in transgression. The word applies to the singular, the dual and the plural. You say: a man who is taghut (ṭāghūt), two men who are taghut, men who are taghut. The Truth says: ﴿Allah is the Protector of those who believe; He brings them out of darkness into light. And those who disbelieve, their protectors are the taghut﴾ (Qur'an 2:257). So the word taghut applies to the singular, the dual and the plural.

Is the taghut Satan? That is correct. Is it the oppressive tyrant whom submission to his injustice makes more arrogant? That is correct. Is it the one who imposes evil on people so that they guard against his evil? That is correct. All these varieties are called "taghut."

The Qur'anic style varies. Sometimes it says: ﴿There has already been a sign for you in the two armies which met: one fighting in the cause of Allah and another disbelieving﴾ (Qur'an 3:13).

Look at the contrast here: ﴿Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah and those who disbelieve fight in the cause of the taghut.﴾ Here "believe" is contrasted with "disbelieve," and here too "the cause of Allah" is contrasted with "the cause of the taghut." These are opposites of those. In order to know the expressions which our Lord scatters, we must perceive in them the miraculous swiftness. He said in this verse: ﴿Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah and those who disbelieve﴾: these are contrasts, because the disbeliever is understood to be taghut. But when you mention in the second part a counterpart to something omitted from the first, or omit from the first a counterpart to the second, this is called in rhetorical style "ihtibak" (a device of mutual omission and implication). How? 

Here is His saying, glorified and exalted: ﴿There has already been a sign for you in the two armies which met: one fighting in the cause of Allah and another disbelieving﴾, meaning, fighting in the cause of the taghut. Opposite to it is the group which fights in the cause of Allah, and it must be believing.

So the whole speech is coherent. He said: ﴿There has already been a sign for you in the two armies which met: one fighting in the cause of Allah and another disbelieving﴾, and He omitted the description of the first as believing, and He said: ﴿fighting in the cause of Allah﴾, and we will immediately know that it is believing. Our Lord stirs our minds so that He does not give us matters in absolute clarity, but so that we exercise our thinking, so that there is no repetition, and so that you know that when He says "in the cause of Allah" it means a believer, and when He says "in the cause of the taghut" it means a disbeliever.

The Truth continues: ﴿So fight the allies of Satan.﴾ That is, the helpers of Satan who blow on his principles, who support his whispering in their souls in order to spread it among people. These are the allies of Satan, because Satan, as we know, when the dialogue took place between him and his Creator, said:

He said: ﴿By Your might, I will surely mislead them all﴾ (Qur'an 38:82).

But he knew his limits and kept to them, so he said:

﴿Except Your sincere servants among them﴾ (Qur'an 38:83).

That is, the one whom You, O Lord, want, I have no power over. This shows us that the battle is not between Iblis and Allah, for exalted is Allah above anyone entering into a battle with Him. Rather, the battle is between Iblis and the lost ones among creation. When he said: ﴿By Your might, I will surely mislead them all﴾, this shows that he knew how to swear and take an oath, because if our Lord had wanted all people to be believers, Satan could not have approached anyone. But our Lord is mighty above His creation: whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve. From here Satan entered: Satan entered through Your might over Your creation, glory be to You, because if You wanted them all to be believers, Satan would have achieved nothing. The evidence is His saying: ﴿Except Your sincere servants among them﴾, meaning, I have no power over them. The oath of Satan shows that he is studious and attentive to the matter of his entry upon the servants, so he said: ﴿I will surely sit in ambush for them on Your straight path﴾ (Qur'an 7:16).

So Satan will not come upon the crooked path, because the one who walks the crooked path and the wrong road does not want a satan; he is comfortable for Satan and helps him in his task, so he becomes his ally. Thus the allies of Satan are all those who oppose the method, and they are the helpers of Satan.

And the Truth commands us: ﴿So fight the allies of Satan.﴾ Those who have loyalty between them and Satan: this one supports that one, and that one supports this one. The Truth reassures us about this by saying: ﴿Indeed, the plot of Satan is ever weak﴾, because when Satan plots, his plot is set against the plot of his Lord, so his plot must be very weak in comparison with the plot of Allah. Satan has no authority that overpowers the body of a human being to make him act, and he cannot compel you to act, and he has no argument with which to convince you.

The difference between one who forces your body and one who convinces your heart: you do the act while you hate it. As when a person threatens you and holds a pistol to you and says: "Prostrate to me," for example. Then he has overpowered your body. But can he overpower your heart so that you say, "Love me"? No, it is impossible. So the tyrant can compel the body, but he cannot overpower the heart. What overpowers the heart is proof and argument; by it one is convinced to do the act without being compelled to it. So the first is force, and the second is argument.

The Truth, glorified and exalted, makes clear to us: know that this Satan is very weak. He has no power to compel you. If he misleads you, you can say to him: "I will not do it." He cannot come to your heart and say: "You must do it," and carry you to the act by force against your will. He has no argument with which to convince you to act. He is weak, so why do you obey him? You obey him out of your heedlessness and your love of desire. Satan does not overpower your heart, nor does he overpower your body. Rather, he is satisfied to point (suggest) to you! And for this reason Satan will say in his argument on the Day of Resurrection to the creation: ﴿I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me﴾ (Qur'an 14:22).

That is: I had no authority over you, neither the authority of power that compelled you by force upon the body, nor the authority of argument that compelled you by the heart. That is, you are the wrongdoers and I have no concern. So the plot of Satan is weak. And "al-kayd" (plot), as we know, is: an attempt to corrupt a situation by trickery. There is one who corrupts a situation but not by stratagem, and there is one who wants to corrupt it so that if you seize him he says to you: "I did nothing," because he does wrong in secret, and corrupts the situation by deceit. Plotting is not resorted to except by the weak.

The strong person is one who confronts the one who plots against him. The one who slips poison to another person in coffee, for example, is one who commits an act to corrupt a situation by deceit, because he is unable to confront. As for the strong, he disdains to do that. Even one who kills someone, even face to face, we say to him: "You are afraid. By your boldness in killing him you prove that you cannot bear his life." But manliness and courage require that you say: "I will leave him while I am in front of him, to see what he can do."

So the plot of Satan came weak, because he does not possess a power by which he overpowers a body, nor an argument by which he overpowers a heart to convince you. He signals to you by deceit, and you come to him. Only the weak resort to deceit. And whenever one is weaker, his plotting is greater. For this reason people used to say, for example: "Women are stronger than men," because our Lord says:

﴿Indeed, your plotting is great﴾ (Qur'an 12:28).

We say to them: since their plotting is great, then their weakness is greater; otherwise why would they plot? For this reason the Arab poet brings out this meaning, saying:

*A weak woman, when she gets an opportunity, kills; likewise is the power of the weak.*

Because the weak, at the moment he seizes his adversary once, and circumstances empower him over him, says: "I will not leave him, because if I leave him he will do such and such to me." But the strong, when he seizes his adversary, says: "Leave him; and if he does something else, I will seize him and strike him on his head." So if plotting is great, weakness is greater.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 4, verse 77:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿Have you not seen those who were told, "Restrain your hands, establish prayer, and give zakat"? But when fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a party of them fear men as they should fear God, or even more intensely fear. And they say, "Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only You had delayed us to a near term." Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear God, and you will not be wronged even as much as a thread."﴾

We know that when the Truth says ﴿Have you not seen﴾, if it refers to something visible in its time, then you may contemplate the event as it truly is; and if it refers to something not visible, then its meaning is: "Have you not known?" But knowledge through the report of God is more truthful than sight. When the Truth says ﴿Restrain your hands﴾, there must have been the first signs of extending the hands, for no one who has not extended his hand is told, "Restrain your hand." The discussion here is about fighting, so they had been restraining their hands from fighting, as evidenced by the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, saying in contrast ﴿But when fighting was prescribed for them﴾. Thus they were told ﴿Restrain your hands﴾ because the first signs of extending hands to fight had appeared among them, either verbally, by saying, "Let us fight, O Messenger of God," or practically, by preparing for battle. When the Qur'an says ﴿But when fighting was prescribed for them﴾, this statement indicates two periods regarding this verse: a period in which they were told, "Restrain your hands," and a period in which fighting was prescribed for them. From this we understand that there were signs of extending the hand to fight before fighting was prescribed for them. Those who said, "Let us fight," were Ibn 'Awf and his companions; and had the matter of fighting been left to the Messenger, he would have commanded them as soon as they said that.

On the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with him and his father, that 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf and some companions of his came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in Mecca. They said, "O Prophet of God, we were in honor while we were polytheists; now that we have believed, we have become humiliated." He said, "I have been commanded to forgive, so do not fight the people." When God transferred him to Medina, He commanded him to fight, and they restrained themselves, so God revealed ﴿Have you not seen those who were told, "Restrain your hands"﴾ (1).

This is evidence that he was awaiting the command from heaven. Afterward God prescribed fighting for them, and when fighting was prescribed for them, some of them slipped away from it, in confirmation of the Truth's saying ﴿But when fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a party of them fear men as they should fear God, or even more intensely fear﴾. Why this fear, when they are believers? Does this mean that they feared people, or that they turned back on their faith? Just as some of the Children of Israel also requested fighting:

﴿Have you not considered the chiefs of the Children of Israel after Moses, when they said to a prophet of theirs, "Appoint for us a king, and we will fight in the way of God"? He said, "Would you perhaps refrain from fighting if fighting were prescribed for you?" They said, "And why would we not fight in the way of God while we have been expelled from our homes and our children?" But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, except for a few of them. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah).

So when the matter reaches the practical application, weakness and fear may stir in their souls. The Truth, glorified be He, did not prevent misfortunes from afflicting the believer, for as long as a person is not a messenger or infallible, do not say, "So-and-so did such-and-such." Because this person did not claim to be infallible, it is correct that errors may come from him, thoughts may come to his mind, anxieties may come into his head, and sometimes he stands in a position of weakness. Therefore, when someone says to you, "So-and-so did such-and-such, and so-and-so did such-and-such," say to him: "Did anyone claim these people are infallible?" And as long as they are not infallible, this may happen from them.

God says ﴿a party of them﴾, and this means they are not all alike: one party was afflicted with weakness, while another party remained steadfast and firm in its faith, not bent, and no weakness or frailty reached it. Then observe the courtesy of expression: He did not say "So-and-so or so-and-so," but said ﴿a party of them﴾. This requires every person to examine himself, and this is a process by which the Truth intended to conceal the servant. Since the concealment came from the Lord, let us know that our Lord is more jealous over His servant than the servant is over himself. Therefore we always say: when our Lord conceals the hidden matters of people from people, this means honoring all people.

Suppose God revealed to you the hidden matters of people: would you like people to reveal your hidden matters? No. So when you see that our Lord has concealed your hidden matters from people and concealed people's hidden matters from you, know that this is a blessing and a mercy; for a person is a son of his jealousies. It may be that someone has wronged you in his heart and did not wish you to know that, and you also want to be rid of him and hate him. If God had revealed to him what is in your heart, or revealed to you what is in his heart, there would have been a battle in which each of you wounds the other's dignity. But our Lord concealed the hidden matters of His creation from His creation, out of mercy toward His creatures.

And you too, O servant, may disobey Him, and He loves to conceal it from you, and commands others not to pursue reports of your disobedience toward Him. By God, is there a lord like this Lord? A wondrous thing: you may be disobeying Him, and He loves to conceal you, and commands others: "Beware of pursuing the faults of people," for they may have some modesty, and they remain covered in their rags and clothing. Why? So that they do not lose themselves or lose the path of repentance to their Lord.

Thus the Truth has mercy on society, but the disappointment from people is that they insist on knowing the unseen and seek out someone who will reveal their fortune to them. We say to whoever does this: O man, God has concealed the unseen from you as a blessing from Him upon you, so keep it concealed as God wills.

Truly the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, says ﴿a party of them fear men as they should fear God, or even more intensely fear﴾. A member of this party fears fighting and killing, and fears death, because it will take him to the recompense of the deeds he did in this world. Therefore we find one of the Companions saying: "I dislike the Truth." Another Companion asked: "How do you dislike the Truth?" He said: "I dislike death, and who among us loves it?"

And why do people fear fighting? Because God, when He causes death, causes it without demolishing the structure, but enemies in battle may cut off a person's body and mutilate him; yet if the servant recalls the recompense for this mutilation, the matter becomes easy for him.

﴿a party of them fear men as they should fear God, or even more intensely fear, and say, "Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us?"﴾ As if they had forgotten that they themselves had requested fighting; so that we know that the human soul, when it is far from a thing, desires it, and when it comes to it, it opposes it.

﴿"Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only You had delayed us to a near term."﴾ Did this speech come from them as a question? God clarifies this for us: they are saying, "O Lord, why have You tested us with this trial, when we may not be able to bear it in the hour of fear of meeting battles?" Therefore they asked that God postpone it and let them die a natural death, not by the hand of the enemy. The phrase ﴿to a near term﴾ shows that each of them fully knows that he will certainly die, but none of them wants his life to end by killing.

And why do you ask for delay? Out of love for this world and its enjoyments? The answer of the Truth comes: ﴿Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little"﴾, and it is not proper for you, O believers, to be so eager for it that it prevents you from going forth to fight. All of you will die, and each one of us will be recompensed by our Lord for his deeds; but whoever is killed in the way of God, his Lord will recompense him for his deed immediately, and will give him another life in exchange for death, because he will attain martyrdom. Therefore the Truth commands His Messenger to say ﴿Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little"﴾, if you compare it with the great reward a person attains if he is killed in war in struggle in the way of God. Some of them said: "If death is unavoidable, why do we not go to fight in the way of God? If we are killed, let our death be at a price greater than our deeds." Thus this is an arrangement and cultivation of benefit. Therefore the wise man said:

"Had life remained for any living being, we would have counted the brave among us the most astray."

That is, if life remained for a living being, the most misguided people among us would be the brave who kill themselves in war; but the matter is not like that. The Arab poet says:

"Oh you who rebuke me, attend the battle, and witness the pleasures: will you make me immortal?"

And al-Mutanabbi says:

"I see all of us seek life for himself, eager for it, enamored with it, infatuated."
"The coward's love of the soul was inherited from fear, and the brave man's love of the soul led him into war."

So both love their souls, but there is a difference between foolish love and deeper love.

When we look at the overall context of the verse, we find that the Truth, glorified be He, in the early days of Islam was educating the believing community with a faith-based education that does not submit to the tribalism of ignorance nor to the zeal of the self. A group of believers in Mecca who had tasted persecution wished to fight, but the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, informed them that he had not yet been commanded to fight, and he commanded them to establish prayer and give zakat, and to be patient in what they were in until God gives permission for fighting. That was the first education of the believing community, because Islam came while the Arabs had zeal, tribalism, pride, and haughtiness; whenever one of them was provoked in something, he resorted to his sword and his tribe and waged war. So God, glorified be He, wanted to draw out from the believing community anger for the self, anger for tribalism, and anger for zeal, and He wanted to make all anger for God.

When permission for fighting came, it came not to impose a creed on people, nor to compel them to Islam, but to protect the human soul from the stronger who wants to make the weaker subservient to him. He, glorified be He, wanted to free human choice, so fighting was to safeguard human dignity from being a subordinate in belief to another. Afterward He presents the matter of Islam in a rational way: whoever responds to it is welcome, and whoever does not respond may remain upon his religion. This shows that Islam is a religion that prevents coercion over people's beliefs and guarantees them freedom to choose the beliefs they love after clarifying for them right guidance from error.

When God prescribed fighting, He prescribed it without any intrusion of the anger of the self, nor its zeal, nor its honor. The Truth, glorified and exalted be He, wills to depict the human emotions that confront Islam and that Islam confronts in a natural way. He shows us that human nature is treated through education; therefore we find that some of those who requested fighting became afraid: ﴿a party of them fear men as they should fear God, or even more intensely fear﴾.

So there is a difference between the theory of fighting and actually engaging in combat. Therefore you find that some of them feared going to fight, lest they be killed; and killing, as you know, is the demolition of the structure, but natural death is what God uses to withdraw the human soul, without demolishing the structure or breaking it. Also, fighting is the occasion of killing, and fear of fighting is the occasion of delay of the term; killing is a near death before the fighter, but the natural death its knowledge is with God. Therefore they said: ﴿Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us?﴾

Was their request for fighting for the sake of zeal? God wants to free the believer from fighting out of zeal, because He, exalted be He, wants the battle to be faith-based, so that the word of God may be supreme, even if the opponent has ties of kinship, ties of tribal affiliation, or ties of emotion.

The Truth, glorified and exalted be He, wants to teach us this, because the Islamic nation will face fierce violence in establishing the principle of faith-based choice among mankind. So the Truth said to His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him: if they say that to you, ﴿Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little"﴾. The eagerness of the believer to preserve himself from being killed, so that he may die after a near term, means that he wants to take a larger share of life; so the Truth made it clear: No. Set up a measure by which you assess benefit. Thus He said: ﴿Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their wealth in exchange for their having Paradise﴾ (part of verse 111, Surat al-Tawbah).

It is a purchase and a sale. Also He, glorified be He, said about the faith-based transaction:

﴿Shall I direct you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment?﴾ (part of verse 10, Surat al-Saff).

So God deals with us according to the perspective of human utility, and the clever, perceptive, intelligent person is the one who trades in the profitable deal, or the guaranteed one, or the one whose benefit and gain is greater than others.

(1) Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim; also narrated by al-Nasa'i and al-Hakim.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 4, verse 78:

Indeed, when He (glory be to Him) conceals from us the time of death and keeps it hidden from us, the meaning is that a person may meet death at any moment. Is there any clearer statement than this? For although He has not withheld from us the knowledge of its time, He has spread its time across every time, so no one is able to take precaution against the time of death. The same is true of the place of death.

And here is the Truth (al-Haqq) saying:

﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you are in towers built high. And if good befalls them, they say, "This is from Allah," and if evil befalls them, they say, "This is from you." Say, "All is from Allah." So what is wrong with these people that they can hardly understand any word?﴾ [4:78]

Here the Truth addresses the matter of death together with place, saying: ﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you are in towers built high﴾. The human mind, which imagines that it can take precaution against death through place, must understand well that it cannot do so. The presence of a person in some circumstance neither repels nor prevents death from him. Being "with" someone, whether in the camp of unbelief or in the camp of faith, will not prevent death from occurring.

And "being with" (al-'indiyya), as we know, gives the sense of place. The subtlety with which death penetrates is such that it pierces any place and any time, as long as the Truth has decreed it. The enemies of a human being in his health and in his life are many, but if we look at them in terms of violence, we find that violence is in proportion to subtlety. The more subtle and fine an enemy of a human being is, the more violent he is; and the more massive he is, the less violent. Whatever has great bulk may terrify and frighten a person, but a person is able to repel it. But when is an enemy difficult? An enemy is difficult whenever he is small and subtle and does not fall within perception, so that he slips into a person.

An example of this: suppose a man is building a house in an open wasteland, and a person passes by to bless him at the laying of the foundation. He says to the owner of the house: "You have not taken precaution for a place like this. It is full of wolves and foxes, and you must put iron on the windows of the first floor, so that these predatory animals do not enter upon you."

The owner of the house places iron on the windows of the first floor. Then a second person comes and says to him: "You have overlooked that this place has many snakes, and you must narrow the openings of the iron." The owner does so to ward off the snakes. Then a third comes to visit the owner and says: "I am amazed at you, how you guard against wolves and snakes but do not take precaution against the flies of this region. They are poisonous flies." Here the owner places wire on the windows. Then a fourth comes to tell the owner: "In this region there are insects smaller than flies and more violent than mosquitoes, and they can slip through the openings of the wire you place on your windows." So the owner removes the wire hung on the windows and installs another wire whose openings are narrower so that these insects cannot pass through it. Thus: the more your enemy is subtle and fine, beyond perception, the more violent he is.

Therefore the most dangerous microbes are those that slip into a person, and a person does not know how they entered his body or how they knocked on his skin, and he does not know he has been infected until the incubation period specific to them passes and their pains and troubles appear in his body. They enter a person's body without his knowing, and he knows no time or place for it.

He (glory be to Him) draws our attention to the fact that a thing, the finer it is with us, the more violent it becomes, and no entrance can prevent it. So what of death, which is finer than all of this, and no one is able ever to take precaution against it?

And what is the opposite of death? It is life, in which the soul exists within the body. And what is the reality of the soul? No one knows the reality of the soul, although one carries it within oneself. No one knows where the soul is or what its form is, and no one knows who has seen it, heard it, or touched it.

When Allah seizes it, life ends. The Truth is the One who gave the living a soul, and when He breathes it into him, life comes.

Glory be to Him, He draws our attention and alerts us to this, leaving in some of our materiality things whose reality and essence physicians and microscopes cannot know. We do not know, for example, the virus that causes some diseases.

If Allah has given the human being a soul by which He grants him life, why do we not imagine that death has a reality, which, when it slips into a person, takes the soul from him? By this we can understand the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him, in Surat al-Mulk:

﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion, and He is over all things competent. He who created death and life to test you as to which of you is best in deed.﴾ (Part of verse 1 and part of verse 2 of Surat al-Mulk.)

So death is not a negative process, as some people imagine, but a positive process, and it is created with a precise secret that matches the precision of the Creator. The Truth described the matter of death and life in Surat al-Mulk and mentioned death before life; although in outward appearance we see that life comes first and then death comes. No, death comes first, and after it life. Life gives a person a selfhood with which he receives created causes, so he tills the land, trades in things, or makes what suits his life and enjoys hearing and sight, and thus he thinks that life is what was created first.

The Truth alerts us and makes clear: life is not received unless one first receives what contradicts life. He says of Himself: ﴿He who created death and life﴾, and this makes it easy for us to understand the noble holy hadith, which explains to us the situation after the people of Paradise are in Paradise and the people of the Fire are in the Fire, and the Truth (glory be to Him) brings death in the form of a ram and slaughters it.

From Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Death will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be stopped upon the Bridge (al-sirat), and it will be said: 'O people of Paradise!' They will look up fearful and anxious that they might be removed from their place in which they are. Then it will be said: 'Do you know this?' They will say: 'Yes, our Lord, this is death.' Then it will be said: 'O people of the Fire!' They will look up joyful and glad, hoping they might be removed from their place in which they are. Then it will be said: 'Do you know this?' They will say: 'Yes, this is death.' Then He will command it, and it will be slaughtered upon the Bridge. Then it will be said to both groups: 'Eternity, for what you have will have no death in it, forever.'"¹ ²

The embodiment of death in the form of a ram means that death has an existence. Allah tells us that He will bring death to an end, and we will live in eternity without death. He alerts those people who disbelieved and thought that those who were killed in the way of Allah would not have died had they been with them. We say to them: being "with" you does not prevent death. Even if one whose term has come and whose time has arrived were dwelling in towers built high, death would overtake him.

The Qur'anic mode of address is varied: there is what we understand from the words, and there is what we understand from the stylistic guidance of the Qur'an, because it is the speech of the Lord. Human beings address one another with linguistic faculties and rational faculties, but when the Truth addresses creation, He (glory be to Him) addresses all the faculties of the soul. That is why we find a small child memorizing the Qur'an and filled with joy, and one of the adults asks him: "What delights you in memorizing the Qur'an?" The child answers: "I feel harmony, and that is enough." He does not know why he feels harmony from hearing or memorizing the Qur'an, for the speaker is Allah, and He, by His power and the beauty of His perfection, addresses all the psychological faculties.

Glory be to Him and exalted is He, saying: ﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you﴾, meaning: wherever you exist, death will overtake you. The word ﴿yudrikukum﴾ (will overtake you) is evidence that when the soul is breathed into a person, death sets out together with the soul, until it overtakes it at the time Allah has decreed. The word ﴿yudrik﴾ (overtakes) makes clear to us that death pursues the soul until, when it overtakes it, it seizes it. As the good report says about death's pursuit of life: "Until when it overtakes it, it runs off, and none of you is except that it will overtake him." That is why the people of knowledge and illumination say: "Death is an arrow sent toward you, and your life is only the measure of its journey toward you."

Thus we know that His saying, the Truth, ﴿yudrikukum﴾ indicates that death pursues the life of a human being and runs after his soul until it overtakes it.

The Truth says: ﴿even if you are in towers built high﴾. When we examine the root letters of the word ﴿al-buruj﴾ (towers), we can see its general meaning. The root letters of this word are "ba'," "ra'," and "jim," and all of them indicate height and prominence.

It is said: "This is a woman who has a burj," meaning that her eyes are wide and occupy a great part of her face and are clear; so burj is breadth and prominence.

Towers were customarily built high, like fortresses and castles, which we now build of cement and iron. The intent of ﴿mushayyada﴾ (built high/well-constructed) is that its construction has been completed with firmness, for a thing may be high but fragile. As for the built-up thing, it derives from "al-shayd," which is "plaster" (al-jiss), and from "al-shayd" in the sense of "height," and the meaning is that the bricks of the tower are joined in their parts and pieces with plaster, so it is high and cohesive.

When you see a group and it is set against another group, this means that the division gives us units. At the moment a teacher enters the classroom and says to his students: "Take out your books," the meaning of this speech is that each pupil takes out his book. By this analogy: if every person built for himself a towering tower, death would come to him.

The plural is also intended: that is, if you were all sheltered in a tower surrounded by another tower, and a third and a fourth? It is like a fortified fort, for forts are sometimes built as though they were a point surrounded by a small circle, and around the circle another, wider circle. Thus you find the fort as a point surrounded by a number of forts. Death overtakes human beings even if they are in a tower surrounded by towers. Both meanings make clear the power of the Truth to carry out His command of death.

When He (glory be to Him) speaks of death and life in the context of jihad, He wants to bring people out of darknesses into light, for religion is a light that comes upon darkness. Those who live in darkness have become accustomed to darkness and disorder, and each of them transgresses against the others. When religion came, some of them fled from the coming of the light, because light deprives them of the pleasures of error, and because light makes vision clear.

Therefore He (glory be to Him) makes clear that He has brought death to fulfil two needs. The first need: whoever believes must keep death in mind, for his reward has no outlet except that he dies and meets his Lord, and he knows that the barrier between him and the Creator's reward is death. So when he hears the word death, he looks forward to meeting Allah, for he is going toward reward.

The second need: the one who does not believe fears death and dreads it and does not prepare for it, and fears that he will meet his Lord. So the word "death" gives both desire and dread. The believer, when he hears the word death, says to himself: the hardships of this world will not last; I want to meet my Lord.

Therefore believers in Allah must keep this matter in mind. When they keep this matter in mind, every affliction in a dear one becomes easy for them; for a person, as long as he is a believer, knows that the dear one who has departed from him is either a believer or not a believer. If he was a believer, let the believer who has lost him rejoice for him, for Allah hastened him to see his good; but if you grieve for the loss of a believing relative, you are grieving for yourself. And if the one who went to his Lord was not a believer, the believer is relieved of his evil. So death is a relief, and the one who did righteous deeds looks forward to it; this is desire. As for the disbeliever, he is afraid; this is dread.

Therefore it is foolish for a person to grieve over a dead person, and he should turn his attention to the saying of the Truth: ﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you are in towers built high.﴾

The Truth continues: ﴿And if good befalls them, they say, "This is from Allah," and if evil befalls them, they say, "This is from you." Say, "All is from Allah." So what is wrong with these people that they can hardly understand any word?﴾ And to whom is such speech most fitting?

The one who says of good that it is from Allah believes in Allah, and this word has a conception in his mind. The verse does not mean this kind of people; rather, some of them want to separate Muhammad from his Lord. They attribute good and good deeds to Allah, and they attribute evil and bad deeds to Muhammad. On this basis, those who said such a thing are either hypocrites who declared their Islam and loyalty to the Messenger of Allah while unbelief was in their hearts, or they are...

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself. And We have sent you as a Messenger to mankind, and sufficient is Allah as a witness.﴾ (79)

So if a cosmic law (sunnah kawniyyah) brings you good, it is from Allah. But if evil befalls you in a matter in which you have a part (dakhl), then it is from yourself. The matter is of two kinds: something in which you have a part, and something in which you have no part. And you must regard it as good, because it establishes a doctrinal principle (qadiyyah 'aqadiyyah) in the universe.

So the believer stands between blaming himself for a calamity that results from something he had a hand in, and trust in the wisdom of the One who brings about what he has no hand in, and He is Allah, glorified is He: ﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself. And We have sent you as a Messenger to mankind.﴾

And who is the Messenger?

The Messenger is one who conveys (muballigh) from the One who sent him to those to whom he is sent. And since he is a messenger conveying from Allah, whatever occurs from him is from Allah.

When the Truth says: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as a witness﴾, it means: it does not harm you, O Muhammad, that they say, "What befell them of evil is from you," because it is sufficient for you that Allah is on your side, since they possess no power to requite what they say, whereas your Lord is the One who possesses recompense, and He bears witness for you that you are truthful in conveying from Him, and that no evil has come from you as they claimed.

And after that, the Truth (Allah) says:

﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has indeed obeyed Allah; and whoever turns away — We have not sent you as a guardian over them.﴾ (4:80)

Obedience to the Messenger is obedience to Allah, and this is a logical matter, because he is a messenger: whoever obeys the Messenger, his obedience is obedience to Allah, since the Messenger only conveys on behalf of the one who sent him.

Accordingly, in matters of personal opinion which our master, the Messenger of Allah, did as a human being, and which he then put forward as a human matter from himself, and when their incorrectness became evident, the Messenger of Allah gave us an example of his trustworthiness.

On the authority of Anas (may Allah be pleased with him): the Prophet (ﷺ) passed by some people who were pollinating (palm trees), and he said: "If you did not do it, it would be better." He said: so they produced shriveled dates (shees), and he passed by them and said: "What is the matter with your palm trees?" They said: "You said such and such." He said: ﴿You are more knowledgeable about the affairs of your world.﴾ (1)

That is, in matters subject to laboratory experiment and in which the heavens have no role. As for matters subject to the laws of the cosmos, he does not leave them to the servants. It is remarkable that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he acts in a matter for which Allah had no prior decree, and Allah corrects it for him privately, Muhammad is the one who conveys this correction to us, so that we witness in reality that he is truthful in conveying from Allah, even if it be against himself. This noble verse came after the statement of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿And We have sent you to mankind as a messenger, and Allah suffices as a witness﴾ (part of verse 79, Surah an-Nisa').

The messenger, as we know, is one who conveys from Allah His law, by which He wishes to govern the movement of the life of the khalifah (vicegerent) on earth, who is man. When we look at the root derived from r-s-l (ر-س-ل), we find the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, saying in another verse: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he spoke, Satan cast [something] into his recitation﴾ (part of verse 52, Surah al-Hajj).

Thus the messenger may be a messenger in the sense understood by us, and may be a prophet; both are sent by Allah. But the difference is that the messenger comes with a law he is commanded to follow, and he is also commanded to convey it to people so that they may act by it, whereas the prophet is sent by Allah only to affirm an exemplary conduct for the religion that preceded him; he is sent as a behavioral model. But the messenger in his technical sense (al-ist-ilah) brings a new method that may differ in its branches from the method that preceded it. Both are messengers: the one brings the method and the conduct and applies it, and the prophet brings conduct only and applies it, to be a model for a method preceded by a messenger.

And since the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, sent the messengers and made the seal of the messengers our master Muhammad, it means that his message (ﷺ) will be a message against which the heavens have no corrective addition; and if his message (ﷺ) is a message against which the heavens have no corrective addition, how is it conceivable that his message should become a subject for human correction?

Since Allah has concluded the message with him, and revealed to him: ﴿This day I have perfected for you your religion, and completed My favour upon you, and have approved for you Islam as a religion﴾ — so there is no longer any corrective addition from the heavens to this message. How, then, can a person, contemporary or otherwise, come and say: "No, we want to correct such-and-such," or say: "This ruling is not suited to the age," when Allah has not made for the heavens any corrective addition to the message, because Allah has perfected and completed it? How is it permissible for humans to be correcting the message?

The messenger, when he is attributed (idafah), is attributed sometimes to Allah and sometimes to those to whom he is sent, because he is the intermediary of connection between the sender and the one sent to. If you intend the attribution in the sense of "min" (from, indicating origin), you say: "Rasul Allah" — i.e., a messenger from Allah. If you intend the purpose of the message, you say: "rasul ila an-nas" (a messenger to people) or "rasul li-n-nas" (a messenger for people). Thus the attribution comes sometimes in the sense of "min," sometimes in the sense of "li" (for), and sometimes in the sense of "ila" (to).

The matter of the message is necessary for mankind, because a person, if he surveys and traces all existence by his nature and his sound intellect without a messenger coming to him, will be guided by his nature to the realization that this cosmos cannot have come to be except from a Creator who possesses a power befitting this wise and wondrous attribute. And He must be Self-Subsisting (qayyum), because He constantly sustains us with things. But can we know by reason what this power wills? We only conclude that behind the cosmos there is a force, and this force possesses such power, wisdom, knowledge, will and attributes of perfection that it creates this wondrous cosmos in that marvelous form with its precise geometry, and this cosmos has a purpose. Can reason then give a name to this force? Its being a force necessitates that it have power and wisdom, but we do not know its name. So it was necessary that a messenger should come; this messenger gives people the answer to what has occupied them, namely: what is the force that created this cosmos and made it with this wondrous craftsmanship?

Here the intellect pauses. When the messenger comes and says: "I guide you to this force, by name and by what it requires of you," it was obligatory for creatures to prick up their ears to him, because he would resolve for them that riddle which they saw with their own eyes and which put them in bewilderment. The believer and the unbeliever alike believe this, because he finds himself in a cosmos in which serve him kinds stronger than himself that never fail in serving him, and kinds that are beyond his capacity and power, and which produce for him things whose workings his intellect does not comprehend. So it was necessary that he believe.

We have given an example and said: if a person's plane crashed or he was cut off on a road in a desert, with no provisions and no water, and then he sat down, sleep overcame him, and he slept; then he woke and found a table set with choice foods and delicious drink. By God, tell me: would his mind not be occupied with thought about who brought the food before he ate anything from it? Therefore, before we benefit from these things, it was necessary that we draw our attention: who made this craftsmanship? Yet God left us a period so that we might reflect, until a messenger came saying: "The force you are seeking by your intellect has this name and requires this of you; and you are its creature and made by it first, and to it you will return at last."

The summary of the matter: before He created creatures, Allah, glorified and exalted is He, prepared for them the table of the cosmos, in which are the kinds that serve them, as we said: a chain of kinds and their service makes you wonder and ask: how does what is stronger than me serve me?

The sun, which is not within my power; the moon, which I cannot take hold of; the wind, over which I have no control; the earth, with which I cannot communicate: how are these services rendered to me? There must be One stronger than me and than them, and it is He who subjected them to serve me. Have you ever seen any of these things refuse to render you service, or fall short of it in any way? It has never happened, because they are subjected. So when a messenger comes from Allah to resolve for us the riddle of this life and guide us to its Originator, it was obligatory that we open our ears to him and listen; so that when he says to me: "The One who created the cosmos for you is Allah, and the One who created you is Allah, and He is your Maker, and He sent me with a method for you so that you may perform your duty as it should be: do this and do not do that; and you are returning to Him to account you for what you did" — and this method is the essence of all religions.

Therefore the coming of the messenger is necessary; and then Allah, glorified is He, supports him with a miracle that establishes his truthfulness. And since He sent him with the method which is: do and do not do, this means you must obey this Messenger. Our Lord says in another verse:

﴿And We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed by Allah's permission﴾ (part of verse 64, Surah an-Nisa').

That is, obedience is not inherent to him; rather obedience proceeds from Allah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is distinguished from all the other messengers, because his miracle which attests to his truthfulness in conveying from Allah is the very book of his method in its fundamentals, whereas all the other messengers were otherwise. A messenger would come with a miracle and come with a book of method: the staff and the white hand were the miracle of Moses, but his method was in the "Torah"; so the miracle was separate from the method.

Our master Jesus, for example, his miracle was that he healed the blind and the leper, but the book of his method is the "Gospel." Except our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whose miracle, the Qur'an, is the very essence of his method; because Allah willed that in the final religion the miracle should not be separated from the method.

As for the miracles of the earlier messengers before the Messenger of Allah, whoever saw them believes in them, and whoever did not see them hears a report about them; and if he trusts the one who reported to him, he believes him; and if he is not confident, because they are not before him, he does not believe him. Had Allah not informed us of these miracles in the Qur'an, it would have been possible for us to hesitate about them.

As for the miracle of the Prophet (ﷺ), it remains as long as his method remains. Every Muslim can say at the end of the world's life: "Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," and that is his miracle. As for any other messenger, no one can come and say "So-and-so is the messenger of Allah, and that is his miracle," because it happened and ended. But the Qur'an remains as long as the message and the cosmos remain.

When the Messenger (ﷺ) comes with the conveying from Allah, the Truth makes clear to us: "I sent the Messenger to be obeyed." The logic is that the Qur'an should say: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾, because the Messenger came as a conveyor from Allah; the one who is directly before us is the Messenger of Allah. We have known before that if a command of obedience comes from Allah together with a command from His Messenger, we obey both. If Allah has given a general ruling, such as zakat and hajj, and the Messenger came and specified it, we obey Allah in the general ruling and obey the Messenger in the detailed ruling. And if Allah has given no ruling, neither general nor detailed, then legislation came from the Messenger by the delegation with which Allah delegated to His Messenger, by His saying:

﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾ (part of verse 7, Surah al-Hashr).

So the only messenger to whom Allah gave delegation in legislation is Muhammad, Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). All the messengers conveyed from Allah, and none of them conveyed anything from himself except our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); for Allah, glorified and exalted is He, delegated him by His saying: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it.﴾ So the Messenger has a function that falls within the framework of the Qur'an as well. An example of this in our lives: someone says to an employee: "The employee who is absent for fifteen days, according to the state's law, they dismiss him." Then an employee comes with the constitution of the country to reply and say: "This is the constitution, and I have read it and did not find this law in it, and what you say about dismissing the employee is unconstitutional."

We say to him: The constitution said on this matter: "A body shall be formed to regulate the work of those employed in this field." So by delegation there exists a body which sets a system to be applied to the employees, and so this is from the constitution; all the clauses of the employees' law fall within the delegation stipulated in the constitution to the bodies or committees that enact subsidiary legislation. Likewise, if you are asked: "Bring me a proof from the Qur'an that the Maghrib prayer is three rak'ahs, the Fajr is two, the Zuhr four, and the 'Isha four; bring a proof from the Qur'an for these," you say: "My proof from the Qur'an is: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it.﴾" And the Messenger (ﷺ), in order to guarantee the integrity of the method against the distortions they fabricate, said: "Let me not find any one of you reclining on his couch, to whom an order from what I have commanded or forbidden comes, and he says: 'I do not know; whatever we find in the Book of Allah we follow.'"

And in another narration, from al-Miqdam ibn Ma'd Yakrib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Behold, perhaps a man reclining on his couch, to whom a hadith from me is conveyed, will say: 'Between us and you is the Book of Allah; whatever we find in it as lawful we deem lawful, and whatever we find in it as unlawful we deem unlawful.' Indeed, what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made unlawful is like what Allah made unlawful." (2)

I narrate this hadith from the Messenger so that you may know the stupidity of those who say this; and let us say to them: your saying this is itself evidence of the truthfulness of the Messenger. By God, if no one had come with a statement like yours, that there is nothing but the Qur'an, by God what would we have said to the narrators who transmitted the hadith of the Messenger of Allah? And had they not said this, we would have said: The Prophet said: "A man reclines on his couch and speaks," and no one would have spoken contrary to this statement. So,

Here the Truth clarifies to His Messenger: you will encounter a group from the nation of the call (ummat al-da'wah), namely those whom God has commanded you to invite to enter Islam. As for the nation of response (ummat al-ijabah), they are those who responded to God and the Messenger and truly believed. These people say to you, when you command them to do something or ask them for something, whether an order or a prohibition: ﴿They say, "Obedience."﴾ That is: our matter and our affair is obedience, meaning your command is obeyed. ﴿But when they go out from you, a group of them plans by night other than what you say.﴾

It is said: bara means he went out to the open space (al-biraz), and al-biraz is the wide open ground. For this reason, a warrior who challenges someone says: "Come out to me" (ibraz li), meaning come out from the shelter or the fortress. In the past, the Arabs did not relieve themselves inside their homes; when they wanted to relieve themselves, they went to a distant open area (al-gha'it). From this word came the term that expresses relieving oneself in the open (qada' al-hajah fi al-khala').

﴿When they go out from you﴾: that is, they went out. They turn over the matter of the obedience they were commanded to perform in their heads, find it burdensome, and so they plan to disobey. We know that the word "bayt" (house) means the shelter in which a person takes refuge. The best time for taking shelter is the night, so the dwelling we live in is called "mabit" (a place of spending the night), because we usually spend the night in a house that is fixed in a place and made up of rooms, and is covered. They say: "This matter was planned by night" (bayyatahu bi-layl), meaning they arranged it at night. Does this mean they must not plan during the day? No, but it is common that they plan at night. They do this while far from eyes, so they arrange it carefully. If the intended meaning is planning in darkness, this meaning is also suitable; and if it is secret, the meaning is also valid.

Thus the basic meaning of tabyit is that it occurs in a house, and the basic sense of bayta is that it happens at night, and the whole root revolves around concealment. So when something is planned in darkness, we say it was planned by night (bayyata bi-layl), and when it is planned secretly, we also say it was planned by night.

﴿They say, "Obedience," but when they go out from you, a group of them plans by night other than what you say﴾: that is, when they leave, they plan a matter other than what you say. They proclaim obedience with their tongues, while their conduct is the opposite; their conduct is disobedience, or "obedience" other than what they utter. If you say, "Do it," they will not do it; and if you say, "Do not do it," they do the opposite of what you command. They obey their desires and their devils.

﴿They say, "Obedience," but when they go out from you, a group of them plans by night other than what you say﴾: meaning, a group says, "Our matter and affair is obedience to what you say," or "We obey you with obedience," but they plan other than what you say, so they are then in disobedience. ﴿And God records what they plan by night.﴾ God, glory be to Him, records the result of His knowledge. He used the word "records" so that they know their actions are registered against them, such that when their book is presented to them they can read what is written in it. Had it not been written, they might say: "No, that did not happen." The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to warn against this group, because they would weaken the affair of the call. Therefore the Truth clarifies: you will not be supported by those to whom you were sent, but you will be supported by the One who sent you, so beware lest this affect your resolve or weaken it toward the call. If something from a group of them of this kind happens, then ﴿turn away from them﴾, that is, do not address them regarding any of these matters; leave them, and leave vengeance to Me, for I will support you despite their opposition to you, and turn toward the command of God who sent you.

We know that the benefit in all messages lies with the One who sends, but the addressed may be wearied by the new call, because it will take him out of his self's desires and the requirements of his recklessness. So the One who sent you, O Muhammad, is the guarantor for you that your call will succeed.

﴿So turn away from them, and put your trust in God, and God suffices as a Guardian﴾. Why? Because those who believe in you have limited power, limited means, and limited equipment, but the One who sent you can make the number of your opponents and the equipment of your opponents into soldiers for you, and support you from where you do not expect. Therefore, the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, began the matter of Islam when its adherents were few; had He made them many, they would have said: a multitude, if united in injustice, would succeed. But when the few succeed, this is a good omen and indicates that you are not supported by these people, but that you are supported by the aid of God.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 4, verse 82:

Then the Truth says:

﴿Will they not then reflect upon the Qur'an? Had it been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much discrepancy.﴾ (4:82)

When you hear the expression "afala" (will they not), know that the style is rebuking those who do not employ the faculty that follows it. ﴿Will they not then reflect upon the Qur'an?﴾ means: it was incumbent upon them to reflect (tadabbur) upon the Qur'an. There is a thing called "tadabbur" (reflection), a thing called "tafakkur" (contemplation), a third called "tadhakkur" (remembrance), a fourth called "ilm" (knowledge), and a fifth called "ta'aqqul" (intellection). All these styles occur in the Qur'an: ﴿Will they not know?﴾, ﴿Will they not understand?﴾, ﴿Will they not remember?﴾, ﴿Will you not contemplate?﴾. They are, then: reflection, contemplation, remembrance, understanding, and knowledge.

When someone comes to you asking you to bring to mind the word "tadabbur", the meaning is that he is confident that if you exercised your mind vigorously you would reach the sought-after truth. But one who wants to deceive you does not stir up in you the means of inspection. Take the merchant to whom you go to buy cloth: he displays his cloth and wants to prove to you that it is natural and strong and not synthetic, so he wets it for you and tries to tear it, but it does not tear. He stirs up in you the critical senses. So when he stirs up in you the critical senses, the meaning is that he is confident that exercising the critical senses is in favour of what he claims. Had his cloth not been in favour of what he claimed, he would have tried to deceive you; instead he says to you: look carefully and test it.

And the Truth says: ﴿Will they not then reflect upon the Qur'an?﴾. Tadabbur is every matter presented to the intellect in which it has work to do, so you contemplate it in order to examine the evidence of its truthfulness. This is the first stage. Then, once you know the evidence of its truthfulness, look at the outcome that would result for you if you did not act upon it. "Tatadabbar" means to look at the backs (adbar) of things and their consequences (a'qab). The Messenger conveys to you: God is one; investigate the proofs with your thought, and when you reach them you will believe that there is one God. Beware of saying that it is a matter of luxury or sophistry, for when you look at the consequence of not believing in the one God, your reward will be the Fire.

Thus "tadabbartu" means: I looked at the backs of things and tried to see the consequences that arise from them, and this is a stage after tafakkur. Tafakkur requires that you remember what you already knew, should forgetfulness befall you. Tafakkur comes first, and after it comes tadabbur. For example, you say to your son: so that your future may be high and you may become an engineer or a doctor, you must study and strive; the boy then thinks of being of standing like those who excel in the various professions in society, and he exerts effort.

So the first stage is tafakkur, the second is tadabbur. If you become heedless, we say to you: remember what you thought about and arrived at, and reflect upon the outcome. All these are mental operations: thinking begins with the intellect, the intellect also looks at the outcome, then the memory works to remind you of what has passed and what was at the focus of consciousness, then you move to the margin of consciousness. If you have understood a matter for yourself, it is said: "aqaltuhu" (I comprehended it). If you understand what another has comprehended, then you have known what so-and-so comprehended.

So it is not necessary that you have reached knowledge by your own intellect; rather you have taken the yield of another's intellection. For this reason, when our Lord negates knowledge from someone, He has negated intellection from him all the more, since knowledge means one's ability to comprehend the capacities of others, without reaching their laws, rules and principles. He merely knows how to benefit from and profit by them. In our daily lives we find that the illiterate person benefits from television and benefits from electricity; he has benefited from the knowledge of others, yet he does not comprehend the capacities of that scientist. So the circle of knowledge is wider, because you know by your own intellect, whereas in the circle of knowledge you know and understand what another has comprehended.

For this reason, when our Lord presents this matter, He says: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Follow what Allah has sent down," they say, "Rather we follow what we found our fathers upon." Even though their fathers did not understand anything, nor were they guided?﴾ (2:170).

In the same sense, in another verse, when He says to them: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has sent down and to the Messenger," they say, "Sufficient for us is what we found our fathers upon." Even though their fathers did not know anything, nor were they guided?﴾ (5:104).

In the first verse He said ﴿do not understand﴾ because they said ﴿Rather we follow what we found our fathers upon﴾ without rejecting anything else; in the second they said ﴿Sufficient for us is what we found our fathers upon﴾ with insistence on rejecting others and submitting to someone other than Him. So He said ﴿Even though their fathers did not know anything, nor were they guided﴾, and here He negated from their fathers knowledge, which is broader than negation of intellection, because negation of intellection means negation of the ability to derive inferences. But it does not negate that a person may benefit from what another has derived.

﴿Will they not then reflect upon the Qur'an? Had it been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much discrepancy.﴾ When the Almighty and Exalted urges the listeners to listen to His speech, especially those who oppose His method, to reflect upon the Qur'an, the meaning is that He wants them to exercise their minds on what they hear, because the Truth knows that if they exercised their minds on what they hear they would arrive at the matter of truth without dispute. But what puts them in positions where they proclaim obedience {so when they depart from you, a group of them plans other than what you say}: this is evidence that they have not reflected upon the Qur'an. His saying the Truth, ﴿Will they not then reflect?﴾, comes after that verse, as if it came with its evidence preceding it: had they reflected upon the Qur'an they would have known that the Messenger is truthful in conveying from Allah and that this is true speech.

And by God, when they plot in their souls or plot by night something other than what they said to the Messenger of Allah, who told the Messenger of Allah that they had plotted this?

So if they reflected on such matters, they would know that the One who informed the Messenger of Allah of their secrets, their plotting and their deceit is God. Therefore the Messenger of Allah is truthful in conveying from God, and since the Messenger of Allah is truthful in conveying from God, you return to the earlier verse ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾, and all verses serve one another. When the Qur'an was revealed in the Arabic tongue, Allah willed not to make every Arab listener believe in it first; for had they all believed in it first, they would have said: their belief in the Qur'an made them overlook its challenge to them. Yet a people among those confronted by the Qur'an remain in their disbelief, and the disbeliever needs to oppose and counter-oppose. When the Qur'an challenged him to bring its like, and challenged him to bring ten surahs like it, and challenged him to bring the shortest surah like it, this is the challenge to the disbeliever. Does this challenge not stir up in him the instinct of obstinacy? Yet none of them said a word. What does that mean? It means that they were convinced they could never achieve that, and they persisted in their disbelief and were bold, saying what they said. Nevertheless, the Qur'an passes over them and they find in it no point of correction.

It would have been possible for them to say: Muhammad says the Qur'an is inimitable and eloquent, and he has erred in such-and-such. Had they been believers they would have concealed that, but they are disbelievers, and the disbeliever is concerned to spread any error about the Qur'an. Then there come people who lack command of the Arabic language and its eloquence, to say that the Qur'an contains contradictions! How can they manage that, when they have no mastery of Arabic, their language is a manufactured one, and they lack the faculty of eloquence? How can they say the Qur'an contains contradictions? The disbelieving Arabs were more entitled to say so, for they had mastery and eloquence and were contemporaries of the revelation, and they disbelieved in what Muhammad brought, yet they did not say that there is discrepancy in the Qur'an! This is evidence that the orientalists who claimed it suffer from a deficiency in the language.

We say to them: the Qur'an addressed matters to establish its eloquence and rhetoric among the people to whom it was first revealed. Among them were those who would carry the method of the call, then the Qur'an bore other miracles for non-Arab peoples. The miracle of the Qur'an is not eloquence alone; otherwise someone would say: it is the Arabs who are unable, so what of the Persians and the Romans? And we say to him: was all the inimitability in its style? No. The inimitability lies in matters in which all the tongues of the world agree, because it came to establish that the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, by the testimony of his adversaries, had never left the Arabian Peninsula except on a trading journey to Syria, and it is not established that he sat with a teacher. All of them know this. Even the mistake they made, our Lord turned against them, saying: ﴿And We know that they say, "It is only a human who teaches him." The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue﴾ (16:103).

By "human" they mean a slave of Huwaytib ibn Abd al-Uzza who had embraced Islam and whose Islam was good, or another slave who was Roman, or Salman the Persian. The Truth clarified: understand well, Muhammad did not sit with a teacher and did not go on journeys. Then the Qur'an came as a challenge, not by logic, nor by language, nor by eloquence, nor by exposition alone, but by a matter comprehensive to all minds: the book of the cosmos, its events and occurrences, in which all people share.

The cosmos, as we know it, has veils: a past matter is veiled by past time, and whoever lived in its days knows it, while whoever was not in its days does not know it. Thus the events of the past are veiled by past time, and future events are withheld by the future, since they have not yet occurred. The present is before us, and place serves as its barrier. The Qur'an, in its styles, pierces all these veils, and then challenges, for example, saying: ﴿And you were not on the western side when We decreed to Moses the command, nor were you among the witnesses﴾ (28:44).

And He, glorified, says: ﴿Nor were you a dweller among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses﴾ (28:45, part).

And He says: ﴿And you did not recite before it any book, nor did you write it with your right hand; otherwise the falsifiers would have doubted﴾ (29:48).

Every "you were not" in the Qur'an brings reports of things that happened in the past. By God, if they knew that he had learned or sat with a teacher, would they have kept silent?
