By the subtlety of Allah, He did not say "khā'in," because the khā'in is one who betrayed once in passing and the matter ended, and Allah does not remove him from the circle of concealment unless he has taken betrayal as a habit, a custom and a trade. There came to our master 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) a woman whose son had been seized for theft, and 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) wanted to apply the prescribed punishment (hadd) to that son. The mother wept and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, by Allah, he did this only this once." 'Umar said: "You have lied; by Allah, Allah would not seize a servant for his first time."

For this reason they say: when a sin of a man becomes known and manifest, know that it has sisters. Allah cannot expose a person's first sin, because He, glorified is He, loves to conceal His servants; so He conceals the servant once and a second time. Then if the servant persists in the sin, Allah exposes it: "Indeed, Allah does not love one who is a habitual betrayer, sinful."

Al-Ithm (sin) is the most abhorrent of disobediences. The people who went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) seeking his intercession on behalf of Ibn Ubayriq, so that the Messenger would rule in his favour against the Jew, why did they do this? Because they found it abhorrent that the affair of a Muslim should be exposed while a Jew was cleared. They were ashamed for this to happen. The Qur'an dealt with this matter in order to bring the underlying cause that prompted them to do this, and to eliminate such an act at its root. So He said:

﴿They hide from the people, but they cannot hide from Allah, for He is with them when they plot by night in speech that does not please Him. And Allah is ever encompassing of what they do.﴾ (4:108)

They seek to be cleared before the people, claiming that Ta'mah did not commit the theft. But do the people possess what Allah possesses concerning them? He, glorified is He, is more worthy of that than the people. So if you wish to conceal matters in the judgment of the earth, you will not be able to conceal them from the judgment of the heavens. This matter must govern the movement of the believer. If a person attributed to Islam considers doing something that angers Allah, he should reflect: "If I did that, I would disgrace myself, or disgrace my son, or disgrace my family, or disgrace the Muslims." A Muslim should not fear the people if a brother of his does something that brings shame upon the Muslims; rather, he should take him by the hand and turn him back from his deed. We say to whoever hides himself from the people: you have hidden from the people and have not hidden from Allah, and therefore you are not trustworthy to hold any authority.

"They hide from the people, but they cannot hide from Allah, for He is with them": the word "with them" here is meant to make the believer certain that nothing is hidden from Allah. It is possible for a person to conceal himself from people, but he can never conceal himself from Allah, because Allah is with every human being in privacy and in public. If someone is able to hide from people, he will never be able to hide from Allah.

"They hide from the people, but they cannot hide from Allah, for He is with them when they plot by night in speech that does not please Him." "Yubayyitu" means that he carries out his affair at night, because people used to retire to their homes at night. Tabyit means to devise a plot in the house at night. Every scheme carried out in secrecy is called "tabyit," even if it takes place in broad daylight. No person plots in secret except out of desire to escape the eyes of observers. We say to him: you escape the eyes of those like you, but the eternal eyes, which are the eyes of Truth, you will never be able to escape.

﴿They hide from the people, but they cannot hide from Allah, for He is with them when they plot by night in speech that does not please Him. And Allah is ever encompassing of what they do.﴾ (Surah an-Nisa')

When we hear the word "muhit" (encompassing), let us know that ihatah is the surrounding of the encompassed by the encompasser, such that one cannot escape from it in knowledge of his state, nor has the ability to escape from its outcome and consequence. He, glorified is He, encompasses by knowledge, because nothing is hidden from Him, and He encompasses by power, so no one can escape Him to the outside. He, glorified is He, encompasses with knowledge every particular and detail of the cosmos, and He is capable over all things. So when we hear the word "muhit," its meaning is that the True One, glorified and exalted is He, encompasses whatever is encompassed, with knowledge of all its particulars, so that no particular can flee from the knowledge of the Truth. And He, glorified is He, encompasses everything in power, so that nothing can escape its due outcome of true recompense.

Then the Truth, exalted is He, says:

﴿Here you are, you who argued on their behalf in the life of this world. But who will argue with God on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their guardian (wakil)?﴾

The one who argued on behalf of Ibn Ubayriq wanted to clear his name before the people and condemn the Jew. And in that he argued before a human being on behalf of a human being. Will the matter end with this ease? No, because this world is not the abode of recompense. Suppose he escaped the human punishment: will he escape the punishment of God in the Hereafter? No. Therefore, the one who argues wants to blind the judgment of the earth, but he will not be able to blind the judgment of the Truth, and on the Day of Resurrection he will not find anyone to argue on behalf of such a wrong. And this is not all: the Truth concludes the verse with: "or who will be their guardian (wakil)?" That is, who then can be a wakil (guardian/advocate) for these people on the Day of Resurrection? We know that the wakil is the skilled person whom some people choose to be able to persuade the one before him. So who can perform that task before God? No one.

The Almighty further says:

﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks forgiveness from Allah, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (4:110)

When Allah, glorified and exalted is He, created creation, He made them beings of change (ahl aghyar). Therefore He did not will that any sinner, through his sin, should fall outside the sphere of His power and mercy. Rather, He, glorified is He, legislated repentance for the sinner as a protection for society against the spread of his evil. For if everyone who committed a sin were cut off from the mercy of Allah, society would suffer from the evils of such a person, and all his deeds would become a calamity of far-spreading evil upon society. Thus repentance from Allah, both its legislation and its acceptance, is a protection for mankind from the savagery of the one who commits the first sin. In this way repentance came to protect people from the savagery of the people of disobedience who began with a single act of disobedience.

As for those who stood in an attempt to exonerate "Ibn Abiraq" (Ibn Ubayriq), they split into two groups: a group whose intention was to clear "Ibn Abiraq," and a group whose intention was not to expose a Muslim. Each of the two groups had committed a sin, but does this sin remove them from the mercy of Allah? No. He, glorified is He, says: "will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful." And the Truth pardons that matter. Both groups became obligated to do a good deed after the Messenger explained to them and they understood the intent of the Truth, and He, glorified is He, keeps them within the ranks of the faithful. The Messenger of Allah ruled in favour of the Jew against "Ibn Abiraq." Afterwards, "Ibn Abiraq" apostatised and went to Mecca, accompanying his habit of treachery, and he broke into a wall of a man to steal his property, the wall fell upon him, and he died.

The Truth, glorified is He, sets the standards: whoever commits a sin or wrongs himself by a transgression, then seeks forgiveness from Allah, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful. We observe that some superficial people do not understand well the saying of the Truth: "And whoever does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks forgiveness from Allah, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful," so they ask: Is not the one who committed the evil deed one who has wronged himself?

We say: The precision of the Qur'an clarifies the meaning for us. "Doing evil" (su') means an act that harms others; it is other than one who commits something that harms himself alone. Whoever steals, kills, or transgresses against another by slander, beating, or humiliation, such acts are the commission of evil (su'), for evil is an act that people dislike; one says, "So-and-so is a man of evil (swon)," meaning he confronts people with what they dislike.

But one who drinks wine may be in isolation from people, having harmed no one, yet he has wronged himself, because the Muslim is required to have guardianship over himself as well, and the methodology protects the Muslim even from himself, and protects the self from its owner. The evidence is that we punish the one who kills another, and likewise Allah forbids from Paradise the one who kills himself by suicide.

Thus we see the protection of the methodology for the human being and how it surrounds him from every direction, because the human being is an individual of Allah's creation, and the Truth requires of every individual that he protect himself. So if he does evil, that is, harms another, this is called "evil" (su'); but when he does an act that harms himself, this is the wronging of the self:

﴿And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins — and who forgives sins except Allah? — and do not persist in what they have done while they know.﴾ (Surat Al 'Imran, 3:135)

Is committing immorality different from wronging the self? It is also an harm to another, but wronging the self is the act that harms the self alone, or that a person commits a sin and gives himself enjoyment through it for a moment, without bringing to mind its severe punishment in the Hereafter. You may find a person who commits disobedience to give another person pleasure. An example of this is the false witness who gives one person's right to another person, and takes nothing for himself, but has sold his religion for the worldly gain of another. The saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ applies to him:

"Hasten to good deeds before trials come like pieces of the dark night: a man will be a believer in the morning and a disbeliever by evening, or a believer by evening and a disbeliever by morning, selling his religion for a trifle of worldly goods." (1)

﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks forgiveness from Allah, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ Allah is Forgiving and Merciful eternally and perpetually, and the servant who repents sees the forgiveness and mercy of Allah.

(1) Narrated by Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and Ahmad.

The Lord then says:

﴿And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself. And Allah is ever Knowing, Wise.﴾ (4:111)

The Truth uses the word "kasaba" (to earn, acquire by one's own effort) when it speaks of a good deed a person has done, and describes the commission of an evil act with "iktasaba" (to acquire, to get by deliberate effort). Why? Because doing good is a natural process in a human being, one that he feels no shame about, whereas evil is always a process about which a person feels shame, and so he loves to carry it out in secret, and it requires contrivance on his part.

Let us give an example for clarification, and to God belongs the highest similitude. We find a man who looks upon the beauty of his wife with all his faculties, yet if he looks at another woman who is not one of his unmarriageable kin, he performs an operation to deceive the faculties of the soul so that he may spy to see this woman, and he tries by stratagem and contrivance to spy upon what is not his. For this reason it is said of the lawful that it is "kasb," and it is said of the unlawful that it is "iktisab."

Now when the Qur'an comes to the evil deed and says: "kasaba sayyi'ah" (he earned an evil deed), this is a matter that deserves attention. A person may commit an evil deed and regret it as soon as he has finished, if he is among the people of goodness; we find him reproaching and blaming himself and resolving never to return to it. But if someone commits an evil and is happy about it, as though it had achieved for him a gain, and takes pride in it, forgetting the grave danger he will face on the Day of Resurrection and the black destiny, then his taking pride in the disobedience is a declaration of the corruption of his nature and the dominance of wickedness in his depths. He differs from the one upon whom the sin is committed, who, at the moment he recalls it, his skin shivers and he seeks forgiveness from Allah.

"And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself." So beware, O human being, of supposing that when you wrong someone by an evil act you have gained the world. By Allah, if the wrongdoer knew what Allah has prepared for the one wronged, he would begrudge his enemy the chance to wrong him. Let us give an example for clarification, and to God belongs the highest similitude: suppose a man has two sons, and one of them comes and strikes his brother or snatches from him something he owns, and the father sees this incident. Where is the father's heart, and with whom does he stand?

The father stands with the one wronged, and tries to satisfy him. If the wronging brother has taken from him something worth ten piastres, the father compensates the wronged son with something worth a hundred piastres, and the wrongdoer lives in regret. Had he known his father would honor his wronged brother, he would never have wronged him. Thus wrongdoing is the peak of stupidity.

Among the paradoxes that are related is one that says: "If you must backbite, then backbite your parents." The hearer will say: "And how can I backbite my father and mother?" The author of the paradox will reply: "Your parents are more deserving of your good deeds. Instead of giving your good deeds to your enemy, seek out those you love and give them your good deeds." The reasoning is: "Do not be foolish, O backbiter, for you only backbite out of enmity, and how will you give your good deeds to your enemy when they are the fruit of your own works?"

We know what the master al-Hasan al-Basri did when he learned that someone had backbitten him: he sent to the backbiter a tray of fresh dates with a messenger, and said to the messenger: "Take this tray to so-and-so and say: My master informs you that you backbit him yesterday, so I have given him your good deeds, and your good deeds are without doubt more precious than these dates." In this there is sufficient clarification for condemning backbiting.

"And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself, and Allah is ever Knowing, Wise." We know that whenever any attribute of the Truth enters into the form of a state of being, that is, is preceded by "kāna" (was), beware of taking "kāna" as a description of something that happened in a past time. Rather, let us say "kāna wa mā zāl" (was and still is). Why? Because Allah was eternally; He is Forgiving and Merciful before anyone exists to be forgiven or shown mercy. Allah is not among the beings of contingency and changing attributes; the attributes are fixed for Him, because time in events changes only with respect to contingent beings. For example, we find a human being healthy at one time and sick at another.

Therefore the future does not go beyond the past except for those subject to contingency, and likewise the future does not go beyond the present except in those subject to contingency. Since Allah is the One who changes and is not changed, no time will alter Him. Rather He was in eternity Forgiving and Merciful, and He still is Forgiving and Merciful. Likewise, Allah's knowledge is eternal, and His wisdom has no limits.

Then the Almighty says:

{And whoever earns a sin or a wrong and then throws it onto an innocent person has certainly borne a slander and a manifest sin (112).

They have said: sin (khati'ah) is that which is not intentional. An example of this: when we teach a student a rule of grammar (qa'idah nahwiyyah), then ask him to read a text, and we notice that the student has put the subject (fa'il) in the accusative and the object (maf'ul) in the nominative, and we correct the mistake for him. He did not do it intentionally; rather he forgot the rule and did not recall it, and we keep correcting the mistake for him until he remembers the grammatical rule. Through practice, i'rab (grammatical inflection) becomes a habit (malakah) in the student, and then he does not err.

So khati'ah is an unintentional error, whereas ithm (sin) is that which is intentional. How then, when one person throws onto another a sin that he himself committed or an error that he himself made, what is God's ruling on that?

﴿And whoever earns a sin or a wrong and then throws it onto an innocent person has certainly borne a slander and a manifest sin (112)﴾ (Surat an-Nisa').

He has committed the sin or the wrong, and would that he had been content with this! Rather, he wants to escalate the crime by committing a second crime, namely by throwing the sin or wrong onto an innocent person. His sin is compound, and therefore the Almighty said: "then he has borne a slander and a manifest sin." The Almighty's use here of the word "ihtamala" (bore, with effort) rather than "hamala" (carried) confirms for us that there is treatment, struggle and hardship in order for a person to bear this heavy thing. The crime is two crimes, not one: he committed the sin and threw it onto an innocent person. The doer of a sin regrets its commission once, and he also regrets attaching enmity to it. It is easy for him to commit the disobedience, but after the frenzy of enmity has calmed, regret comes to him. The Almighty said: ﴿And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth, when they both offered an offering, and it was accepted from one of them and was not accepted from the other. He said, "I will surely kill you." He said, "Allah only accepts from the righteous" (27)﴾ (Surat al-Ma'idah).

Habil, then, asks Qabil: "What is my fault in this? It is Allah who accepts the offering, not I. So why do you kill me?"

The wise speech continues: ﴿If you extend your hand against me to kill me, I shall not extend my hand against you to kill you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds (28)﴾ (Surat al-Ma'idah).

And what does the Almighty say after that?

﴿So his soul permitted him the murder of his brother, and he killed him and became among the losers (30)﴾ (Surat al-Ma'idah).

It is as if the matter of killing was a laborious operation, not an easy one, and it required struggle. For example, no one would say "I made the rope obedient (tawwa'tu al-habl)," but one may say "I made the iron obedient (tawwa'tu al-hadid)." The frenzy of anger made Qabil forget everything at the time of the crime; after it had occurred and the frenzy of anger, which had concealed the balances of values, subsided, the balances of values appeared bright within the soul.

For this reason we find someone who commits a crime and then goes to surrender himself to the police, and he does this because the frenzy of the crime has ended and the light of the balances of values has shone forth. On this basis we understand the Almighty's words: "then he has borne a slander and a manifest sin."

This shows that whoever commits a crime and then throws it onto an innocent person is doing something that requires hardship, and his soul is torn: once by regret, because he committed the crime, and a second time because he threw the crime onto an innocent person. Therefore the Almighty said: "he has borne a slander and a manifest sin." When we hear the word "buhtan" (slander), it derives from the root "bahata," and buhtan is a matter at which one is astonished that it proceeds from its doer. For example, the Almighty's words in relating the case of Sayyidna Ibrahim with Nimrod, where He says, on the tongue of Sayyidna Ibrahim:

﴿Indeed, Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west﴾ (part of 2:258). So what was the response of the man? ﴿So the one who disbelieved was confounded (bahata)﴾ (part of 2:258). That is, he heard a strange thing that silenced him from speaking. Sayyidna Ibrahim had brought him a matter of wonder that did not occur to his mind, and he could find no escape from it. Thus matters that oppose the logic of truth and the demands of values are strange to people; they are buhtan, and the proof of this is that their doers conceal them from people.

When we look at the case for which the verse was revealed, we find that a thief stole and wished to clear himself and to draw an innocent person into the crime and attach it to him. The criminal committed the crime, and this bears a sin upon him. But that he transfers the crime to someone else shows the existence of another capacity by which he may bear what he did. This is difficult for the soul, and no one is astonished at hearing something unless that thing is contrary to what is familiar and known. There is clear and evident proof in the dialogue between Sayyidna Ibrahim and Nimrod. When Nimrod said:

﴿I give life and cause death﴾ (part of 2:258), he meant by it his power to kill a person and leave another alive for his purpose. Here Sayyidna Ibrahim overwhelmed him with a matter that confounded him, without entering into this verbal wrangling, and said: ﴿Indeed, Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west.﴾ So the one who disbelieved was confounded (part of 2:258).

That is, Nimrod heard a strange statement and did not have the intelligence by which to guard against it and repel it. Likewise the man who committed the crime and then threw it onto another needed a capacity to bear this. This shows that sound nature abhors the doing of ugliness; if a person commits a sin, he has borne buhtan, and if he goes further and carries it onto an innocent person, that means the matter requires another capacity.

So His words: "he has borne a slander and a manifest sin" mean that he has borne a wondrous matter that stuns the hearer, who wonders how it happened, and the one who does this also bears the sin.

As we have known, ithm is the deliberate evil. The Almighty clarifies this matter: Allah, glorified and exalted, surrounds you, O Muhammad, with His care, His protection and His grace. Even if some of the weak in faith try to draw you away from this matter and to make it appear fair to you to acquit a guilty person and convict an innocent one, whether the guilty is a Muslim and the innocent is not, and Allah did not send Muhammad to judge only among believers, but the beginning of this verse makes clear to us that Allah sent His Messenger to judge in truth: "that you may judge between the people" (105), that is, to judge between people in their entirety. So beware, when you judge or say: "This one is a Muslim and that one is a disbeliever," or say: "This one is a Muslim and that one is of the People of the Book." Rather, all people stand equal before the cases of truth.

For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took that dose of faith that came with an incident, and afterwards, in the story of the Makhzumite woman when she stole and he wished to implement the hadd punishment upon her, his beloved Usamah ibn Zayd spoke to him about lifting the hadd from her. The Messenger of Allah said:

On the authority of 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her): The Quraysh were concerned about the matter of the Makhzumite woman who had stolen, and they said: "Who will speak to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about her?" They said: "Who would dare to, except Usamah, the beloved of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" So Usamah spoke to him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you intercede concerning one of the hudud of Allah?" Then he stood up and addressed the people, saying: "O people, those before you were destroyed because when a nobleman stole among them they left him, and when a weak person stole among them they implemented the hadd upon him. By Allah, if Fatimah the daughter of Muhammad had stolen, Muhammad would have cut off her hand." (1)

This statement is derived from the preceding case, and the Almighty says:

﴿And were it not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, a group of them would have resolved to mislead you, but they mislead none except themselves, and they cannot harm you at all. And Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom and taught you what you did not know. And ever has the bounty of Allah been upon you tremendous (113)﴾.

(1) Narrated by Muslim.

The Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 4, verse 113:

Here we ask: did anyone intend to lead the Messenger of Allah astray? We must understand that "al-hamm" (intention, resolve) is of two kinds: the intention of execution (hamm infadh) and the intention of embellishment (hamm tazyin). The Messenger of Allah rejected the intention of execution, and Allah repelled it from him, because He, glorified and exalted is He, surrounds His Messenger with His grace and mercy and brings about events in order to teach him a new ruling. The grace of Allah upon His Messenger and His mercy made the intention coming from them only an intention of embellishment, and Allah also protected His Messenger from it. When the Messenger learned this new ruling, he began to judge by it thereafter in all the disputes of the people. So whenever an event occurred and a ruling came to him from heaven which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had not known, the grace belongs to Allah, because He increases His Messenger in knowledge: ﴿And taught you that which you did not know﴾ (part of verse 113, surah an-Nisa').

The aim of those who defended "Ubayriq" was to embellish matters for the Messenger of Allah, and this is the intention of embellishment, not the intention of execution. The purpose of the embellishment was to harm the Messenger and mislead him, Allah forbid, to take him away from the path of truth and the path of guidance. This is a matter that harms the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. For if the Messenger had acquitted a guilty person whom he knew to be guilty, it would have settled in the mind of the guilty that the matters of religion are not serious. As for the innocent person whom the Messenger was supposed to condemn, what would his position be? He would have to say to himself: "The religion of Muhammad has no truthfulness in it, for it punishes an innocent man." So the intention of embellishment harms the Messenger both in the eyes of the one who is exonerated and in the eyes of the one against whom the crime is to be attached. But Allah protected His Messenger from this as well, through grace and mercy.

﴿They had certainly intended to mislead you, but they mislead not except themselves, and they cannot harm you at all. And Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom﴾ (part of verse 113, surah an-Nisa').

The Truth (al-Haqq) sent down a Book to settle the matter, and the descent of the ruling after that incident occurred came, among what it clarifies, to explain the secret of the Qur'an being revealed in stages (tanjim), because the Qur'an deals with real events. It leaves the matter until the event occurs, and then pours Allah's ruling, which descends from heaven at the time the event happens, upon the event. Otherwise, how would the Qur'an address events if it had descended all at once while the events had not yet occurred? Therefore Allah willed that the events occur first, and then the ruling comes. The disbelievers had already said:

﴿Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?﴾ (part of verse 32, surah al-Furqan).

No, Allah willed the Qur'an to be revealed in stages, dispersed and divided. Why?

﴿Thus, that We may strengthen thereby your heart; and We have separated it [recitation] distinctly﴾ (part of verse 32, surah al-Furqan).

Whenever a tremor struck the heart from obstinacy, fierce contention, and stubbornness, there would be a response from the disbelievers and their turning back to the truth, though they know it as they know their own sons. A star of the Qur'an would descend, and amid the people's tumult with the Messenger, the mercy of heaven would descend to steady the heart. If the heart grew weary from the people's tumult, the verses of the Messenger's connection with heaven and with revelation would remove these hardships from him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in the matter of the call, used to experience shocks every day, and therefore at every moment he needed steadying. When the Qur'anic star descends after the wrangling with opponents, the sweetness of the Qur'anic star makes the matter easy for him; and when another matter comes to the Messenger ﷺ that disturbs his peace, he awaits the sweetness of revelation to descend upon him. This is the meaning of His word, the Truth: ﴿Thus, that We may strengthen thereby your heart﴾ (part of verse 32, surah al-Furqan).

That is: We sent it down in stages so that We might strengthen your heart by it. Had the Qur'an been sent down all at once, it would have reduced the number of times heaven connected with Muhammad ﷺ, while he desires the continuity of heaven's connection with him.

The proof is that when revelation paused, the Messenger sat looking toward the sky, longing. Why? At the beginning of the descent, revelation exhausted him; therefore the Messenger said: "He embraced me until I reached the limit of exertion" (1).

Khadijah, may Allah be pleased with her, saw him "and his forehead was dripping with sweat" (2). The connection of Jibril, with his angelic nature and luminosity, to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in his human nature must cause a chemical change in the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ self.

From 'A'isha, the Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her, that al-Harith ibn Hisham, may Allah be pleased with him, asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, how does revelation come to you?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Sometimes it comes to me like the ringing of a bell, and it is the hardest on me, and it departs from me and I have retained what it said. And sometimes the angel appears to me as a man and speaks to me, and I retain what he says." 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "Indeed I saw him when revelation descended upon him on an extremely cold day, and it departed from him, and his forehead was dripping with sweat" (3).

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ faced hardships, and Allah willed through the pause of revelation that Muhammad should feel the sweetness of the revelation that came down to him, and that he should yearn for it, for longing helps the Messenger bear the hardships of revelation when it comes. For this reason we find that the process of sweating did not last long, because the Truth said:

{And the Hereafter is better for you than the first [life]} (4), (surah ad-Duha).

That is, the Truth made clear to His Messenger: you will find longing, sweetness and pleasure in receiving these things.

﴿Thus, that We may strengthen thereby your heart; and We have separated it [recitation] distinctly﴾ (part of verse 32, surah al-Furqan).

Thus the Qur'an descended in stages over periods, and the Companions heard a number of Qur'anic verses, memorized them, and the scribes of revelation wrote them down. Then comes another miracle of the Qur'an with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: a complete surah descends upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and after he is relieved, he says to the scribes: "Write this." The Messenger arranges the verses in their places within the surah, then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recites the surah in prayer, and the worshippers hear the recitation in which every verse is in its place. This is evidence that the matter was carefully studied, and that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he relates, relates truthfully.

Otherwise, tell me: how does revelation come down to the Messenger as a whole surah, and he dictates it to the scribes, then recites it in prayer as it was revealed, and as his Companions wrote it down? How could that happen if what was sent down to him were not complete truth from Allah? We may find a person who speaks for a quarter of an hour, but if we say to him, "Repeat what you said," he will never repeat the very same words. But the Messenger of Allah ﷺ repeats the verses as they were revealed. This shows that he recites the Book of Allah, which falsehood cannot approach from before it or behind it; it is a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy. Therefore the Truth says:

﴿And they bring you no example but that We bring you the truth and best explanation﴾ (verse 33, surah al-Furqan).

That is: they bring you no incident occurring but that We bring you the truth concerning it.

Thus the Qur'an was revealed in stages only to strengthen the heart of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ against the successive shocks he encountered, and Allah willed to make the connection of heaven with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ continuous over the twenty-three years that the mission lasted.

Tartil is the tanjim and separation with which the Qur'an was revealed, so that the Messenger recites it in prayer just as it was revealed to him before, without distortion or alteration. The Truth says: {We shall make you recite, and you will not forget} (6), (surah al-A'la).

Whenever an event occurs, Allah sends down what suits it from the Qur'an, just as the theft of Ibn Ubayriq occurred and the ruling was revealed concerning it. The Truth says: "And taught you that which you did not know, and the bounty of Allah upon you has been great."

So when Allah has taught you, O Messenger of Allah, what you did not know through the descent of the Book, are you, O my master, O Messenger of Allah, only a lawgiver by what has been revealed in the Book? No. The Book is a miracle, and in it legislation occurs, and that is a distinction that no messenger before him had, as evidenced by the Truth's word:

﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾ (part of verse 7, surah al-Hashr).

The messengers before the Messenger ﷺ conveyed what they received from Allah, but Allah, glorified is He, distinguished Muhammad ﷺ by delegating legislation to him. The Truth made clear that He taught His Messenger the Book and the wisdom. And wisdom is intended to mean the Sunnah, as He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom﴾ (part of verse 34, surah al-Ahzab).

Glorified is He, the possessor of grace over all creation and the possessor of grace over His Messenger: "And Allah sent down to you the Book and wisdom, and taught you that which you did not know, and the bounty of Allah upon you has been great." We should note that "the bounty of Allah" is repeated twice in this verse. The first bounty of Allah in this verse is that He protected him from a group that would mislead him and distance him from the truth. Then the second bounty of Allah upon him is that He sent down to him the Book with all its rulings, and gave him wisdom, which is the delegation from Allah to His Messenger to legislate. Thus the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, made the Sunnah of the Messenger ﷺ an extension of His revelation. Therefore, when a people try to cast doubt upon the hadith of the Messenger, saying: "Prayer is not mentioned in the Qur'an,"

we say, asking one of them: "Is prayer performed or not?"

He says: "I pray."

We say to him: "How many obligatory prayers do you pray?"

He says: "Five obligatory prayers."

We say: "Bring these five obligatory prayers from the Qur'an." He will be struck dumb, and the matter of determining the dawn prayer as two rak'ahs, the noon prayer as four, the afternoon prayer likewise, the sunset prayer as three, and the night prayer as four rak'ahs will become confused for him, and he will finally admit that he prays in light of the saying of the Messenger: "Pray as you have seen me pray" (5). And this is from the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

"And taught you that which you did not know, and the bounty of Allah upon you has been great." Perhaps we find one of the people of shallowness and obstinacy who says: "The Qur'an repeats words in more than one place. Why does it mention the bounty of Allah at the start of this verse and mention it again at the end of the same verse?"

We say: You will not notice the bounty of Allah in the first part, because He rescued His Messenger from the intention of embellishment, by judging against a man of the People of the Book unjustly; and in the second part, it is a bounty in completion, in that He taught His Messenger the Book and the wisdom, and this bounty was truly great.

(1) Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of: Beginning of Revelation.
(2) Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of: Beginning of Revelation.
(3) Narrated by al-Bukhari and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra.

And when these people go to inform the Messenger about the matter of Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq, did they not sit together to plot how Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq might escape the crime?

They conferred among themselves about Ṭu'ma's affair and agreed to go to the Messenger. Thus the secret consultation (najwā) was close to what is forbidden, and for this reason the etiquette of Islam was keen to respect the dignity of a third companion: when there are two, they should not hold a private conversation without their companion, because that would grieve him.

It may be permissible if there are four present, for then one speaks with another, and two may hold a private conversation there. So najwā means secret speech (al-musārra), and secret speech is only about a matter they do not want to spread. The people did precisely that before they went to the Messenger to speak about the incident of Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq. Therefore the Truth exposes the matter of this secret conference, and the True Word descends:

﴿There is no good in much of their secret talk, except for one who enjoins charity, or what is right, or reconciliation between people. And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of Allah – We will give him a great reward.﴾ (4:114)

He, glory be to Him, clarifies the matter of this secret talk which contains plotting to mislead. But what if the secret talk assists the truth? He, glory be to Him, makes an exception here. So He did not issue a categorical judgment against every secret talk, but excepted from it the secret talk of one who enjoins charity, or what is right, or reconciliation between people, and He even rewards it with a good recompense. Therefore He said: "And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of the people, We will give him a great reward." (The text here reads "the pleasure of Allah" in the Qur'anic verse; the commentary's wording is reproduced as it stands.) The Truth uses the word "sawfa" here. It could have come as "fa-sanu'tīhi ajran ʿaẓīman" (so We will give him a great reward), but because of the extreme precision of the Qur'anic expression, it came with the farther distance, "sawfa".

We know that when the answer to a conditional clause is near, we use "sīn" (the prefix sa-), and when the answer to the condition is at a far distance, we use "sawfa". The Truth used "sawfa" here because the locus of recompense is the Hereafter. So beware, O servant who believes, of saying: Why did God not give me the reward for good in this world? Because the Truth, glory be to Him, did not say "fa-sanu'tīhi" but said "fa-sawfa nu'tīhi ajran ʿaẓīman", which indicates that the favor and honor come from God; even if it is hastened, it is not the recompense for this deed, because the Truth's reward for His believing servants will be great, and this reward in the Hereafter is indicated only by "fa-sawfa".

We know that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gives his community of believers a promise of something, he is promising them the Hereafter. Let us look at the Pledge of al-ʿAqaba, when the Anṣār came from Medina to pledge allegiance to the Messenger of Allah:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them, while around him was a band of his Companions: "Pledge to me that you will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill your children, nor bring a slander that you fabricate between your hands and feet, nor disobey in what is right. Whoever among you fulfils it, his reward is with Allah; and whoever incurs any of that and is punished for it in this world, it is an expiation for him; and whoever incurs any of that and Allah conceals it, then if He wills He pardons him and if He wills He punishes him." (1)

They said: "O Messenger of Allah, you have taken for yourself, and we want to take for ourselves. What is for us if we fulfil this?" Observe the greatness of the answer and the inspired response. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "For you is Paradise."

It was within the power of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to tell them: You will be victorious, and you will take the eastern and western parts of the earth, and the best of all Islamic lands will come to you. But in his wisdom he never said that, for one of them might be martyred in battle for the victory of God's religion, so what will he take in this world? He will not receive his share of honor in this world, but he will receive the recompense in the Hereafter. Therefore he brought the recompense that will include everyone, which is Paradise, to show them that this world is too trivial for God's recompense to be confined to it, and to urge the believers to seek the recompense of the Hereafter. We all know this anecdote: a man says to his companion, "Do you love me?" The companion answers, "Yes, I love you." The questioner asks, "To what measure do you love me?" The companion says, "To the measure of this world." The man replies, "How insignificant you are in my eyes."

The Truth says: "And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of Allah, We will give him a great reward." Who is the referent of "nu'tīhi" and who is the doer of this giving? It is Allah, glory be to Him, who described the reward as a great reward, as if the Truth were conveying to us:

O community of the believing nation, cling to the method of the Messenger of Allah and merge with it so that you may be one thing with him. Beware lest you have an opinion separate from the method, for he conveys from God. Whoever believes in him, let him cling to him. Therefore we find that our master Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (may Allah be pleased with him), when they related to him the account of the Night Journey and the Ascension, asked his interlocutor: "Did the Messenger of Allah say what you have said?" They said: "Yes, he did say it." Al-Ṣiddīq replied to them: "If he said it, then he has spoken the truth." Al-Ṣiddīq Abū Bakr does not need proof of the truth of what the Messenger of Allah said.

(1) Narrated by al-Bukhārī in the Book of Faith.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 4, verse 115:

The Truth (al-Haqq) follows this with a contrast, saying:

﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him, and follows other than the way of the believers – We will leave him in what he has turned to, and burn him in Hell, and evil is it as a destination.﴾

The word "yushaqqiq" (opposes) indicates that a split has occurred in a matter that was once joined together, just as we split a piece of wood and make it into two parts after it was one solid mass. You, O believers, have become joined to the method of the Messenger of Allah through faith, and you have acknowledged him as a messenger and a truthful conveyor from Allah. So beware of splitting this joining. If a ruling comes and one of the believers tries to step out of it, this is opposition (shiqaq) to the Messenger, God forbid. Or the meaning is: whoever takes a path other than the one the Messenger brought, so that he is in one split while the Shari'ah of Allah is in another split.

"And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him." Yes, guidance becomes clear to the Muslim when he believes in Allah as Creator and Lord, and believes in the Messenger as the one who conveys. Thereby he has surrendered his reins to Allah. For this reason we have said: the function of the intellect is to examine the evidences for the Supreme Existence of Allah. When a person believes in the Supreme Existence of Allah, one level remains: that he believe in the Messenger who conveys from Allah. This is because the utmost that reason seeks from the evidence of faith regarding the existence of Allah is that behind man and behind the universe there is a powerful, wise, knowing power, possessing all the attributes of perfection.

Reason cannot know the name of this power, nor can reason recognize what it requires. Therefore there must be a conveying (bala') from this power. When guidance regarding the Supreme Existence and regarding the conveying from Allah has become clear to a person, he must join himself to the method brought by the one who conveys from Allah, and perform what the Supreme Power requires, because Allah has commanded it, and because the Messenger of Allah has conveyed the command, or done it, or approved it. As for when a person engages in disputation (mumahakah), we say to him: review your faith in Allah first, and your faith in the Messenger of Allah second. Therefore the Truth says:

﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him, and follows other than the way of the believers – We will leave him in what he has turned to, and burn him in Hell, and evil is it as a destination.﴾ (Surah an-Nisa', 115).

Guidance, as we know, is the path that leads to the goal. Every action of creatures must have an aim, and whoever does an action without an aim is regarded by society as lacking discernment. But if a person has an aim, he recognizes the seriousness and importance of his aim and seeks for it the shortest path. This path is what we call al-huda (guidance). Whoever knows the path leading to guidance and then follows other than the way of the believers, he opposes the Messenger, and does not join himself to the method of faith nor adhere to it. And whoever opposes only turns back from his faith.

Thus we know that there is a way and path of the Messenger, and believers who followed the Messenger by joining the method. Whoever opposes the Messenger contradicts the method brought by the Messenger and also contradicts the believers.

And the Truth is the One who says:

﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it, and do not follow the [other] ways﴾ (part of verse 153, Surah al-An'am).

There is no way to the Truth except one path, and whoever departs from this path, what happens to him? Here is the answer of the Truth: "We will leave him in what he has turned to, and burn him in Hell, and evil is it as a destination." The word (min) may be a conditional particle or a relative pronoun, as in our saying: "man yudhakkir yanjah" with damma on both, where "man" is a relative pronoun: the one who studies is the one who succeeds. We may also say "man yudhakkir yanjah" with sukun, where "man" is conditional.

In the relative construction the sentence proceeds as it is, but if it is conditional there is jazm (apocopation), which requires the verb to be in sukun, and the response of the condition is likewise in sukun. "Man" may be a relative pronoun or a conditional particle, and we usually recognize its status from what follows it. An example of this is the Truth's saying:

"And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him, and follows" – here "yattabi'" bears the sukun of jazm, which shows that "man" is conditional.

The reading differs if we consider "man" to be a relative pronoun, because that requires leaving the verb "yushaqqiq" in its state as an imperfect verb in the raf' case marked by damma; likewise "yattabi'" would be an imperfect verb in raf' marked by damma. In that case we say: "nuwalliyhi ma tawalla wa nusalliyhi." But if we consider "man" a conditional particle, and in this verse it is conditional, then the verb must be in jazm. So we read: "man yushaqqiq al-Rasula min ba'di ma tabayyana lahu al-huda," and likewise the coordinated verb, which is "wa yattabi'" (yattabi'), is in jazm, and the response of the condition and what is coordinated with it, which is "wa nuwallihi" and "wa nusallihi", are in jazm by the deletion of the weak letter at their end, which is the ya'. "Yattabi' ghayra sabil al-mu'minina nuwallihi ma tawalla wa nusallihi jahannama wa saa'at masiran." The meaning of "tawalla" is "approached"; one says: so-and-so is a wali of so-and-so, meaning he has become close to him. Whoever follows other than the way of the believers, the Truth does not desire for him, but brings him close to non-believers and entrusts him to the people of disbelief. Behold, the Truth, glory be to Him, says: "I am the most independent of partners from association; whoever does an action in which he associates another with Me, I abandon him and his association."(1)

The one who needs an associate is one who has a weak corner and wants a partner to strengthen him in it. For example, and to Allah belongs the highest similitude, we find no one partnering with another in trade unless he owns sufficient wealth to run the trade or cannot manage its affairs by himself. And He, glory be to Him, teaches us: "I am the most independent of partners from association; whoever does an action in which he associates another with Me, I abandon him and his association."

That is, He possesses absolute effective power, which needs no aid and no partner, because partnership, when first witnessed, witnesses weakness in one partner and need for a stranger. Therefore whoever opposes the Messenger in a matter of faith, the Truth turns him over to the one who disbelieved and brings him close to what he wants. And He, glory be to Him, knows that a person will not benefit from anything that opposes the Messenger of Allah. Rather, the recompense of the one who opposes the Messenger of Allah and follows other than the way of the believers is that Allah brings him close and draws him near to the people of disbelief and sin, joins him to them, and gathers him in their company. This does not mean that Allah withholds provision from the servant; no, provision is for the believer and the disbeliever alike. Allah has made the causes serve the servant if he takes them. Out of Allah's mercy and grace, He does not withdraw blessing from such a servant: the sun gives him light and warmth, the air blows upon him, and the earth gives him good from its elements:

﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We will increase him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We will give him of it, but he will have no share in the Hereafter.﴾ (20) (Surah ash-Shura).

And He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿All of these – those and these – We extend from the gift of your Lord; and the gift of your Lord has never been restricted.﴾ (20) (Surah al-Isra').

Thus we find that the divine gift is not confined to believers only, but is for the believer and the disbeliever alike. And if there were nothing from Allah but this matter, it would be sufficient reason for us to join ourselves to His method and love it.

"And follows other than the way of the believers – We will leave him in what he has turned to, and burn him in Hell, and evil is it as a destination." The destination leading to Hell must be an extreme of evil.

(1) Related by Muslim and Ibn Majah from Abu Hurairah.

Then comes the account of the supreme betrayal of faith. It is the word of the Truth, glory be to Him:

﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills. And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly strayed far astray.﴾ (4:116)

Here the Truth speaks of a person who did not repent of shirk and then believed. Faith erases what came before it, that is, it cuts off the disbelief and the sins that do not concern the rights of others, such as one person wronging another. Part of the greatness of faith is that when a person believes in Allah, his intention is made sincere through this faith, and then the decree of Allah comes to him in the form of death. Allah may then give him a bliss that surpasses that of one who lived as a believer for a long time, and who may have committed some misdeeds and suffered their consequences.

An example of this is Mukhayriq. When the Prophet (ﷺ) went out to Uhud, Mukhayriq said to the Jews: "Will you not help Muhammad? By Allah, you know that supporting him is a duty upon you." They said: "Today is the Sabbath." He said: "There is no Sabbath." He took his sword and went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and fought until his wounds prevented him from standing. When death came to him, he said: "My wealth is for Muhammad; let him place it wherever he wishes." He had not prayed a single rak'ah in his life, yet he attained the rank of martyr. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Mukhayriq is the best of the Jews, Salman is the best of the Persians, and Bilal is the best of the Abyssinians."

Allah conveys to us here: "Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills." And to Allah belongs the highest example. In our lives we see a society in which a revolution or coup has taken place. The leaders of the revolution or coup see someone doing whatever he wishes, and they do not approach him, until he attacks the revolution with criticism or tries to stage a coup of his own. Then he is tried for the crime of high treason. How much more so, then, is the one who leaves the realm of faith entirely and associates others with Allah? He will never be forgiven for that, but Allah forgives what is less than it. It is part of Allah's mercy toward creation that He retained the will to forgive, so that people would not rush into committing every sin. Yet the servant must repent of his sin. We know that a servant is not expelled from the mercy of Allah merely for committing a sin. We also know that there is a difference between one who commits a sin, knowing that he is sinning and that the judgment of Allah is correct and true, but whose soul has weakened, and one who rejects the judgment of Allah. Sometimes we find a servant who wants to commit a sin and looks for a way to make it permissible, as when someone says: "Usury is not forbidden." This is rejecting the judgment of Allah. But the servant who says: "I know that usury is forbidden, but my circumstances are harsh and my needs are pressing" is merely a sinful servant; he does not reject the judgment of Allah. Whoever rejects the judgment of Allah is, Allah forbid, a disbeliever.

"Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills." Let us be attentive to the fact that some orientalists, who want to spread corruption on earth, unknowingly spread the virtue of Islam. They are, as the poet says:

"And when God wishes to spread a virtue,
He lets an envious tongue carry it."

When they speak about such matters, they drive the people of faith to seek out the aspect of the Qur'anic inimitability and its eloquence.

They say: "Muhammad conveyed to his people: 'Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills.' But it seems that forgetfulness overcame him, and he said in another verse: ﴿Say, O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins.﴾" (39:53)

They are trying to attribute the Qur'an to Muhammad rather than to Allah, and they try to find a contradiction between the two noble verses. We reply to them: each of you is unlettered and ignorant of the faculty of the language. If language were a natural faculty, an innate disposition and nature for you, one would understand the word of the Truth:

﴿Say, O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins.﴾ (39:53)

It was incumbent upon each of you to understand that shirk is a matter greater than sin. Sin is when a person knows a matter of faith and then opposes it. But the polytheist does not fall within this entire category, because he is a disbeliever at the very summit. Therefore there is no contradiction, no conflict, and no opposition between the two noble verses. The orientalists are merely a people who do not grasp the true meanings of the Qur'an.

"Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills. And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly strayed far astray." However much enjoyment the polytheist takes in his life, his life is limited. If the enjoyments remain with him, he will leave them behind; and if they do not remain with him, they will leave him. So he is either one who leaves enjoyments through death, or enjoyments leave him through the changes of circumstance. He is between two states: either he loses them, or they lose him, and he returns to Allah. When he goes to Allah in the Hereafter and the reckoning, the Hereafter has no time, and therefore how long his misery will be because of his crime! This is a very far straying. As for one who strays only slightly, he returns again to his right guidance. Among those who associate others with Allah are those who do not dispute the divinity of the Truth but make partners for Allah. Some polytheists deny divinity altogether, and this is disbelief. Thus there is a polytheist who believes in Allah but makes partners for Him.

That is why we find that the polytheists in the time of the Messenger of Allah said of the idols: ﴿We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position.﴾ (39:3)

Had they said: "We only slaughter for them so that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position," it would have been permissible for them to enter into the worship of Allah. But they affirmed worship for the idols, so there is no escape from their entry into shirk. Our master Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said about the idols: ﴿Indeed, they are enemies to me, except the Lord of the worlds.﴾ (26:77)

He uses the exception to define clearly and decisively, saying to his people: "What you worship of idols is all an enemy to me, except the Lord of the worlds." It is as though the people of Ibrahim believed in Allah but placed some partners with Him. That is why Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said of Allah:

﴿Who created me, and it is He who guides me. And who feeds me and gives me drink.﴾ (26:78–79)

Thus, shirk is not merely the denial of God's existence; it may also be the association of others with God. Let us see whom they worship and call upon in their calamities:

﴿They call upon none besides Him except females, and they call upon none except a rebellious Satan.﴾ (4:117)

Here "in" (إن) means "mā" (لا/ما, i.e., "not"). The particle "in" is sometimes conditional and sometimes negating, as in His saying elsewhere:

﴿Their mothers are none other than those who bore them﴾ (58:2), meaning: "Their mothers are none other than those who bore them." Likewise "in" in His saying "in yad'ūna min dūnihi illā ināthan" (they call upon none besides Him except females). The Arabs used to attribute to the woman everything that is weak and feeble, and therefore the Truth says:

﴿Is one who is brought up in ornaments, and is in dispute not clear [in argument]?﴾ (43:18)

Thus, in the custom of the Arabs, females cannot give victory or defence. Hence the poet says:

"I do not know, nor do I think I know, whether the people of Ḥiṣn are men or women."

Here "al-qawm" (the people) is intended to mean men, because they stand up to confront problems. So why do you call upon females besides God? Do you do so because they are weak, or because you say: "The angels are the daughters of God"? They used to worship the angels, and when you make the division, why do you assign daughters to God, although He created sons and daughters?

Therefore the Truth says:

﴿That, then, is an unjust division﴾ (53:22), meaning an unjust division in which justice was not observed.

When we look at all the idols, we find that their names are feminine names:

﴿Have you considered al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā, and Manāt, the third, the other?﴾ (53:19–20)

Likewise there was an idol named "Isāf" and "Nā'ilah." Are these idols females? And how do you call upon women, when women neither give victory nor benefit? Or are what you worship besides God idols with female names, or are they women, or are they angels?

And the Truth says: "They call upon none besides Him except females." The construction here is one of restriction (qaṣr): it means that they call upon none except females, just as we say: "I honour none but Zayd." This negates honouring anyone other than Zayd and affirms honouring Zayd. So when the Truth says "They call upon none besides Him except females," it means they do not call upon anyone other than females; therefore the Truth conjoins with it: "and they call upon none except a rebellious Satan."

In the opening of the verse He used the construction of restriction (al-qaṣr). The restriction means that the act is confined to what is restricted and does not extend beyond it to others. So they worship females: this is the first restriction. Then the second restriction is His saying: "and they call upon none except a rebellious Satan."

The servants of the idols used to claim that inside every idol there is something that speaks to them. Therefore there had to be a devil inside each idol speaking to them, and this was a kind of deception. Devils are not only jinn but also human beings.

There are custodians and servants who attend to the service of the deities and want to give the deities authority and influence, so that good things come to the deities, such as offerings and vows, and the custodians are made happy by that. Therefore they used to hire someone with a hoarse voice who would speak from behind the idol and say: "Slaughter for me such-and-such, or bring me such-and-such," just as happens with charlatans, in order to establish authority for themselves. Thus, whoever spoke within these idols was either a devil from the jinn or a devil from mankind. The word "shayṭān" derives from "shaṭn," which means "distance."

Describing the devil as "mārid" (rebellious) requires us to know that there is the word "mārid" and the word "marīd," and that all matters that are absent from the senses are derived from sensible matters. When we take up the root m-r-d, we find words such as "amrad" (beardless, smooth-cheeked), "imra'ah marda'" (a smooth-skinned woman), "shajarah marda'" (a smooth tree), and "ṣarḥ mumarrad" (a smoothed palace).

The whole root revolves around smoothness of texture. Amrad means smooth, i.e., the places where hair grows are soft. "Ṣarḥ mumarrad," like the palace of Bilqīs, means a palace polished with a soft polish, to such a degree that it was mistaken for water, and therefore she uncovered her shins for fear that her garment would get wet.

A "shajarah marda'" is one on which it is impossible to climb because of the extreme smoothness of its trunk, just like the palm tree, on which no branches remain; therefore they drive some large nails into the trunk of this palm in order to climb up it.

The "mārid" devil is the rebel whom you cannot grasp. So "mārid," "marīd," "mumarrad," "marda'" and "amrad" all derive from smoothness of texture.

﴿They call upon none except a rebellious Satan.﴾

When the disobedient try to grasp the devil on the Day of Judgement, he says to them:

﴿I had no authority over you, except that I called you and you responded to me﴾ (14:22). In this way he disowns those who followed him, because he did not possess any power of persuasion or power of compulsion; he merely called out to some of creation, their sight was dazzled, and they followed him out of extreme foolishness.

The Satan is described as one whom God expelled from His mercy. So He says:

﴿Allah has cursed him, and he said, "I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion."﴾ (118)

Why this curse? Satan sinned and disobeyed God. Adam also sinned and disobeyed God. So why did God curse Satan and why did He pardon Adam? The answer is found in the Qur'an:

{Then Adam received from his Lord words, and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.} (37, Surat al-Baqarah)

From this statement we understand that there is a difference between a created being rejecting God's ruling (hukm) and committing disobedience out of heedlessness. When God commanded Iblis to prostrate, Iblis said:

﴿He said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay."﴾ (part of 12, Surat al-A'raf)

This is a rejection of God's ruling, and it differs from the words of Adam and Eve, who said:

﴿"Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves."﴾ (part of 23, Surat al-A'raf)

Thus we find that Adam acknowledged God's ruling and acknowledged that he could not control himself. Therefore, every person should beware of coming to what God has forbidden and saying, "No, this matter is not forbidden." Rather, if he cannot control himself, let him acknowledge and say, "What God has forbidden is forbidden, but I am unable to control myself." In this way he removes disbelief (kufr) from himself, and he remains merely a sinner. Perhaps repentance (tawbah) or seeking forgiveness (istighfar) will remove his misdeeds. As for the one who declares lawful what God has forbidden, he persists in disbelief, and God seals his insight as a result.

Glorified and exalted is He, who describes Satan by saying, "Allah has cursed him," meaning He expelled him from His mercy, so that the son of Adam should be alert to Satan's snares and beware of him, because he is expelled from the mercy of God.

Had our master Adam (peace be upon him) applied his mind, he would have refuted Satan's statement and his scheming, because Satan's scheming is weak. But Adam (peace be upon him) did not imagine that anyone would swear falsely by God. Satan had sworn:

﴿And he swore to them, "Indeed, I am to you of the sincere advisors."﴾ (21, Surat al-A'raf)

Adam's heedlessness (peace be upon him) concerned a matter God willed, namely that Adam be a vicegerent (khalifah) on this earth. Therefore it was easy for Satan to whisper to Adam and his wife:

﴿Then Satan whispered to them to reveal to them what was concealed from them of their private parts. He said, "Your Lord did not forbid you from this tree except that you become angels or become of the eternal."﴾ (20, Surat al-A'raf)

Satan deceived Adam and Eve by claiming that God had forbidden them to eat from that tree so that they would not become angels and so that they would not remain eternal. Had Adam applied his mind to the matter, he would have said to Satan: "Eat from the tree so that you become an angel and become of the eternal, you who said, in great fear of God:"

﴿"My Lord, then reprieve me until the day they are resurrected."﴾ (36, Surat al-Hijr)

God wants us to learn from Adam's heedlessness, so the believer must be vigilant.

So He says of Satan: "Allah has cursed him, and he said, 'I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion.'"

When the Qur'an addresses a matter, that matter requires reflection. We notice that Iblis spoke these words when no humans existed except Adam and Eve. How did he know what would happen in the future, that he would have followers among humans? And how did he say, "I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion"?

He knew that he had gained power over their father Adam and their mother Eve, so he would surely gain power over their children and take some of these children to his side. He said this on the basis of a supposition arising from his power over Adam and Eve. Those among humans who followed Iblis confirmed Iblis's supposition, and this supposition was at the moment he said: "I will surely take from among Your servants an appointed portion."

Iblis drew this supposition because he had gained power over Adam and Eve, even though Adam and Eve had received the obligation (taklif, religious responsibility) directly from God. So what about the children, who did not receive the obligation directly but through the messengers (rusul)? Thus Iblis's supposition was based on evidence. Supposition (zann), as we know, is a probability that is not certain, and it is opposed by delusion (wahm), which is an improbable likelihood. God says:

﴿And Iblis had already confirmed his assumption about them.﴾ (part of 20, Surat Saba')

For this reason Iblis also said:

﴿"If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely seize his descendants, except a few."﴾ (part of 62, Surat al-Isra')

He also said:

{He said, "By Your might, I will surely mislead them all."} (82, Surat Sad)

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 4, verse 119:

Since Iblis has said, "I will surely take from among Your servants a determined portion" (﴿لأتخذن من عبادك نصيبا مفروضا﴾), this is an acknowledgment that he will not be able to take all the children of Adam. The fard (determined, obligatory portion), as we know, means that which is cut off, and of a thing described as mafrud it is said that it is the cut-off matter about which there is never any dispute.

What, then, is Iblis's means of taking a determined portion from the children of Adam?

God Almighty clarifies for us Iblis's methods, in Iblis's own words:

﴿And I will mislead them, and I will arouse in them desires, and I will command them so they will slit the ears of cattle, and I will command them so they will alter the creation of God. And whoever takes Satan as an ally instead of God has certainly suffered a clear loss.﴾ (4:119)

In this verse there is a detailing of the ways in which Iblis takes a determined portion from the children of Adam. Iblis is the one who said, as the Qur'an relates: ﴿Surely I will sit in wait for them on Your straight path﴾ (7:16).

We have already known that he sits only on the good path, because the path of one who has chosen evil conduct does not need a devil, for he is himself a devil. Therefore Iblis does not go to the tavern; rather, he stands at the door of the mosque to watch people doing good, and then he whispers to them. In this there is an answer to those who say, "The whisperings come to me at the moment of prayer." Prayer, as we know, is the most noble station of the servant, for he stands before his Lord; therefore Satan tries to distract the person from it so as to withhold reward from him. These whisperings are a healthy sign of faith, but they require vigilance. So whenever Satan prods a person with a prod, let him remember the saying of the Truth:

﴿And if a prompting from Satan should prod you, then seek refuge in God﴾ (7:200).

When we seek refuge in God immediately, Satan knows that you are alert to him. Even if you are reciting the Qur'an during prayer and Satan whispers to you, stop the recitation, seek refuge in God, then continue the recitation and the prayer. When Satan knows that you are alert to him once, twice and thrice, he withdraws from you, and he does not come to you afterwards except when he senses heedlessness in you.

The Truth shows us a method of taking the determined portion from the servants of God, and He said, concerning Iblis: "And I will mislead them." Misguidance (al-idlal) means that Satan leads a person along a way that does not lead to the praiseworthy goal, because when a person follows the shortest route that leads to the set goal, that means he has been guided; but if he goes far away from the goal, this is misguidance. The Truth, Glorified and Exalted is He, by setting out the method of guidance, has given us the shortest straight path to the goal; so if we deviate here and there, the deviation at the beginning widens until we end up at no goal at all.

We have given this example in the past: there is a point at the centre of every circle called the centre of the circle. If the one heading towards it deviates by a ratio of one in a thousand of a millimetre, the distance of his separation from it widens as he proceeds at that same rate of deviation, even though it is assumed that every step he takes brings him nearer to the goal.

We have also given an illustrative example of the "kiosk" that is found before railway stations, where a "kiosk" attendant directs the trains' directions onto the various tracks and allows each train to stop at a particular platform so that the trains do not collide. To accomplish this task, the switching attendant in this "kiosk" moves a rail whose thickness is, at times, a number of millimetres, so that this rail joins with another rail, and in this way it allows the train's wheels to pass from one rail to another.

Misguidance, then, is for a person to follow a path that does not lead to the goal; and every step a person takes on this path takes him further from it. This distancing from the goal is far misguidance. Misguidance from Satan occurs by his adorning evil and ugliness for the person, to distance him from the paths of goodness and virtue.

After that comes, on Satan's tongue, what the Truth said in this verse: "And I will arouse in them desires" (wa la-umanniyannahum). Wishful thinking (al-amani) means that a person sets up in his imagination something he enjoys, without taking a single step of action that would bring him closer to it. An example of this is the person we see sitting and wishing for himself, saying, "I will have such-and-such and such-and-such," and he does not advance a single step to achieve it.

For this reason the poet says, consoling himself:

"Wish—if it be true, it is the best of wishes;
and if not, we have lived by it a pleasant while."

That is, he enjoyed these wishes in daydreams, whether these dreams were owning a palace, a car or other things. Every wish that does not stir a person to an action that brings him closer to it is a false wish. For this reason it is said: "Wishes are the merchandise of fools." Satan gives a person the wish that there is no resurrection and no recompense.

After that Satan says: "And I will command them so they will slit the ears of cattle" (fa-layubattunna adhan al-an'am). Al-batk means cutting, and al-an'am are camels, cattle and sheep; that is, cutting the ears of livestock. The Qur'an mentions the livestock:

﴿Eight pairs: of the sheep two, and of the goats two. Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or that which the wombs of the two females contain? Inform me with knowledge, if you are truthful. And of the camels two, and of the cattle two. Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or that which the wombs of the two females contain?﴾ (6:143–144, part).

If "zawj" (pair) meant "two," the number would be only four. The Qur'anic expression teaches us, and makes clear, that we should distinguish well in order to understand that the meaning of the word "zawj" is never "two," but rather: one that has with it another of its kind or species. Thus one says of a shoe "zawj" because there is another single shoe with it. Another example: the word "tawam" (twin), which we think means "two," but the real meaning is that a twin is one who has another twin; when we wish to express two, we say "tawamān" (two twins).

As for Satan's plan, "And I will command them so they will slit the ears of cattle," there is a story behind it. We know that those who profit from misguidance create for themselves a temporal authority so as to bind people to themselves. The custodians of the idols would attend to their service, and no one noticed that it is foolish to accept the idea that mankind should serve the gods, whereas God is the Sustainer of His creation, who cares for them and manages their affairs. These people were the ones who profited from the heedlessness that afflicted mankind, and they lived as custodians in order to take the good. Naturally, Satan, whether from mankind or the jinn, found this a means: he would sit inside the idol and speak, and the custodians and attendants would take this matter to promote propaganda for the idol. The foolish would bring them camels, cattle and sheep, which they would slaughter and eat. For this reason the custodians were always, and in most cases, people of corpulence, because they were people of bellies. The Prophet (ﷺ) said:

("Indeed God dislikes the fat scholar.") (1)

Such a scholar readily takes the best of people and benefits from them; he profits from people's misguidance. Whoever profits from error wishes that the error continue, just like the one who profits from the drug trade: he wishes that all people would take drugs, and when campaigns are launched to combat drugs, he becomes angry and grieved.

Likewise is the black-market merchant, who is distressed when goods arrive in sufficient quantity to meet people's needs. Every hidden corruption has behind it people who profit from it. When the one who profits from corruption sees a reform, he becomes angry and tries to find a means to keep the corruption going. For this reason the custodians would blow into the idols so that they produced sounds, and thereby they would make demands upon the foolish believers who trusted them, just like the charlatans we hear about, where one of them says to the family of a patient: "The patient has a demon, and the demon demands a she-camel, or a sacrifice, or blood."

This is how the custodians acted, trying by every means of tricks and deceptions to take camels, cattle and sheep from the heedless and naive. When the owner of a camel, cow or sheep slits the ear of any one of them, this means that it has been vowed to the idols; and idols by their nature do not eat, but the custodians eat.

In another verse the Truth says:

﴿Say: Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision, and you made from it the forbidden and the lawful?﴾ (10:59, part).

And the Truth also mentions in this matter:

﴿Eight pairs: of the sheep two, and of the goats two. Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or that which the wombs of the two females contain? Inform me with knowledge, if you are truthful. And of the camels two, and of the cattle two. Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or that which the wombs of the two females contain? Or were you witnesses when God enjoined this upon you? Who then is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against God to mislead people without knowledge? Surely God does not guide the unjust people.﴾ (6:143–144).

So is the forbidden "the males," or "the females," or that which the wombs of the females contain?

None of these is forbidden; God created all of them as lawful provision, and the blessing itself knows its function. We notice in the Egyptian countryside that when a water buffalo, cow or sheep is choked by its rope, or suffers harm or illness, it lies down and stretches out its neck, and it is said: "It has sought the lawful" (laqad talab al-halal), as though the beast were saying to its owner: "Hasten me to slaughter so that you may benefit from my flesh."
