The Truth, glorified, has clarified: I created inclination to serve the building of the universe, but I want you to elevate desire and rise above it in this inclination. When you take multiple wives, I do not ask you to be entirely free of all inclination, because that is a matter not governed by rational logic. Rather, I want you to define inclination and place it in its heart-domain alone, and it is not right for inclination in any one of you to extend beyond the heart into conduct.

O servant who believes, love whom you wish and hate whom you wish, but do not let this love drive your body to give the one you love what belongs to another out of injustice. And hate, O servant, whom you wish; no legislator can legislate for the heart to hate or to love. But do not let your hatred pass from your heart to your limbs, so as to wrong the one you hate.

We have an example in our master 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, when the killer of his brother passed by him, and a companion of his drew his attention: "This is the killer of your brother."

Here 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "And what should I do with him, when Allah has guided him to Islam?" As if this killer's Islam had ended the matter for 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him. When this killer came to 'Umar's gathering, 'Umar said to him: "When you approach me, turn your face away from me, for my heart is not at ease with you." The man asked: "Does your not loving me prevent me from any of my rights?" 'Umar said: "No."

The man said: "Only women weep over love." This is 'Umar, who is the Caliph, and the man is one of the subjects. But 'Umar, the Caliph, fears injustice, and he owns this person, who is under the command and rule of the Caliph 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, the capacity to reject feelings of love and hatred, so long as they do not prevent his rights as a citizen.

When the Truth, glorified and exalted, creates the inclinations of hearts, He also establishes the rule: beware, O believer, of letting the inclination of the heart pass into conduct. Let the inclination of the heart be as you wish. Likewise, if you, O believer, marry and then marry another woman, the method does not require you to achieve the absolute justice that applies to something you do not own, which is your heart's inclination. Rather, the method sets for you the rules by which the conduct of your body proceeds: you must be just in dividing time, maintenance, clothing, cheerfulness of face, and good speech, and you must not subject these to the inclination of the heart. After that, you and your heart are free.

We see some of those who wish to appear among people as understanders of the Qur'an or as advocates of renewal, who ride the wave against polygamy. Before one of you rides the wave against polygamy and takes the stand of rejecting it, claiming that he understands the Qur'anic text, we say to him: you must search for the causes of resentment toward polygamy. They are not in polygamy itself, but come from the fact that the Muslim takes Allah's permission of polygamy and does not take Allah's command regarding justice. Had the Muslim applied justice with polygamy, we would not have found such a crisis. For this reason one of these people says: the Truth, glorified and exalted, commanded keeping to one wife and restricting oneself to her when there is fear of failing to be just in polygamy, so He said: ﴿But if you fear that you will not be just, then one [only]﴾ (4:3).

Then He came in another verse and said: "And you will never be able to be just between wives, even if you should strive."

We say: if one of you wishes to understand the Qur'an, he must know that the Truth, in this verse, did not stop at His words "even if you should strive." Rather, He made a consequence of the inability to be just: "So do not incline completely." He, glorified, made a consequence of the inability to be just, and commanded not to incline completely. That is the wisdom of the First Legislator, who knows whom He created and how He created them. Had the Truth not made a consequence of "And you will never be able to," it would have been permissible for those who ride the wave to demand what they say, abolishing polygamy. So we say to them: be mindful that the Truth, glorified, has clarified that your inability to be just is a matter I know, and therefore I ask you not to incline completely, which is within your capacity. This means that He, glorified, has kept the ruling and did not revoke it.

"So do not incline completely, leaving her as if suspended." In this statement is a command not to leave the man's first wife as "suspended," the woman whose fate and course in life have not been determined: she is neither without a husband to marry, nor married so as to take her share and portion from her husband. Rather, he must give her her portion of lodging, maintenance, clothing, good reception, cheerfulness, companionship, and consolation.

Then the Truth says: "And if you amend and fear Allah, indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful."

His words "amend" indicate that there was corruption present, and what is required is that you search for the causes that made the man corrupt his marital relationship so as to end it. After that, the Muslim must renew a new piety in dealing, in light of what Allah legislated. When the Muslim amends what he corrupted, by making the first wife no longer "suspended," giving her her right to lodging and maintenance, caring for her children, and turning toward her and the children in a good manner, then Allah, glorified, forgives and has mercy. The Muslim does not amend what he corrupted except while intending not to resume any deed except in accordance with the method of the pious, and he finds the Truth forgiving of what has passed and merciful to him.

If the man cannot do this, and the woman does not agree to give up some of her portion to appease him, then separation here becomes a necessity. It is not reasonable to bind married and family life with chains of iron, and we cannot tie the spouses together without separation if the hearts are repelling one another. Likewise we cannot be assured for the woman that she will live in this way.

To the one who says: it is not right to separate the spouses, we say: how do you want to govern married life with chains? Marriage is a bond whose foundation is tranquility, affection, and mercy. If these elements are absent, how does the marriage continue, and how can you compel a husband to live with a wife he does not love and does not accept, and compel a wife to live with a husband she does not love? Separating them in such a case may be a means that Allah, glorified and exalted, wills, so that the husband is granted better than her, and the wife is granted better than him.

We have witnessed this often in real life: the husband lived happily with a new wife, and the wife lived happily with a new husband. As for those who boasted about the matter of not separating while married life is impossible, and who attacked Islam in this field, they are repeating what was among the people of the West: that marriage admits no separation.

(1) Narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Darimi.

Now we see the whole world today, all the Christians, Jews and others among the religions and sects, resorting to divorce, because events have forced them to legislate divorce. It is as though they have come to Islam not as Islam, but as the only solution to their problems. So, if it is established that those who attack a detail of the religion are compelled to adopt it under the pressure of events, we must warn them against hastiness and haste, and against judging the matters of the Islamic religion as unsuitable, because the truth compels even one who is not a Muslim to implement an Islamic matter. For He is the One who said:

﴿And if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance. And ever is Allah All-Encompassing and Wise.﴾ (4:130)

He, glory be to Him, possesses abundant bounty. He is able to grant the husband a righteous wife who satisfies all his needs, and to grant the wife another husband who fulfills all her needs and accepts her plainness, if she is plain, and Allah makes him one with eyes that see the aspects of goodness and beauty in her. We may find a man whom events have afflicted with the beauty of a woman he had been married to, which bewildered him and made his thoughts confused and troubled. After that, Allah grants him one whom he longs for, a trustworthy woman who guards him, and he is at ease when he is away from her in his work, and suspicions do not fill his breast, because his heart has become full of trust in her, even if she has little share of beauty.

"And if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance, and ever is Allah All-Encompassing and Wise." So beware of thinking that Allah does not have what brings comfort to every person. Rather, He, glory be to Him, has everything that brings comfort to all people, and the pharmacy of Allah's method is full of medicines, but some creatures do not understand how to use these medicines to treat their illnesses.

And of His wisdom, He, glory be to Him, does not compel two people to live together while they both dislike it, because they have lost affection and mercy between them.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 4, verse 131:

Then the Truth follows it with a verse:

﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. We have already instructed those who were given the Scripture before you, and you, to fear Allah. But if you disbelieve, then indeed to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is ever Free of need, Praiseworthy.﴾

He, glory be to Him, is the One who satisfies the husband if he separates from his wife, and satisfies the wife if she separates from her husband, because He, exalted and high, created the world, which will never be too narrow for the desire of the man or the woman after separation by divorce. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and He is able to grant the man a wife better than the one he parted from, and to grant the woman a man better than the one she parted from. Nothing has gone outside the dominion of Allah, and He is the Vast in giving.

We often find a man who marries a woman and she does not bear children, and it is said of her that she is barren. The two go to the testing laboratories, and sometimes it is said: the woman is the cause of the absence of offspring, or: the man is the cause of the absence of offspring. The two separate, each marries another, and the woman bears children from the new husband, and the man has children from the new wife, because the whole matter is the decrees of Allah. The affairs of life are not merely the completion of causes that compel Allah; rather He is always the Causer. He is the One who says:

﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills. He bestows female [children] upon whom He wills and bestows males upon whom He wills. Or He gives them both males and females, and He renders whom He wills barren. Indeed, He is Knowing and Competent.﴾

How many images, then, do we have of such a situation? "He bestows female [children] upon whom He wills and bestows males upon whom He wills, or He gives them both males and females, and renders whom He wills barren": these are four decrees that apply to man and woman. When Allah bestows females upon the believer, he is happy, and likewise when He bestows males. When Allah gives a family sons only, the wife yearns to have a daughter; and if the Truth gives a family daughters only, the man and woman both wish for a son. When Allah gives them both males and females, we find them having reached the state that usually gladdens the eyes, and the state that gladdens the eyes is usually delayed.

The state that the soul dislikes, the Truth brings it closer to the first of the gifts. So He first said: "He creates what He wills," and after that: "He bestows female [children] upon whom He wills," then He mentioned the giving of males, and then He brings the state in which the giving reaches its peak: "or He gives them both males and females."

Finally, He brings the fourth decree, which He applies to some of His creatures: "and renders whom He wills barren."

Why does a person rejoice in the decree of Allah when Allah bestows females or males upon him, and his joy increases in the decree of Allah when He, glory be to Him, bestows both males and females? And why, then, O human, do you not rejoice in the decree of Allah when He makes you barren? Do you think you take the decree you love and reject the decree that is not to your liking? The four situations are all a decree from Allah.

If a person looks at each of the four matters, he would be content with them.

He, glory be to Him, creates what He wills and renders whom He wills barren. If a person receives this with a tranquil acceptance of the decree of Allah, then Allah may gladden his eye just as He gladdened the eyes of others with females, or with males, or with males and females together. I swear to you that if a person or a couple accepted the decree of Allah in barrenness, as they accepted it in the other previous situations, with contentment, Allah would surely provide for them. I do not say with sons and daughters who burden them in pregnancy, upbringing and other things, but He would provide them with people who serve them, whom others have raised. What makes the couples lacking offspring live in constriction is that they are, in their lives, discontent with the decree of Allah, God forbid, so Allah makes their life a discontent. He is the One who says in His Hadith Qudsi:

From Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Allah, the Exalted, says: "I am as My servant thinks I am, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself; and if he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than theirs; and if he draws near to Me a span, I draw near to him a cubit; and if he draws near to Me a cubit, I draw near to him a fathom; and if he comes to Me walking, I come to him running."(1)

So the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, says: "To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth." Beware of saying that Allah would be constrained in providing for the man who separates from his wife, or the woman who separates from her husband, from His bounty to them. As long as He, glory be to Him, has decreed separation as a solution for the lack of harmony in their life together, He, glory be to Him, will give abundantly to the husband and abundantly to the wife. It is incumbent upon you, O Muslim, to obey the method of the Truth as everything in the heavens and everything on the earth obeys it. Then ask yourself this question: who settles all your interests?

It is the Truth, glory be to Him, who has subjected things that are not within your power. Did you compel the sun to shine on you with light and heat? Did you compel water to evaporate and descend as pure rain? Did you compel the wind to blow? Did you strike the earth, telling it: nourish what I place in you of seed with the elements that accompany it and that it needs, so that it produces plants? All this is not within the power of your will; rather it is subjected to you by the command of Allah. If you desired uprightness in your affair, you would be like the subjected in what Allah has made for you to have choice in, and you would say to Allah: "I love Your method, O Lord, and what it asks of me I will carry out to the best of my ability," and then your heart and your body would be in accord with the commands and prohibitions of the method, and the universe would harmonize and agree with you, just as the subjected, compelled, driven universe is in harmony.

﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ is a reminder that everything is owned by Allah and is in obedience to Him. So do not deviate, O vicegerent of Allah, from the universe; everything in it serves you. Ask yourself: do you live in the light of the method of Allah or not? For the universe has harmonized, being subjected to Allah, and no disorder has occurred in its general laws. He, glory be to Him, says:

{And the heaven He raised and imposed the balance. That you not transgress within the balance. So establish weight with justice and do not make deficient the balance.} (Surat al-Rahman)

This is a clarification from the Truth, blessed and exalted: if you want your voluntary affairs to be set right, then look at the universe, for subjected things never suffer any disorder at all. Rather, disorder comes only from the choices of man that depart from the method of Allah.

"We have already instructed those who were given the Scripture before you, and you, to fear Allah." He, glory be to Him, clarifies: We instructed those to whom We sent the method before you, and We instruct you, the people of the final nation, to adhere to the method through the commands and prohibitions, so that you make your choices submit to what Allah wills from you, until you are harmonious like the universe in which you live, and everything becomes orderly in your life. The Truth did not state this matter only for Muslims; rather it is a universal matter that every messenger brought: "We have already instructed those who were given the Scripture before you."

He did not say "We legislated for those who were given the Scripture before you," nor "We made obligatory," but He said "We instructed" (waṣṣainā), and the word "instruction" (waṣiyyah) makes the one who receives it feel the love of the one who instructs for the one instructed: "We have already instructed those who were given the Scripture before you, and you, to fear Allah." Fear of Allah means that we do what Allah commands and avoid what He forbids, so that we govern the movement of our choices by the method of our Lord. If we govern the movement of our choices by the method of Allah, we become with the universe as though we were subjected to the causes of interest and good.

Then the Truth says: "But if you disbelieve, then indeed to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is ever Free of need, Praiseworthy." The opposite of disbelief is faith, and whoever departs from faith, Allah is free of him. So do not think, O you addressed by the method of Allah, that I am courting you to faith because I am in need of your faith; no. I only want from you that you be a sound society, a happy society. And if you disbelieve, the whole dominion will still belong to Allah, even if you were rebellious in the grip of your Lord's decrees. You will not control birth, death, or destinies. The universe is stable and sound, and the Qur'an has drawn attention to the order of the universe. The Truth says:

{Have they not looked at the sky above them, how We built it and adorned it, and it has no flaws? And the earth — We spread it and cast therein firmly set mountains and caused to grow therein of every beautiful kind, an insight and a reminder for every servant turning back [to Allah]. And We send down from the sky blessed water, and We caused to grow thereby gardens and grain for harvest, and tall palm trees with layered spathes, as provision for the servants. And We give life thereby to a dead land. Thus will be the Emergence.} (Surat Qaf)

Yet at a moment, the Truth commands one of His worlds and its order is disturbed, so you see the stable earth quaking, of which He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿And He cast into the earth firmly set mountains lest it shake with you﴾ (part of verse 15, Surat al-Nahl).

He, glory be to Him, is the One who possesses it, so He makes it convulse and causes an earthquake in some place on it, so that the buildings upon it crumble, until you understand that the world is not governed automatically, but governed by causes, and its reins remain in the self-subsistence of the Causer. We also turn to some of the whirlwinds of dust that close off the whole airspace so that no one can see through them. This is a drawing of attention from Allah to us, clarifying: these laws were made by My power, and these laws will not go outside the absoluteness of My power.

We see countries that live on constant rains which nourish the earth; we find greenery covering the mountains, and we do not find a single hand's breadth without fertility, greenery, or trees. One may suppose that this matter is mechanical, but the Truth brings the decree of drought upon this region, so the rain is withheld, the fertile land turns to barrenness, the livestock perish and die, and people die of thirst. This is so that the Truth may draw our attention to the fact that the matter is not mechanical, but the decrees of One who wills.

In another place on the globe, we find a calm, level land with a beautiful mountain rising over it, and suddenly the peak of the mountain turns into a volcanic crater hurling lava and spewing fire, and people run to save themselves. Therefore we must know that the intellect of the intelligent person is manifested in choosing his own wills in accord with the wills of Allah. For example, the human intellect was not given the innate capacity to foresee earthquakes, but the donkey possesses this capacity.

"But if you disbelieve, then indeed to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is ever Free of need, Praiseworthy." He opened the verse with the same statement: "To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth," in order to establish and affirm the necessity of obedience to the method of Allah, so that man harmonizes with the universe. The statement comes a second time within the same verse to establish that the Truth is Free of need. Do not say that the statement was repeated more than once in one verse, but say: the Truth brought it at the beginning of the verse to establish one meaning, and it came at the end of the verse to establish another meaning. So He, glory be to Him, is Free of need from the servants: ﴿And say, "The truth is from your Lord; so whoever wills - let him believe; and whoever wills - let him disbelieve."﴾ (part of verse 29, Surat al-Kahf).

The coming of "To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth" [at the start] is to establish the basis that the servant should obey his Creator, and the coming of "To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth" [at the end of the verse] is to establish the basis of Allah's freedom from need of all the servants. The same statement comes in the next verse, where He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.﴾ (132)

1 Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Tawhid, and recorded by Muslim in his Sahih by three routes.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 4, verse 132:

﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And Allah is sufficient as Disposer of affairs.﴾

The repetition of this statement a third time serves to reassure the human being that God guarantees and preserves the foundations of life. The sun will not rebel one day and fail to rise, the air will not rebel and fail to blow, and the earth will not withhold its elements from you, because all these things are subjected by the command of Allah, who created you, created them, and measured within them your sustenance.

For this reason our Lord makes clear: "I am the Disposer (al-Wakil) who entrusts you with affairs, suffices you, and makes you independent of every other disposer."

The wakil (disposer, trustee) is the one who carries out your duties for you while you sit at ease. When a person among us appoints a wakil to perform some tasks for him, he feels happy, even though this human wakil may err, become confused, betray, lose his wisdom, or accept bribes. But the Truth, with His full power, reassures the servant that He is the capable Wakil. So be at peace that the foundations of your existence are secure: He is the Owner of the sun, so it will not step outside His subjection; He is the Owner of the waters, the Owner of the wind, and the Owner of all the elements of the earth. And since Allah is the Sovereign (al-Malik), He is the Guardian (al-Hafiz) over all these things, and He is the best Wakil, because He is a capable Wakil with no interest of His own.

Come, let us read this hadith:

It is narrated that a Bedouin came, made his mount kneel, tied it, and prayed behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished the prayer, he came to his mount, untied its rope, mounted it, and called out: "O Allah, have mercy on me and on Muhammad, and do not share our mercy with anyone else." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you say this man is more misguided, or his camel? Did you not hear what he said?" They said: "Yes." He said: "He has restricted (hazara) a vast mercy. Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, created one hundred mercies; He sent down one mercy by which creatures show compassion to one another, jinn and humans and animals, and He kept with Himself ninety-nine mercies. Do you say he is more misguided, or his camel?"(2)

So He is indeed "sufficient as Disposer" and "the best Disposer," and He reassures His servants. He makes clear that He is al-Qayyum (the Self-Subsisting Sustainer), where the meaning is intensive in standing; therefore everything in the universe needs a sustainer, and He is al-Qayyum. He also tells every human: strive in work, and after you have tired, sleep deeply, for I am the Living, the Self-Subsisting; slumber and sleep do not overtake Me. So is there a better disposer than this? "And Allah is sufficient as Disposer."

1 hazara: prevented and restricted.
2 Narrated by Ahmad and Abu Dawud.

Then the Truth brings another ground that confirms He is free of need of the worlds. It is not enough for Him to say that He is self-sufficient and that He created all that is in the heavens and the earth, and that if you disbelieve, O human being, the sin is upon you, and if you believe, belief is a safeguard for you. He makes it clear: do not, O mankind, think that you were created and left scattered, and that God has no authority over you. No. God, glorified is He, says:

﴿If He wills, He can take you away, O people, and bring others. And God is ever capable of that.﴾ (133)

Some of the men lacking insight among the philosophers said: "It is true that God created us, but we have gone out of the sphere of His power." No. Rather, glory be to Him, if He wills He would take you all away and bring others, and that is not difficult for God. And He is the One who said: "And God is ever capable of that."

When we read "kāna" beside the word "Allah," it does not carry the meaning of time. God is capable even before there is anything over which He is capable. He was not capable only when He created man; rather, by the attribute of power He created man, because God, exalted is He, has changes [of state], so He remains capable and existent at every moment, and He was and still is.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 4, verse 134:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿Whoever desires the reward of this world, then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. And Allah is ever Hearing, Seeing.﴾ (4:134)

Since the messengers have conveyed to man that with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter, why this heedlessness? Why not take the increase? And why do we go only for the bargain of this world, since the Truth possesses the reward of this world, of health, wealth and everything? If a person strives in the means, he takes the result of his means. The Truth says:

﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him thereof, but he has no share in the Hereafter.﴾ (42:20) (Surat al-Shura).

The Truth did not say that "the Hereafter" stands in opposition to this world, and that whoever takes this world will not take the Hereafter or vice versa. Rather, He, glory be to Him, wants man to take both this world and the Hereafter together. So, O you who desire the reward of this world, do not deprive yourself, through foolishness, of the reward of the Hereafter. The word "reward" (thawab) has a noteworthy point: there are things that act for you even though you do not ask them to act, and you benefit from their action; and there are other things that are affected by your movement, so if you move, strive and work upon them, they give to you.

An example of this is the earth: if you sow seed in it, it produces crops. The differences among people in this world, in advancement and backwardness, civilization and primitiveness, strength and weakness, come only from the category that is affected (yanfa'il) for man, not from the category that acts (yaf'al) for man and is subjected to him. The advancement of some people in civilization came about because they researched matter and elements and achieved tremendous scientific accomplishments in laboratories. So if you wish to be advanced, you must deal with the elements that are affected for you. All nations take their civilization from the category of what is affected for them, and they and the backward are only partners in what acts for them and is subjected for their benefit.

If we wish to ascend further in civilization, we must go to what acts and is subjected for us, and deal with it until it is affected for us. How? 

The sun gives us light and heat, and we can deal with the sun in another way that makes it affected for us, just as we have brought a lens called the "convergent lens" (al-'adasa al-lamma), which receives the rays of the sun, and the rays converge at the focal point of the lens, producing heat that ignites fire. That is, we made what acts for us become something affected for us as well, and they call that the emissive ambition (al-tumuh al-inba'ithi). Rain acts for man when it falls from the sky into valleys, and man can turn it into something affected when he installs huge turbines in its paths of descent, so it produces electricity.

Thus the civilizations of nations arise in stages. The first stage: they use what is affected for them. The second stage: they advance and use what is affected together with them. The third stage: they use what acts for them as something affected for them. An example of this is the use of solar energy by means of devices that gather this energy, an advancement together with the use of what acts for man so that it is affected together with man.

The most sublime thing in civilization now is laser rays, which produce near-miracles in the world of medicine. The word "laser" is taken, letter by letter, from words that carry the meaning of energy amplification through stimulated emission. So the word "laser" is like the word "ليمتد" (la-yamtadd): the lam is from one word, the ya from another, the mim from another, the ta from another and the dal from another, in order to indicate a named thing.

The translation of the name "laser" is: energy amplification through stimulated emission. In it there is spontaneous emission, which is the source of energy that acts for man even if he does not ask for it, whereas stimulated emission is produced when man stimulates energy to act for him in another way. Spontaneous emission is embodied in the sun, which gives light and heat. When scientists sat in laboratories and designed the lens that produces these rays, they excited and stirred them up and took them to make great energy from them, and thus they produced laser rays, which are energy amplification through stimulated emission. And because the full title was long, they took a letter from each word and formed the word "laser."

So civilizational advancements come through man's dealing with the category that is affected for man, and by stimulating and using what acts for him in its spontaneous manner so that it is affected together with him, like the rays of the sun, for example.

We have brought up all of this in order to clarify the horizons of the Truth's saying: "Whoever desires the reward of this world." The word "reward" (thawab) thus suggests that there is an action, for reward is recompense for deeds. If you desire the reward of this world, you must work for it; no one takes the reward of this world without work.

Out of the greatness, gentleness, bounty and mercy of the Truth, He made the reward of this world a prize for whoever works, whether he believes or disbelieves; but He specified for the believers a lasting reward in the Hereafter.

That is why it is said: "The world is a enjoyment (matA')," and the Truth adds to that: "With Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter, and Allah is ever Hearing, Seeing." It is foolishness that there should exist a path that gives man two recompenses and yet he restricts his aspiration to one.

Here is another point: when the Truth spoke of the reward of this world, He indicated that work is necessary to take the world, and the Truth did not mention a reward for the Hereafter separately, but made the reward for both the world and the Hereafter. So whoever among the believers works for the world also takes the Hereafter, because the Hereafter is the abode of recompense, and this world is a mount, a road and a way. It is as if every deed a Muslim does, keeping Allah in mind, Allah gives him a reward in this world and gives him a reward in the Hereafter.

The Truth concludes the verse: "And Allah is ever Hearing, Seeing." So the reward of this world and the Hereafter is attained only through work, and work is every event that occurs from the limbs of man. Speech, for example, is an event that occurs from the tongue, and it is also work. The counterpart of speech is action (fi'l), so deeds are divided into two kinds: sayings and doings. To clarify this matter, we read the Truth's saying:

﴿Nay, but you do not honour the orphan, and you do not urge one another to feed the poor, and you devour the inheritance, devouring greedily.﴾ (89:17-19) (Surat al-Fajr).

When the rich heard this saying, they recognized their conduct. And when the poor heard this saying, it was as if they said: "We do not have what we can feed the poor with." So in His saying, "and you do not urge one another to feed the poor," there is what clarifies for them the path to giving: that is, urge others to give. The one who does not own can speak to the wealthy so that he gives to the poor, and urging is speech, and speech is a kind of work.

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, calls the believers to arms to support the religion of Allah, saying:

﴿There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick, nor upon those who do not find what to spend, when they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger. There is no way (to blame) against the good-doers. And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.﴾ (9:91) (Surat al-Tawba).

He, glory be to Him, excused the weak, the sick and those who do not find what to spend from fighting, and dropped it from them and did not hold them accountable for it. But in the verse itself there is what defines what is required of these people: that they be sincere to Allah and His Messenger. So the one who is unable can speak of doing good, remind others of it and advise it. This is the meaning of the Truth's saying: "And Allah is ever Hearing, Seeing." He, glory be to Him, hears the speech of one who cannot and does not have the ability to perform such conduct, and He, glory be to Him, is Seeing, who sees the performer of every conduct.

So the reward of this world requires work, and work is the affecting of every limb toward what is required of it: the tongue speaks and the hand works. All the limbs of man work, but what is the work of the hearts? The work of the hearts is not heard or seen, and therefore the Truth said concerning sincerity of the heart, in a hadith qudsi:

("Sincerity is one of My secrets, which I have deposited in the heart of whomever I love of My servants.")¹

Thus we know that the intention of hearts belongs to Allah directly and does not enter the jurisdiction of the watchers and recorders (raqib and 'atid), the two angels charged with observing and recording the conduct and deeds of man. Therefore we find the Truth describing His essence in many places in the Qur'an as Subtle, Aware: Subtle, with knowledge of what enters and penetrates things, and Aware of everything, and Capable over everything. And we find the noble hadith tells us:

("Actions are only by intentions, and every person will have only what he intended. So whoever's emigration was to Allah and His Messenger, his emigration is to Allah and His Messenger; and whoever's emigration was for a worldly gain he might obtain or a woman he might marry, his emigration is to what he emigrated for.")²

So work is by the limbs, and among the limbs is the tongue. And so that we may regulate this matter, let us differentiate between action (fi'l) and work ('amal), and read and understand the verse:

﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ (61:2) (Surat al-Saff).

We find that the counterpart of saying is doing, and all of it is work. There is another kind of work that is neither saying nor doing, and that is "the intention of the heart." When the Truth says that He is Hearing and Seeing, the meaning is that He hears the saying and sees the doing.

1 Narrated by Abu al-Qasim al-Qushayri in al-Risala from a hadith of Ali ibn Abi Talib with a weak chain; the Qur'anic verses and sound hadiths on this theme are numerous.

2 Narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim and others among the compilers of the Sunan.

Almighty God then says: ﴿O you who have believed, be persistent in upholding justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether he is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both. So do not follow [your] desires, lest you not be just. And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse [to give it], then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.﴾ (4:135)

Whenever al-Haqq (the Truth) calls His believing servants, saying: "O you who have believed," He is in effect presenting the basis (haythiyya) of the ruling that comes after it. We see human judgment, before it pronounces its verdict, state its basis, saying: "Since legal article No. such-and-such stipulates such-and-such, we have ruled thus-and-so." So the bases precede the ruling, and the basis of the ruling that Allah issues is faith in Him, as in the saying of al-Haqq:

﴿O you who have believed, fasting has been prescribed for you﴾ (2:183).

The basis of the prescription here, and in any other ruling, is the servant's faith in Allah as Lord. So let the servant hear from his Lord, for He, glory be to Him, does not impose the duties of faith on all people, but imposes them only on the believers. And He says: "O you who have believed, be persistent in upholding justice." So the believer enters upon faith with the summit of justice (qist). Justice (qist) is equity ('adl), and equity is that the equitable person gives each possessor his right. The right of the One God is that a person believe in Him and acknowledge that He is one God.

Thus the summit of justice is faith, and since the believer began his faith with the summit of justice, which is faith, let him make justice prevail in all his conduct. Beware of making justice a matter or event that occurs once and then ends; otherwise al-Haqq would not have said, together with your believing brethren: "O you who have believed, be persistent in upholding justice."

Al-Haqq did not say to you, together with your believing brethren: "Be standing (qa'imin) in justice," but said "be persistent (qawwamin) in justice," meaning that what is required is continuity in just conduct. We say "fulan is standing (qa'im)" and "fulan is persistent (qawwam)," and we know that the word qawwam is an intensive form (sigha mubalagha). Accordingly the divine command to every believer is: do not uphold justice only once, but make it an inherent trait in you, and practise justice in all the affairs of your life. Justice, as we have known before, in its apparent meaning is equity ('adl), and also iqsat (the act of rectifying) is equity.

The word "qist" has caused a stir among the scholars, and in comment on this we have said: the matter is from the root qasata, yaqsutu, qusutan, meaning he oppressed and wronged. When a person removes oppression and wrong, one says: "aqsata fulan," meaning he removed the wrong. Thus "al-qist" (with a kasra on the qaf) is initial equity, but "al-iqsat" is equity that removes a wrong that had occurred.

Suppose people came to a judge who ruled between them with equity; this is qist. Then one of the two parties may appeal the judgment of the court of first instance, and the appellate court finds an error in application and issues a ruling removing the wrong; this second-degree ruling is called iqsat. In this way the scholars' dispute over this matter ends: qist is equity from the first instance, while iqsat means that there had been wrong and it was lifted, because it is preceded by a hamza called "the hamza of removal" (hamzat al-izala). Thus one says a'jama al-kitab, meaning the book had 'ujma (obscurity) in it, that is, something hidden and obscure to them existed in the book, and he removed the obscurity in it. The dictionaries of the language are called mu'jamat (lexicons), and the singular is mu'jam, which gives the meanings of words and thus removes their obscurity. Likewise the meaning of "aqsata" is that he removed the wrong.

Al-Haqq says: "O you who have believed, be persistent in upholding justice." So you, O believer, have by reason achieved the first rank of justice, and you have returned faith to the Lord, for He is the one deserving it, and it is incumbent upon you to spread all justice in all your conduct.

"Be persistent in upholding justice as witnesses for Allah." It is not enough for the believer merely to be upholding justice; the testimony must also be for Allah. Why? 

Suppose a man were an unbeliever in Allah, God forbid, yet upholds justice among people; but he does not bring that justice into the basis of faith. The one who enters into the basis of faith is upholding justice while Allah is in his mind, and thus the testimony and the establishment of Allah's rights are for no benefit, no end, no desire, and no purpose, but so that the order of Allah's creation may be upright as Allah willed. Otherwise, if anyone judged by desire, the earth would be corrupted. Al-Haqq says:

﴿And if the Truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been corrupted﴾ (23:71).

Therefore the believer must be persistently upholding justice with Allah in his mind, and so upholding justice alone is not enough. We hear: "So-and-so is just," even if he is of another religion than Islam or is an atheist, and we say: this just person of any religion or creed other than Islam receives the praise of people, but he does not receive the praise of Allah nor His reward; therefore upholding justice must be done with the intention of carrying out Allah's command, in order to obtain reward from Allah.

"Be persistent in upholding justice as witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves." The witness, customarily, is one who testifies for the interest of one party against another. When a witness acknowledges a wrong, he has testified against himself; and a witness for one party does so to tip the ruling. The witness against himself confesses what he did, and confession is the master of proofs; the witness's testimony presents the judge with the proof upon which the ruling is based. Thus the believer testifies against himself.

There is another meaning: he testifies against himself even if the testimony brings ruin upon him. These meanings are among the emanations of Qur'anic illuminations. The believer testifies against himself by way of confession; yet the testimony may not be against the self, but may be an obligation upon him, which he discharges for the benefit of another, and the witness does not fear the ruler in it, even if the ruler oppresses the believer and afflicts him in his person or property. Some people have been afflicted in their persons or families by the ruler merely for a word of truth spoken. The ruler may not take a man for his own sin, but may take his family for that sin; and al-Haqq makes clear to the servant: do not concern yourself with that, and do not say, "They will torment my dependants, or they will take everything," for I am the Existent who guarantees My servants.

Al-Haqq asks of the believers: "Be persistent in upholding justice as witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives." When a person testifies against himself, his father, his mother, or any of his relatives will be no dearer to him than himself.

Then al-Haqq brings us to the point that the impulses that oppose justice enter through desires, and when a person prefers false, unrealized falsehood over realized truth, the one preferred is the desire of the soul. The source of desire is that the one testified against is wealthy, so a person fears to testify against him, and this prevents him from some good.

Therefore al-Haqq has defined the believers' uprightness as justice and as testimony for Allah, even against the self or the father, the mother, or the relatives. It is not proper for any believer to put the wealth or poverty of the one testified for or against in mind; rather the mind must be with Allah alone. Therefore He said: "Whether he is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both. So do not follow [your] desires, lest you not be just."

Someone may say: "Desire may incline toward the rich out of covetousness for his wealth; why then does Allah mention the poor as well?" We say: desire may incline toward the poor out of mercy for the poor, so the witness tells himself "he is poor and deserves mercy." Therefore al-Haqq warns us against leaning toward the rich or toward the poor.

Testimony has no bearing on the wealth of the wealthy or the poverty of the poor, because the believing servant is not more entitled or more worthy to look after people's interests than their Creator, exalted is He; therefore He brought the restraining basis: "Allah is more worthy of both. So do not follow [your] desires, lest you not be just." That is, you, O servant, did not create either of them, but Allah created both and is more worthy of them; so you have no right to establish your testimony on wealth or on poverty, for you are not the custodian of existence.

What corrupts and confuses justice is desire. The Arab proverb says: "The bane of judgment is desire." Beware, O believers, of following desire, lest your capacity for justice be corrupted and you deviate far from it. Arab history preserves in its memory the account of a virtuous man who went to the caliph and said: "Excuse me from judgeship." The caliph said: "Then who will be for judgeship, when you are the just one whom all people have testified to be so?"

The judge said: "By Allah, O Commander of the Faithful, people know of me that I love fresh dates (ruṭab), that is, young dates. While I was in my house, behold, the servant entered carrying a tray of fresh dates; it was the early season of dates, and naturally the soul is eager for them as long as it loves them." The judge continued his account to the caliph: "I said to the servants, 'Who brought it?' The servant answered, 'A man of such-and-such description.' I remembered that the one who had sent the dates was one of the litigants before me, so I returned the dates to him. When the day of decision in the case of the owner of the dates came, the man entered upon me and I recognized him. By Allah, O Commander of the Faithful, he and his opponent were not equal in my eyes, although I had returned the tray." Thus the Arab Muslim judge resigned from the post of judgeship.

Al-Haqq, glory be to Him, continues: "And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse [to give it], then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted." "Distorting" (talwu) in testimony is tahrif, that is, you distort the testimony and alter it, and Allah is Acquainted with what you do; or it is that a person refrains from giving testimony because he fears the one testified against. Thus it is said that he fears the one testified against, because testimony tips the ruling in favour of the one testified for; so he refrains from testimony, and if he comes to give testimony, he twists the words and bends his tongue with them. Therefore al-Haqq says: "And if you distort or refuse, then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted."

Thus what corrupts justice is desire, and desire is an act of the heart; therefore we need the knowledge of the Acquainted, the Subtle One. We must know that intentions are acts of the hearts. Thus the act now divides before us into three parts: a person's speech, the deed performed by members other than the person, and the intentions and desires of the heart.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 4, verse 136:

And after that, the Truthful, glory be to Him, says:

﴿O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger and the Book which He sent down before. And whoever disbelieves in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers and the Last Day has certainly strayed far astray.﴾

Someone may say: How can the Truth, at the beginning of this verse, address the believers with belief, saying "believe," and then afterward demand that they believe? We say: Sometimes we see a man who utters the word of faith with his tongue while Allah knows that his heart does not affirm what he says. So the word of faith is a true statement, but with respect to its agreement with his heart it is not true. And we are confronted with the acceptance of the Truth's saying:

﴿When the hypocrites come to you they say, "We testify that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah." And Allah knows that you are His Messenger, and Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars.﴾ (Surah al-Munafiqun)

The hypocrites testified that the Messenger of Allah is sent from Allah, and this is a matter of truth. But Allah, the All-Knowing of what is in the hearts, reveals their condition to the Messenger, so He says: ﴿And Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars.﴾ (Part of verse 1, Surah al-Munafiqun.)

Their testimony with their tongues agreed with what Allah knows, but their speech contradicted what was in their hearts. So the Truth testified that they are liars, and He, glory be to Him, knows their lie in their testimony, because the hypocrite among them did not give a sound testimony, for the true testimony is that the tongue agrees with the heart. Some of the foolish who try to correct the Qur'an have had their insight blinded from sensing the language and understanding its secrets, so they stumble in understanding; they do not know the attributes of receiving from Allah. They said: there is contradiction in the Qur'an, and they did not know that the lie of the hypocrites was not in the statement "Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," but in their testimony to that and Allah's calling them liars in their saying "we testify" alone. They announced faith with their tongues, but their hearts did not believe.

If we wish to understand that the address to the believers in general, to believe, is a call to advance with more faith, then for us in the Truth's saying there is a clear example in His speech to the Prophet. The Truth said:

﴿O Prophet, fear Allah, and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾ (Surah al-Ahzab)

Here the Truth says to the first of the God-fearing, Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Fear Allah," that is, He commands him to always stand in piety.

So the meaning of the Truth's saying, "O you who have believed, believe," is that the Truth addresses you with the word of faith and wills that your faith, after His true speech, be connected with your faith before His speech, so the thread of faith is never cut or broken. Rather, there must be persistence in faith, and no believer should abandon this honor. If one of you sees that he is called by a description, and after it a request is made for that description, then let him know that what is meant is persistence.

We know that the Truth here addresses believers, hypocrites and People of the Book, so the verse "O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger" must include them, because if a person believes in Allah only, this requires that the believer in Allah seek what Allah requires, and what Allah requires came through a messenger. Therefore, belief in Allah necessitates that a person believe in a messenger, for the utmost that reason gives you, O human, is that you believe that behind the universe there is a god who created it and manages it. But what is the name of this God? A person does not know that except through the Messenger.

These matters are not known by reason, but must be reported, and likewise the requirements of Allah, and likewise the reward of believers for the goodness of their faith, and therefore there must be a messenger for conveying.

So, along with belief in Allah, you must believe in the Messenger, and as long as you, O believer, have believed in His Messenger, you must believe in the books that came through the tongue of the Messenger. These books tell you that there is a creation of Allah that you do not see, namely the angels, and the angel comes with revelation and brings it down to the Messenger, although you have not seen the angel, yet you believe in his existence.

So the summit of faith is to believe in Allah, and its necessary consequence is to believe in the Messenger of Allah, and to believe in the book with the Messenger, and to believe in what Allah says about a creation you cannot perceive, such as the angels. This command to believe is directed to the People of the Book, because they believed in their messengers, and they are asked to believe in the Messenger of Allah and in what was sent down to him. The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, leaves it to His creatures to discover the existence of beings that were not known, because they were informed that in the universe there are beings whose existence Allah has told us of and whom we do not perceive, namely the angels. So the evidence among them urges them and pushes them toward discovery and research.

An example of this is the microbe, which mankind did not know until the seventeenth century CE, though the microbe existed from the beginning. But we did not perceive it, and after mankind arrived at the making of microscopes, we perceived it and came to know its characteristics, its families and its types, and discoveries still seek to know what is new about it. It is new in relation to us, but ancient in its existence.

The meaning of this is that Allah makes clear to us: if a truthful person informs you, O human, that in the universe there is a creation you do not now perceive, then you must believe. Before the discovery of the microbe, if someone had told people during the darkness of the Middle Ages that microbes exist, they would not have believed it, even though the microbe is a substance of the same substance as the human himself, but it is so small in size that no instrument of perception perceives it. And when we invented and discovered devices that multiply the image of a thing hundreds of times, we were able to see it. So the non-seeing of a thing does not mean that it does not exist.

Thus, when Allah tells us about the creation of the angels, the jinn, and the devil who runs in a person like the blood, here the disbeliever and the atheist must believe and affirm this, because he believes that the microbe enters the body without the person feeling it, and afterward reacts with the blood, then the symptoms of disease appear afterward, and this was known only after the conditions of sight and knowledge were prepared. If Allah has created kinds from other than the substance of the human, then let us affirm the Truth:

﴿O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger and the Book which He sent down before.﴾ (Part of verse 136, Surah al-Nisa')

It is well known that "the Book" is the Qur'an, and it is its proper name. As for "the Book which He sent down before," let us know that what is meant by it is the category of the Book, that is, all the books that were sent down to the messengers before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). That is why the "al-" preceding the second occurrence of the word "Book" is said to be the "al-" of the category (jinsiyyah), and the category, as we know, has many individuals under it, as evidenced by the fact that the Truth, glory be to Him, uses the singular with the definite article and excepts a group from it, for example:

﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who have believed and done righteous deeds﴾ (Surah al-'Asr)

We find "mankind" here is singular, with the "al-" attached to it, and a group is excepted from mankind, namely those who believed, and this is evidence that "mankind" is more than one group. That is why they say: exception is the criterion of generality, meaning that the word from which we exclude and remove something is a general word.

The Truth demands from us belief in the Book, that is, the Qur'an. If the phrase "the Book" is used absolutely, it refers to the Qur'an, because the "al-" here is that of dominance (lil-ghalabah). For example, one says "He is the man," meaning he is a man singularly possessing the qualities of manhood, its nobility and its strength. So when we say "the Book," it means the Qur'an, because the phrase "the Book" has come to be used of the Qur'an, so it is not applied except to it. Or it is the complete Book, which has no abrogation or alteration, so the "al-" here is for perfection. As for "the Book which He sent down before," it includes the Torah, the Gospel, and all the scriptures and pages sent down upon the earlier prophets.

"And whoever disbelieves in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers and the Last Day has certainly strayed far astray" means that whoever believes in Allah but disbelieves in the rest of what is mentioned in the verse is also a disbeliever.

Some Jews, such as Abdullah ibn Salam, Salam the brother of his sister, Salamah the brother of his [own] brother, Asad and Usayd the two sons of Ka'b, Tha'labah ibn Qays, and Yamin ibn Yamin, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "We believe in you and your book and Moses and the Torah and 'Uzayr, and we disbelieve in whatever else of the books and messengers." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Rather, believe in Allah and His Messenger Muhammad and his book, the Qur'an, and in every book that was before it." They said: "We will not do so." So the verse was revealed: "O you who have believed, believe," all of them. (1)

The address and call also include the hypocrites, that is, "O you who have believed" outwardly through hypocrisy. Sincere yourselves to Allah and make your hearts agree with your tongues. So the call includes the believers, that they may persist and continue in their faith, and it embraces the disbelievers among the People of the Book, that they may believe in every messenger and every book, and it is also for the hypocrites, that they may be sincere in their faith until their hearts agree and correspond with their tongues.

So whoever disbelieves in anything Allah mentioned in this verse has disbelieved in Allah.

"And whoever disbelieves in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers and the Last Day has certainly strayed far astray." "Strayed" means he went off without guidance. When a person loses his intended goal, it is said: he strayed from the road. And one who "strayed far astray" is one who goes into a distant wilderness, and what is meant by it is the wilderness of disbelief.

There is straying from guidance that can be corrected, but far straying and drowning in the wilderness of disbelief are difficult to correct. The strayers share a starting point, but they are two groups who differ: one of them walks the path of faith, being always attentive to its goal, which is the pleasure of Allah by carrying out His requirements, and he is wary of disobeying His command; the other deviated from the beginning and arrived at the wilderness of disbelief.

1 Al-Kashshaf of Jar Allah al-Zamakhshari.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 4, verse 137:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿Indeed, those who believed and then disbelieved, then believed and then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief — Allah will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path.﴾ (4:137)

These are the hypocrites (al-munafiqun), who announced faith and concealed disbelief. And Allah said about them:

﴿And a group of the People of the Book said: "Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day, and disbelieve at its end; perhaps they will return."﴾ (Surah Al 'Imran, 3:72)

So they turned faith from a belief into a mere word that is spoken. They were most eager to carry out the requirements of Islam through outward acts, so that they might ward off suspicion from their Islam, while their hearts remained with disbelief. For this reason they wanted to confuse the discourse and deceive within it.

﴿The Bedouins say: "We have believed." Say: "You have not believed; rather say, 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts."﴾ (part of 49:14, Surah al-Hujurat)

The Truth exposes them before themselves, and before God, when they realise that they are merely Muslims in tongue, while their hearts have not believed. The Messenger informs them of this and says to them, as a message from Allah: "Say: You have not believed; rather say, 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts." They were the foremost of people to the rows of prayer. When the Messenger exposed them and made clear to them: "You have not believed, you have only submitted," they then knew that Muhammad had known the secrets of their hearts through a message from Allah.

Had they said that Muhammad himself had known these secrets, their acknowledgement of him would not have been limited to him as a messenger; rather they might have gone further into error and wished to make him a god. But the Messenger of Allah settles the matter, and makes clear to them that Allah is the One who informed him, as evidenced by His command that he say to them: "Say: You have not believed."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) affirms that this matter contains nothing of his own; rather he is commanded to convey from Allah his Lord. In our age, Bernard Shaw said: "Those who deny that Muhammad is the messenger of God want to make him a god. So from where did he obtain these things that were not known in his age?"

All people are obliged to believe in Muhammad as a messenger from Allah, for he spoke of things that no human being could say; and the Messenger (ﷺ) himself clarifies this statement decisively, showing that it is not from him but from Allah.

"The Bedouins say: 'We have believed.' Say: 'You have not believed; rather say, "We have submitted," for faith has not yet entered your hearts.'" This is a disclosure that is both embarrassing and logical regarding what is in their hearts. For this reason, those who heard the verse said: "Praise be to Allah, that there is hope that faith may enter our hearts," and faith had indeed entered their hearts in fact, because the word (lamma) indicates the negation of faith from them in the past tense, but it also indicates the expectation and occurrence of faith from them, and it has occurred.

"Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief" — meaning they died in disbelief; or they believed in Moses, then disbelieved in Jesus, and other people came who believed in Jesus, and they increased in disbelief by not believing in Muhammad. There is no correction after Muhammad (ﷺ).

He (glorified is He) tells us of their destiny: "Allah will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path," because they entered faith once and then left faith. The meaning of their conduct is that they intended temptation (fitnah), because the others would see them as believers, and would see them disbelieving, and they would explain that by saying that they had delved into doctrinal matters and disbelieved, doing this in order to belittle the standing of Islam. For this reason the Almighty says:

﴿And a group of the People of the Book said: "Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day, and disbelieve at its end; perhaps they will return."﴾ (Surah Al 'Imran, 3:72)

They therefore intend temptation by displaying faith and then announcing disbelief, and in this there is casting doubt upon the Muslims. The fate of one who wavers between faith and disbelief, and whose final outcome is that he increases in disbelief, is what is stated in His saying: "Allah will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path." They have entered into the supreme treason of faith, which is governed by the saying of the Truth:

﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills.﴾ (part of 4:48, Surah al-Nisa')

The Truth says of them here: "Allah will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path." Guidance, as we know, carries several meanings. It may mean indication (dalalah): thus, if you wish, enter faith, and if you wish, do not; no one has any concern with you. The second meaning is assistance (ma'unah): that is, Allah provides you with what actually guides you. When the Qur'an addressed this matter, it said:

﴿As for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance, so the bolt of the humiliating punishment seized them for what they used to earn.﴾ (41:17, Surah Fussilat)

Here He has indicated to them the guidance but did not grant them actual guidance, because they preferred blindness over guidance. It is as though Allah has pointed to the method that conveys goodness and righteousness to all people; whoever approaches with faith, He supplies him with the guidance of assistance and helps him to increase in guidance, in confirmation of His saying:

﴿Indeed, they were youths who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance.﴾ (part of 18:13, Surah al-Kahf)

We do not want this example to be absent from minds, so I always emphasise it: a traffic policeman standing at the start of a desert road is asked by a traveller: "I am going to Alexandria; which way?" He directs him to the road that leads to Alexandria. Here the policeman has done the indicating; then the man thanks the policeman and praises Allah for the policeman's good explanation. The traffic man feels and experiences happiness, warns the traveller of the obstacles on the road, and rides with him to point out those obstacles so that he may avoid them. That is, after the indication, assistance has taken place. Likewise, the Truth indicates to people faith and the method, and whoever believes in it, He helps him and makes obedience easy for him. The Truth (glorified is He) said concerning prayer:

﴿And indeed, it is heavy except for the humble.﴾ (part of 2:45, Surah al-Baqarah)

Thus we find guidance in two stages: the guidance of indication and the guidance of assistance.

The Truth wills that the matter of faith be a firm and rooted matter, such that it does not float up to the intellect to be debated anew, for the principle of faith does not change through the succession of messages from our master Adam until He sealed them with our master Muhammad (ﷺ).

He (glorified is He) said:

﴿O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Book that He sent down upon His Messenger and the Book that He sent down before. And whoever disbelieves in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers and the Last Day has certainly gone far astray.﴾ (4:136)

Thus He wants the believer to believe in the highest summit, which is belief in Allah, the Necessarily Existent Supreme, and to believe in the message conveyed from Him as a Book, and to believe in the message conveyed from Him as a mission upon the tongue of any messenger. Those who believe in one messenger and then disbelieve in another, or who believe in a messenger and then disbelieve by ascribing a consort or a son to Allah, and then increase in disbelief concerning the Seal, who is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), have no path to guidance to Allah, because Islam came with the final conclusion, and there is no correction for heaven after that, and no one has any correction after that. That is why He said at the beginning of the verse: "believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved," and said at the end of the verse: "then increased in disbelief," meaning that they did not believe in Muhammad (ﷺ), and there is no room for them to await another messenger to annul their disbelief in Muhammad and believe in the new messenger.

He (glorified is He) makes clear: "Allah would not have guided them," because they are the ones who turned themselves away from Him. Allah does not withhold guidance from one who extends his hand toward Him; rather He assists him in his guidance. But whoever withdraws his hand from the hand of Allah, He does not grant him the pledge of faith, for Allah is free of need of him. And as long as Allah is free of need of him, he will remain in his misguidance, because guidance comes only from Allah, and "Allah would not have guided them to a path" to any other guidance, and there is no guide but Him. Nor would He have guided them to a path to Paradise, because they did not put forward the causes that qualify them to enter Paradise.

Therefore Allah explains it in another verse:

﴿Allah would not forgive them, nor would He guide them to a road, except the road of Hellfire, abiding therein forever.﴾ (part of 4:168 and part of 4:169, Surah al-Nisa')

Thus we find the road of Hellfire paved and made easy for them.

Then the Exalted says: ﴿Give the hypocrites the good news that for them there is a painful punishment.﴾

The trait of wavering and vacillating between faith and disbelief does not come from someone genuinely rooted in faith. It comes from someone fickle in faith: causes appear to him and he believes, then after that changes appear to him and he disbelieves. That is the condition of the hypocrites, who waver between these and those, so the Truth says: "Give the hypocrites the good news that for them there is a painful punishment."

We know that the hypocrite (munafiq) is the one who combined two matters: declaring Islam outwardly and concealing disbelief inwardly. Hypocrisy (nifaq) is taken from nafaqa' al-yarbu' (the escape hole of the jerboa), which is one of its burrows in which it hides and conceals itself. The jerboa is a desert animal that deceives whoever intends it harm: it prepares for itself two openings, so that when a man enters by one, it exits by the other. If the man waits for it at one opening, the jerboa comes out of the other.

"Give the good news" (bashshir): glad tidings (bushra) is the report of something pleasing that will come about later. Do the hypocrites receive glad tidings? No. Glad tidings are of good, so we would expect the hypocrites to be warned and not given good news. But God, in His rhetorical methods, has expressions for intensifying punishment. Had He said, "Warn them of a painful punishment," the speech would have been open to interpretation, for hypocrites as such are prepared to hear evil. But the Truth says: "Give the hypocrites the good news that for them there is a painful punishment." This is sarcasm (tahakkum), mockery (istihza') and derision (sukhriyya), and these are among the means by which the eloquent speaker accomplishes his rhetorical task. We hear incongruities at times, which give us a picture more truthful than reality. If you come to a miser, for example, and say to him: "Welcome, O Hatim," what would be the reaction of those attending this meeting?

You move him from the reality of the miser to the image of Hatim al-Ta'i, the origin of generosity. In this way you have moved the miser twice: first from his condition as a miser, then mocking him, because saying to a miser "O Hatim" is reproach, sarcasm and derision, since you have moved him from a base and contemptible description to an opposite description that is lofty and great, belittling him and ridiculing him. From the comparison the difference appears great. Likewise if you come to a very tall man and say, "Welcome, O dwarf," this is the incongruity; as you say to a short man, "Welcome, O giant." Or if you come to a tall man to shake his hand, and he sits on the ground to greet you, this too is an incongruity; and if you come to a short man to shake his hand, and you sit on the ground to greet him, this is sarcasm and mockery.

These incongruities come only for the rhetorical expression of the meaning the speaker intends. The Truth's words "Give the hypocrites the good news" mean: you, hypocrites, have brought upon yourselves by hypocrisy what you used to love, as if you pretended only because you love punishment. Since you pretended because you love punishment, I give you the good news that you will be punished. Does the one who feigns faith seek any end other than this? Therefore the Truth depicts for him that his end is punishment, and so He says: "Give the hypocrites the good news that for them there is a painful punishment."

When you want to escalate a matter, you move your addressee from one thing to its opposite, its contrary. For example: a thirsty person who is detained or imprisoned wishes to drink a sip of water. The guard may say to him, "No," and make him despair of anyone bringing him a cup of water. But if the guard wishes to escalate the punishment for him, he goes and brings a cup of water and brings it near him; then when the prisoner stretches out his hand to take the cup, the guard pours the water onto the ground. This is the escalation of punishment. When one says "give good news," the listener understands that there is something pleasing; then when the Truth says "that for them there is a painful punishment," it means that grief comes compounded: He first expanded their selves with the glad tidings, then ended it with the warning.

By way of example, and to God belongs the highest similitude, a father says to his son: "Study, my son, so that you do not fail." But the son continues playing. Then the father says: "My son, the examination has drawn near, and you must study." The son pays no attention to his father's words. Then the examination comes, and on the day the results are announced the father goes, and the son has failed. The father says to his son: "I congratulate you, you have failed the examination." His saying "I congratulate you" expands the son's soul, because he expects to hear pleasant news; then hearing "you have failed" gives him the feeling of constriction.

The Exalted says to His Messenger: "Give the hypocrites the good news that for them there is a painful punishment." "Bashshir" (give good news) is related to the derived meaning, because emotions show their effect on the skin of the face: if the emotion is sorrow, the face shows sorrow by contraction; if the emotion is joy, the face shows joy by expansion. The skin reflects the emotions of the human soul, of joy, cheerfulness and radiance, or frowning and scowling. So bushra is suitable for reporting news that pleases or news that grieves and wounds, but it has come to be applied predominantly to pleasing news, while the warning (nidhara) is reserved for news that saddens and constricts the soul.

"Give the hypocrites the good news that for them there is a painful punishment." As we have said, bushra suggests that there is pleasing news, and then the news comes unpleasant. As the Truth says in another verse, depicting the punishment of the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection and how He escalates the punishment for them:

﴿And if they seek relief, they will be relieved with water﴾ (Qur'an 18:29).

When we hear "And if they seek relief, they will be relieved with water," we understand that coolness comes to them or mercy blows upon them. But the relief that comes to them is "like molten brass" (al-muhl) (Qur'an 18:29).

The hearer or reader asks: is this relief or torment? This is a depiction of escalating punishment, for the water given to them, being like molten brass, raises the pain in their souls.

Punishment, as we know, draws its strength from the one who punishes: if the punisher has limited power, the punishment is limited; if the punisher's power is unlimited, the punishment is unlimited. When punishment is attributed to the might of the Mighty, who is God, how could it be? Punishment is described sometimes as painful (alim), sometimes as humiliating (muhin), and sometimes as great (azim). All these descriptions combine, and each description has its own aspect. Pain is the soul's sensation of what wearies it; great punishment is the punishment that reaches the peak. Punishment may reach its peak while the one punished endures stoically; but the punishment of the Truth exceeds the capacity of the one receiving it, so he cannot conceal the pain, for no human's endurance, however stoic, can repel pain. And with great punishment we find it also painful, so the painful, great punishment pains the body; but the soul may be stoic and defiant, and then it collapses, and at that point the punishment becomes humiliating.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 4, verse 139:

Because the hypocrites and the disbelievers are immersed in materialism, God chose to describe the punishment as painful (alīm), since pain applies to the body. Then the Almighty describes some attributes of the hypocrites, saying:

﴿Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do they seek honour with them? Indeed, honour belongs entirely to God.﴾ (4:139)

The first manifestation of hypocrisy is that the hypocrite takes the disbeliever as an ally (walī) whom he draws near to, loves, seeks from him support, aid, companionship and society, and abandons the believers. We know that every human action must arise for an aim (ghāyah) sought from it, and an action is stripped of its aim only in the case of the madman, who performs actions without any aim. But the sane person performs an action for an aim and a goal he hopes for. So for what aim and what goal do the hypocrites take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers?

God uncovers this matter and clarifies it: they seek honour (ʿizzah) from the disbelievers, and that is why they took them as allies instead of the believers.
