And He, glory be to Him, draws their attention to their ignorance, because they have taken a path that leads them to the very opposite of their aim.

Since they seek honour, let them first know: what is honour? ʿIzzah is derived from a material meaning, namely hardness and firmness. Thus "ʿazāz" land is the hard land that the pickaxe cannot penetrate. The term was then transferred to everything, so that everything hard or firm has ʿizzah in it. The meaning intended here is dominance and victory, and all these meanings are contained in ʿizzah.

When it is said "God is ʿAzīz", it means that He, glory be to Him, prevails over His affair, is mighty, and no one can be capable of overcoming His plan, His stratagem, His power or His punishment. When it is said "So-and-so is ʿazīz", it means he cannot be overcome. When it is said "this thing is ʿazīz", it means it is rare, and since a thing that is rare is precious, the precious metals have all taken their share of their rarity and scarcity.

And as long as you, O hypocrites, seek honour, should you not seek it from the One who possesses it? Will you seek it from your equals? When you seek honour, that is because you do not possess inherent honour. Had you possessed inherent honour, you would not have sought honour from the disbelievers. This is proof of their lack of honour, because they sought it from one equal to them among the contingent beings (aghyār). The hypocrites are human beings and the disbelievers are human beings, and since all human beings are contingent, it is possible that they will be honoured today and humbled tomorrow, because the causes of honour are wealth, power or rank, and all of these are contingent.

So you, O hypocrites, have sought honour from one who has no advantage over you, being a contingent being like you, and you did not seek it from the possessor of inherent, eternal, everlasting honour, who is God, glory be to Him. If you wanted true honour, which would make you independent of seeking it from contingent beings like yourselves, then go to the source of honour that contingent beings cannot reach, who is God, glory be to Him.

Therefore God clarified to them: if you want to learn how to seek honour, you must change your method of seeking it. You take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers and seek honour from them, and they are of the contingent beings, and contingent beings change from day to day. If the disbelievers are rich today, they will not be so tomorrow. You have seen, as humans, that the wealthy become poor, and you have seen the strong become weak. To seek honour from contingent beings means that you are not honoured. Yet you seek honour from other than its proper place. If you want true honour, then seek it from the One whose honour never changes, who is God, glory be to Him: "Indeed, honour belongs entirely to God."

In this statement there is a correction of the seeking of honour, so that every person should seek honour through faith in God. He, glory be to Him, is the One who bestows honour and whose honour never changes: "Indeed, honour belongs entirely to God." The word "jamīʿan" (entirely) shows that honour has various kinds: the honour of wealth, the honour of authority, the honour of rank. If anyone wishes to know it and learn it, it is all together in God, glory be to Him.

The believers, in their servitude to God, are servants of one God, and God has enriched us through servitude to Him so that we need not abase ourselves before many people. He, glory be to Him, has by faith rescued the believer from abasing himself before any source of power: He rescued the weak from abasing himself before the strong, rescued the poor from abasing himself before the rich, and rescued the sick from abasing himself before the healthy.

So when the Almighty says "Indeed, honour belongs entirely to God", its meaning is: if you, O human, want an honour that is well-ordered and surpasses every honour, then go to God, for He, glory be to Him, has honoured us, since we are His creation. For example, we find that the Almighty did not make the poor man borrow, but said:

﴿Who is it that will lend to God a goodly loan, so He may multiply it for him?﴾ (2:245)

Here God raises His poor servant to the highest degrees of honour. The poor servant does not borrow, but the loan is sought by God. That is why one of them said to a weak man: "You ask people; would you not refrain and not ask?" He said: "I asked people by the command of God." The one who asks, asks by God, that is, he takes God as an intercessor and asks by Him. When a person seeks honour from one like himself, he takes pride in the strength of that creature, and that strength is a gift granted to him by God, which He may take back from him. How much more so the infinite power of God! Every power in this world is bestowed by God: wealth is bestowed by Him, rank is bestowed by Him, and every honour belongs to God.

Almighty Allah says after that:

﴿And it has already been revealed to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being rejected and mocked, do not sit with them until they engage in a different discourse. Indeed, you would then be like them. Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers in Hell all together.﴾ (4:140)

The Truth commands the believers that when they hear some of the disbelievers mocking the verses of Allah or rejecting them, they should not sit with them unless the conversation turns to another topic. This is so that they do not become like the disbelievers, for He, glorified is He, will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers in Hell. Thus Allah alone protects the people of faith and safeguards them from any assault upon them. Those who are jealous for the faith are the ones who have believed. So, since you have believed and have accepted Islam for yourself, beware of tolerating those who attack the religion, for if you tolerate them, you will hold them in higher esteem in your soul than faith. And since you, O believer, have accepted faith as your path and creed, then protect this faith from anyone attacking it. If anyone dares to attack faith with some criticism, ridicule, or the casting of falsehood, then the zeal of faith in the Muslim obliges him to reject that gathering.

The believers were at the beginning a weak minority, unable to stand against the disbelievers or the hypocrites. Thus, when the believers abandon the disbelievers or the hypocrites at the moment of idle talk about the verses of Allah, the disbelievers and hypocrites understand from that behaviour that the honour of faith is more precious to the Muslims than sitting with these people. But if a Muslim sits with them while they engage in discourse against faith, this means that they are more precious to him than faith. The disbelievers may make it a continuous topic in order to probe the depths of faith in the hearts of the Muslims. But when a disbeliever sees a believer rise up and withdraw from any talk containing mockery of Islam, the disbeliever then knows that the faith of the Muslim is dear to him.

This verse is not an initial ruling; rather, it points to a ruling that came before. We know that it was revealed in Medina, for the Truth says: "And it has already been revealed to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being rejected." This means that a verse had been revealed earlier in Mecca, in which the Truth says:

﴿And when you see those who engage in discourse about Our verses, turn away from them until they engage in a different discourse. And if Satan causes you to forget, then do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people.﴾ (6:68, Surat al-An'am)

Here the Truth points out that He had revealed a ruling at the beginning, which is the ruling that was revealed with regard to the disbelievers in Mecca, where the disbelievers oppressed the believers and the religious method had not yet come to prohibit the believers from sitting with the disbelievers. Some believers were slaves of the disbelievers, and some early Muslims had established common interests with the disbelievers, and the ruling came: if these disbelievers persist in discourse about religion in falsehood, then leave them the place.

Here, in Surat an-Nisa, He, glorified is He, reminds the believers that the ruling to abandon the disbelievers at the moment of idle talk about faith is a ruling that extends and is transmitted to the believers from the first environment, where you, O believers, were among the polytheists who worshipped idols, and the ruling also continues in Medina, where some People of the Book are present. The obligation from Allah is an obligation within what human beings can bear. Man is prone to forget, and he must, as soon as he remembers, rise and leave those who engage in discourse about the verses of Allah. The Qur'an has revealed that when the believers hear someone rejecting the verses of Allah and mocking them, they should leave the place. We note that what was revealed in the first verse was not hearing but seeing:

﴿And when you see those who engage in discourse about Our verses, turn away from them.﴾ (part of 6:68, Surat al-An'am)

Hearing comes in the verse we are now reflecting on: "And it has already been revealed to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being rejected." What matters is simply knowledge, whether by seeing or by hearing, that they are engaging in discourse about the religion of Allah. The people of polytheism or others among the enemies of Islam may engage in discourse that is seen, and they may engage in discourse that is heard, and some polytheists may engage in it through insinuation or defamation at the moment they see a Muslim.

The Truth's words: "do not sit with them until they engage in a different discourse" suggest that if they turn to a discourse other than discourse about the verses of Allah, then the believers may sit with them. That was at the beginning of Islam, when the believers had common interests with the polytheists and the People of the Book, and the Islamic society at that time could not distinguish itself by its unity. Had the Truth, through His Messenger, said "do not sit with the disbelievers or the polytheists immediately," that would have cut off the interests of the believers.

The word "yakhuduna" (they engage in discourse / wade in) gives a clear, concrete meaning, for the basic sense of khawd is to enter a liquid, such as wading into water or mud, and the aim in entering a liquid or fluid is to create a passage towards an end.

When you wade into a liquid, the liquid does not separate to become one part here and another part there, nor does it open a path for you; as soon as a person walks and leaves the liquid, it flows back together again. Therefore it is impossible to make a path for yourself in a liquid. But if a person enters a sandy path, he first pushes the sand aside and clears a path for himself, and the sand does not return to block the way except by the action of someone. From this meaning, they took the description of a false matter as khawd. For falsehood has no goal; it is mixed and confused, and disputation over falsehood does not reach any conclusion.

So "khawd" is entering into falsehood or entering into something whose discourse does not reach an end. The scholars state: do not engage in the matter of the divine attributes, for engaging in it is not valid, and discourse about it will never reach an end. For this reason, the Truth says in another place in the Qur'an:

﴿And they did not measure Allah with His true measure when they said, "Allah has not sent down to a human anything." Say, "Who sent down the Book which Moses brought as light and guidance for the people, which you make into scattered pages, displaying them and concealing much? And you were taught that which you knew not, neither you nor your fathers." Say, "Allah." Then leave them in their discourse, playing.﴾ (6:91, Surat al-An'am)

O Muhammad, you have conveyed to them that the One who sent down the Book upon you is the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, who sent down the Torah before, and you concealed part of it and displayed another part; then, after the delivery, leave them to engage in their falsehood.

In another place the Truth speaks of khawd:

﴿The hypocrites fear that a surah will be revealed about them, informing them of what is in their hearts. Say, "Mock on; indeed, Allah will bring out what you fear."﴾ (9:64) ﴿And if you asked them, they would surely say, "We were only engaging in discourse and playing." Say, "Is it Allah and His verses and His Messenger you were mocking?"﴾ (9:65, Surat at-Tawbah)

So khawd is entering a liquid, and as long as you have entered a liquid, you will not find a defined path in it, but what you enter becomes mixed with what you enter into, and things are not distinguished. From it is taken khawd in falsehood or khawd in play that has no goal.

"And it has already been revealed to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being rejected and mocked, do not sit with them until they engage in a different discourse."

Then comes the word that frightens and terrifies the believer: "Indeed, you would then be like them." That is, if you sit with them while they wade into the verses of Allah, you would be disbelievers like them, because you hear the discourse about religion in falsehood, and whoever is content with disbelief becomes a disbeliever.

The verse has given us an initial, gradual stage. If the faithful environment is a self-sustaining, mutually supportive society, then no believer may sit with the disbelievers or make them allies unless they make alliance with us, for sitting with them during discourse about religion emboldens them against the methods of Allah. The believer must rebuke any mocker of religion, and the believers must turn away from whoever deviates from the method of Allah or confronts it. But contemporary societies honour those who engage in falsehood, and in that is an enticement to people to engage in falsehood about religion.

But if we turn away from this, those who deviate from the method of Allah will seek a means other than the path of emboldening against religion and wading into falsehood about the religion and method of Allah. The corruption of society arises precisely from our seeing that whoever wades into the religion of Allah with falsehood is honoured by some and given status and rank.

The Truth's words: "And it has already been revealed to you in the Book that when you hear" give us a means of human information: that a person sees an action or hears a statement. If you see, O Muslim, an action that encourages the method of corruption on earth, then know that this is wading into the religion of Allah with falsehood.

The Truth's words: "do not sit with them" are a notice of boycott. If a person of this kind lives in a house and goes to the grocer to buy something to eat, and he is refused service, and likewise the butcher, and likewise any person who holds an interest in the hands of such a person who has departed from the method, then the boycott is thereby established until he is disciplined and every person knows that society is jealous of its religion in which it believes, and that Allah is more precious to them than every honour they see in their society. If each of these deviants and those deeply immersed in falsehood saw society boycotting them and setting limits for them, they would turn to what is right and seek another field from which to earn their living and feed their children the lawful morsel from this permissible work.

The Truth says: "Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers in Hell all together." Do not be slow regarding this life, for the Muslim does not measure affairs by the age of the world, as a century or two or even ten centuries; rather, he must know that for him the world is his lifespan in it, and lifespan may end suddenly. The Muslim works not for the sake of this world alone, but so that he may meet Allah as a Muslim in the Hereafter. The believer fears that Allah will gather him with the hypocrites and the disbelievers in Hell, and this is the fate of whoever accepts mockery or ridicule of his religion.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 4, verse 141:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

{Those who wait for you: if there comes to you a victory from God, they say, "Were we not with you?" And if the disbelievers have a share, they say, "Did we not gain mastery over you and protect you from the believers?" God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and God will never grant the disbelievers any way over the believers.} (4:141)

His saying, the Truth: "Those who wait for you" is a description of the hypocrites (munafiqun). To "wait for" (yatarabbas) someone means that one person is alert, watching to spy on the news of another, and arranging his own needs from him according to what he sees of events. We understood this meaning from His saying, the Truth: ﴿Say: Do you await for us except one of the two best things?﴾ (9:52)

The hypocrites watch the believers because, if good comes to them, they want to benefit from it, and if evil comes, the hypocrites turn to benefit from the adversaries. Outwardly they proclaim faith, while inwardly they are disbelievers, and they wait for the believers, expecting what will happen and so that they may arrange their affairs according to what comes.

"Those who wait for you: if there comes to you a victory from God, they say, 'Were we not with you?'" When God grants victory to the believers in a battle and they take spoils, the hypocrites say, "Were we not with you?" so there must be a share for us in this booty. And if the disbelievers win, they go over to the disbelievers, in confirmation of the saying of the Truth: "And if the disbelievers have a share, they say, 'Did we not gain mastery over you and protect you from the believers?'"

They try, then, to benefit from the disbelievers by saying: We waited for the believers and awaited what would happen to them, and we must have a share. The Truth puts on their tongues: "Did we not gain mastery over you and protect you from the believers?" To "gain mastery" (istahwadha) over a thing means to possess it, to place it within one's domain, control and authority. And the Truth is the One who says: ﴿Satan has gained mastery over them and caused them to forget the remembrance of God﴾ (58:19).

That is, Satan placed them within his domain. The saying of the hypocrites to the disbelievers, "Did we not gain mastery over you?", reveals their stance when a battle takes place between the camps of disbelief and faith: the hypocrites try to learn the details of what the believers intend. At the moment the hypocrites enter the battlefield, they play the role of one who takes the disbelievers captive to shield them from the swords of the believers, and then they say to the disbelievers: "We gained mastery over you," meaning, we prevented the believers from killing you, and they demand payment from them.

Now observe the rhetorical expression: when He speaks of the victory of the believers, He says "a victory (fath) from God," whereas the Qur'an's expression for the victory of the disbelievers comes with the word "share" (nasib), meaning merely some temporary portion of dominance. Then comes the decisive word of the Truth: "God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and God will never grant the disbelievers any way over the believers."

When the Truth decides the matter of the disbelievers and the believers, He does not always refer it to a term which may not extend to the lifetime of the hearer, so that he might see it in this world; rather He brings in a matter that is certain. Therefore the believer does not say, "You will certainly be victorious," for the believer may die before he sees victory. For this reason He brings the certain matter, which is the Day of Resurrection, when Paradise will be the certain destination of every believer, because life is too trivial to be the price of faith.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) taught us not to seek the price in this world, for the ends of worldly things are subject to changes in this world. The pleasures of life either pass away from a person or the person passes away from them, whereas the price of faith remains with the permanence of the One in whom one believed. The principle of faith says: whoever does righteous deeds enters Paradise, and the Truth says of these righteous ones:

﴿And as for those who were made happy, they will be in the mercy of God, wherein they will abide forever﴾ (3:107).

That is, Paradise remains by God's preserving it, though He is able to annihilate it; but the mercy of God has no end, because it is one of His attributes, and He is the Everlasting forever. When the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says: "God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection," it means there will be no overturning of this judgment, for there is no god but Him, and the matter is concluded. God, the Truth, has judged some of the relatives of Muhammad (ﷺ). He judged the uncle of the Messenger, saying of him:

﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he! His wealth and what he gained will not avail him. He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame, and his wife, the carrier of firewood, around her neck a rope of palm fiber﴾ (111:1-5).

The saying of the Truth, glorified is He: "He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame" indicates that Abu Lahab would die in disbelief and God would not guide him to faith, although many of those who took a hostile stance toward the Messenger of God (ﷺ) believed in the Messenger of God (ﷺ). The camp of disbelief witnessed the loss of a number of its champions who went over to the camp of faith: here is Umar ibn al-Khattab, Khalid ibn al-Walid, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, and others; all of these believed. So what did Muhammad (ﷺ) know that Abu Lahab would not be among these? And why did he not say to Abu Lahab: "My nephew said: I will burn in a Fire of blazing flame; and I testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God," and he would have uttered the word of faith? But he did not say that, and God, who judged him, knew that he would not utter the word of faith.

Could Abu Lahab and his wife not have said together: "We testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God," and the matter would have ended? But God, whose judgment none can reverse, had decreed their disbelief. After the Truth sends down this decisive word concerning Abu Lahab and his wife, the Truth's words come in their order in the Mushaf to clarify: beware of supposing that this matter may be overturned. Then "He will burn... Abu Lahab... and his wife, the carrier of firewood," and immediately after, the Truth said:

﴿Say: He is God, the One. God, the Eternal Refuge﴾ (112:1-2),

so no one will change the judgment of God.

Thus His saying, the Truth: "God will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection" means there is no reversing the judgment of God, and there is no god other than Him to overturn it. ﴿And God will never grant the disbelievers any way over the believers﴾: this is a result of the judgment of God. It is not possible for God to decide in favour of the disbelievers over the believers, and the disbelievers will have no argument, strength or path over the believers. Does this matter come to pass in this world or in the Hereafter? We know that the Truth judges in the Hereafter, where means are suspended; but He placed means in this world. Whoever takes the means, the results of the means give to him, for the principle of lordship (rububiyyah) gives to believer and disbeliever alike. If the disbelievers take the means and the believers do not, then God grants them a way over the believers, and the believers may be defeated before the disbelievers.

The Arab wisdom teaches us: beware of considering that error is not among the soldiers of right, for when a person errs, the error is corrected for him. When the teacher teaches his pupil that the subject is in the nominative, and the pupil errs once and puts the subject in the accusative, this means he first took the rule and then forgot it, and the teacher corrects his mistake, so the rule clings to the pupil's mind that the subject is nominative. Thus error is among the soldiers of right, and falsehood too is among the soldiers of truth.

When corruption spreads among people, the call of truth emerges among them. Thus we see falsehood itself among the soldiers of truth: it is falsehood that makes the sting of spreading corruption manifest and makes people cry out. Likewise, the pain that afflicts a person is among the soldiers of healing, for pain says to the person: "Hey, there is something abnormal in this place," and were it not for pain, a person would not go to the doctor.

We must therefore know this as a rule: error is among the soldiers of right, falsehood is among the soldiers of truth, pain is among the soldiers of healing, and every error leads to right, but with a sting, so that a person does not forget it. The history of the Arabic language recounts the scholar Sibawayh, whom we mention when someone commits a grammatical error in language, and we say: "Sibawayh was angered by the one who erred." For Sibawayh is the one who clarified grammar and its rules, so much so that when we say the word "al-Kitab" in the usage of the language, the meaning turns to the book of Sibawayh, for he is the author of "al-Kitab."

Sibawayh was not originally a grammarian but a scholar of the Qur'anic readings (qira'at). It happened that he was sitting and a grammatical slip was pointed out to him in an assembly, that is, he erred in grammar and those around him criticised it. He became angry with himself and grieved, and said: "By God, I will perfect Arabic so that I never err in it," and he became an author in grammar.

Another example: the Imam al-Shatibi, may God be pleased with him, was not a scholar of readings but a scholar of grammar. Afterwards a problem arose for him concerning the readings which he did not recognise, so he swore to sit down and study the readings thoroughly, and after that he became a shaykh of the readers. Thus a slip, that is, a mistake, made Sibawayh a scholar of grammar, and a problem and a failure to find guidance in the readings made the Imam al-Shatibi a shaykh of the readers, even though Sibawayh was a scholar of readings and al-Shatibi was a man of grammar.

Therefore I repeat it so that we understand it well: error is among the soldiers of right, falsehood is among the soldiers of truth, and pain is among the soldiers of healing and wellbeing.

We may find the disbelievers having apparently won over the believers in some encounters, such as Uhud, and that was for education. At Uhud some of the believing fighters disobeyed the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and defeat was a prelude to correction. Likewise was the battle of Hunayn, when they were impressed by their great numbers:

﴿And on the day of Hunayn, when your large numbers pleased you but they availed you nothing, and the earth was constricted for you despite its vastness, then you turned back in retreat﴾ (9:25).

The Arab poet who addressed this matter said:
"Defeat is not defeat
unless it uproots its causes;
but if one strives to drive away a blemish,
then the utmost folly is in blaming it."

When a person uproots the causes of defeat, it becomes victory, and this happened at Uhud: they disagreed at first, the enemies overcame them, and then it became a lesson learned that cleared the way for victory.

So if you, O Muslim, see a way for the disbelievers over the believers, know that faith has become loosened in the souls of the Muslims, for there is no result without causes. If the believers take the causes, He gives them the results, for He is the One who says:

﴿And prepare against them whatever you can of power﴾ (8:60).

If the believers do not prepare what they are able to, or the multitude deceives them, then the outcome is defeat, deservedly. Every believer must fix in his certainty this divine saying:

﴿Then do they await but the way of the former peoples? But you will not find any change in the way of God, and you will not find any alteration in the way of God﴾ (35:43).

The declaration of faith in God is not the end of anything but the beginning, and the believer in God receives his reward according to his deed. God is jealous over His believing servant when he errs, so He disciplines him and trains him. And to God belongs the highest likeness: we find that one of us may not be patient in reviewing lessons with his children, so he brings a teacher to do so, because a father's love for his children drives him to become agitated when a child errs, and he may strike him; whereas the outside teacher is not agitated but takes matters in their ordinary measure. Thus whenever a person loves, he intervenes by the measure of affection, and sometimes is harsh with the one he loves.

The Arab poet says:
"So be stern that they may be restrained, and whoever is wise,
let him sometimes be stern with the one he loves."

Another example, and to God belongs the highest likeness: a man enters his home and finds in the courtyard children playing backgammon (maysir), among them his son and the neighbour's son, and another child whom he does not know. He immediately goes to his son to slap him and orders him to return at once to the apartment. As for the other children, the neighbour's son will receive only a word of reproach, and the child whom he does not know, he will not speak to at all.

Thus we find punishment in proportion to love and affection, and discipline in proportion to one's standing in the heart.

Whoever we do not care about, we do not pay attention to his bad conduct. So when we see a way for the disbelievers over the believers, let us know that one of the matters of faith has become disordered in their souls, and God does not want them to remain so; rather the Truth purifies them of these errors by having events bite them, so that they awaken to the fact that they are not taking the causes ordained by God.

Then the Almighty says:

{ Indeed, the hypocrites deceive Allah, but it is He who deceives them. And when they stand up to prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to the people, and they do not remember Allah except a little. }(142)

We know the reality of the hypocrites: they display faith and conceal disbelief. The Truth clarifies: Beware lest you think that any created being has the power to do anything without Allah's knowledge. A person may scheme against you while knowing that you know of his scheme. Is this a scheme? No, because scheming (makr) is an act carried out secretly, by a plan you do not know about. The basic principle of scheming is that the one being schemed against knows nothing of it. The hypocrites, when they display faith and conceal disbelief, are deceiving the One who knows what lies hidden in the breasts. They should have taken a lesson from how Allah dealt with them through the believers. The believers preserved the blood and property of the hypocrites, and the Muslims applied to them the rulings of Islam. But what has Allah planned for these hypocrites? He has prepared for them the lowest depth of the Fire. So who, then, is more capable of deception?

Truly, the clever person is not one who deceives someone he knows is able to expose the deception. The word "khada'a" (deceived) means that one schemes against another, showing him words and deeds while concealing other things, until he trusts him, and after that carries out the scheme. There is the word "khada'a" and the word "khadi'a" (deceiver). In this verse, the Truth did not say that Allah deceives them; rather He said: "They deceive Allah, but He is their Deceiver" (yukhadi'una / khadi'uhum).

"Khadi'a" (deceiving, in the form of mukhadaʿa) implies that two actions occur, like our saying: "So-and-so fought (qatala) so-and-so," where fighting happens between two parties. Likewise we say: "So-and-so shared (sharaka) with so-and-so," because the pattern of "fa'ala" requires two parties. But when we say "qatala" (killed), the act happens from one side only, and deception begins from one side. When the person being deceived sees that his opponent is stronger than him, he plots another deception against him, and the whole process is called "mukhadaʿa." It is said: "Khadaʿahu fakhadaʿahu" when he overcame him and was craftier than him. Then who is the one who prevailed? The one who plotted the deception in response to his opponent's deception is the victor.

Because deception occurs first, and after that the "deceived" receives a greater plot, he becomes the "deceiver" (khadi'), and the one who prevails is described as "akhda'ahu," meaning he nullified his deception. Allah, glory be to Him, dealt with them in the same manner they wished to deal with the believers. The hypocrites first displayed faith and concealed disbelief. Allah gave them, in outward matters, the rulings of Muslims, while inwardly He decided to punish them with the punishment of disbelievers, and even more than that, because they will be in the lowest depth of the Fire.

"Indeed, the hypocrites deceive Allah, but He is their Deceiver." O Muslim, beware of deriving from this act a name for Allah and saying "al-Mukhadi'" (the Deceiver), because the names of Allah are tawqifiyya (restricted to what is revealed; that is, we name Allah only by the names with which He named Himself). He acts, glory be to Him, through the act, but do not derive a name from this act. Here the Truth gives us "mushakala" (the use of a word for something else because of its occurrence alongside it) to clarify for us that the hypocrites scheme and plot evil against the believers. You, O Muslim, know that a person plots evil according to the extent of his capacity, which, however great it may be, is limited in comparison with the unbounded power of Allah. Therefore Allah exposes this evil plotted by these hypocrites. When they scheme, Allah, by the sweep of His power, schemes against them, meaning He nullifies their scheme and repays them for the evil of their deed. But we do not say "Allah is makir" (the Schemer), and Allah may say in the matter of mushakala whatever He wills.

"Indeed, the hypocrites deceive Allah, but He is their Deceiver, and when they stand up to prayer, they stand lazily."

The ends of actions are what give the limbs their eagerness toward those actions. If you love the action you turn to, you turn to it with all longing and eagerness. People measure the eagerness of a meeting because it is the measure of love. The Arab poet describes the meeting of a lover with his beloved:

The meeting of the two reveals its limit:
its yearning, how, and the lengthening of its duration.

The moment of meeting shows the affection between the two lovers. If the distance between them were ten steps, they would hasten with eagerness and cover the ten steps in three, and this means shortening the time of separation. Likewise the manner in which a greeting is performed shows the degree of affection: one of them may greet the other coldly, or with half affection, or with great affection, or with affection accompanied by eagerness and a mutual embrace. Also, the affection in which each embraces the other: is it a minute, two minutes, or three?

So what reveals the value of affection is: the eagerness, the manner, and the duration. These three elements have been used by poets to express affection and love among people. In earlier times, those who were smitten with women would conceal their affection in greetings. In Western civilization, where the values of religions have fallen, we find that a man receives a woman with kisses.

In some countries we find a man shaking hands with a woman. Does he shake her hand with eagerness, and does she return this eagerness? If you find the palm extended and spread out only for a handshake, this is an ordinary greeting. But if one of them bends the ring finger over the other's palm, so that the whole hand is enclosed in his hand, then you must observe which party bent his finger to embrace the whole hand. If it is from the man, the eagerness is from him; if it is from the woman, the eagerness is from her; if it is from both, the eagerness is from both together. Then, what is the duration for which the hand remains in the hand?

Sometimes both of them like to speak together, a man and a woman, as though speech has taken hold of them, so that each forgets that his hand is in the other's hand.

Greeting of two kinds
reveals its limit:
its yearning, how, and the lengthening of its duration.

Thus a person meets events: if the event is pleasant, he turns to it with eagerness; if it is otherwise, he approaches it heavily. The hypocrites used to stand up to prayer heavily and lazily: "And when they stand up to prayer, they stand lazily," as if they performed the prayer as a veil with which to conceal their hypocrisy, and to hide themselves from the eyes of the Muslims. Their standing for prayer was not out of longing for meeting Allah, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Bilal (may Allah be pleased with him), asking him to call the adhan for prayer:

"O Bilal, give us rest with the prayer" (1).

Because the believer finds rest when he performs the prayer, whereas for the hypocrite it is a laborious act, because he performs it only to hide himself from the eyes of the Muslims, and therefore he stands to it lazily. "And when they stand up to prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to the people, and they do not remember Allah except a little."

They establish the prayer in front of people in order to deceive the Muslims, and so that others may see them praying. In the prayer by which they show off to people, they do not say everything required for its completion; they say only what is required to be said aloud, such as reciting al-Fatiha and some of the Qur'an. But during bowing (ruku') they do not say "Glory be to my Lord, the Mighty," and likewise in prostration they do not say "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High."

Within every hypocrite there are two opposing currents: a current by which he appears with the believers, and another with the disbelievers. The current that is with the believers compels the hypocrite to stand up to prayer and remember Allah a little, while the current that is with the disbelievers makes him lazy about it, so he does not remember Allah much.

If we count how much a worshipper says aloud and how much he says silently, we will find that what he says silently during the prayer is more than what he says aloud. In bowing he says "Glory be to my Lord, the Mighty" three times, and he says "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High" in every prostration three times. But the hypocrite does not remember Allah except aloud, and that is little remembrance. We find that the hypocrite does not perform any act except when it is seen and heard by others. This is the meaning of showing off (riya'), whereas acts and words that are not seen or heard by people, he does not perform.

Nothing shakes and crumbles societies and destroys them except this showing off, because the Almighty loves that a Muslim perform every deed while keeping Allah in mind, He who nothing is hidden from. Our attention is drawn to this matter by our master Muhammad (ﷺ), when he spoke about ihsan (excellence):

"That you worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, indeed He sees you" (2).

If a person is ashamed to cheat a fellow human being in an outward way, how much more should be the one who tries to cheat Allah while knowing that Allah sees him? And why would that servant make his Lord the least of those who look at him?

When someone cheats another and the other discovers his cheating, the other punishes him. So how much more so with cheating Allah? Therefore you find the Messenger (ﷺ) conveying to us the state of the one who shows off to people, when he said: "Indeed what I fear most for you is minor shirk." They said: "And what is minor shirk, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Riya' (showing off). Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say on the Day of Resurrection, when He repays the servants for their deeds: Go to those for whom you used to show off in the world, and see whether you find reward with them" (3).

And the Messenger (ﷺ) said:

"Indeed the one who shows off will be called on the Day of Resurrection: 'O wicked one! O treacherous one! O show-off! Your deed is lost and your reward is void. So take your reward from the one for whom you used to work'" (4).

Thus the hypocrite is only deceiving himself. He pretends to pray so that people may see him, gives zakat so that people may see him, and performs Hajj so that people may see him. He does what Allah has commanded, but he does not do it for Allah. That is why the Qur'an says:

﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain, which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, and finds Allah with him, so He pays him in full his account, and Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ (Surah an-Nur, 24:39).

And He spoke about another form of their hypocrisy:

﴿Like one who spends his wealth to be seen by people and does not believe in Allah and the Last Day. His example is that of a smooth rock with a little dust on it; a heavy rain falls on it and leaves it bare. They have no power over anything they have earned, and Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾ (part of 2:264, Surah al-Baqara).

Safwan is the completely smooth stone, which has no roughness. Because if a stone has some roughness and dust is on it, and then rain falls on it, the dust settles into the roughness; but the smooth stone, as soon as the rain falls, the dust slides off it. Whoever shows off to the believers must take his reward from the one for whom he worked.

(1) Narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad.
(2) Narrated by Muslim, from the hadith of Jibril.
(3) Narrated by Ahmad and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, and al-Tabarani, from the narration of Mahmud ibn Labid from Rafi' ibn Khadij.
(4) Narrated by Ibn Abi al-Dunya, and its chain is weak.

Al-Sha'rawi continues to describe the psychological state of the hypocrites, saying:

﴿Wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those. And whoever Allah leaves astray, you will never find for him a way.﴾ (4:143)

The thing that is mudhabdhab (wavering, unsteady) is like something suspended on a thread: the wind takes it toward one side, then throws it toward another, because it is not fixed. It is derived from al-mudhabba (the fly-whisk), and from it comes the name al-dhubab (the fly), which a person swats away only for it to return again. Among the habits of the fly is that when it is driven away from a place, it must return to it.

"Wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those": Is it they who made themselves waver, or is that their nature? Let us reflect on the greatness of the Truth who fashioned the human soul. Within the single self there is a commander and one commanded, and the Truth says: ﴿O you who believe, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire﴾ (66:6).

That is, a person protects himself by making the commanding part direct its command to the commanded part, and making the commanded part obey the commander. The proof of this is the Truth's words about Qabil (Cain): ﴿So his soul permitted him the murder of his brother﴾ (5:30).

That is, a part of the self was what subdued the rest of Qabil's self so that he killed Habil (Abel). God created the human soul as multiple faculties: one faculty loves generosity (al-aryahiyya), and another loves stinginess (al-shuhh). The faculty that loves generosity seeks the praise of people, while the one that loves stinginess does so in order to assure its owner that he possesses what will suffice him. Both faculties struggle within the one soul. Therefore the Truth says: "protect yourselves," for the self protects the self, since its faculties are many, and some faculties love to achieve pleasure and desire. But there is a faith-based faculty that says: remember that these desires are hasty, yet their hardships afterward are great.

So there is a struggle within the faculties of man, and the Truth clarifies this struggle in His words: ﴿So his soul permitted him the murder of his brother﴾.

For Qabil wanted to kill Habil out of the instinct of domination, and his soul contended with him out of fear of sin. Solicitation turned in Qabil's soul until the instinct of domination prevailed, commanding the killing, and it subdued the rest of the self. This reveals to us that the human soul contains multiple faculties, each faculty having its own aim, and that religion is what establishes peaceful coexistence among the faculties.

Another example: the sexual instinct raises a frenzy in the soul, so faith-consciousness restrains it by saying to the faithful soul: beware of defiling the honour of people, lest people defile your honour; and why do you not go and marry as God prescribed, and not cuckold your sons on another's bed? For the instinct is created by God, so do not let the authority of instinct command and forbid.

Thus we see that the self encompasses and includes faculties and instincts, and it is not right for a person to let one instinct overstep into another matter, for if the desires transgress, the world is corrupted.

For instance, we use electricity, which gives us light within the limits drawn by the electrical engineer, who placed the positive pole in its place and likewise the negative pole, so that we take the light we want, or it gives us a spark that we use as power to run a machine. But if the positive pole met the negative pole contrary to the engineer's design, an electrical short-circuit would occur, causing fire or corruption. Likewise with the human soul: if male and female meet as God prescribed, humanity is made happy; but if anything else happens, what occurs in society becomes a psychological and social fire with no limit to its harmful effects. Thus we see that the soul does not have a single drive, but multiple drives.

We find the instinct of hunger moving the soul toward food, and religion responds to this, but it enjoins that a person eat on the condition that eating does not turn into gluttony, as came in the hadith: "The son of Adam needs only a few morsels to keep his spine upright." (1)

Food is for the survival of the species, and man loves exploration, so Islam commands man to investigate the signs of God in the universe in order to increase the good of the cosmos, and Islam forbids using the love of exploration for spying on people. Thus the faculties are balanced by the method of Islam, and the Muslim must live with his faculties in the light of God's method, a sound coexistence, so that the human soul is mutually supportive, not mutually antagonistic, and so that all faculties live in peace and each apparatus performs its task as God willed.

But the hypocrite lives wavering, and he has done this to himself, for he has loosed the reins of some faculties at the expense of others: ﴿wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those.﴾ The disbeliever is distinguished from the hypocrite outwardly by being at one with himself: he does not believe in Islam and declares it, but in reality he struggles with his fitra (innate nature), which calls him to faith.

Someone may say: how can one who shows faith and conceals disbelief be equal to one who declares disbelief? We say: the disbeliever has not deceived the believing group, nor did he claim, as the hypocrite does, to be of the believing company while not being part of it. Rather, the disbeliever declares his disbelief, at one with himself; but the hypocrite is wavering, base in his human and manly condition.

﴿Wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those. And whoever Allah leaves astray, you will never find for him a way.﴾

God does not lead a servant astray directly. He first teaches His creatures through the messengers and the method, but He leaves astray whoever insists on disbelief, so He leaves him in his error and blindness. It is true that it is within God's power to bring him to faith by compulsion, but He leaves the human being to his choice.

When a person turns to God, He helps him toward guidance; but if he does not turn, let him go to the wilderness of error. He adorns the world for him and gives him of it, but he will not find a way, for the way of God is one, and there are not two ways.

We mention this anecdote to know the value of God's way. Al-Asma'i, a great Arab author whose literary ear inclined toward beautiful styles of poetry and prose, once saw a man standing at the door of the Multazam at the Holy Ka'ba, supplicating God fervently: "O Lord, I am disobeying You, and had I not been disobeying You I would not have come to ask You for forgiveness. There is no god but You. I ought to be ashamed of my disobedience, but what can I do?" Al-Asma'i was impressed by the supplication and said: "O man, God will forgive you for the goodness of your request."

(1) From a hadith narrated by al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah.

Then the Truth says:

﴿O you who believe, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do you want to give Allah a clear proof against yourselves?﴾

The Truth has taken it upon the hypocrites that they take the disbelievers as allies instead of Allah. Likewise, the believers have taken it upon the hypocrites that they have adopted, from the camp of disbelief, a patron for themselves instead of Allah and instead of the believers. Therefore it is more fitting for the believers not to do such a thing. Glorified is He, He clarifies: "Indeed We have taken it upon the hypocrites that they take the disbelievers as allies instead of Allah, so beware lest you do as they do."

"O you who believe, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do you want to give Allah a clear proof against yourselves?"

This is a logical command that is in harmony with the method of faith, because if you do that, you are presenting the proof for Allah to punish you with. You know that the hypocrite proclaims faith with his tongue and conceals disbelief in his heart. So how can the situation of the believer with the disbeliever be like the situation of the hypocrite with the disbeliever? That is a matter that does not fit, and whoever does that is only presenting a proof to Allah so that He may punish him.

In His sending of the messengers, in His supporting the messengers with miracles, and in His sending of comprehensive methods to organize human movement in life, all of that is to cut off the proof against people, so that no one may say: "You did not tell us, O Lord, how we should walk according to a certain method." Therefore Glorified is He did not leave man to think with his intellect so that through his thinking he would arrive at the existence of God and discover that there is a Creator of the universe. He, Glorified is He, did not leave us to these conjectures, but sent us messengers with a clear method, so that people would have no proof against Allah after the messengers, so that no one may say: "You did not warn me, O Lord." Ignorance of the law in human legislation does not exempt a person from punishment if he commits a crime. But Allah does not act that way, for He is more generous to His servants than they are to themselves. Therefore He sends the Messenger to bear the method that makes clear the lawful from the unlawful:

﴿That he who perishes might perish upon clear proof, and he who lives might live upon clear proof﴾ (part of verse 42, Surat al-Anfal).

So no one may say: "Allah took us unawares." And you, O believers, if you take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers, and draw close to them and support them, then you are worse in evil than the hypocrites, because the hypocrite has his excuses, and in his depths there is a thread of disbelief and a thread of faith. The proof is clear against you, O believers, for the Truth has conveyed the method to you and you have declared faith in it. If you do otherwise, you give the Truth the proof to punish you.

"Do you want to give Allah a clear proof against yourselves?" The clear authority (sultan mubin) is the evident, all-encompassing authority that no one can repel. If there is a proof, a person may be able to refute it, like a lawyer before the courts, but Allah's proof is a clear authority, meaning it can never be overturned.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 4, verse 145:

And after that, the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire, and you will not find for them any helper.﴾ (4:145)

Let us observe the precision of faith-based education. The Truth did not place a separate section in His Book devoted to the hypocrites, presenting in it everything related to them. Rather, He gives a glimpse of the hypocrites, then gives another snapshot of the believers, so that the listener is repelled by the condition of the hypocrite and made to love the attributes of the believer. Here He says: "Indeed, the hypocrites are in the lowest depth of the Fire, and you will not find for them any helper." The word "dark" (darak) is pronounced sometimes with a sukun on the rā' and sometimes with a fatḥa on the rā', like the word "nahr" (river). Ad-darak is always a descent. The authentic report clarifies this by saying: "The Fire has descending levels (darakat) just as Paradise has ascending levels (darajat)" (1).

So descending downward is ad-darak, and ascending upward is the climbing of the stairs (ad-daraj). In our era we take sea level as a measure, because land is uneven, whereas the sea is level.

We also use the water level for precise matters. When rain falls on roads, it reveals the work of the contractor who paved them: did he perfect this work or not? And when we pour a bucket of water into the bathroom after tiling it, the quality or poor quality of the worker's work is exposed. So there is something that exposes something else. The common Egyptian saying is: "The one who does the plastering is the one who exposes the mason." If the wall is not level, the plasterer is compelled to fill the gaps and the unevenness until the surface of the wall becomes even. What exposes the quality of the plasterer is the painter of the wall, for he either uses a great deal of filler to fill the uneven areas of the wall, or he finds the task easy. What exposes the quality or poor quality of the painter's work are natural things such as dust. The worker who wants to cheat is the one who hurries to hand over the building, because the dust present in the air moves in a straight line, and when there is a wall painted with inferior material, the dust sticks to it. It is as if God wanted by this to expose the one who does not perfect his work. Everything ultimately returns to God, so that all creatures will arrive at the Truth, exalted is He, exposed, except the believers who do righteous deeds; these are the ones whom God covers with their righteous deeds.

"Indeed, the hypocrites are in the lowest depth of the Fire, and you will not find for them any helper." Exalted and glorified is He, who had already presented to us the image of the hypocrites as wavering, having no stability in any opinion, and having no standing in any color that the society in which they live respects. He said about them: ﴿Wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those﴾ (part of 4:143).

Dhabdhaba (wavering) is a kind of instability of personality that has no intrinsic foundation. When He, exalted and glorified, presented them in this distorted manner, He makes clear that His requital for them is a right that corresponds to what they did.

He prepared minds to be ready to accept the judgment He sent down upon them, so that people would not be seized by pity for them or mercy toward them. When He, exalted, issues a judgment, He guarantees by His self-subsistence (qayyūmiyya) and His oneness that there will be no contender to Him in the judgment. It would have been possible for Him to say, "I will place him in the lowest depth of the Fire, and no other power will rescue the hypocrite," so the Truth follows the judgment with His saying: "and you will not find for them any helper." That is, it is a judgment encompassed by execution, and no one of God's creation can overturn it. He alone possesses sovereignty, and He has given sovereignty in this world to people's causes as well, but in the Hereafter there is no sovereignty for anyone, and no sovereignty for anyone.

﴿Whose is the sovereignty today? It is God's, the One, the Subduer﴾ (part of 40:16).

(1) Tafsir of Imam Ibn Kathir.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 4, verse 146:

After that, the Truth grants groups of the hypocrites the opportunity to reconsider their position on the matter, to declare their faith, and to repent of what they had done. He, glory be to Him, gave them the opportunity to review themselves and hold themselves to account, and He did not close the door before them, but said:

﴿Except for those who repent, amend, hold fast to God, and make their religion sincerely God's. Those are with the believers, and God will give the believers a mighty reward.﴾

So it is possible that there may be an opening of goodness that may move a person to repentance, and so that no one thinks the judgment here is final. This is so that a person does not lose himself and become entangled in further evils. Therefore He said: "Except those who repent," meaning those who repent of their earlier hypocrisy. If their earlier hypocrisy has caused corruption, then they must correct what they have corrupted, hold fast to God, and devote their intention and their deeds sincerely to God. "Except those who repent, amend, hold fast to God, and make their religion sincerely God's." Thus the conditions for salvation from the lowest level of the Fire are repentance, reforming what has been corrupted, holding fast to God, and making His religion sincerely His.

Repentance here means giving up hypocrisy, and that the hypocrite should not leave the corruption that his hypocrisy produced, but must strive earnestly to set right what this hypocrisy has damaged. As for holding fast to God, how does it come about?

We have already known that they used to do this seeking honor with the disbelievers, meaning that the soul of the hypocrite finds comfort in these disbelievers, so he takes refuge with them and takes pride in their strength and firmness. Therefore God clarifies: remove this idea from your heads, and let your holding fast be to God alone, for no one can grant protection against God. Make honor belong to God and recourse to Him alone.

It is noticeable that the one who repents, amends, and holds fast to God has fulfilled the pillars of certainty in faith in God. Yet the Truth says: "and make their religion sincerely God's." So why did He emphasize sincerity here? Because the planning of hypocrisy originated first in their hearts, and we know that the heart may sin. The sin of a bodily member is to transgress; for example, the eye sins when it looks upon what is forbidden of others, and the tongue sins when it attacks people with insult or abuse. Thus every bodily member has a sphere of disobedience, and here the sphere of the heart's disobedience is hypocrisy, which is a hidden matter. Therefore His saying: "and make their religion sincerely God's" came to affirm the necessity of sincerity in repenting from hypocrisy, and sincerity has its seat in the heart.

So the repentance of the hearts is other than the repentance of the limbs. The repentance of the limbs is that they refrain from the sphere of their sins, while the repentance of the heart is that it refrains from the sphere of its hypocrisy by becoming sincere. Thus the Truth established the distinction of the believers who did not plunge into hypocrisy, and made the repentant hypocrites to be with the believers. So the basis of being granted bliss and attaining the great reward is to be in the company of the believers. "Those are with the believers, and God will give the believers a mighty reward."

From here we know that the great reward belongs to the believers, and whoever is with the believers attains the same reward. The Truth has made the recompense of the same kind as the deed. The hypocrites used to feign faith in order to take from the believers the outward features of Islam, such as the protection of property and blood, and so that everyone would regard them outwardly and formally as Muslims. When they were hypocritical toward the Muslims, the Muslims gave them what they had. When they repented, amended, held fast to God, and made religion sincerely God's, God placed them with the believers, and He, glory be to Him, gives the people of faith a mighty reward.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe? And Allah is ever Appreciative, Knowing.﴾

He, glory be to Him, had already made clear that the hypocrites are in the lowest level of the Fire, and He excepted from them those who repent, reform, hold fast to Allah, and act sincerely. Here He speaks of the very idea of punishment itself, to clarify it, saying: "What would Allah do with your punishment?" This is a question, and a question is originally an inquiry from one who asks, requiring an answer from one who responds. Glory be to Him and exalted is He wants to present a matter that is established, so He does not present it as a statement. He is capable of saying: "I do not gain anything by punishing you, nor do I achieve for My Self any benefit through it. I do not bring about by it any benefit for Myself, nor do I repel by it any harm from Myself."

But here He does not present this matter as a statement from Himself. Rather, He makes the hypocrites say it themselves. An example of this, and to Allah belongs the highest similitude, is that one person says to another: "You have insulted me," and the other may reply: "I did not insult you, and I swear to you that I did not insult you," and he may add: "Bring me a witness." Here we find the stages of the matter: it begins with the report of no insult, then the oath that no insult occurred, and after that the demand for a witness that the alleged insult did take place.

A person may also respond to one who accuses him of insult, saying: "I leave this matter to you. What did I say to you that you consider it an insult?" One who says this is confident that whoever felt insulted, if he turned his head and mind, would not find a single word that carries any suspicion of insult.

If a person is certain that he insulted the other, he fears that the other will produce proof of the validity of his accusation. But when he says to him: "What did I say to you that you consider it an insult?", then he must search and will not find anything, and thus the judgment has been issued against himself.

When Allah says: "What would Allah do with your punishment?", this is an address to a group who were going to be punished, and among them were those who opposed Allah, and He accepted their testimony. It is as if this is an allusion that the disobedient deserves punishment by the text of the verse: "What would Allah do with your punishment?", and is prepared for this punishment because he opposes Allah. But Allah accepts from him and from those like him that they testify. This is evidence that the innate faith in the human soul, when it is afflicted and the matter grows severe upon it, finds nothing but the logic of faith.

The Truth makes clear to the hypocrites: what would I do with your punishment? They will find no reason specific to Allah to punish them. It is as if the natural disposition has awakened in them, for they will turn the matter over in their souls.

Among us humans, we see that what drives a person to punish another person is only to cure the anger of his heart, or to take revenge on him, because he has hurt him so he wants to return this pain, or to prevent its harm from himself. Glory be to Him and exalted is He cannot be in any of these positions. So if the hypocrites turn this matter over naturally without faith, their answer will be nothing but the following: "Allah will not do anything with our punishment, if we are grateful and believe."

From this we conclude that when the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted is He, wants to present a matter in which the ruling is established from the opponent himself, He casts it in the form of a question, and it would have been possible for Him to render this matter as a statement. However, a statement is a testimony from Allah for Himself, whereas a question's answer will be an acknowledgment from the other party. This means that they were disobedient and opposing, and it is as if He has entrusted them with this answer, because the answer is an innate matter from which there is no escape. When the disbeliever turns his head to think ill of Allah in a way that is not fitting, he will never find such an assumption.

"What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe, and Allah is ever Appreciative, Knowing." And if they do not thank and do not believe, then what does the Truth gain from their punishment? We know that the greatness of the Truth is that no act of obedience returns any benefit to Allah, and no act of disobedience returns any harm to Allah, but He considers benefit and harm to return to the creation of Allah, not to Allah, glory be to Him.

Glory be to Him wants us obedient so that we achieve safety in society, the safety of people from one another. Therefore, the matter the Truth desires, He does not desire for Himself. He existed before creating creation, with all attributes of perfection belonging to Him, and with the attributes of perfection He brought creation into being, and bringing creation into being adds nothing to Him. Therefore He said in the Hadith Qudsi:

"O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most pious heart of one man among you, that would not increase anything in My dominion. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most wicked heart of one man among you, that would not decrease anything from My dominion. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, stood in one open plain and asked Me, and I gave each human his request, that would not diminish what is with Me except as a needle diminishes when it is dipped into the sea." (1)

Thus obedience with respect to Allah and disobedience with respect to Allah are only for something that returns to the creation of Allah. Let us look at the mercy of the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, who created creation and then protected the creation from the creation, and glory be to Him considered that whoever treats well a creature like himself is obedient to Allah, and Allah loves him because he has done good to the handiwork of Allah.

"What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe?" So if you are grateful and believe, Allah will do nothing with your punishment, meaning you have removed yourselves far from deserving punishment.

Glory be to Him wants to balance the temperament of society and the interactions of its individuals with one another, so that society may have continuity, growth, and coexistence. We know that every person has a trait and a talent, and society desires this talent.

It may be that a person has land and wants to build upon it, and the owner of the land is not required to study engineering first in order to design the building and its drawings, nor is he required to master the craft of building in order to build the house. Likewise, he is not required to learn the trades of painting and electricity and others.

Similarly, one who wants to wear a robe is not required to learn shearing wool from sheep or spinning cotton, or how to weave it and then how to tailor and sew it. No, every person must have a work that benefits people. So every person has a work through which he benefits people, so that the beneficial exchange is achieved. Because each of us needs the other, there must be a framework of peaceful coexistence in life, not that strife should be the basis of everything, because strife weakens strength and wastes it in vain. Glory be to Him wants all the forces of society to support one another, not oppose one another. Therefore He said: "What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe?" As for if you do not thank and do not believe, then your punishment is a discipline for you that returns nothing to Allah.

Why did the Truth place gratitude with faith? First, let us know what gratitude is. Gratitude is offering praise to the benefactor from one who has received his favor, so directing gratitude means that you say to one who has done you a kindness: "May your goodness increase." What is faith? It is certainty that Allah is One. But which comes first, gratitude or faith? Faith in its essence comes after benefiting from the blessing. When a human came into the universe, he found the universe orderly, and no one told him anything about any religion or creator. Does this human's soul not yearn to seek to know who made this universe for him?

When a messenger comes, the messenger says to the human: "You are seeking the power that created for you all this universe that surrounds you; its name is Allah, and what is required of you is to walk upon this method." Here faith has been placed in its position after the blessing, so gratitude comes first, and after that faith exists. Gratitude is general recognition, and faith is detailed recognition. Gratitude relates to the blessing, and faith relates to the Essence that bestowed the blessing.

"What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe, and Allah is ever Appreciative, Knowing." The Truth, glory be to Him, here clarifies: I am the God who bestows the blessing; I show appreciation to you. How is that? Let us strike this example, and to Allah belongs the highest similitude: you bought your son some toys, and you did not do so until you had fulfilled the necessities of life, for no one brings toys to his son while he has not brought him food or clothing.

So you bring your son toys after food and clothing in order to fill his free time, and this means that the necessities have been completed. When you tell your son: "This toy is only for play; you will take it for an hour when you want to play and put it back in its place when you study," then everything in this house has a function it must perform. This means that you, as a father, want to discipline your son so that he plays with his toy at playtime and does not play with anything else in the house, because if he played with everything in the house he would certainly break something. So there is no room for play with the television, the clock, the refrigerator, or the washing machine, lest those devices be damaged.

You as a father want to distinguish between something one plays with and something one uses seriously, and serious things are only present when requested. The washing machine is used only at the hour of washing clothes, the clock is used only at the moment we wish to know the time, and the refrigerator is opened only when you want to take out something to eat or drink. The father gives the son a little play to set a boundary for him between the things he may play with and the things he must not play with. The household items must not be approached by the son except at the time of their use, but as for the toy, the son plays with it when playtime comes, yet he must look after it. When the father watches his son and finds him carrying out instructions, guarding the household's belongings, and playing with his toys while keeping them safe, and if the father did not teach his son this, the son might spoil his toys.

When the son carries out his father's instructions, the father is pleased with him and delighted by him. When a new toy comes out in the market, the father who is pleased with his son buys him this new toy, because the boy has become trustworthy: he knows the rules of play while preserving the play-things, and he also knows how to preserve the household's belongings. The father's pleasure with the son's conduct increases, and from this pleasure it results that the father buys new toys. If this is what happens in the relationship between a father and a son, and both are creatures of Allah, then what of the Supreme Creator, glory be to Him and exalted, who brought all creatures into being?

When a person places all matters in the light of the method of Allah, Allah is Appreciative and Knowing, because Allah is pleased with the servant who walks upon His method, and when the Lord is pleased with the servant He gives him more. So Allah is Appreciative means that if humans receive blessings well, placing each blessing in its proper sphere, so that a serious blessing is not exceeded by a frivolous one and a frivolous blessing is not exceeded by a serious one, then Allah is pleased with the servants.

The meaning of Allah's pleasure is that He gives humans things that are not merely necessities, but what is beyond that, which makes humans happy. Glory be to Him gives necessities to all, even the disbeliever, and He gives what is beyond necessities, which are things that bring happiness to humans.

So the meaning that Allah is Appreciative is that He, glory be to Him and exalted, is pleased and rewards as a result, giving the human things of the same kind, and His giving rises, in confirmation of His saying, the Truth: ﴿If you are grateful, I will surely increase you﴾ (Ibrahim 14:7).

So gratitude here is directed from the servant to the Lord, and the increase is from the Lord to the servant. Beware, O human, of doing things only outwardly, like the child who guards his toy only at the moment he sees his father, and the instant his father disappears from the child's eyes he spoils the toy. Allah is not like the father at all: the father's capacities are limited, but Allah is the Supreme Creator, from whom nothing is hidden, and glory be to Him, He is Appreciative, and He is also Knowing.

(1) Related by Muslim, Abu 'Awana, Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim from Abu Dhar.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 4, verse 148:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Allah does not like the public utterance of evil speech, except by one who has been wronged. And Allah is ever Hearing, Knowing.﴾ (4:148)

He, glorified and exalted is He, wants to protect the ears of the community of faith from "evil talk" (qalat al-su'), that is, from vile words. For we know that people speak only what they hear. A word the ear does not hear, no tongue will utter. We find a child raised in a refined household who does not utter ugly words, and then ugly words come from his tongue. At that point we ask: where did these words come to the lips of this son? We know they came from the street, because the child's constant environment contains no vile words. When a person investigates the source of these words, he finds that the refined child spent some time in another environment from which some vile words seeped into him.

So language is the daughter of imitation: what the ear hears, the tongue reproduces. We know that language is neither a race nor a blood. In other words, if an English child is raised in an Arab environment, he will speak Arabic, and if we take an Arab child and place him in an English environment, he will speak English.

Every language contains words that no tongue speaks unless it has heard them, and if a person does not hear them, he will not utter them. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, wants to protect the community of faith from evil talk that strikes people's ears, because it would give them a vile language. For if people speak evil talk, the shape of society would become strange, and evil talk would echo in the ears of the wicked. It is as if the Truth, glorified is He, is clarifying: beware that your tongues utter things that Allah does not love. The matter is not merely that a person relieves himself by uttering a word; rather, the utterance of that word will burden generations, because whoever hears the vile word will repeat it, and others will hear it and repeat it, and the bad example will continue, and the person who first uttered the word of evil will bear its burden.

This evil talk may be true or false. If it is true, for instance, we cannot say that all people are wicked; and a person may begin with abuse, and it is permissible for a person to claim abuse against another. Thus the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, wants to protect the ears of faith from the tongues of evil. Therefore He says: "Allah does not like the public utterance of evil speech." Its counterpart, naturally, is: Allah loves the public utterance of good speech. When the Truth binds the community with this faithful bond, does He treat one faculty at the expense of another? No.

We know that the soul contains the love of revenge, the love of self-defense, the love of retaliation, and that by which a person relieves himself and lightens the rage he feels. The Arab proverb says: "Whoever is provoked and does not become angry is a donkey," because the one who is provoked and does not become angry is deficient in constitution. Does this mean that Allah prevents people from uttering a word of evil by which a person vents his chest and relieves his soul? No. Rather, He, glorified is He, places a condition on the word of evil: "except by one who has been wronged." For injustice is taking a person's right for another, and every person is keen on himself and on his rights. If an injustice befalls a person, the faculties of his soul become angry and boil, and then either he vents what he says from himself, or he suppresses and conceals it.

If Allah had said, "Allah does not like the public utterance of evil speech," and stopped there, it would have been a suppression of the human soul. And this suppression, although it is obedience to the command of Allah, because He does not like the public utterance of evil speech, may burst forth at the moment of agitation and explode. Therefore the Truth places the condition, which is the occurrence of injustice, and clarifies, glorified is He: I do not love the public utterance of evil speech, but I permit it within its limits, as a release of the rage of hearts, because I do not love to correct one faculty at the expense of another.

This is why the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Anger is an ember kindled in the heart. Have you not seen the swelling of its veins and the redness of its eyes? So when one of you feels something of that, if he is standing, let him sit; if he is sitting, let him lie down; and if that does not cease, let him perform ablution with cold water or bathe, for fire is only extinguished by water." (1)
