That is, a person should move immediately upon feeling anger, changing his position, or rising to pray after performing ablution or bathing, for by this he vents a physical release, to lighten the pressure of the emotions upon the active soul, just as a person opens a valve on a machine containing steam to let out some of the steam.

So whoever is wronged may publicly speak evil, and the public utterance has two benefits. The first: a person vents from himself and is not suppressed. Second: he makes it known and announces that this man is a wrongdoer, so that people take precautions in dealing with him, and so that a person does not deceive himself into thinking he is safe from his own misdeeds. For if every person concealed the injustice done to him, injustice would spread in the performance of evil deeds. But beware, O servant, of broadening your understanding of this word "injustice," for what reaches you from the one who wronged you is either an act or a word, and you, O Muslim, must measure the matter by a precise measure, in proportion to the injustice that befell you.

﴿Whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you.﴾ (2:194)

Thus the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, grants us the exception only to the extent of necessity, and clarifies: beware that you exceed this necessity. If your wrong is by speech, then I am the Hearing; and if your wrong is by act, then I am the Knowing. So let no one exceed the bounds of decency.

Thus the Truth establishes the faith-based and psychological controls. He removed suppression, and at the same time did not close the door of faith-based aspiration. He permitted the servant to speak out if an injustice befalls him, but if a person possesses faith-based aspiration, he may refrain from speaking out and forgive. So there is a difference between a matter the Truth places in the hand of a person and a matter He obliges him to by compulsion and coercion. As for speaking out, He, glorified is He, left the matter in the hand of the person, and He loves that a person forgive, for the Qur'anic principles support one another. He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Repel [evil] with that which is better, and then the one between whom and you there is enmity will become as though he were a devoted friend.﴾ (41:34)

If Allah permits you to speak out with evil speech when someone wrongs you, He has also given you the option of not speaking out but rather forgiving him. It is most likely that the one of evil character will be humbled and will know that there are people better than him in character. No one tires except by seeing someone better than himself in something. When the wrongdoer sees that the wronged one has forgiven, the desire to be better than him may burst forth in his soul.

So the faith-based principle, "Repel with that which is better," Allah made a beloved domain, and did not make it compulsion; for if you give a person his right, and then leave to his generosity the choice to relinquish the right, this satisfies everyone. Thus the Truth cultivates faith-based generosity in the human soul, because if He had made it compulsory, He would have corrected one faculty at the expense of another. Therefore, if you see a person who has transgressed against another, and the one transgressed against repels the transgressor with what is better, forgives and reforms, the condition of the transgressor may be reformed. He, glorified is He, said: (Repel with that which is better, and then the one between whom and you there is enmity will become as though he were a devoted friend).

If the transgressor persists after that, the person must know that Allah never lies, and there must be a flaw in your conduct, O you who think you have repelled with what is better.

Perhaps the one who repelled with what is better said in a tone of arrogance: "I will forgive you." Such arrogant conduct does not make anyone a devoted friend. But if one truly repels with what is better, in humility and magnanimity, then the matter must come to what Allah said: (then the one between whom and you there is enmity will become as though he were a devoted friend). Allah sets the reciprocal psychological interactions within clear frameworks, and He, glorified is He, said:

﴿Whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you.﴾ (2:194)

This is so that the transgressor does not also spread his corruption. There is a person who, if we leave him once and again, spreads; but if we stop him at his limit, he falls silent. In this way we spare society from the spread of corruption, and the Truth makes the matter of repelling aggression difficult.

A question arises: who is capable of achieving equivalence with justice? For example, we find a person who struck another a slap on the face: with what force did he strike, and in what place did he strike? Therefore we find that returning aggression with exact equivalence is difficult. And since what is commanded is that I transgress in the same manner as I was transgressed against, and I cannot achieve equivalence, perhaps the matter will exceed the equivalence, and having been the one wronged, I become the wrongdoer. In that case forgiveness is closer and safer.

The emotional process that overtakes a person in reciprocal interactions has agitations in the soul that drive toward inclination, and the process of inclination is the response to what a person perceives. If a person harms you, wearies you, and transgresses against you, you exert effort to suppress your rage, that is, to hold back the rage with force. So the rage exists, but what is required is that the person prevent the movement of inclination only, and the enraged one must restrain himself from acting on it, even if the rage remains in the heart.

﴿And those who suppress their anger﴾ (3:134)

This is a first stage, followed by a second stage:

﴿And those who pardon people﴾ (3:134)

If the requirement in the first stage is to prevent the act of inclination, then what is more exalted than that is to forgive, and forgiveness is to remove the matter that angers you from your heart. And if you seek a higher stage in suppressing anger and forgiving, then do good to him, for whoever commits transgressions is the one who is spiritually sick, and when you see a person sick in his body you help him and assist him even if he is your enemy, and you overlook his enmity; how much more so the one afflicted in his values. He needs us to suppress anger, or to forgive as a higher degree, or to do good to him as a stage of higher ascent. Thus the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, permits you to retaliate in kind, then leaves room for us to suppress anger so that we do not retaliate, but the cause remains in the heart; then He elevates us another stage to forgiveness and to removing the matter from our hearts; then He ascends us to yet another rise, and He, glorified is He, says: (And Allah loves the good-doers). And who among us is not desirous of Allah's love? Thus we see that the Islamic religion commands the believer to do good to whoever wronged him.

Someone may ask: how do you ask me to do good to one who wronged me? The answer: you and he are not beyond the reach of Al-Qayyum. He is Al-Qayyum, neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him, and everything is visible to Him, and both of you are His creation. When Allah sees one of His creatures transgress against you or wrong you, He, glorified is He, is with you and grants you protection, and stands at your side because you are the one wronged. Thus the wrong done by the other makes the Truth, glorified is He, on your side, and that wrong, in its essence, becomes a gift to you.

When we philosophize about all matters, we find that the one who forgives has gained more than if he had taken revenge and avenged himself, because if he takes revenge, he does so with his limited power; but when he forgives, he leaves the matter to Allah, whose power is unlimited, if He wishes to respond to him, and with unlimited giving if He wishes to satisfy the one who wronged him. This is the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, when the wronged one who forgives and does good turns to Him, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing of everything.

1 Related by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman and al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Abu Sa'id, without the phrase (توقد); and Ahmad and Abu Dawud related it.

The Almighty then says:

﴿If you disclose good or conceal it, or pardon an evil, then indeed Allah is ever Pardoning, Competent.﴾ (4:149)

We have already learned that the Truth does not permit you to voice evil speech except when you have been wronged. This means that the matter admits of both disclosure and concealment. He said: "If you disclose good" — that is, if you make good manifest, or conceal it, or pardon an evil. All of these matters, whether apparent or hidden, belong to human circumstances. But nothing is hidden from Allah. Pardon cannot have a faith-based merit unless it is accompanied by power; if one were incapable, he could not say "I have pardoned." Subhanahu pardons while able. So if you wish to pardon, then adopt the character of the method of Allah, so that your pardon comes with power. We should also know that the Truth does not want us to be humiliated or made to submit, but He wants us to be capable. And as long as we are capable, pardon is pardon from strength, and this is the faith-based merit, for the pardon of the incapable is not considered pardon.

People look at the one who is incapable and says, "I have pardoned," while he has no power; you see him as one who has been humiliated. As for the one who wishes to adopt the character of the method of Allah, let him take from the bounties of Allah in the universe, so that he may be capable and honored, such that if evil reaches him, he pardons from a position of power. "Indeed Allah is ever Pardoning, Competent."

We said before: when you notice the word "kāna" (was) applied to Allah, such as in attributing forgiveness or mercy to Him, we must say: "He was and still is," because the act with Allah is free from the past, the present and the future. So since He has been, and no circumstances touch Him, He continues forever.

Then the Truth (may He be exalted) says:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers, and want to make a distinction between Allah and His messengers, and say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and want to adopt a way in between. Those are the disbelievers in truth. And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.﴾

Glorified is He, He wants to make the matter of faith one single, comprehensive matter with no parts to it. Declaring belief in Allah alone is not sufficient for a person to be a believer, because the requirement of believing in Allah calls for a messenger who makes you know that the Creator, who subjected the forces of the universe to you, is the one whose name is Allah, and you cannot be guided to knowing the name of the creative Power except through a messenger sent down from Allah.

We know that the work of the intellect in doctrinal deduction is incapable of knowing the name of the Creator of the universe, because man came into an organized universe, and it was incumbent upon him to turn his attention to know the power that preceded this existence and created it, and that man came into an existence that is complete. A person may hear from his father, for example, that this house was built by the father or grandfather, and that thing was made by so-and-so, son of so-and-so, but no one has heard anyone say to him, "And who built the heavens?" and no one has heard anyone say, "And who created the sun?" Although people claim what is not theirs, how then can the greatest thing in Allah's universe be left without our knowing who brought it into being?

We find people writing the history of a thing that is trivial or relatively important in their lives. We find studies on the history of stones, and studies on the history of the manufacture of things, such as the history of the electric lamp that Edison invented, who generated electricity from its meagre sources and operated it. In short, we find that everything in this existence has a history, and this history traces the thing back to the origin of its existence. And if you trace any craft, however important or trivial, you will discover that one person received it from another, and he did not originate it all at once.

Every innovator took what had been reached before him and began a new work, until inventions reached their birth. Who would believe that a lamp that lights up, goes out and burns is made by a human, and we know its history, and then we look at the sun, which has not dimmed, weakened, gone out or burned out, while the lamp illuminates a small, limited space and the sun illuminates a universe and an existence? Does the sun not need someone to reflect on its history?

We have already said: when a person looks at the universe with a view remote from the idea of religion and remote from the message of the messengers about the Creator, the way of creation and the method of guidance, he says to himself: people's ranks differ according to their positions and power in what they do. There is one who sits on a chair of sycamore wood, another on a chair made of rose wood, and a third who sits on a mat.

Man lives by the crafts of other human beings according to his destiny and station. The villager or the Bedouin lights fire by striking a steel piece against flint and keeps the fire for use more than once. When he advances in using fire, he uses a "misrajah" (oil lamp), and when he became more civilized he used a "gas lamp" with glass, and it had numbers indicating its power of illumination.

There is a lamp number five, and its number is evidence of its weak power. The power of the "lamp" multiplies after that according to the area to be lit. When man advanced further, he used the "kulub" (pressure lamp), and when he advanced further still, he used electricity, neon, or solar energy. When the sun rises, every person turns off the light he is using, for its light suffices from any light. At night a person tries to keep the electricity in his house in good condition, fearing that some wire may be cut and the place go dark. So what of the sun, which never suffers such a thing?

We find that man throughout history tries to ascend to understanding the boundless power of the Truth, even if no messenger had come. But the names of the creative power are not known by anyone through reason, rather only through the messengers. The name "Allah" is a tawqifi name (one known only through revelation). How then could there be a statement such as these people's: "We will believe in Allah and disbelieve in His messengers"? How did they know, then, that the power they will believe in is named Allah? They must have known that through a messenger, because belief in Allah comes only after a communication from Allah conveyed by a messenger, to tell his name to whoever believes in him.

Is belief in Allah as a hidden, vague and great power sufficient? Or must a person think about what this power demands of him? And if this power demands of man that he follow a specific way, who conveys the way?

There must then be a messenger who tells us the name of the creative power and what it requires of man in following the way, and explains to us how to obey this power. No one, therefore, can separate belief in Allah from the messenger, otherwise it would be belief in a vague power. The proponent of this kind of belief does not dare to say that the name of this power is "Allah", because this name requires a communication from a messenger.

So when one of us hears a person say, "I believe in Allah and I do not believe in the messengers," we must say to him: this is the first intellectual slip, because belief in Allah requires belief in a message brought by a messenger, since belief in Allah is not separable from belief in the messenger.

The Truth, glorified and exalted, created Adam after He created the universe and the rest of the creatures, and we find no one claiming that Adam was the first to inhabit this existence. Adam, in the logic of reason, is one; but by analogy, there are many Adams. It may be said that there were many creatures who preceded Adam in existence, but Adam is the first of the human race. When Allah created him, He taught him all the names so that he could move about in existence; for had he not learned the names, he could not have spoken with any of his children, and could not, for example, have said to one of his sons: "Look, has the sun risen or not?"

So it was necessary for Adam to know all the names through a teacher, because language is the daughter of imitation: no one can say a word until he has heard it. Each of us heard from his father, the fathers heard from the grandfathers, and the matter continues until it reaches Adam. From whom did Adam hear so that he could speak his first word? It must have been Allah, and this is a matter that every rational person must acknowledge. Therefore the Truth's statement in the Qur'an: ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them﴾ (Qur'an 2:31).

It is logical speech by inductive enumeration, and it is a statement distinguished by utmost truthfulness.

When one of us teaches his child speech, he teaches him the nouns; as for verbs, no one knows how they are learned. A person says to his child: "This is a cup, this is a table, that is a plate, this is food," but no one tells his child, "'shariba' (he drank) means such-and-such, and 'akala' (he ate) means such-and-such." So the first seed of speech is nouns, and after that come practice and exercise, so that man learns verbs.

The Truth has left us in His universe great proofs befitting His greatness as the Creator of this universe, and the messenger is the one who brings the message from Him, glorified is He, so He tells us the name of the power, "Allah", and its attributes are "such-and-such", and whoever obeys it enters Paradise, and whoever disobeys it enters Hell. Without a messenger we would remain lost, not knowing the name of the creative power or its requirements. This is what is used to refute the group that worships the sun, the moon or the stars, and we say to them: Do you worship the sun? Perhaps you did that because it is the greatest power in your view.

But there is a question: "What is worship?" The answer is: worship is the obedience of the worshipper to the worshipped. So what has the sun demanded of you that you do, and what has it forbidden and prevented you from doing? The worshippers of the sun admit: the sun has demanded nothing of us. Accordingly, their worship of the sun has no basis, because it has not specified a method of worship, nor can it reward anyone who worships it. A god without a method has no value. Thus we see that worship of any power other than Allah is worship that carries its own denial, and belief in Allah is never separable from belief in the power that communicates from Allah, namely the messengers.

The messenger explains to us how he connects with this divine power, and the divine power explains to us how it connects with the human messenger through another creation that this absolute power created, because the messenger is from among humans, and humans cannot receive directly from the great effective power. We do similar things in our own crafts. We know that when a person wants to sleep, he does not wish for light during his sleep, so he takes the night as his dwelling and enjoys the darkness. But if he wakes in the night, he fears walking in his house without light lest he collide with something. So he may light a small lamp of the strength of a small candle to give himself light, and we call it the "wanasa" (night lamp).

We cannot connect this small lamp directly to electricity, but we install a small transformer that takes from the high electric power and gives to the small lamp. So what of the power of powers?

Allah made another creation, the angels, to be an intermediary between Him and His messengers. These messengers He prepared, glorified is He, with a special preparation to receive this mission. So to those who want to believe in Allah and then disbelieve in His messengers, we say: No, this is deficient faith. The Truth, glorified and exalted, put belief in the messengers in the plural form so that no nation would understand that its messenger alone is the messenger sent down from Allah; rather every nation must believe in all the messengers, because each messenger came at his appointed time according to the requirements of the society contemporary with him, and they all brought one doctrine. No messenger came with a doctrine contrary to the doctrine of another messenger, though they differed in the means and the matters on which the life advancements depend. The Truth first created our master Adam, and from him created his wife Eve, just two, then said, glorified is He:

﴿And from the two of them He spread many men and women﴾ (Qur'an 4:1).

The two lived together and had a number of children, and the children multiplied, so each family needed a house, and each house with a family needed a plot of land from which the family members could draw the produce that suffices for food, and each individual needs at least half a feddan to draw from it his food needs. As offspring increased, the expanse of existence widened through primitive transport. A man whose region became too narrow for him moved to another region with more rain to benefit from or more produce to extract. Groups spread and became isolated, and each group came to have customs, traditions, diseases and faults not found in the other group. Therefore the Truth, glorified and exalted, sent a messenger to each group to treat the ailments of each environment separately. The Truth, glorified and exalted, subjected some minds to the discoveries of the universe, and after that the universe became one piece: the event happens in America and we see it at the very same moment in Egypt. Advancements increased, so bad habits almost became uniform across all human society, so the evil appears in America or Germany and we find it in our society. Thus the ambitious advancements made the world one unit: its afflictions are one, its customs are one, and when one messenger comes he encompasses them all.

Therefore it was necessary for the seal of the messengers, the comprehensive one, peace and blessings be upon him, to come, because the world was no longer isolated, to address the whole of it. He is the best of the messengers, and his nation is the best of nations if it follows his teachings. And it is a requirement of the faith of the Messenger of Allah and those with him that they believe in those messengers who preceded.

As for those who try to distinguish between the messengers, they are a people who do not understand. The Jews believed in Moses, peace be upon him, and burdened him, and disbelieved in Jesus. When Jesus, peace be upon him, came, some believed in him, and when Muhammad, peace be upon him, came, some believed in him and some disbelieved in him. Therefore the Truth named their disbelief in the Seal of the Prophets (﴿then they increased in disbelief﴾), meaning that their disbelief reached its peak, for no prophet will come after him, and with him the procession of the messages was completed, peace and blessings be upon him.

So the purpose of the verse is that faith has a peak: you believe in a power but you do not know its name, nor its requirements, nor what the power has prepared as reward for the obedient or punishment for the disobedient. Therefore a messenger had to exist, because reason leads to the necessity of believing in Allah and the messengers, and the messengers came in succession...

"Those are truly the disbelievers" (﴿أولئك هم الكافرون حقا﴾) is meant to show that the reality of disbelief exists in them. For we may find someone who says: "Is there a true disbeliever and another kind of disbeliever?" Yes. The one who does not believe in all the messages of heaven may possess some excuse, because he did not find the Messenger who conveyed to him. But the one to whom a messenger came, and who has a bond of faith with him, and this bond of faith connects him to heaven through revelation, if this person disbelieves, his disbelief is grievous and certain: "Those are truly the disbelievers."

We notice that when the Truth (al-Haqq) speaks of the disbelievers, He does not isolate them from the judgment and the recompense awaiting them. Rather, the ruling is present with them within the same verse, and the Truth does not refer the ruling to another verse: "Those are truly the disbelievers, and We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment." Here He has joined the recompense for disbelief directly to disbelief. Glorified is He: He has indeed readied the humiliating punishment and prepared it for the disbelievers, and He has not postponed their matter or delayed it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"Paradise was displayed to me, and if I had wished, I would have brought you a cluster of its fruit, and I would have done so."(1)

Allah has indeed prepared Paradise and Hell in fact, and displayed them to the Messenger (ﷺ). Had the Messenger wished to bring the believers a cluster of the fruits of Paradise, he would have done so. So beware of believing that Allah will remain until the Hour comes, then see how many have disbelieved and prepare punishment for them according to their number, or how many have believed and prepare for them Paradise and bliss according to their number. Rather, the Truth has prepared Paradise on the basis that all people are believers and have a place in Paradise, and has prepared Hell on the basis that all people are disbelievers and have places in Hell. Then the believer, in the Hereafter, comes and takes the place prepared for him, and also takes some of the places in Paradise that had been prepared for the one who disbelieved, in confirmation of the words of the Truth:

﴿Those are the inheritors, who will inherit Paradise; therein they will abide forever.﴾ (Surat al-Mu'minun)

So He, glorified, did not wait nor postpone the matter until a census was taken, to ask who believed and who disbelieved, so as to prepare for each group Fire or Paradise according to their count. Rather, He dealt with His creation on the basis that each human who comes to Him may be a believer, so He prepared for each of them a place in Paradise, or that he may be a disbeliever, so He prepared for each of them a place in Hell. And we find the question put to Hell in the Hereafter:

﴿The Day We say to Hell, "Are you filled?" and it says, "Are there any more?"﴾ (Surat Qaf)

So Hell seeks more places, those that had been prepared for whoever did not enter it because he believed in Allah. And the believers inherit the places that had been prepared for whoever did not enter Paradise because he disbelieved in Allah and His messengers, and made a distinction between Allah and His messengers, saying: "We believe in some and disbelieve in others." Then there follows, by contrast, those who disbelieved in Allah and His messengers, namely the believers. This is the logical counterpart.

The use of opposites is more effective in fixing a matter in the mind. For example, when a school principal looks at two young men, each of them in the secondary certificate year, and says: "So-and-so has succeeded because he worked hard, while the second has failed and lost." This contrast occurs in the listener's mind as a comparison between the conduct of the two.

(1) Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Adhan, Ibn Majah in al-Iqamah, and Ahmad.

Here, the Truth presents the counterpart to those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers:

﴿Those who believe in Allah and His messengers, and do not make any distinction between any of them—those, He will soon give them their rewards. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (4:152)

Here the Truth emphasizes a clear matter: "and do not make any distinction between any of them." The word "aḥad" (أحد, "any one") in the language is used sometimes to mean the singular, sometimes to mean the feminine singular, sometimes the dual, whether masculine or feminine dual, or the plural of females or the plural of males, and so on. Thus "aḥad" in this verse encompasses all the messengers, as evidenced by the saying of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He:

﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any of the [other] women﴾ (part of 33:32).

So the word "aḥad" applies equally to the masculine, the feminine, the dual, the singular and the plural. And as the Truth said about those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers, or who make distinctions between the messengers: "Those are the disbelievers in truth, and We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment," the Truth says in this verse about those who believe in Allah and His messengers and do not make any distinction between any of them: "Those, He will soon give them their rewards. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful." So every counterpart has come with its ruling.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 4, verse 153:

And after that, the Truth says:

﴿They ask you, the People of the Book, to bring down to them a Book from heaven. But they asked Moses for something greater than that, when they said, "Show us God openly," so the thunderbolt seized them for their wrongdoing. Then they took the calf after clear proofs had come to them, and We pardoned that. And We gave Moses clear authority.﴾ (4:153)

This is an error on their part in the question. What should have been said was: "The People of the Book ask you to ask God to send down to them a Book." The polytheists of Mecca tried to find a flaw in the Qur'an, but they found none, for they were a people of eloquence, rhetoric and language. They acknowledged that the Qur'an was great, but the calamity, as far as they were concerned, was that it was sent down to Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿They said, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from the two cities?"﴾ (Surat al-Zukhruf, 43:31).

They acknowledged the greatness of the Qur'an, and their acknowledgment of its greatness, together with their rage at its being sent down to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), left them intellectually confused. They acknowledged the greatness of the Qur'an after they had looked at it. At one time they said it was sorcery; at another they said it was taught by some human; they said it was poetry, and they said it was the fables of the ancients. All of this was awe in the face of the greatness of the Qur'an. Finally they said: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from the two cities?﴾

But was it not the very Qur'an that was sent down? So their problem is that it was sent down to Muhammad (ﷺ), and that is out of envy: ﴿Or do they envy the people for what God has given them of His bounty?﴾ (part of 4:54).

Their speech is never characterised by objectivity; rather, all their talk is far from the truth and confused. At one time they said of the Qur'an that it was sorcery, but when people asked them, "Why then did the Qur'an not bewitch you?" (for the bewitched has no will in the presence of the sorcerer), they had no answer. At another time they said of the Qur'an that it was poetry, and the people were astonished at them, because they were a nation of poetry, and they had previously hung the Mu'allaqat on the wall of the Ka'bah. But this is the speech of confusion.

So the whole matter comes down to their refusal to believe. When proof seizes them by the collar in one matter, they move on to another.

God clarifies: if they are asking for a book, the Book has already been sent down, just as a book was sent down to Moses before. Since they confirm the sending down of the Book to Moses, why do they not confirm the sending down of the Book to Muhammad? There must be a special meaning behind the Truth's words: "They ask you, the People of the Book, to bring down to them a Book from heaven." We know that the Book was sent down to Moses written all at once, and they, as People of the Book, ask for the Qur'an to be sent down in the same manner. When we examine the verse, we find them asking that the Book be sent down to them from heaven, as though they wish to isolate the Messenger of God and to have the speech come directly from God to them. Therefore the Truth says in another place:

﴿Is it they who apportion the mercy of your Lord? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and We have raised some of them above others in degrees.﴾ (part of 43:32).

The Truth, then, apportioned affairs in the life of this world, so how do they interfere in the matter of revelation, which is part of the mercy of God: "They ask you, the People of the Book, to bring down to them a Book from heaven"? They have attributed the sending down to the Messenger of God, yet the Messenger of God never said, "I was sent down," but said: "It was sent down to me."

It is said in one narration that Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and the group around him wanted revelation to come down to each of them with a book, and that the revelation said to Ka'b: "O Ka'b, believe in Muhammad."

Or [they wanted] a separate book to come down to each of them in this particular manner, or that God would send down to them a special book along with the Qur'an. And how could they ask for that when they have the Torah? God clarifies, as consolation to His Messenger (ﷺ): do not be overly troubled, O Muhammad, that they ask you for a book to be sent down to them, for they asked Moses for something greater than that. Their request for the sending down of a book is a request for an act from God, and they had previously gone to excess even more when they said to Moses: "Show us God openly." By such a statement they overstepped from the act of God to the Essence of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He. Therefore do not consider their request for a book to be sent down to them as too much, for they asked Moses, who was their messenger, to see God openly: ﴿They ask you, the People of the Book, to bring down to them a Book from heaven. But they asked Moses for something greater than that, when they said, "Show us God openly," so the thunderbolt seized them for their wrongdoing.﴾

When you hear the word "thunderbolt" (al-sa'iqah), understand that it is something that comes from above, beginning with a disturbing sound, as we mentioned earlier during our reflections on a verse in Surat al-Baqarah:

﴿They put their fingers in their ears because of the thunderclaps.﴾ (part of 2:19).

That is, they put their fingers in their ears because of the thunderclaps. This is evidence that the sound of thunder is disturbing and may burst the eardrum, and evidence that the disturbance of thunder exceeds what a single finger can block, because when a person plugs his ears he plugs them with the tip of a finger, not with all the fingers. And so intense was the disturbance of the sound that whenever they placed their fingertips in their ears, the disturbing sound was not prevented.

So the thunderbolt is a disturbing sound that comes from above, and after that the decree of God descends, either as a destructive matter, or as a fire that burns, or as a wind that destroys: "the thunderbolt seized them for their wrongdoing." Wrongdoing (zulm) is to place a right in other than its rightful place; and one does not place a right in other than its rightful place unless one has taken a right from its rightful owner. Their request was a kind of wrongdoing, because perception of things is the encompassing of the perceived by the perceiver.

When you perceive something with your eye, it means that your eye has encompassed the perceived thing and confined it in detail; likewise the ear when it hears a sound, likewise the nose when it smells a scent, likewise touch for knowing softness or roughness, likewise taste so that a person senses flavour. Thus the meaning of perception by any means is that you encompass the perceived thing with a comprehensive, all-embracing encompassing.

So if they asked to see God openly, it means they asked that the instrument of perception, namely the eye, should encompass God. When the perceived is encompassed by the perceiver, one says that it has been "measured" (qadara 'alayh). Would the Supreme Almighty then become something measured? Far be it from God. That is absolute wrongdoing and its extreme. It is permissible for a person to see a person, but it is never right or proper for a person to transfer this matter to God. Why? Because He, glorified is He, said:

﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision.﴾ (part of 6:103).

And since God is the capable Deity, He will not become something made subject to measure.

If we give someone a problem to solve, that means his mind has been able to master it; but if we give him a problem and he cannot solve it, then his mind has not been able to master it. So everything that falls within the sphere of perception tells us that the perceiving instrument has been able to master it.

The Truth, glorified and exalted, is the Supreme Capable, who is never made subject to measure by what He has created. "So the thunderbolt seized them for their wrongdoing. Then they took the calf after clear proofs had come to them." It would have sufficed, after the thunderbolt had seized them, that they should have shown good manners and not presumed against God. But they took the calf after the Truth had carried them across the sea and brought them through it, as facilitation for them and support, and showed them a true miracle, after they had said:

﴿Indeed, we are going to be overtaken.﴾ (26:61).

The sea was before them and Pharaoh behind them, and there was no escape from destruction, for the natural course was for Pharaoh to overtake them. God inspired Moses with revelation, and he said:

﴿He said, "No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me."﴾ (26:62).

Moses resorted to the highest law, the law of God, and God commanded him to strike the sea with his staff; the sea parted and each division became like a mountain and a great peak. After they had walked through the sea, and Pharaoh had been drowned before them, and He had saved them, glorified is He, yet after all that they took the calf as a god.

Thus they met the beauty of God with denial and ingratitude: "Then they took the calf after clear proofs had come to them, so We pardoned that, and We gave Moses clear authority." The clear authority that God gave Moses, peace be upon him, was the manifest dominion and mastery over them, when He commanded them to kill themselves, and they came with swords, because God had given our master Moses strength so that no one could go against his command, and strength is overpowering authority.

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿And We raised above them the mount (Tur) for their covenant, and We said to them, "Enter the gate prostrating," and We said to them, "Do not transgress in the Sabbath," and We took from them a solemn covenant.﴾ (4:154)

So their audacity at the beginning was in asking to see God openly (jahratan), then the second action was their taking the calf as a god. God deals with these people through tangible commands, so He lifted the mountain above them:

(And when We shook the mountain over them as though it were a canopy, and they thought it was going to fall upon them.) (Part of 7:171)

People like these do not submit except to material signs. Therefore God raised the mountain above them: either they take what God has given them with strength and carry out what is required of them, or the mountain falls on them. Thus we see that all their convictions were the result of a material command, and all matters came to them from the direction of matter. "And We said, Enter the gate prostrating": that is, that they should enter bowing down. This too is a material compulsion. This gate which Moses commanded them to enter prostrating was the gate of the town of Jericho in al-Sham. "And We said to them, Do not transgress in the Sabbath." And concerning them, He (glorified is He) said:

﴿When their fish come to them on their Sabbath openly, and on the day they do not keep Sabbath, they do not come to them.﴾ (Part of 7:163)

The word "al-Sabt" (Sabbath) derives linguistically from "sabata" and "yasbutu," meaning he rested and became still. The Truth (subhanahu) says:

﴿And He it is who made the night for you as a garment, and sleep for rest (subatan).﴾ (Part of 25:47)

That is, He made sleep a repose for you, a cessation of your works and rest for your bodies. "And We said to them, Do not transgress in the Sabbath": that is, God forbade them to hunt on the Sabbath day. When the Sabbath day comes, the fish come to them enticingly, lifting their fins out of their side-fins while swimming on the surface of the water or appearing on the face of the water from every direction. This is among the trials. "And on the day they do not keep Sabbath, they do not come to them": that is, on the days when they are permitted to hunt, the fish do not come to them. Therefore they resort to cunning and build fixed enclosures of wire so that the fish enter them on the Sabbath day and cannot get out.

Thus they schemed against the command of God. In this way the Truth (subhanahu wa ta'ala) shows the evasiveness of the Children of Israel. God dealt with them in all of that, but they schemed, rebelled, and rejected it. When the Truth shows forbearance toward the people He calls to faith, He (subhanahu) takes into account that He created them and takes into account the human disposition, which may be difficult to soften at the first call. He calls it once and it does not respond, so He pardons. God took from them a firm, solemn covenant to obey Him, but they disobeyed and broke the covenant. After that the report tells us, so that we learn that God does not tire until you, O humans, tire.

Then He, glory be to Him, says after that:

﴿So for their breaking their covenant, and their disbelief in the signs of Allah, and their killing of the prophets without right, and their saying, "Our hearts are wrapped up." Nay, Allah has set a seal upon them for their disbelief, so they do not believe, except a few.﴾ (4:155)

They broke all the covenants and the matters that had preceded. The meaning of mithaq (covenant) is a firm, confirmed pledge, and naqd al-mithaq (breaking the covenant) is its dissolution. This is what entails the punishment with which Allah threatens them. They disbelieved in the signs of Allah, which He sent down to support Musa (peace be upon him). They killed the prophets of Allah without right. And they offered as a justification for this that their hearts are ghulf, unable to hear the call to faith. That is, their hearts are covered, wrapped in a sheath, so that nothing within them comes out and nothing from outside enters them. By this they intended to correct Allah, saying: "Our hearts do not let error out or let faith in." This has already occurred before in the words of the Truth:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe. Allah has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their eyes is a covering, and for them is a great punishment.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 2:6-7)

We say: Were the hearts created ghulf, meaning that the hearts were created sealed, so that guidance cannot enter them and error cannot come out of them? Or is it you who made the seal and you who fashioned the sheath?

In the two verses of Surah al-Baqarah, He, glory be to Him, made clear that it is He who set a seal upon their hearts and their hearing, and over their eyes a covering. The sealing of the heart is so that they do not come to recognise the proof, because the heart is the locus of proofs, certainty and beliefs. The sealing of the hearing and sight is the sealing of the instruments by which the clear signs of the existence of the Supreme Truth are perceived. So the seat of beliefs is sealed, which is the heart, and a covering is placed over the ears and the sight. Is this, then, something inherent in the natural constitution of these people? No. For if it were by natural constitution, why would Allah single them out with that constitution? And why were those who were guided not sealed, neither upon their hearts, nor upon their hearing, nor upon their sight?

However, each of them justifies to himself and to others his deviation and excess against himself by saying, "Allah created me thus." This is a false and deceitful statement, because the one who says it has disbelieved first. When he disbelieved and turned away from the truth, Allah left him in his state, for Allah is the most free of partners from association; whoever takes a partner with Allah, it belongs to the partner and not to Allah. Thus the sealing came as a consequence of disbelief.

The verses of Surah al-Baqarah set out the sequence of causes: disbelief occurs first, then the sealing of the heart, hearing and sight comes as a result of it. Here, in the verse of Surah al-Nisa, "and their saying, 'Our hearts are wrapped up.' Nay, Allah has set a seal upon them for their disbelief," so disbelief came first. In this there is a rebuttal to anyone who says, "Allah does not guide me," without considering that Allah does not guide those who disbelieve in Him. Likewise the wrongdoer or the corrupt, and the greatest example of this is Iblis, who disbelieved first, and after that Allah left him to himself and dispensed with him.

Here we pause at a linguistic point regarding His words: "So for their breaking" (fa-bima naqdihim). The superficial understanding of the principles of style may ask: why did "ma" come here? Some have said that "ma" here is superfluous (za'idah). We say: beware of saying that there is a superfluous particle in the speech of Allah, for that would mean the meaning is complete without it, and it would be an excess beyond the need with no benefit in it. Rather, you should say: "I do not understand why this particle came." Especially since we live in this age as a nation whose eloquence is acquired, not natural, and we do not possess the innate Arabic tongue. Had we not learned Arabic, we could not speak it. As for the eloquent Arab upon whom the Qur'an was revealed, he spoke the Arabic language without sitting before a teacher, and did not learn that the subject is marfu' (nominative) and the object is mansub (accusative); rather he spoke the language by his nature and innate faculty.

As for us, we live in a different time: non-Arabic speech has overwhelmed us, our ears are filled with grammatical errors, and we have come to teach ourselves the rules of the Arabic language so that we may speak in correct style.

The rules of grammar (nahw) were derived by deduction from the original Arab linguistic disposition (saliqah), which existed without instruction. The scholars surveyed Arabic usages and found that the subject is marfu', the dual is raised by the alif, and the sound masculine plural is raised by the waw; thus we took the rules from those who had no rules, but who spoke by disposition, nature and innate faculty.

The Arab of old, at the time the Qur'an was revealed, heard His words, "So for their breaking," and not one of them noticed that anything had departed from correct style. We know that some of the Arabs were disbelievers in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and did not accept the Qur'an. Had there been a single word departing from what is customary in the language, they would have cried it out and proclaimed it. But the Qur'an came as an inimitable speech upon the tongue of Muhammad (ﷺ) to convey it to them, declaring: "I have brought you the Qur'an as a miracle you cannot imitate, even though you are Arabs and eloquent."

The challenger always seeks to pick out some error, yet none of the Arabs said that the Qur'an contains a solecism. This is proof that the Qur'anic style conforms to the Arabic faculty.

The words of the Truth, "fa-bima naqdihim," originally mean: "By their breaking the covenant, We did to them what they came to." Why does "ma" come here? Some scholars said it is superfluous, added for emphasis. Again we say: beware of saying there is a superfluous particle in the speech of Allah. "Ma" came here for a clear meaning, and the Truth says in another place of the Qur'an:

﴿There came to us no bringer of good tidings nor warner.﴾ (5:19)

They said the original phrase was "ma jaa'anaa bashir," and that "min" came in superfluously to smooth the wording. We say: had the phrase come as they claimed, the meaning would not be sound. To clarify this, let me strike this example, and to Allah belongs the highest likeness: when someone says, "I have no money" (ma 'indi mal), this negates that the speaker has money, though perhaps he has a small amount that does not deserve to be called money. But if someone says, "I have not any money at all" (ma 'indi min mal), the meaning is that he does not own money in any sense, that he is utterly bankrupt and possesses nothing at all of what could be called money. Thus "ma jaa'anaa bashir" is not like "ma jaa'anaa min bashir"; the meaning of the latter is that no messenger at all came to them as a bringer of good tidings or a warner, from the very beginning of what could be called a messenger.

So the words of the Truth, "fa-bima naqdihim mithaqahum," mean: "because of the breaking of the covenant, We did such-and-such to them." Why, then, have the scholars raised this uproar? The reason is the presence of what comes after the "ba'" and before the verbal noun: that is, they broke the covenant in every form of it. Breaking the covenant has many forms, so "ma" here is interrogative, used for amazement: "In what form of breaking and violating the covenant have We cursed them?" We cursed them for the multitude of covenants and pledges they broke. And the Truth has said:

﴿So for their breaking their covenant, and their disbelief in the signs of Allah, and their killing of the prophets without right, and their saying, "Our hearts are wrapped up." Nay, Allah has set a seal upon them for their disbelief, so they do not believe, except a few.﴾ (Surah al-Nisa)

He did not say: "So for their breaking their covenant, their disbelief in the signs of Allah, their killing of the prophets without right, and their saying, 'Our hearts are wrapped up,' Allah sealed upon their hearts." The presence of "bal" (nay/rather) shows us that there is a matter we are turning away from. When we say, "Zayd came to me, bal 'Amr" (rather Amr), the speaker erred in saying "Zayd came to me," then corrected himself, saying "rather Amr," thereby negating the coming of Zayd and affirming the coming of Amr.

The Truth said: "Nay, Allah has set a seal upon them for their disbelief, so they do not believe, except a few." In ordinary style one would expect: "for their disbelief and their killing of the prophets, Allah set a seal upon their hearts." But Allah, glory be to Him, did not say that, for a profound wisdom. And so that we may know that wisdom, let us seek the counterpart of "Allah set a seal upon their hearts": the counterpart is "Allah opened their hearts to guidance."

The words of the Truth came expressing exactly their position: "So for their breaking their covenant, their disbelief in the signs of Allah, their killing of the prophets without right, and their saying, 'Our hearts are wrapped up.' Nay, Allah has set a seal upon them."

Thus we see the greatness of the Qur'an, which brings precise meaning, and we must reflect upon it and ponder every word of it.

The Truth, then, presents the causes for what He did to them, by way of justifications: their breaking the covenant, their disbelief in the signs of Allah, and their killing of the prophets without right. Therefore Allah did not open to them with guidance; rather Allah set a seal upon their hearts with disbelief. So the presence of "bal" is evidence that something has been negated and something has been affirmed. The matter Allah negated is that He did not open guidance and faith to them; the matter affirmed is that He set a seal upon their hearts with disbelief. In another verse He says of them:

﴿And they say, "Our hearts are wrapped up." Nay, Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so little is it that they believe.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 2:88)

Their hearts are not wrapped; rather, it is Allah's curse upon them, His distancing and expelling of them, and His dispensing with them. Therefore He left them to themselves, so desires overcame them. Why did the Truth close the verse with "so they do not believe, except a few"? Because its purpose is not to close the door of faith absolutely before these people: as we have known before, it is "preserving the possibility" (siyanat al-ihtimal). One of them may declare the faith he has hidden in himself, so how would he find the opportunity for that if Allah had said of them all, "Allah has set a seal upon their hearts"?

For the one among them who wishes to declare faith, the door does not seem open to him; but when he finds the Truth saying, "so they do not believe, except a few," he knows that the door of faith is open to all.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 4, verse 156:

Then, after that, the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿And for their disbelief, and their saying against Mary a tremendous slander.﴾

One might ask: did the Truth not say earlier that "their disbelief" was one of the causes of God sealing their hearts? I say: beware of saying that there is a repeated word in the Qur'an, for the One who speaks is God, the Exalted, who forgets nothing and does not repeat without reason. Disbelief also has degrees: sometimes it is disbelief in God, sometimes disbelief in the signs of God, a third time disbelief in the messengers, a fourth time disbelief in some of the prophets, and a fifth time disbelief in some of the heavenly books.

So the forms of disbelief are many. The disbelief in the previous verse was disbelief in the signs of God, while their disbelief in this verse is explained by the Truth in His words: "and for their disbelief, and their saying against Mary a tremendous slander." They disbelieved in Jesus, peace be upon him, and they uttered a great slander against Mary. This is disbelief in the signs of God and in a messenger from God.

His words, the Truth, "and for their disbelief" are coordinated (ʿaṭf) with "their breaking of the covenant," with "their disbelief in the signs of God," with "their killing of the prophets," and with "their saying: our hearts are uncircumcised." We observe here that the Truth did not mention the bāʾ (the preposition "for/because of") that came at the beginning of the previous verse when He said: "So for their breaking of their covenant."

This indicates that we are before the criterion of mercy from our Lord, the Exalted. It would have been enough for the commission of any one of these mentioned deeds for God to seal their hearts. Yet they committed all the mentioned deeds together, and did not commit just one of them. This is evidence that God does not lie in wait for His servants, nor hunt them, nor scheme to cast them into disbelief; rather He draws the servants toward faith.

They committed four grave acts: they broke the covenant, they disbelieved in the signs of God, they killed the prophets without right, and they claimed that God had sealed their hearts.

When He made these four acts one single crime, this was grace and mercy from Him.

Then He mentions to them another crime: "and for their disbelief, and their saying against Mary a tremendous slander." Here we find that He, glorified is He, has equated their saying of slander against Mary with all the preceding acts, because they objected to the messengership and prophethood of Jesus, peace be upon him, who is one of the prophets of firm resolve (ulu al-ʿazm) among the messengers, with things that may be among the causes that led some people into trial concerning him. God created him by a special creation. He, glorified is He, created all people from Adam, peace be upon him, whom God shaped from clay and then breathed into him the spirit, and the creation of the rest came through mating.

As for Jesus, peace be upon him, God created him in a special manner. So how could they disbelieve in him, and how could they accuse his mother Mary, peace be upon her, who was a virgin (batūl)?

It is permissible for a woman to be accused, to be slandered, and to be described with everything: a liar, a thief, or ugly. But an accusation against her honour: no. The Truth here specifies two subjects of disbelief: their saying of slander against Mary, which is disbelief in God, and their disbelief in Jesus, who came with a birth other than the ordinary manner of birth, despite the fact that this is an honour for him and a rebuke to the Jews who had drowned in materialism to the point that they said: "Show us God openly" (Q. 4:153).

Indeed, the Truth provided for them with an unseen provision whose causes they do not know: in the wilderness He provided them with manna and quails. The manna was like cream in colour and the taste of white honey, a substance that falls on the leaves of trees in some environments, and the quail is a bird resembling the common quail. They used to take the manna from the trees, gather it and eat it, a provision that came to them without their sowing it or working for it. But they said: "No, we want to plant a crop that grows from the earth, and we will not wait for the unseen, for the unseen may withhold from us."

﴿So call upon your Lord for us to bring forth for us from what the earth produces: its herbs...﴾ (Q. 2:61).

They, then, do not trust what is in the hand of God, and they want the material matter. Therefore the Truth startles them with a compelling turn and brings a matter that contradicts the law of matter at its foundation, namely the birth of Jesus, peace be upon him, in a non-conventional manner. A human comes into the world from a father and a mother, but the Truth brought Jesus created from a mother without a father. Thus materialism was refuted, and they, as materialists, had overlooked the first creation:

﴿Were We then wearied by the first creation? Nay, they are in doubt about a new creation.﴾ (Q. 50:15).

So why the trial concerning Jesus, peace be upon him? He overturned before them the conventional material foundation of a human's coming into the world from a male and a female, and Jesus, peace be upon him, came from a mother without a father, so that God, glorified is He, might establish the absoluteness of power, and that He made causes for mankind. If mankind wants a causer, then they must take the causes; but God, glorified is He, is the Causer of causes and their Creator, and He alone is able to bring a thing into being by setting aside all causes.

We know that the question of creation revolves around four modes. Either a thing arises from the existence of two things: this is the first form. Or a thing arises from the non-existence of two things: this is the second form. Or a thing arises from the existence of the first thing and the non-existence of the second: this is the third form. Or a thing arises from the existence of the second thing with the non-existence of the first: this is the fourth form.

These are the four forms of the existence of any thing. God did not will that creation, which is man, the honoured one for whom the Truth subjected everything in the universe, should be in one single manner, lest anyone say: causation is conditioned for existence.

Rather, the caused is what is conditioned in existence, as evidenced by the fact that He, glorified is He, created Adam, peace be upon him, without a father or a mother; created us all from a father and a mother; created Jesus, peace be upon him, from a mother without a father; and created Eve from a father without a mother.

This is the clear rational division. The matter is not one of racial origin, but of value and capable power. The power of the Truth is also manifest before us when the causes exist, such as a father and a mother, yet God wills that both be barren. He is the One who said:

﴿To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He creates what He wills; He bestows female offspring on whom He wills and bestows male offspring on whom He wills, or He pairs them, males and females, and He makes barren whom He wills.﴾ (Q. 42:49–50).

So the matter is not a question of causes that produce existence, but a Causer who wills to bring something into existence. The Truth willed that the coming of Jesus, peace be upon him, be in this form, to draw the Children of Israel, perhaps they would emerge from the errors of materialism. He brought him into existence from a mother without a father, and this was a sign of the absoluteness of His power. But the Jews received this matter in a manner contrary to God's intention, so they denied Jesus, and the denial occurred before Jesus spoke the Gospel, and they stood against his message with violence. What shows us that they are a people of lies is their desire to continue their religious domination. They had a law that required stoning for the adulteress. So why did they not accuse Mary of fornication when she bore Jesus? And why did they not punish her according to the law of the Torah? And why did they wait until Jesus, peace be upon him, came with the Gospel to say: "O fornicator, O son of the fornicator"? Their waiting was evidence that the birth of Jesus, peace be upon him, was a clear sign that shattered them and turned them away from that. Jesus, peace be upon him, spoke after his birth, and Mary never spoke, because what had happened was a matter beyond her speech, and God had prepared her for this situation, commanding her to be silent when they questioned her and to point to the infant in the cradle:

﴿So she pointed to him. They said: "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?" He said: "Indeed I am a servant of God; He has given me the Book and made me a prophet, and He has made me blessed wherever I be, and has enjoined upon me prayer and zakat as long as I live."﴾ (Q. 19:29–31).

They were astonished with an astonishment that broke their strength, for the power of the adversary, at the moment it sees this, finds nothing but collapse. The Truth is manifest, and falsehood is confused... So the matter was in their hands, and in their Torah it was that whoever commits adultery is stoned; then why did they not stone the mother of Jesus? It must be that they were struck by a force that made the scales of their hatred unbalanced. The overwhelming miracle is the speech of Jesus, son of Mary, in the cradle: "Indeed I am a servant of God; He has given me the Book and made me a prophet," and the surprise made the strongest among them collapse, and their strength gave way.

This is on the side of the Jews. As for the side of some followers of Jesus, peace be upon him: a child speaking in the cradle is a miracle by every measure. How then do their books lack the saying of Jesus in the cradle: "Indeed I am a servant of God"? The word must have been carefully studied and not forgotten. And the soldiers of God, glorified and exalted is He, preserved the word that affirms the humanity of Jesus, peace be upon him.

When we say this, our aim is not to correct anyone's beliefs; we only wish that the logic of faith become clear to the minds of Muslims. As for the adherents of other religions, they are free in what they believe, and what matters to us is that our religion and our Qur'an be clear before our eyes, and that no one dare to distort it.

"And for their disbelief, and their saying against Mary a tremendous slander." As Muslims, we disdain to say what they said of slander against Mary the virgin. Slander (buhtān) is the fierce lie. There is a kind of lie that may be acceptable and a kind that is not acceptable. If someone says of a pious man: "He drank wine," while the speaker knows that he is lying, this is a heavy, fierce lie, which whoever hears it is bewildered and astonished, and this is buhtān. The Jews did not feel shame or refrain when they hurled at the pure Mary, by God's command, the buhtān, although they knew that Mary had a past of goodness and uprightness.

Mary's past was luminous. She lived in the sanctuary (miḥrāb), devoted to the One who created her. Therefore the Truth describes this slander as great, for it wounded Mary in her honour. Had they gone back to their history before Mary bore Jesus, they would have found that every one of the daughters of the Children of Israel used to hope that the prophet who would be born after Moses would come from her womb, and they knew that the prophet who would come after Moses would be born of a virgin. The Children of Israel had informed their daughters of how the coming prophet would come, Jesus son of Mary, exactly as the good tidings of the Messenger of God, Muhammad, peace be upon him, were announced:

﴿So when there came to them what they recognised, they disbelieved in it; so the curse of God is upon the disbelievers.﴾ (Q. 2:89).

And from God's mercy toward Mary herself, God provided preliminary signs that proved to her own self that she was innocent, and that the whole process had been accomplished by God's "Be" (kun). God did not make the matter a secret from Mary, so that she would conceive by the command "Be" without knowing. Rather, He, glorified is He, willed it to be a material process: the angel came to Mary and breathed into her the pregnancy, and she knew the cause materially through the angel and the breathing, so that she would not blame herself or suspect that something had happened to her while she was asleep or otherwise.

God willed the matter in that form to make it for her a matter that dispels doubt in her heart. She had been given the good tidings of it, to reassure her, when she was young before puberty, and Zachariah came to her, he being her guardian, who brought her food, and he entered the sanctuary and found provision with her, and asked her:

(Whence is this for you?) She answered: ﴿It is from God; indeed God provides for whom He wills without reckoning.﴾ (Q. 3:37).

Mary the virgin had earlier said: "Indeed God provides for whom He wills without reckoning." It is by reckoning that a woman should have a husband in order to be provided with a child, but God provides for whom He wills without reckoning. Remarkably, in this saying she alerted Zachariah to a matter that was at the centre of his consciousness, and therefore the Truth says:

﴿There Zachariah called upon his Lord and said: "My Lord, grant me from You a good offspring; indeed You are the Hearer of supplication." The angels called to him while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary: "God gives you good tidings of Yahya, confirming a word from God, and a lord and chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous." He said: "My Lord, how can I have a son when old age has reached me and my wife is barren?" He said: "Thus God does what He wills."﴾ (Q. 3:38–40).

So Mary encouraged Zachariah to call upon his Lord, and that was a preparatory sequence to reassure Mary's feeling that her bearing of Jesus, peace be upon him, had come by "Be." The Truth also brought her summer fruit in winter. When she said to our master Zachariah: "Indeed God provides for whom He wills without reckoning," he took notice and entered through this door, and he called upon his Lord, although he knew that his wife was barren and that he had reached extreme old age. The meaning for us of a man's saying about himself that he has reached extreme old age is clear: that he no longer has the capacity to

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (*Tafsir al-Sha'rawi*, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 4, verse 157:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿And [for] their saying, "Indeed, we killed the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the Messenger of Allah." And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them. And indeed, those who differ over it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption. And they did not kill him for certain.﴾ (157)

We note that the verse begins with the conjunction *wa* (and), connecting it to what precedes it, which is His saying, the Truth:

﴿So for their breaking of their covenant, and their disbelief in the signs of Allah, and their killing of the prophets without right, and their saying, "Our hearts are wrapped." Rather, Allah has sealed them for their disbelief, so they believe not, except a few. And for their disbelief and their saying against Mary a great slander.﴾ (155-156) (Surah an-Nisa')

He (glorified is He) adds to these crimes this new crime: "And their saying, 'Indeed, we killed the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the Messenger of Allah.'" What is most astonishing in this saying is the phrase "the Messenger of Allah." Is it here part of their saying? If they said it, this is evidence of absolute obstinacy, and had they said only that they killed him, the crime would have been less severe. But if they knew that he was the Messenger of Allah and killed him, then this is an extremely grave crime. Or else the phrase "the Messenger of Allah" in this verse is not part of their genuine saying but of their sarcastic saying.

Let me give an example to clarify this matter. Suppose a person of immense strength, famous for his power, is struck and defeated by another man, who then tells his group: "I have struck the strong youth among you." So their saying "the Messenger of Allah" may be of the category of sarcasm, or the phrase "the Messenger of Allah" here is from the saying of the Truth (glorified and exalted is He), added to their saying in order to make their deed appear more monstrous.

"And their saying: 'Indeed, we killed the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the Messenger of Allah.'" It is as if the Truth did not wish to mention Jesus, son of Mary, except linked or described by the phrase "the Messenger of Allah," so that we may know the monstrousness of what they did. Jesus, son of Mary, is the Messenger of Allah in spite of their noses (i.e., despite their wishes), especially since the matter concerns their denial and ingratitude toward the blessings of Allah and their disbelief in the signs of Allah. It is as if the Truth is mocking them, because Allah would not send a messenger to clarify His method to the people and then allow the people to dominate and kill him before he has completed his mission. He brought the phrase "the Messenger of Allah" here as a preface, so that the mind would turn to the fact that what they said is a lie.

After that He says to us: "And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him." The phrase "nor did they crucify him" here serves to clarify that their mere assumption that they had killed the Messiah led them to spread it and announce it to the people. They did this before they turned to the idea of crucifixion. They killed a person whom Allah made to resemble him for them, and he was not the Messiah, and they crucified him afterward. As soon as this person was killed, they spread the news of the killing before the idea of crucifixion began. Allah cuts this matter short for them, so He says: "And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them."

He had previously drawn our attention to the birth of the Messiah and how the Children of Israel received it with an uproar. Despite their knowledge of the news that the Messiah would come by birth without a father, and despite the fact that they had taught their daughters to hope that any one of them would have the honour of bearing the Messiah, they nevertheless uttered slander against Mary, whom Allah had chosen. Likewise, the matter of his death was also a cause of uproar.

The combination of the two uproars, the uproar of the birth and the uproar of the death, together in the message of Messiah (peace be upon him), shows us that the intellect must have a unified interpretive framework. When the intellect speaks about the matter of the birth of Jesus, son of Mary, a person must sense that the matter came contrary to an established custom. And when the Truth informs us that the Children of Israel plotted to kill Jesus, son of Mary, and that Allah raised him to Himself, the matter has likewise come with a contrary case. We must believe what Allah has informed us of, and the intellect must remember that the birth was contrary (to custom). So why should the end not be contrary as well?

Just as we accept that Jesus, son of Mary, came without a father, we must accept that the Truth raised him in the end and took him. The birth would not have been within the bounds of the intellect's conception had the Truth not informed us of it. Likewise, his death must be acceptable within the bounds of the Truth's communication to us. The birth and the end concerning Jesus, son of Mary, are each marvellous. If we understand the first marvel, the birth, then we regard it as a preface to Jesus, son of Mary, entering existence and entering life by a marvellous matter. Why should he not leave it by a marvellous matter? And if the Truth tells us that Jesus, son of Mary, left life by a marvellous matter, we do not wonder at that, because whoever began with a marvel should not be surprised to end with a marvel.

He (glorified and exalted is He) has judged and said: "And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them." The phrase "it was made to appear so to them" is evidence of the haste of the attempt to kill. He had cast his likeness upon another person, and that is evidence that the matter was not natural, having none of the firm verification from the lying-in-wait killers. We know that the disciples (al-hawariyyun) and followers of our master Jesus used to wrap their heads and conceal their features. That is why the Truth said to us: "but it was made to appear so to them," meaning that it was made to seem to them that they had killed him.

The reports differ concerning the phrase "it was made to appear so to them." Some say that when they sought Jesus, son of Mary, in order to kill him, he entered a *khawkhah*, and the *khawkhah* is a door within a door. In old houses, a house had a large door for bringing in large things, and within this large door there was a small door that allowed individuals to pass. In the roof of the house there was an opening and a window called *rawzanah* or *nawzah*.

When they sought Jesus, he entered the *khawkhah*, and a man named Tiṭanus entered behind him. When our master Jesus saw this matter, Allah inspired him to look upward, and he found something lifting him. When the people were slow to see Tiṭanus, he came out to them, and they asked: "If this is Tiṭanus, where is Jesus? And if this is Jesus, where is Tiṭanus?"

So the resemblance became confused for them between Tiṭanus and Jesus, and Allah cast the likeness of Jesus upon Tiṭanus, so they killed him. Or else, when they came upon Jesus (peace be upon him), the disciples were with him, and Jesus said to them: "Which of you will have cast upon him my likeness, and for him is Paradise?" What more could a disciple desire for himself than Paradise? Jesus (peace be upon him) offered the greatest reward to any believer, and one of the disciples accepted this task, who is called Sarkhas. He cast the likeness of the Messiah Jesus upon him, and the Jews killed Sarkhas.

They also said that when some of those who had gone to kill Jesus learned that he had been raised, they feared that the story of Jesus's being raised would spread among the people, and they would believe in the message of Jesus, and the people might take revenge upon those who had wanted to kill him. Therefore the killers brought a person and killed him and cast upon this slain man the likeness of Jesus, and the killers announced that they had killed Jesus, son of Mary. Or else the slain man was one of those who had sold the Prophet of Allah, Jesus, to the Jews. When he saw the scene and found the lying-in-wait men entering upon the disciples, with Jesus among them, and the lying-in-wait men asked the disciples: "Which of you is Jesus?" the impulse of repentance awoke in the soul of the one who had betrayed Jesus, and the pangs of conscience for betraying the Messenger led him to say: "I am Jesus." The lying-in-wait men did not imagine that a person would answer their question, "Which of you is Jesus?", unless he were actually Jesus. Since the scene of the lying-in-wait men suggested that they would kill Jesus, they killed the one who confessed about himself without verification. Or else one man sold Jesus for thirty dinars, and it was confused for them, so they killed the informer, and they did not obtain Jesus, son of Mary. We, as Muslims, do not give great attention to those reports. What matters is that they said, "We killed Jesus and crucified him."

Our Qur'an, which was revealed to our Messenger (may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him), says: "And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them." And the Truth told us: "Rather, Allah raised him to Himself." The matter has ended for us, because we, as believers, do not first take the religious particulars and then believe if we confirm them. Rather, we first believe in the One who revealed these particulars and then confirm everything that comes from Him (glorified is He). He said that, so we believed in Him, and the matter ended.

Investigating this matter does not concern us in any way. It is sufficient for us that the Truth (glorified and exalted is He) said: "And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them." This statement shows us that the killers did not verify the identity of the slain person, which is an expected matter in such an affair, where things can become confused.

We see, in any incident that occurs in the presence of large numbers of people with their eyes open, that the reports about it differ, and sometimes the incident is filmed and recorded, yet the reports still differ. So what about an incident like this in an ancient time when all the precautions we see in our time did not exist? Therefore the confusion of opinions and reports about that incident is an expected matter, and it is sufficient for us that the Truth (glorified and exalted is He) said: "And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him."

So Jesus remains (alive), because the Truth did not bring us news of the death of Jesus, and the matter stays on the basis of what the verses established, that Allah (glorified and exalted is He) raised Jesus, son of Mary. As Muslims, we do not find it unlikely that the Truth (glorified and exalted is He) raised him to heaven, because the principle of the existence of a human being in heaven has been established for our Messenger (may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him). He told us (peace be upon him) that he was taken up to heaven, that he ascended, met the prophets, and saw many visions. So the principle of a human being ascending from the earth while still living the material human life to heaven is an expected matter, and the disagreement is about the length of time, but that disagreement does not undermine the principle, whether he ascended and remained in heaven for minutes, hours, or months.
